# Adobe Commerce: Product Types & Catalog Configuration

## 1. Product Types Overview

Adobe Commerce supports **six core product types** shared with Open Source, plus a **seventh Commerce-exclusive type (Gift Card)**. Understanding which type to use — and the specific rules governing each — is fundamental to both implementation and the certification exam.

```
+-------------------+------------------------------------------+------------------+
|   Product Type    |        Primary Use Case                  |  Has Own Stock?  |
+-------------------+------------------------------------------+------------------+
| Simple            | Single SKU, tangible physical item       |       YES        |
| Configurable      | Parent + child simples (e.g. size/color) |       NO         |
| Grouped           | Collection of linked simple products     |  Per child only  |
| Bundle            | Build-your-own kit with options          |       NO*        |
| Virtual           | Services, memberships, no shipping       |       YES        |
| Downloadable      | Digital files or links                   |       YES        |
| Gift Card (EE)    | Physical, virtual, or combined gift card |       YES        |
+-------------------+------------------------------------------+------------------+
* Bundle stock is derived from selected bundle items (simple/virtual products)
```

- **Exam focus:** Know which product types trigger shipping. Virtual, Downloadable, and virtual Gift Cards do **not** trigger shipping; all others (Simple, Configurable children, Grouped children, Bundle items when physical, physical Gift Cards) **do**.
- **Exam focus:** The six core product types are: Simple, Configurable, Grouped, Bundle, Virtual, Downloadable. Adobe Commerce (EE) adds **Gift Card** as a seventh type. There is no "Complex" type — that is not official terminology.

---

## 2. Simple Products

### Definition
A Simple product is a **single SKU** representing a physical item with no variations. It is the foundational unit upon which Configurable, Grouped, and Bundle products are built.

### Key Characteristics
- Has its own **stock quantity** tracked individually
- Can be sold standalone or as a **child/component** of other product types
- Requires a **weight** field (used for shipping calculations)
- Supports all standard pricing: regular price, special price, tier pricing, group pricing

### Creating a Simple Product (Admin Path)
```
Catalog → Products → Add Product → (default type: Simple Product)
```

### Required Fields
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Attribute Set | Determines which attributes appear on the form |
| Product Name | Displayed on storefront |
| SKU | Unique identifier (auto-generated or manual) |
| Price | Base price |
| Stock | Qty and stock status |
| Visibility | Not Visible Individually / Catalog / Search / Catalog, Search |

### Visibility Setting — Critical Concept
```
Not Visible Individually  <--  Used for child simples of a Configurable product
Catalog                   <--  Appears in category pages only
Search                    <--  Appears in search results only
Catalog, Search           <--  Default for standalone products
```

- **Exam focus:** Child simples (used inside Configurable products) should be set to **"Not Visible Individually"** so they don't appear as duplicate standalone listings on the storefront.

---

## 3. Configurable Products

### Definition
A Configurable product is a **parent SKU** that presents the customer with one or more dropdown or swatch selectors (e.g., Size, Color). Each combination of attribute values corresponds to a **child Simple product** that holds actual inventory.

### Architecture Diagram
```
Configurable Product (Parent)
   |
   |-- SKU: shirt-blue-sm   (Simple, size=S, color=Blue)
   |-- SKU: shirt-blue-md   (Simple, size=M, color=Blue)
   |-- SKU: shirt-red-sm    (Simple, size=S, color=Red)
   +-- SKU: shirt-red-md    (Simple, size=M, color=Red)

  Parent has NO own stock.
  Parent price = price of child (or overridden per child).
```

### Critical Stock Rule
> **The parent Configurable product has NO stock of its own.** Stock is tracked at the **child Simple product** level. When all children are out of stock, the parent becomes unavailable.

- **Exam focus:** This is one of the most commonly tested facts. The parent Configurable product **does not have a Qty field** that matters for inventory; it derives availability from its children.

### Configurable Attributes — Requirements
For an attribute to be usable as a configurable "axis":
1. **Scope** must be **Global**
2. **Input type** must be **Dropdown** (or visual/text swatch)
3. Must be a **user-defined** attribute (system attributes like Status or Visibility cannot be used)

The system automatically determines eligibility based on these criteria — there is no separate "Use to Create Configurable Product" toggle in the Magento 2 admin UI. If an attribute meets all three requirements above, it appears as available when creating configurable product variations.

```
Stores → Attributes → Product → [Edit Attribute]
  - Scope: Global          ← REQUIRED
  - Catalog Input Type: Dropdown / Visual Swatch / Text Swatch
  - Must be User Defined (not a system attribute)
```

- **Exam focus:** An attribute with store-level or website-level scope **cannot** be used as a configurable attribute axis. System-defined attributes (e.g., status, visibility) also cannot be used even if they are Global scope.

### Creating a Configurable Product — Step Sequence
```
Step 1: Catalog → Products → Add Product → Configurable Product
Step 2: Choose Attribute Set
Step 3: Fill basic info (Name, SKU, Price, Category)
Step 4: Configurations tab → "Create Configurations" wizard
   a. Select attributes (e.g., Color, Size)
   b. Select or create attribute values
   c. System generates child SKUs (bulk or manual naming)
   d. Assign images, price adjustments, qty per variation
Step 5: Save
```

### Price on Configurable Products
- The **parent price** serves as a **base/default display price**
- Each child simple can have its own **price override**
- When a customer selects a variation, the displayed price updates to the child's price
- **Price adjustments** (e.g., +$5 for XL) can be configured per variation

### Swatches for Configurable Products
| Swatch Type | Input Type | Visual |
|-------------|------------|--------|
| Visual Swatch | Visual Swatch | Color blocks or uploaded images |
| Text Swatch | Text Swatch | Text labels (e.g., "S", "M", "L") |
| Dropdown | Dropdown | Standard HTML select element |

---

## 4. Grouped Products

### Definition
A Grouped product displays a **collection of linked Simple (or Virtual) products** on a single product page. Each item has its own quantity input and can be added to cart independently. There is **no inherent parent SKU price** — each child has its own price.

### Key Characteristics
- Each linked product is a **separate Simple or Virtual product** with its own SKU, price, and stock
- Customers can set **individual quantities** for each item (including 0 to skip an item)
- The Grouped product itself has **no price** and **no stock** — it is purely a presentational container
- Child products remain independently purchasable (unless visibility is set otherwise)

### Architecture Diagram
```
Grouped Product: "Living Room Set"
   |
   +-- Simple: Sofa          $999  [Qty: ___]
   +-- Simple: Coffee Table  $299  [Qty: ___]
   +-- Simple: Side Table    $149  [Qty: ___]

  Each item added to cart separately as its own line item.
```

### Admin Path
```
Catalog → Products → Add Product → Grouped Product
  → "Grouped Products" tab → Add Products to Group
```

- **Exam focus:** Grouped products do NOT have a price field. Attempting to set a price on the Grouped parent itself is not supported. The price shown to customers is per individual linked product.
- **Exam focus:** Unlike Bundle or Configurable, Grouped products appear in the cart as **multiple separate line items** — one per product selected.

---

## 5. Bundle Products

### Definition
A Bundle product lets customers **build their own product** by selecting options from predefined sets. Each option contains one or more Simple or Virtual products. This is essentially a "build-your-own" kit.

### Bundle Option Types (Input Types)
| Input Type | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| Drop-down | One choice from a list |
| Radio Buttons | One choice per option group |
| Checkbox | Multiple choices allowed |
| Multiple Select | Multiple choices from list |

### Pricing Models — CRITICAL DISTINCTION

#### Dynamic Pricing
```
Bundle Price = Sum of selected items' prices
  + Any price adjustments
  + Applicable tax

Use when:
  - Items have varying prices
  - You want the bundle price to reflect current item prices
  - Items may be on sale and you want the bundle to reflect that
```

#### Fixed Pricing
```
Bundle Price = Predetermined fixed price set on the Bundle parent
  (Items inside do NOT contribute their own prices)

Use when:
  - You want a consistent bundle price regardless of item prices
  - Running promotions with a set bundle discount
  - Simpler pricing display is required
```

- **Exam focus:** **Dynamic pricing** = price calculated from components. **Fixed pricing** = single price on the bundle itself. This distinction is heavily tested.
- **Exam focus:** With **Fixed Price** bundles, a special price and tier prices can be set on the bundle parent. With **Dynamic Price** bundles, special prices and tier prices are set on the **individual items**.

### Required vs. Optional Options
```
Each Bundle Option can be marked as:
  - Required: Customer MUST make a selection for this option
  - Optional: Customer may skip this option

If all options are optional and customer skips them all → still add to cart
```

### Bundle Stock Logic
```
Bundle product is In Stock if:
  - At least one item in each REQUIRED option is in stock

Bundle product is Out of Stock if:
  - Any required option has ALL its products out of stock
```

- **Exam focus:** The Bundle parent has no stock of its own; availability is determined by the **required option** item availability.

### Creating a Bundle Product
```
Catalog → Products → Add Product → Bundle Product
  → Dynamic Price: Yes/No
  → Bundle Items tab:
      + Add Option
        - Option Title (e.g., "Storage Size")
        - Input Type (dropdown/radio/checkbox/multiple)
        - Required: Yes/No
        + Add Products to Option (search and select Simples/Virtuals)
          - Each product: Default Qty, User Defined Qty (Yes/No)
```

### User Defined Quantity
When **User Defined Qty = Yes**, the customer can enter their own quantity for a bundle item. When **No**, the quantity is fixed to the default.

---

## 6. Virtual Products

### Definition
A Virtual product is identical to a Simple product **except it does not have a weight and does not trigger shipping**. Used for intangible goods: services, warranties, subscriptions, memberships, support packages.

### Key Differences from Simple
| Attribute | Simple | Virtual |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Weight field | Required | Not present |
| Triggers shipping | Yes | No |
| Can be in Grouped | Yes | Yes |
| Can be in Bundle | Yes | Yes |
| Cart behavior | Standard | No shipping step if cart contains only virtual items |

### Checkout Behavior
> If a cart contains **only Virtual (and/or Downloadable) products**, the checkout shipping step is **skipped entirely**.

- **Exam focus:** Virtual products skip the shipping step. If even one physical product is in the cart alongside virtual products, shipping IS shown.

### Common Use Cases
- Extended warranties
- Service fees / installation
- Event tickets
- Software licenses (without file delivery — use Downloadable for files)
- Gift wrapping charges

---

## 7. Downloadable Products

### Definition
A Downloadable product is a digital product delivered via **file download or external URL**. After purchase, the customer receives links to download files from their account.

### Delivery Methods
| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| File Upload | File stored on server; customer downloads from AC |
| URL | External URL (e.g., S3, CDN, third-party host) |

### Key Configuration Options

#### Per Product
```
Downloadable Information tab:
  - Links section:
      - Link Title (e.g., "Download PDF")
      - Price (additional price per link, or $0)
      - File or URL
      - Max Downloads (null = unlimited)
      - Is Shareable: No / Yes / Use Config
      - Sample File or URL
  - Samples section:
      - Provide preview samples (no purchase required)
```

#### Global Configuration
```
Stores → Configuration → Catalog → Catalog → Downloadable Product Options
  - Order Item Status to Enable Downloads: Invoiced / Pending
  - Default Maximum Number of Downloads
  - Shareable: Yes/No
  - Default Sample Title
  - Default Link Title
```

- **Exam focus:** Downloads are only accessible after the order reaches the configured status (typically **"Invoiced"** — meaning payment is captured). Setting it to "Pending" allows download before payment confirmation.

### Shareable vs. Non-Shareable Links
```
Shareable = YES:  Customer can share the download URL; no login required
Shareable = NO:   Customer must be logged in to download; link is session-bound
```

Note: the "Yes/No/Use Config" options exist at the **individual link level** (per product). At the **system configuration level** (Stores → Configuration), only Yes/No is available. "Use Config" on a link means it defers to the system-level setting.

- **Exam focus:** Shareable links bypass the login requirement. Non-shareable links require the customer to be authenticated.

### Checkout: No Shipping
Like Virtual products, Downloadable-only carts **skip the shipping step**.

---

## 8. Product Attributes & Attribute Sets

### What is a Product Attribute?
A product attribute is a **data field** attached to products (e.g., Color, Size, Material, Description). Attributes are grouped into **Attribute Sets**, and each product is assigned exactly one Attribute Set.

### Attribute Sets
```
An Attribute Set = a named group of attributes organized into attribute groups (tabs)

Default Attribute Set includes:
  - Product Details (Name, SKU, Price, Weight, etc.)
  - Images
  - Search Engine Optimization
  - Related Products, Up-Sells, Cross-Sells
  - Customizable Options
  - etc.
```

```
Stores → Attributes → Attribute Set
  → Create new set (from scratch or clone existing)
  → Drag attributes from "Unassigned Attributes" pool to groups
  → Create new groups (tabs) as needed
```

- **Exam focus:** Every product has exactly **one** Attribute Set. You can change the Attribute Set of a product after creation, but doing so may **lose data** stored in attributes that don't exist in the new set.

### Creating a Product Attribute
```
Stores → Attributes → Product → Add New Attribute

Key Fields:
  - Default Label          (e.g., "Color")
  - Catalog Input Type     (see table below)
  - Values Required        Yes/No
  - Unique Value           Yes/No (SKU uses this)
  - Attribute Code         (auto-generated, snake_case, immutable after creation)
  - Scope                  Store View / Website / Global
  - Use in Search          Yes/No
  - Comparable on Storefront Yes/No
  - Use for Promo Rule Conditions Yes/No
  - Visible on Catalog Pages Yes/No
  - Used for Sorting in Product Listing Yes/No
```

### Input Types

| Input Type | Description | Has Options? |
|------------|-------------|--------------|
| Text Field | Single-line text | No |
| Text Area | Multi-line text | No |
| Text Editor | WYSIWYG rich text editor | No |
| Date | Date picker | No |
| Yes/No | Boolean dropdown | No |
| Dropdown | Single-select from options | Yes |
| Multiple Select | Multi-select from options | Yes |
| Price | Numeric price input | No |
| Media Image | Image upload | No |
| Fixed Product Tax | For FPT/WEEE taxes | No |
| Visual Swatch | Color/image swatch | Yes |
| Text Swatch | Text label swatch | Yes |

### Attribute Scope — Critical Concept
```
Store View  → Value can differ per store view (e.g., translated name)
Website     → Value can differ per website
Global      → Single value shared across all scopes (required for configurable axes)
```

- **Exam focus:** Configurable product attributes **must be Global scope** and **user-defined** (not system attributes). Name and Description are typically Store View scope (for translations). Price is Global by default.

### Attribute Codes
- Auto-generated from the Default Label (lowercase, underscores)
- **Cannot be changed after creation**
- Used in code, URL keys, and API calls
- Example: Label "Shirt Color" → Code `shirt_color`

---

## 9. Swatches, Media & Price Attributes

### Visual Swatches

Visual swatches allow color/image-based selection instead of dropdowns.

```
Stores → Attributes → Product → [Color attribute] → Manage Options
  → For each option value:
      - Swatch Type: Color / File / No Image
      - Color picker or image upload
      - Admin label
      - Default store label
```

#### Swatch Configuration (Global)
```
Stores → Configuration → Catalog → Catalog → Storefront
  - Show Swatches in Product List: Yes/No
  - Number of Swatches per Product: [n]
  - Show Swatch Tooltip: Yes/No
```

- **Exam focus:** Swatches are configured at the **attribute option level** (each color/size value gets a swatch). The attribute itself must be Dropdown, Visual Swatch, or Text Swatch input type.

### Media Attributes

Products have a dedicated **Images and Videos** section with four special image roles:

| Role | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Base Image | Main product image on the product detail page |
| Small Image | Used in category listing pages, cart page, related products, and cross-sells |
| Thumbnail | Used in the minicart, product page gallery thumbnails, and wishlist sidebar |
| Swatch Image | Used as the color/pattern swatch on the product page |

```
Product Edit → Images and Videos tab:
  - Upload images (drag & drop or browse)
  - Assign roles by clicking the star/checkbox on each image
  - Set Alt Text per image
  - Drag to reorder (first image = default Base unless role explicitly set)
```

### Price Attributes & Pricing Options

| Price Type | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| Price | The base/regular price |
| Special Price | Sale price with optional date range |
| Cost | Internal cost (not shown on storefront by default) |
| MSRP | Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price (MAP pricing) |
| Tier Price | Quantity-based price breaks |
| Group Price | Customer group-based pricing |

#### Tier Pricing
```
Product → Advanced Pricing → Tier Price table:
  - Website
  - Customer Group (or ALL GROUPS)
  - Minimum Qty (e.g., buy 5+)
  - Price (fixed amount) OR Discount (percentage off)
```

#### Advanced Pricing
```
Product Edit → Advanced Pricing button (above Price field)
  - Special Price + From/To dates
  - Cost
  - MSRP / Apply MAP
  - Tier Prices
  - (For Configurable/Bundle: Dynamic vs Fixed Price switch)
```

- **Exam focus:** **MSRP (MAP)** — when enabled, the actual price is hidden ("Click for price") until the customer clicks, preventing the merchant from displaying below-MAP prices directly.

---

## 10. Catalog Configuration Settings

### Primary Configuration Path
```
Stores → Configuration → Catalog → Catalog
```

### Key Subsections

#### Storefront
```
- List Mode: Grid Only / List Only / Grid (default) / List / List (default) / Grid
- Products per Page on Grid Allowed Values (e.g., 9,15,30)
- Products per Page on Grid Default Value
- Products per Page on List Default Value
- Allow All Products per Page: Yes/No
- Remember Category Pagination: Yes/No
- Product Listing Sort by: Position / Product Name / Price
- Use Flat Catalog Category: Yes/No  ← performance setting
- Use Flat Catalog Product: Yes/No   ← performance setting
- Allow Dynamic Media URLs in Products and Categories: Yes/No
- Show Swatches in Product List
```

- **Exam focus:** **Flat Catalog** (Use Flat Catalog Category/Product) is a **performance optimization** that denormalizes attribute data into flat database tables, reducing JOIN complexity. Requires reindex after enabling. Can cause issues with custom EAV queries.

#### Product Reviews
```
- Enabled: Yes/No
- Allow Guests to Write Reviews: Yes/No
```

#### Product Alerts
```
- Allow Alert When Product Price Changes: Yes/No
- Allow Alert When Product Comes Back in Stock: Yes/No
- Alert Email Sender / Template
- Error Email Sender / Template / Frequency
```

#### Product Image Placeholders
```
- Base Image Placeholder (uploaded image file)
- Small Image Placeholder
- Thumbnail Placeholder
- Swatch Image Placeholder
```

#### Recently Viewed / Compared Products
```
- Number of Products in Recently Viewed Widget
- Number of Products in Recently Compared Widget
```

#### Price
```
- Catalog Price Scope: Global / Website
  - Global: One price for all websites
  - Website: Price can differ per website
```

- **Exam focus:** **Catalog Price Scope** setting is critical for multi-site setups. Set to **Website** to allow different prices on different websites.

#### Search Engine Optimization
```
- Canonical Link Meta Tag for Categories: Yes/No
- Canonical Link Meta Tag for Products: Yes/No
- Popular Search Terms (enable/disable "Popular Searches" feature)
- Product URL Suffix (e.g., .html)
- Category URL Suffix
- Use Categories Path for Product URLs: Yes/No
```

- **Exam focus:** **Product URL Suffix** defaults to `.html`. Changing this after launch can break existing URLs and SEO. A 301 redirect strategy is needed.

#### Category Top Navigation
```
- Max Depth (0 = unlimited)
```

#### Catalog Search (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch)
```
Stores → Configuration → Catalog → Catalog Search
  - Search Engine: Elasticsearch 7 / OpenSearch
  - Server Hostname / Port / Index Prefix
  - Enable HTTP Auth
  - Minimal Query Length
  - Maximum Query Length
  - Number of Top Search Results to Cache
  - Enable Search Suggestions
  - Search Recommendations
```

- **Exam focus:** Adobe Commerce 2.4.x **removed MySQL search** as an option. The search engine **must** be Elasticsearch or OpenSearch. This is a system requirement.

---

## 11. Admin Panel Structure

### Catalog Menu Structure
```
Catalog
  |
  +-- Products
  |     - Product grid (all product types)
  |     - Add Product → [select type]
  |
  +-- Categories
        - Category tree (nested)
        - Root Category → Store Category Hierarchy
```

Note: **Import/Export** is NOT under the Catalog menu. It is located under **System → Data Transfer → Import / Export**.

### Product Grid Features
```
Catalog → Products:
  - Filter by: Type, Attribute Set, SKU, Name, Price, Qty, Visibility, Status, Websites
  - Mass Actions: Delete, Change Status, Update Attributes, Assign Inventory Source
  - Columns: customizable
  - Export to CSV/XML
```

### Category Management
```
Catalog → Categories:
  Left Panel: Category tree
  Right Panel: Category settings

  Tabs:
  - General Information (Name, Is Active, Include in Menu, URL Key)
  - Display Settings (Display Mode, CMS Block, Layered Navigation)
  - SEO (Meta Title, Description, Keywords, Canonical)
  - Design (Custom Theme/Layout)
  - Schedule Design Update
  - Category Products (assign products, set position)
```

#### Category Display Modes
| Mode | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Products only | Standard grid/list of products |
| Static block only | Show CMS block content only (no product grid) |
| Static block and products | CMS block above product grid |

### Stores Menu — Attributes & Configuration
```
Stores
  |
  +-- Configuration
  |     → Catalog → Catalog (main catalog settings)
  |     → Catalog → Inventory (separate section under Catalog tab)
  |     → Catalog → XML Sitemap
  |     → Catalog → RSS Feeds
  |     → Catalog → Email to a Friend
  |
  +-- Attributes
  |     → Product    (individual attribute management)
  |     → Attribute Set  (grouping attributes into sets)
  |     → Rating     (product review ratings configuration)
  |
  +-- Other Configuration
        → Store hierarchy (Website → Store → Store View)
```

### System Menu — Data Transfer
```
System
  |
  +-- Data Transfer
        → Import
        → Export
        → Import History
```

---

## 12. Stock Management & Inventory Concepts

### Single Source vs. Multi Source Inventory (MSI)

Adobe Commerce 2.3+ introduced **MSI (Multi Source Inventory)** as a core module.

```
Single Source Mode (default for simple setups):
  - "Default Source" = the only source
  - Stock = "Default Stock"
  - Behaves like pre-2.3 inventory

Multi Source Mode:
  - Multiple Sources (warehouses, stores, 3PL providers)
  - Each source has its own qty per SKU
  - Sources assigned to Stocks
  - Stocks assigned to Sales Channels (websites)
```

### Inventory Configuration
```
Stores → Configuration → Catalog → Inventory

  - Out-of-Stock Threshold (Minimum Qty Allowed in Shopping Cart)
  - Maximum Qty Allowed in Shopping Cart
  - Qty Increments
  - Stock Options:
      - Display Out of Stock Products: Yes/No
      - Only X left Threshold (e.g., show "Only 3 left!" when qty <= 3)
      - Display Products Availability in Stock on Storefront: Yes/No
  - Product Stock Options:
      - Manage Stock: Yes/No  ← Global default
      - Backorders: No Backorders / Allow Qty Below 0 / Allow Qty Below 0 and Notify Customer
      - Use deferred Stock update: Yes/No (performance; requires Backorders enabled)
```

Note: "Use deferred Stock update" is found in the ScalableInventory module and only applies when Backorders are enabled. It is a global-only setting.

- **Exam focus:** **"Display Out of Stock Products"** — when set to **Yes**, products with zero stock still appear on the storefront (but cannot be added to cart). When **No**, they are hidden from catalog. Note: products are still accessible via their direct URL even when hidden from catalog.
- **Exam focus:** **Backorders** setting: "Allow Qty Below 0 and Notify Customer" allows customers to order even when qty is 0, but shows a warning message.

### Stock for Each Product Type Summary
```
Product Type     | Manages Own Stock | Notes
-----------------+-------------------+----------------------------------------
Simple           | YES               | Direct qty management
Virtual          | YES               | Same as simple, no weight
Downloadable     | YES               | Can set to unlimited (qty = null logic)
Configurable     | NO                | Derived from child simples
Grouped          | NO (parent)       | Each linked product manages own stock
Bundle           | NO (parent)       | Derived from selected bundle items
Gift Card (EE)   | YES               | Has own qty management
```

---

## 13. Hands-On: Configurable Product Walkthrough

### Scenario
Create a T-shirt with Size (S, M, L) and Color (Red, Blue) variations.

### Prerequisites
```bash
# Ensure these attributes exist and are configured correctly:
# 1. "size" attribute:
#    - Input Type: Text Swatch (or Dropdown)
#    - Scope: Global
#    - Must be user-defined
#    - Options: S, M, L

# 2. "color" attribute:
#    - Input Type: Visual Swatch
#    - Scope: Global
#    - Must be user-defined
#    - Options: Red (#FF0000), Blue (#0000FF)
```

### Step-by-Step Admin Process
```
1. Catalog → Products → Add Product
   → Select "Configurable Product"
   → Attribute Set: "Default" (or custom apparel set)

2. Fill Product Details:
   - Product Name: "Classic T-Shirt"
   - SKU: classic-tshirt
   - Price: $29.99
   - Tax Class: Taxable Goods
   - Quantity and Stock Status: (leave as In Stock; actual qty on children)
   - Weight: 0.5 lbs
   - Categories: [select your category]
   - Visibility: Catalog, Search

3. Go to "Configurations" tab → Click "Create Configurations"

4. Step 1 - Select Attributes:
   [x] Color
   [x] Size
   → Next

5. Step 2 - Attribute Values:
   Color: [x] Red  [x] Blue
   Size:  [x] S    [x] M    [x] L
   → Next

6. Step 3 - Bulk Image, Price, Quantity:
   Option A: "Apply unique images by attribute" (Color)
     → Upload Red image → applied to all Red variations
     → Upload Blue image → applied to all Blue variations
   Option B: "Apply single set of images to all SKUs"

   Price: "Apply unique prices by attribute" or "Apply single price to all SKUs"
   Quantity: Enter default qty (e.g., 100) or apply per variation later
   → Next

7. Step 4 - Summary:
   Review generated child SKUs:
   classic-tshirt-Red-S  | Red | S | $29.99 | 100
   classic-tshirt-Red-M  | Red | M | $29.99 | 100
   ... (6 total variations)
   → Generate Products

8. Save the Configurable product.

9. Verify child simples:
   Catalog → Products → Filter by SKU pattern "classic-tshirt-*"
   Each child should have:
   - Visibility: Not Visible Individually
   - Status: Enabled
   - Qty: 100
```

### Post-Creation Checklist
- [ ] Parent configurable product visible in catalog
- [ ] Child simples NOT visible individually on storefront
- [ ] Swatches appear on product page (not dropdowns) if Visual/Text Swatch attribute used
- [ ] Out-of-stock variation shows as grayed out / unavailable
- [ ] Price updates when variation selected (if child prices differ)

---

## 14. Hands-On: Bundle Product Walkthrough

### Scenario
Create a "Home Office Bundle" with a desk, chair, and optional monitor stand.

### Step-by-Step Admin Process
```
1. Prerequisites: Create component Simple products first:
   - SKU: desk-oak      "Oak Standing Desk"     $499
   - SKU: desk-walnut   "Walnut Standing Desk"   $549
   - SKU: chair-basic   "Basic Office Chair"     $199
   - SKU: chair-ergo    "Ergonomic Chair"         $349
   - SKU: monitor-stand "Monitor Stand"           $79

2. Catalog → Products → Add Product → Bundle Product
   → Attribute Set: Default

3. Fill basic info:
   - Product Name: "Home Office Bundle"
   - SKU: home-office-bundle
   - Dynamic Price: YES  (price = sum of selections)
   - Tax Class: Taxable Goods
   - Visibility: Catalog, Search
   - Status: Enabled

4. Bundle Items tab → Add Option:

   Option 1: "Desk"
   - Option Title: Desk
   - Input Type: Radio Buttons
   - Required: Yes
   → Add Products to Option:
     + desk-oak   (Default Qty: 1, User Defined: No)
     + desk-walnut (Default Qty: 1, User Defined: No)

   Option 2: "Chair"
   - Option Title: Chair
   - Input Type: Radio Buttons
   - Required: Yes
   → Add Products to Option:
     + chair-basic  (Default Qty: 1, User Defined: No)
     + chair-ergo   (Default Qty: 1, User Defined: No)

   Option 3: "Monitor Stand"
   - Option Title: Monitor Stand
   - Input Type: Checkbox
   - Required: No  ← optional!
   → Add Products to Option:
     + monitor-stand (Default Qty: 1, User Defined: Yes ← customer can choose qty)

5. Save

6. Verify on storefront:
   - Base price shows starting price (lowest required selection combo)
   - Selecting desk + chair updates total dynamically
   - Monitor stand is optional (can uncheck)
   - Total = selected items' prices summed
```

### Fixed Price Bundle — Same Scenario
```
Step 3 change:
   - Dynamic Price: NO
   - Price: $799.99  ← fixed price regardless of which desk/chair selected

Behavior:
   - Customer selects desk and chair but always pays $799.99
   - Tier prices and special prices can now be set on bundle parent
   - Individual item prices NOT shown in bundle total
```

### Admin Interface Comparison: Configurable vs. Bundle

| Aspect | Configurable | Bundle |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| "Configurations" tab | YES — generate child SKUs | NO |
| "Bundle Items" tab | NO | YES — add option groups |
| Price on parent | Display/base price | Fixed (if Fixed Price) |
| Child products are | Auto-generated simples | Pre-existing simples |
| Customer selects | One value per axis (e.g., S/Red) | One or more per option |
| Cart line items | Single configurable line item | Single bundle line item |
| Stock tracking | Per child simple | Per bundle item product |

---

## 15. Comparison Tables

### All Product Types — Feature Matrix

| Feature | Simple | Configurable | Grouped | Bundle | Virtual | Downloadable | Gift Card (EE) |
|---------|--------|-------------|---------|--------|---------|-------------|----------------|
| Has own stock | Yes | No | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Has weight | Yes | Yes* | No | Yes* | No | No | Depends* |
| Triggers shipping | Yes | Yes* | Yes* | Yes* | No | No | Depends* |
| Has price field | Yes | Yes | No | Conditional | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Child products | No | Yes (simples) | Yes (simples/virtual) | Yes (simples/virtual) | No | No | No |
| Customer selects variation | No | Yes | No (qty per item) | Yes (options) | No | No | Amount |
| Downloadable files | No | No | No | No | No | Yes | No |
| Checkout: skip shipping | No | No | No | No | Yes | Yes | If virtual |

\* = inherits/derives from children or items. Gift Card weight/shipping depends on type (physical, virtual, or combined).

### Bundle: Dynamic vs. Fixed Pricing

| Characteristic | Dynamic Price | Fixed Price |
|----------------|--------------|-------------|
| Price source | Sum of selected item prices | Set on bundle parent |
| Special price | Set on items | Set on bundle parent |
| Tier price | Set on items | Set on bundle parent |
| Customer group price | Set on items | Set on bundle parent |
| Use case | Variable-value kits | Promotional bundles |
| Item prices shown | Yes | Conditionally |

### Product Attribute Scope Comparison

| Scope | When to Use | Example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| Global | Same value everywhere; required for configurable axes | SKU, Weight, Price (default) |
| Website | Differs per website | Price (if Catalog Price Scope = Website) |
| Store View | Differs per language/store view | Name, Description, Meta Title |

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Product Types — Testable Facts

- [ ] **Simple**: Single SKU, has own stock, has weight, triggers shipping
- [ ] **Configurable**: Parent has NO own stock; stock lives in child Simples; parent price is display/base only
- [ ] **Configurable attribute requirements**: Input type = Dropdown/Swatch, Scope = **Global**, must be **user-defined**
- [ ] **Child Simples** of Configurable should have Visibility = **"Not Visible Individually"**
- [ ] **Grouped**: No parent price, no parent stock; children are independent products added as separate cart line items
- [ ] **Bundle Dynamic Price**: Total = sum of selected item prices; special/tier prices on items
- [ ] **Bundle Fixed Price**: Single set price on parent; special/tier prices on parent
- [ ] **Bundle stock**: Out of stock if any **required** option has all items OOS
- [ ] **Bundle option types**: Drop-down, Radio Buttons, Checkbox, Multiple Select
- [ ] **Virtual**: No weight, no shipping step (if cart is all-virtual)
- [ ] **Downloadable**: No weight, no shipping; files or URLs; accessible after order reaches configured status (default: **Invoiced**)
- [ ] **Downloadable Shareable=No**: Must be logged in to download; **Shareable=Yes**: direct URL access without login
- [ ] **Gift Card (Commerce only)**: Can be physical, virtual, or combined; physical triggers shipping, virtual does not

### Attributes — Testable Facts

- [ ] Attribute **code** cannot be changed after creation
- [ ] Attribute **scope** options: Store View / Website / Global
- [ ] Configurable axis attributes **must** be **Global** scope and **user-defined**
- [ ] Visual Swatch and Text Swatch are distinct input types (not just "Swatch")
- [ ] **Text Editor** is a separate input type (WYSIWYG), distinct from Text Area
- [ ] **Attribute Set** = named grouping of attributes; each product has exactly **one** Attribute Set
- [ ] Changing a product's Attribute Set may result in data loss for attributes not in the new set

### Catalog Configuration — Testable Facts

- [ ] **Flat Catalog**: Performance optimization; denormalizes EAV to flat tables; requires reindex
- [ ] **Catalog Price Scope**: Global (one price) vs. Website (price per website)
- [ ] **Product URL Suffix**: Defaults to `.html`; change requires redirect strategy
- [ ] **Search Engine**: Adobe Commerce 2.4.x requires **Elasticsearch or OpenSearch** — MySQL search removed
- [ ] **Display Out of Stock Products = Yes**: OOS products visible but not purchasable; **No** = hidden (still accessible via direct URL)
- [ ] **Backorders**: Three settings — No Backorders, Allow Qty Below 0, Allow Qty Below 0 and Notify Customer
- [ ] **MSRP/MAP**: Hides actual price; shows "Click for price" link until clicked
- [ ] **Canonical link meta tags**: Can be enabled separately for categories and products (SEO)
- [ ] **List Mode options**: Grid Only, List Only, Grid (default) / List, List (default) / Grid

### Admin Structure — Testable Facts

- [ ] Admin path for products: **Catalog → Products**
- [ ] Admin path for categories: **Catalog → Categories**
- [ ] Admin path for attribute sets: **Stores → Attributes → Attribute Set**
- [ ] Admin path for individual attributes: **Stores → Attributes → Product**
- [ ] Admin path for ratings: **Stores → Attributes → Rating**
- [ ] Admin path for catalog config: **Stores → Configuration → Catalog → Catalog**
- [ ] Admin path for inventory config: **Stores → Configuration → Catalog → Inventory** (separate section under Catalog tab)
- [ ] Admin path for import/export: **System → Data Transfer → Import / Export**
- [ ] Category Display Modes: **Products only / Static block only / Static block and products**

### Stock Rules — Testable Facts

- [ ] Only **Simple**, **Virtual**, **Downloadable**, and **Gift Card** manage their own stock
- [ ] **Configurable**, **Grouped**, and **Bundle** parents have no independent stock
- [ ] MSI (Multi Source Inventory) is core since Adobe Commerce 2.3
- [ ] "Only X left Threshold" triggers low-stock messaging on storefront
- [ ] Use deferred Stock update = performance optimization (ScalableInventory module, requires Backorders enabled)

### Image Roles — Testable Facts

- [ ] **Base Image**: Main PDP (Product Detail Page) image
- [ ] **Small Image**: Category listing pages, cart page, related products, cross-sells
- [ ] **Thumbnail**: Minicart, product page gallery thumbnails, wishlist sidebar
- [ ] **Swatch Image**: Swatch display on product page

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Dynamic Pricing and Fixed Pricing on a Bundle product?
flashcards.answer: Dynamic Pricing calculates the bundle price as the sum of selected item prices. Fixed Pricing uses a single predetermined price set on the bundle parent, regardless of which items are selected.
flashcards.hint: One derives price from components, the other ignores component prices entirely.

flashcards.question: How does checkout behave when a cart contains only Virtual and/or Downloadable products?
flashcards.answer: The shipping step is skipped entirely. If even one physical product is in the cart alongside virtual products, the shipping step IS shown.
flashcards.hint: These product types have no weight and nothing to deliver physically.

flashcards.question: What are the six core product types available in both Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source?
flashcards.answer: Simple, Configurable, Grouped, Bundle, Virtual, and Downloadable. Adobe Commerce (EE) adds a seventh type: Gift Card.
flashcards.hint: Think about the different ways products can be structured — from single items to kits to digital goods.

flashcards.question: Does a Configurable product parent have its own stock quantity?
flashcards.answer: No. The parent Configurable product has NO stock of its own. Stock is tracked at the child Simple product level. When all children are out of stock, the parent becomes unavailable.
flashcards.hint: Think about where the actual inventory lives in a parent-child relationship.

flashcards.question: What three requirements must an attribute meet to be usable as a configurable product axis?
flashcards.answer: The attribute must have (1) Global scope, (2) Dropdown or Swatch input type, and (3) be user-defined (not a system attribute).
flashcards.hint: Consider scope level, input type, and who created the attribute.

flashcards.question: What visibility setting should child Simple products of a Configurable product use, and why?
flashcards.answer: Child simples should be set to 'Not Visible Individually' so they don't appear as duplicate standalone listings on the storefront.
flashcards.hint: You want customers to find the parent, not individual size/color variants.

flashcards.question: When do customers gain access to download links for Downloadable products by default?
flashcards.answer: Downloads are accessible after the order reaches the 'Invoiced' status by default, meaning payment has been captured. This can be changed to 'Pending' in configuration to allow downloads before payment confirmation.
flashcards.hint: The default requires proof of payment before granting file access.

flashcards.question: What happens if you change a product's Attribute Set after creation?
flashcards.answer: You may lose data stored in attributes that don't exist in the new Attribute Set. Each product has exactly one Attribute Set.
flashcards.hint: Attributes are grouped into sets, and switching sets means some fields may no longer exist.

flashcards.question: What is the 'Flat Catalog' feature in Adobe Commerce, and what does it do?
flashcards.answer: Flat Catalog is a performance optimization that denormalizes EAV attribute data into flat database tables, reducing JOIN complexity. It requires reindexing after enabling.
flashcards.hint: Think about database performance and reducing the number of table joins needed.

flashcards.question: What search engine options are available in Adobe Commerce 2.4.x?
flashcards.answer: Only Elasticsearch or OpenSearch. MySQL search was removed as an option in 2.4.x — an external search engine is now a system requirement.
flashcards.hint: MySQL-based search was deprecated and removed in the 2.4 line.

flashcards.question: How do Grouped products appear in the shopping cart after a customer adds items?
flashcards.answer: Each child product appears as a separate line item in the cart. Unlike Configurable or Bundle products, Grouped products do not combine into a single cart entry.
flashcards.hint: The grouped parent is just a display container — each item is independent.

flashcards.question: What are the four image roles in Adobe Commerce, and where is each used?
flashcards.answer: Base Image (main PDP image), Small Image (category listings, cart, related/cross-sells), Thumbnail (minicart, gallery thumbnails, wishlist sidebar), and Swatch Image (swatch display on product page).
flashcards.hint: Each role targets a different area of the storefront where the product image appears.

flashcards.question: What does the MSRP/MAP feature do in Adobe Commerce?
flashcards.answer: When enabled, the actual selling price is hidden and replaced with a 'Click for price' link. This prevents the merchant from displaying below-MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) prices directly on catalog pages.
flashcards.hint: Some manufacturers prohibit advertising prices below a certain threshold.

flashcards.question: What determines whether a Bundle product is considered 'Out of Stock'?
flashcards.answer: A Bundle product is Out of Stock if any required option has ALL its products out of stock. The bundle parent has no stock of its own — availability is derived from required option item availability.
flashcards.hint: Focus on required options — optional ones don't affect availability.

flashcards.question: Where is the Catalog Price Scope setting located, and what are its options?
flashcards.answer: Found at Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Price. Options are Global (one price for all websites) or Website (prices can differ per website). This setting is critical for multi-site setups.
flashcards.hint: This determines whether product prices are shared across all websites or can vary.

studyNotes.title: Day 2 — Import/Export & Admin Configuration
studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2 Import/Export & Admin Configuration
## Study Notes — Week 1: Core Features

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Import/Export Framework Overview](#1-importexport-framework-overview)
2. [CSV Format for Products, Customers, and Orders](#2-csv-format-for-products-customers-and-orders)
3. [Import Behaviors](#3-import-behaviors)
4. [Import Validation Errors and How to Fix Them](#4-import-validation-errors-and-how-to-fix-them)
5. [Admin Configuration Scopes](#5-admin-configuration-scopes)
6. [Stores → Configuration Sections](#6-stores--configuration-sections)
7. [Store Information: Currency, Tax, and Per-Website Settings](#7-store-information-currency-tax-and-per-website-settings)
8. [Hands-On: Export, Modify, Re-Import Products](#8-hands-on-export-modify-re-import-products)
9. [Tricky Exam Details](#9-tricky-exam-details)
10. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Import/Export Framework Overview

Magento 2's Import/Export system lives under **System → Data Transfer** in the Admin Panel. It provides a standardized mechanism to bulk-manage catalog, customer, and order data without touching the database directly.

```
Admin Panel
  +-- System
        +-- Data Transfer
              +-- Import          <-- upload CSV to create/update/delete records
              +-- Export          <-- download CSV of existing records
              +-- Import/Export Tax Rates
              +-- Import History  <-- log of past imports
```

### Key Entities Supported

| Entity Type | Import | Export |
|---|---|---|
| Products | Yes | Yes |
| Customers Main File | Yes | Yes |
| Customer Addresses | Yes | Yes |
| Customers and Addresses (single file) | Yes | No |
| Customer Finances (EE) | Yes | Yes |
| Advanced Pricing | Yes | Yes |
| Stock Sources (MSI) | Yes | Yes |

- **Exam focus:** Orders are **not available** in the System → Data Transfer → Import or Export interface. The Sales → Orders admin grid has its own CSV/XML export button, but that is a grid-level feature, not part of the Import/Export framework. This is a common exam distractor.

### How It Works Internally

```
CSV File Upload
     |
     v
Validation Layer  --> Check column names, required fields, data types
     |
     v
Adapter/Entity Model  --> e.g., Magento\CatalogImportExport\Model\Import\Product
     |
     v
Import Behavior Logic  --> Add & Update / Replace / Delete
     |
     v
Database Write (via resource models / bulk insert)
```

---

## 2. CSV Format for Products, Customers, and Orders

### 2.1 General CSV Rules

- **Delimiter:** comma (`,`) by default; configurable to semicolon, pipe, etc.
- **Enclosure:** double-quote (`"`) for values containing commas or newlines
- **First row:** always the **header row** with column names
- **Encoding:** UTF-8 (required — especially for special characters)
- **Column order:** does **not** matter — Magento maps by column name, not position
- **Column names:** are **case-sensitive** — `sku` ≠ `SKU` ≠ `Sku`
- **Multiple value separator:** comma (`,`) by default (configurable in the import form). Used to separate multiple values within a single cell (e.g., multiple categories).

- **Exam focus:** Column *order* does not matter, but column *names* are case-sensitive. This is one of the most frequently tested "tricky" facts.

### 2.2 Product CSV Structure

Products use the most complex CSV format because of configurable products, custom attributes, and multi-store values.

#### Minimum Required Columns for a Simple Product

```csv
sku,store_view_code,attribute_set_code,product_type,categories,product_websites,name,description,short_description,weight,product_online,tax_class_name,visibility,price,url_key,created_at,updated_at,new_from_date,new_to_date,display_product_options_in,map_price,msrp_price,map_enabled,gift_message_available,custom_design,custom_design_from,custom_design_to,custom_layout_update,page_layout,product_image_1,hide_from_product_page,qty,out_of_stock_qty,use_config_min_qty,is_qty_decimal,allow_backorders,use_config_backorders,min_cart_qty,use_config_min_sale_qty,max_cart_qty,use_config_max_sale_qty,is_in_stock,notify_on_stock_below,use_config_notify_stock_qty,manage_stock,use_config_manage_stock,use_config_qty_increments,qty_increments,use_config_enable_qty_inc,enable_qty_increments,is_decimal_divided,website_id,deferred_stock_update,use_config_deferred_stock_update,additional_images,additional_image_labels,hide_additional_image,base_image,base_image_label,small_image,small_image_label,swatch_image,thumbnail,thumbnail_label,bundle_price_type,bundle_sku_type,bundle_price_view,bundle_weight_type,bundle_values,bundle_shipment_type,configurable_variations,configurable_variation_labels,associated_skus
```

#### Practical Minimum (Simple Product)

```csv
sku,attribute_set_code,product_type,name,price,qty,is_in_stock,visibility,status
SKU-001,Default,simple,"My Product",29.99,100,1,4,1
```

| Column | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `sku` | **Yes** | Unique identifier; used as the record key |
| `attribute_set_code` | **Yes** | Must match an existing attribute set name exactly |
| `product_type` | **Yes** | `simple`, `configurable`, `grouped`, `bundle`, `virtual`, `downloadable`, `giftcard` (EE) |
| `name` | Yes | Product name |
| `price` | Yes (simple) | Base price |
| `store_view_code` | No | Empty = applies to all store views; fill for store-view overrides |
| `product_websites` | No | Website code(s), comma-separated within the field |

- **Exam focus:** `attribute_set_code` and `product_type` are **required** columns for product import. Missing or mismatched values will cause validation errors. For existing products being updated, only `sku` is strictly required.

#### Configurable Product CSV Pattern

Configurable products require **multiple rows** in the CSV:

```csv
sku,attribute_set_code,product_type,name,price,configurable_variations
CONF-001,Default,configurable,"T-Shirt",0,,
CONF-001-S-RED,Default,simple,"T-Shirt Small Red",19.99,,
CONF-001-M-RED,Default,simple,"T-Shirt Medium Red",19.99,,
```

Row 1 — the parent configurable SKU, `product_type=configurable`
Rows 2+ — child simple SKUs with `product_type=simple`

The `configurable_variations` column on the parent row links children:

```
configurable_variations
"sku=CONF-001-S-RED,size=Small,color=Red|sku=CONF-001-M-RED,size=Medium,color=Red"
```

Note: Within `configurable_variations`, pipe `|` separates different variations, and comma `,` separates field=value pairs. This is specific to configurable_variations formatting and is separate from the general multiple value separator.

#### Multi-Select / Multiple Values

Use the configured **multiple value separator** (comma `,` by default) to separate multiple values within a single cell:

```csv
categories
"Tops/T-Shirts,Sale/New Arrivals"
```

The slash `/` in category paths is a path separator (parent/child), not a value separator.

#### Store View Overrides

To override a value for a specific store view, add a second row with the same SKU and a `store_view_code`:

```csv
sku,store_view_code,name
SKU-001,,My Product
SKU-001,french_store,Mon Produit
```

### 2.3 Customer CSV Structure

Customers use two separate files (or a combined "Customers and Addresses" single-file format):

#### Main Customer File

```csv
email,_website,_store,firstname,lastname,group_id,dob,gender,taxvat,prefix,suffix,disable_auto_group_change
customer@example.com,base,default,John,Doe,1,,,,,, 0
```

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| `email` | Primary key for customer records (no underscore prefix) |
| `_website` | Website code (note the underscore prefix) |
| `_store` | Store code (note the underscore prefix) |
| `group_id` | 0=Not Logged In, 1=General, 2=Wholesale, 3=Retailer |

#### Customer Address File

```csv
_email,_entity_id,city,company,country_id,fax,firstname,lastname,middlename,postcode,prefix,region,region_id,street,suffix,telephone,vat_id,_address_default_billing_,_address_default_shipping_
customer@example.com,,Austin,,US,,John,Doe,,78701,,Texas,57,"123 Main St",,,0,1,1
```

Note: In the Address import, the email column IS prefixed with underscore (`_email`), unlike the main Customer import where it's just `email`.

### 2.4 Order Data

Since orders are **not available** in the Data Transfer import/export framework, order data can only be exported at the grid level:

- Navigate to **Sales → Orders**
- Use the grid's **Export** button (top-right) to download CSV or XML of the grid data

Key exported columns from the grid:

```csv
Order ID, Order Date, Bill-to Name, Ship-to Name, Grand Total (Base), Grand Total (Purchased), Status, Billing Address, Shipping Address, Shipping Method, Payment Method
```

- **Exam focus:** Order import is **not supported** in Magento 2's standard import framework. Order export is only available through the Sales → Orders admin grid, NOT through System → Data Transfer → Export.

---

## 3. Import Behaviors

When importing, you must choose one of three **behaviors** that dictate what happens when a record already exists.

```
Import Behavior Selection
         |
         +----> Add/Update     (default, safest)
         |
         +----> Replace
         |
         +----> Delete
```

### 3.1 Add & Update (Add and Update)

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| SKU does **not** exist | Creates a new record |
| SKU **already** exists | Updates only the fields present in the CSV; leaves other fields untouched |

```
Existing DB record:  name="Old Name", price=10.00, weight=1.5
CSV row:             sku=X, name="New Name", price=12.00
                     (weight column omitted)

Result:              name="New Name", price=12.00, weight=1.5  <-- weight preserved
```

- **Exam focus:** Add & Update only modifies columns that are **present in the CSV file**. Absent columns retain their existing values. This is the most common import behavior used in practice.

### 3.2 Replace

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| SKU does **not** exist | Creates a new record |
| SKU **already** exists | **Deletes the existing record** and creates a fresh one from the CSV data |

```
Existing DB record:  name="Old Name", price=10.00, weight=1.5, custom_attr="special"
CSV row:             sku=X, name="New Name", price=12.00
                     (weight and custom_attr columns omitted)

Result:              name="New Name", price=12.00, weight=NULL, custom_attr=NULL
                     <-- ALL missing fields are lost/reset
```

- **Exam focus:** Replace is **destructive** for existing records. Fields NOT in the CSV are wiped out. Use with caution.
- **Exam focus:** Replace behavior = delete + re-insert, not a true SQL UPDATE.

### 3.3 Delete

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| SKU does **not** exist | No action (no error) |
| SKU **already** exists | **Deletes the record permanently** |

```csv
sku
SKU-001
SKU-002
SKU-003
```

Only the `sku` column is technically needed for Delete behavior, though other columns may be present and are ignored.

- **Exam focus:** With Delete behavior, Magento only needs the **SKU** (or entity identifier) to find and remove the record. No other data is required.

### Behavior Comparison Table

| Behavior | Record Exists | Record Absent | Data for Missing Columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Add & Update** | Update present fields only | Create new | Preserved from existing |
| **Replace** | Delete & re-create | Create new | Lost (reset to default/NULL) |
| **Delete** | Delete record | No action | N/A |

---

## 4. Import Validation Errors and How to Fix Them

Magento validates the CSV **before** importing. If validation fails, **nothing is imported** — it's all-or-nothing per batch.

### 4.1 Validation Process

```
Upload CSV
     |
     v
[Check File Format]  --> UTF-8? Comma-delimited? Not empty?
     |
     v
[Check Headers]  --> Required columns present? Names correct case?
     |
     v
[Check Each Row]  --> Data types, required fields, FK constraints
     |
     v
Validation Report  --> Errors listed by row number and column
     |
     +-- Errors found?  --> Fix CSV, re-upload
     |
     +-- No errors?     --> Proceed to import
```

### 4.2 Common Validation Errors

| Error Message | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `"sku" column not found` | Header `SKU` or `Sku` instead of `sku` | Rename header to lowercase `sku` |
| `Invalid value in column "product_type"` | Typo in product type (e.g., `Simple` vs `simple`) | Use all-lowercase: `simple`, `configurable`, etc. |
| `Attribute set "X" does not exist` | `attribute_set_code` doesn't match Admin | Verify exact spelling in **Stores → Attributes → Attribute Set** |
| `URL key "X" already exists` | Duplicate URL key in system | Change `url_key` or delete the existing product first |
| `Invalid value for Date field` | Wrong date format | Use format `mm/dd/yy h:i` or `Y-m-d H:i:s` |
| `Super attribute "color" must be unique` | Duplicate variation combination | Remove duplicate child rows |
| `Category path "X" not found` | Category doesn't exist in the system | Create category first, or use the full path `Default Category/Tops` |
| `Value is required` | Required attribute missing from CSV row | Add the column/value to the CSV |
| `Numeric value expected` | Text in a numeric field (price, qty, weight) | Remove commas, currency symbols from numeric fields |
| `File encoding is not UTF-8` | CSV saved in Windows-1252 or Latin-1 | Re-save file as UTF-8 in text editor |

### 4.3 Validation Behavior Settings

Under **System → Data Transfer → Import**, there are two important settings:

| Setting | Options | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Validation Strategy** | Stop on Error | Stops at first error row |
| | Skip error entries | Skips invalid rows, imports valid rows |
| **Allowed Errors Count** | Number (default: 10) | Maximum errors before aborting |

- **Exam focus:** The default behavior is **Stop on Error**. With "Skip error entries," valid rows are imported even if some rows fail — but those failed rows are skipped silently unless you review the error report.

### 4.4 Step-by-Step: Fixing Import Errors

```
1. Attempt import
2. Review the error report (shown on-screen or downloadable)
   - Note the row number(s) and error messages
3. Open the CSV in a spreadsheet editor (LibreOffice Calc / Excel)
4. Navigate to the indicated row(s)
5. Apply fixes:
   a. Case-sensitive column names -> fix header row
   b. Invalid attribute_set_code -> check Admin for exact name
   c. Missing required fields -> add values
   d. Duplicate URL keys -> modify url_key value
   e. Category path errors -> create categories or fix path string
6. Save as CSV (UTF-8, comma-delimited)
7. Re-upload and re-validate
8. Repeat until zero errors
```

### 4.5 Import History

After a successful import, go to **System → Data Transfer → Import History** to review:
- Timestamp
- User who performed the import
- Behavior used
- File name
- Summary (rows processed, errors, etc.)

## 5. Admin Configuration Scopes

Magento 2 uses a **hierarchical scope system** for configuration. Settings can be defined broadly (for all stores) or narrowly (for a single store view).

### 5.1 The Scope Hierarchy

```
Default Config  (global fallback — applies everywhere unless overridden)
     |
     v
Website  (overrides Default for all stores under this website)
     |
     v
Store View  (most specific — overrides everything above)
```

Note: **Store Groups** exist in the Magento hierarchy (Website → Store Group → Store View), but Store Groups do **not** have their own configuration scope. In the admin Configuration panel, you can only switch between Default, Website, and Store View. Store Groups control root category assignment and are managed under Stores → All Stores, not in the Configuration section.

```
Default Config
+-- Website: Main Website (code: base)
|     +-- Store: Main Website Store (root category, etc.)
|           +-- Store View: Default Store View (code: default)
|           +-- Store View: French View (code: french)
|
+-- Website: B2B Website (code: b2b)
      +-- Store: B2B Store
            +-- Store View: B2B English
```

- **Exam focus:** The hierarchy for configuration is **Default → Website → Store View**, from broadest to most specific. A setting at a lower level **overrides** the setting from any higher level.
- **Exam focus:** In the Admin, "Store" in the scope selector actually means "Store Group," not Store View. This naming inconsistency trips up many candidates. However, Store Groups do NOT have their own configuration scope — only Default, Website, and Store View do.

### 5.2 How Scoped Configuration Works in the Admin

When editing a setting in **Stores → Configuration**:

1. Use the **Store View switcher** (top-left dropdown) to select scope
2. Grayed-out fields with checkboxes labeled "Use Default" inherit from the parent scope
3. **Uncheck** "Use Default" to override the value at the current scope
4. **Re-check** "Use Default" to revert to inheriting from the parent

```
[Store View Scope Selected: French View]

Setting: "Store Name"
[ ] Use Website               <- unchecked = this Store View overrides Website scope
Value: [  Boutique Française  ]

If you check "Use Website" -> value reverts to whatever Website scope has
```

- **Exam focus:** When a setting is overridden at a lower scope, the "Use [Parent Scope]" checkbox is **unchecked**. A checked checkbox means the value is **inherited** (not set) at this scope.

### 5.3 Which Settings Can Be Scoped

| Scope Level | Example Settings |
|---|---|
| **Global only** | Catalog Price Scope (if set to Global), customer account sharing, single-store mode |
| **Website** | Base currency, tax calculation settings, minimum order amount |
| **Store View** | Locale/language, store name, CMS pages, product names/descriptions, display currency, guest checkout, payment methods, tax display settings |

- **Exam focus:** **Base currency** is set at the **Website** scope. Display currencies can be set per Store View.
- **Exam focus:** The **root category** is assigned at the **Store (Store Group)** level, not Website or Store View. This is configured in Stores → All Stores, not in the Configuration section.

### 5.4 Scope in Code

Scopes are represented programmatically:

```php
// Store scope constants (Magento\Store\Model\ScopeInterface)
ScopeInterface::SCOPE_STORES    // 'stores'  (Store View)
ScopeInterface::SCOPE_STORE     // 'store'   (Store View, singular)
ScopeInterface::SCOPE_GROUPS    // 'groups'  (Store Group)
ScopeInterface::SCOPE_GROUP     // 'group'   (Store Group, singular)
ScopeInterface::SCOPE_WEBSITES  // 'websites'
ScopeInterface::SCOPE_WEBSITE   // 'website'

// Default scope (Magento\Framework\App\Config\ScopeConfigInterface)
ScopeConfigInterface::SCOPE_TYPE_DEFAULT  // 'default'

// Reading config programmatically
$this->scopeConfig->getValue(
    'general/store_information/name',
    \Magento\Store\Model\ScopeInterface::SCOPE_STORE,
    $storeId
);
```

Note: The default scope constant is on `ScopeConfigInterface`, not `ScopeInterface`.

Navigate to **Stores → Configuration** (under the Settings submenu). Note: In Magento 1, this was under System → Configuration. In all Magento 2 versions, it is always under Stores.

- **Exam focus:** **Locale** (language) is a **Store View** scoped setting. **Timezone** is a **Website** scoped setting.

**Stores → Configuration → Catalog → Inventory**

Note: Inventory is a **separate configuration section** (section ID `cataloginventory`) that appears under the Catalog tab, not nested inside the Catalog → Catalog section.

Configure email templates for:

- **Exam focus:** **Guest Checkout** is configurable per **Store View**, meaning different store views under the same website can have different guest checkout policies.

### 6.4 Payment Methods

**Stores → Configuration → Sales → Payment Methods**

| Payment Method | Notes |
|---|---|
| Check/Money Order | Basic offline payment |

| Braintree | Bundled in Magento 2; credit cards, PayPal |

Payment methods are typically **Website**-scoped, meaning different websites can have different payment options. Some payment methods may also be configurable at Store View level depending on the module.

Each payment method has:
- **Enabled** toggle
- **Title** (shown at checkout)
- **Allowed Countries** (restrict by country)
- **Sort Order** (position in checkout list)

- **Exam focus:** Payment methods are configured at the **Website** scope. A payment method enabled on one website can be disabled on another.
- **Exam focus:** The **Sort Order** field controls the display order of payment methods in checkout — **lower numbers appear first**.

### 6.5 Shipping Methods

**Stores → Configuration → Sales → Shipping Methods**

| Carrier | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Flat Rate | Simple | One fixed rate for all orders |
| Free Shipping | Simple | Activated by minimum order amount or coupon |
| Table Rates | Flexible | Rates based on weight, price, qty; requires CSV upload |
| UPS | Real-time | Requires UPS account credentials |
| USPS | Real-time | Requires USPS account credentials |
| FedEx | Real-time | Requires FedEx account credentials |
| DHL | Real-time | Requires DHL account credentials |

**Table Rates CSV format:**

The 4th column header changes based on the selected condition type:
```csv
# Condition: Price vs. Destination
Country,Region/State,Zip/Postal Code,Order Subtotal (and above),Shipping Price
US,*,*,0,5.00
US,*,*,50,0.00
US,CA,*,0,7.00

# Condition: Weight vs. Destination → header becomes "Weight (and above)"
# Condition: # of Items vs. Destination → header becomes "# of Items (and above)"
```

- **Exam focus:** Table Rates are uploaded as a CSV per **Website**. The CSV is separate from the product/customer import CSV. The import/export button for Table Rates only appears when viewing the configuration at Website scope.
- **Exam focus:** Shipping methods are also **Website**-scoped.
- **Exam focus:** **Free Shipping** method requires either: (a) minimum order amount configured, or (b) a cart price rule that sets shipping to free — the method itself can be configured with a minimum order amount.

## 7. Store Information: Currency, Tax, and Per-Website Settings

### 7.1 Currency Configuration

```
Stores → Configuration → General → Currency Setup
```

| Setting | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Base Currency | Website | The currency used for all financial calculations internally |
| Default Display Currency | Store View | Currency shown by default to customers |
| Allowed Currencies | Store View | All currencies customers can switch to |

Note: Base Currency can only be set at Default or Website level. Default Display Currency and Allowed Currencies can be set per Store View, allowing different store views under the same website to display different currencies while sharing the same base currency.

**Currency Rates:**
```
Stores → Currency → Currency Rates
```
- Rates are set between base currency and allowed currencies
- Can be updated manually or automatically via currency rate services
- Rates are used for **display only** — all stored prices are in **base currency**

```
Example:
  Base Currency: USD
  Display Currency: EUR
  Rate: 1 USD = 0.92 EUR

  Product price stored: $100 USD
  Displayed to customer: €92 EUR (approximately)
  Order is recorded in base currency (USD)
```

- **Exam focus:** The **Base Currency** is the currency Magento uses for all financial calculations. Display currencies are just for presentation. Changing the base currency requires updating product prices.
- **Exam focus:** Base currency is set at the **Website** scope. Display currency and allowed currencies can differ per **Store View**.

### 7.2 Tax Configuration

**Stores → Configuration → Sales → Tax**

```
Tax Configuration Hierarchy:
  +-- Tax Classes
  |     +-- Customer Tax Class (e.g., Retail Customer, Wholesale)
  |     +-- Product Tax Class (e.g., Taxable Goods, Digital Products)
  |
  +-- Tax Zones and Rates
  |     (Stores → Tax → Tax Zones and Rates)
  |     Rate = percentage for Country/Region/Zip combination
  |
  +-- Tax Rules
        (Stores → Tax → Tax Rules)
        Rule = Customer Class + Product Class + Rate = Applied Tax
```

| Tax Setting | Scope | Options |
|---|---|---|
| Tax Calculation Method | Website | Unit Price, Row Total, Total |
| Tax Calculation Based On | Website | Shipping Address, Billing Address, Store Origin |
| Catalog Prices | Website | Excluding Tax, Including Tax |
| Shipping Prices | Website | Excluding Tax, Including Tax |
| Apply Customer Tax | Website | After Discount, Before Discount |
| Apply Discount on Prices | Website | Excluding Tax, Including Tax |
| Display prices in Catalog | Store View | Excluding Tax, Including Tax, Both |
| Display prices in Cart | Store View | Excluding Tax, Including Tax, Both |
| Display Full Tax Summary | Store View | Yes/No |
| VAT Number Validation | Website | Yes/No |

- **Exam focus:** Tax calculation settings are at **Website** scope. Display settings (how taxes are shown) are at **Store View** scope.
- **Exam focus:** **Catalog Prices Excluding Tax** means Magento adds tax at checkout. **Including Tax** means the displayed price already includes tax (common in EU stores).

### 7.3 Per-Website Settings Summary

Settings that are meaningfully different per-website:

| Configuration Area | Per-Website Setting |
|---|---|
| Currency | Base currency |
| Tax | Tax calculation rules |
| Payment Methods | Which methods are active |
| Shipping Methods | Which carriers/rates are active |
| Pricing | Product prices (when Catalog Price Scope = Website) |
| Customer Groups | Applicable discounts/tax classes |
| Country/Region Options | Allowed countries for shipping/billing |

Settings that can differ per-store-view:

| Configuration Area | Per-Store-View Setting |
|---|---|
| Currency | Display currency, allowed currencies |
| Tax | Tax display format (inc/exc/both) |
| Locale | Language, weight unit |
| Checkout | Guest checkout enabled/disabled |
| Content | CMS pages, product names/descriptions |

## 8. Hands-On: Export, Modify, Re-Import Products

### 8.1 Step 1 — Export Products

```
System → Data Transfer → Export
```

1. Set **Entity Type** to `Products`
2. Set **Export File Format** to `CSV`
3. Optionally filter:
   - By attribute set
   - By specific SKUs
   - By category
4. Click **Continue** — file downloads automatically

```
Export Settings Example:
  Entity Type:          Products
  Export File Format:   CSV
  Fields Enclosure:     "  (double quote)

  Filter by attribute:
    sku: [leave blank for all]
    attribute_set_code: [Default]
```

### 8.2 Step 2 — Understand the Exported CSV

Open the file in LibreOffice Calc or Excel:

```
Recommended: LibreOffice Calc
  - File → Open → select CSV
  - Import Wizard: separator = comma, encoding = UTF-8
  - Do NOT let Excel auto-format dates or convert numbers to scientific notation
```

Key things to verify before editing:
- Row 1 = headers (column names)
- Each product = one or more rows (configurable products span multiple rows)
- `store_view_code` column: empty = applies to all store views

### 8.3 Step 3 — Make a Change

Common safe changes for practice:

```csv
# Change product price:
sku,price
SKU-001,34.99

# Change product name at store view level:
sku,store_view_code,name
SKU-001,french,Mon Produit Modifié

# Change stock quantity:
sku,qty,is_in_stock
SKU-001,250,1
```

**Best practice:** For the re-import exercise, only include the columns you're changing plus the `sku` column. Use **Add & Update** behavior so unchanged fields are preserved.

### 8.4 Step 4 — Re-Import

```
System → Data Transfer → Import
```

```
Import Settings:
  Entity Type:           Products
  Import Behavior:       Add/Update
  Allowed Errors Count:  10
  Field separator:       ,  (comma)
  Multiple value sep:    ,  (comma — this is the default)
  Empty attribute value constant: __EMPTY__VALUE__
  Fields enclosure:      "  (double quote)

Upload File: [Browse → select your modified CSV]
```

1. Click **Check Data** — review the validation report
2. If errors: fix the CSV and re-upload
3. If valid: click **Import** button (appears after successful validation)
4. Review the success message: "Created: X, Updated: Y, Deleted: Z"

After import, flush relevant caches (Configuration, Page Cache) and reindex if catalog/pricing data was changed to ensure storefront reflects the updates.

### 8.5 Verification After Import

```
Catalog → Products → Search for SKU
```

Verify:
- The changed field reflects the new value
- Other fields (that weren't in the import CSV) are unchanged
- Check store-view-specific values by switching the scope in the product edit page

```
Product Edit Page:
  [Store View: Default]  <- switch here to verify store-view overrides
```

## 9. Tricky Exam Details

This section compiles the non-obvious, commonly tested details from this topic.

### 9.1 CSV Column Rules (Critical)

```
FACT: Column ORDER does not matter
      Magento maps columns by NAME, not by position.

FACT: Column NAMES are case-sensitive.
      "sku"  != "SKU"  != "Sku"
      "price" != "Price"

      Always use the exact lowercase names from an exported CSV as your reference.
```

### 9.2 Required Columns for Product Import

```
At minimum, every NEW product row MUST have:
  - sku            (unique identifier)
  - attribute_set_code  (must exactly match an attribute set name)
  - product_type   (must be one of the valid type codes)

Without these three, a new product row will ALWAYS fail validation.

For EXISTING products (Add/Update behavior):
  - Only sku is strictly required
  - attribute_set_code and product_type are optional for updates
```

Valid `product_type` values:
```
simple
configurable
grouped
bundle
virtual
downloadable
giftcard        (Adobe Commerce / EE only)
```

- **Exam focus:** `simple`, `configurable`, etc. must be **all lowercase**. `Simple` or `SIMPLE` will fail validation.

### 9.3 Import Behaviors — Subtle Differences

```
Add & Update:
  - "Update" means: only update columns that ARE in the CSV
  - Columns NOT in the CSV are left untouched in the database
  - This is NOT a full record replacement

Replace:
  - Deletes the existing record entirely
  - Re-creates from CSV data
  - Columns NOT in the CSV become NULL or default values
  - Functionally: DELETE + INSERT, not UPDATE

Delete:
  - Only needs the SKU column to function
  - Other columns in the CSV are ignored
```

### 9.4 Scope Naming Confusion

```
Admin UI Label  |  Actual Scope Level  |  Code Constant
----------------|----------------------|------------------
"Default Config"|  Global default      |  ScopeConfigInterface::SCOPE_TYPE_DEFAULT
"Website"       |  Website             |  ScopeInterface::SCOPE_WEBSITES  
"Store"         |  Store Group         |  ScopeInterface::SCOPE_GROUPS
"Store View"    |  Store View          |  ScopeInterface::SCOPE_STORES

!!! "Store" in the Admin UI = Store Group in code !!!
!!! "Store View" in the Admin UI = "stores" in code !!!
```

Note: The default scope constant (`SCOPE_TYPE_DEFAULT`) lives on `ScopeConfigInterface`, not on `ScopeInterface`. Store Groups appear in the scope selector but do not have their own configuration values in `core_config_data` — only Default, Website, and Store View scopes are stored.

- **Exam focus:** This naming mismatch between the UI and code is a well-known Magento gotcha. The admin scope selector shows "Store" but it's actually selecting a "Store Group."

### 9.5 Currency Scoping

```
Base Currency    -> Website scope
                 -> Used for ALL calculations
                 -> Product prices stored in base currency
                 -> Cannot be per-Store-View

Display Currency -> Store View scope
                 -> Can differ per store view under the same website
                 -> For display only; no financial calculations

Allowed Currencies -> Store View scope
                   -> Controls which currencies the customer can switch to
```

### 9.6 Orders Are Not in the Import/Export Framework

```
Entity            | Import | Export (Data Transfer)
------------------|--------|----------------------
Products          |  YES   |  YES
Customers         |  YES   |  YES
Customer Addr     |  YES   |  YES
Advanced Pricing  |  YES   |  YES
Stock Sources     |  YES   |  YES
Orders            |  NO    |  NO   <-- Not available in either direction
```

Note: Orders can be exported from the **Sales → Orders grid** using the grid's CSV/XML export button. This is a grid-level feature, not part of the Data Transfer framework.

### 9.7 Validation is All-or-Nothing (Default)

```
Default (Stop on Error):
  - If ANY row has an error, the ENTIRE import is rejected
  - Not a single row is imported
  - Fix ALL errors before re-importing

With "Skip error entries":
  - Invalid rows are SKIPPED
  - Valid rows ARE imported
  - You get a report of what was skipped
```

### 9.8 The "Use Default" Checkbox in Configuration

```
When "Use [Parent]" is CHECKED:
  - Field is GREY/disabled
  - Value is INHERITED from parent scope
  - No scope-specific record saved in core_config_data

When "Use [Parent]" is UNCHECKED:
  - Field is EDITABLE (white background)
  - Value is OVERRIDDEN at this scope
  - A record IS saved in core_config_data for this scope
```

### 9.9 Table Rates are Per Website

```
Stores → Configuration → Sales → Shipping Methods → Table Rates
  → "Import" button for rate CSV (only visible at Website scope)

This is a DIFFERENT CSV from the product/customer import CSV.
It uses a specific format for rates based on:
  - Destination (Country, Region, Zip)
  - Condition: Weight vs. Price vs. # of Items
  - The 4th CSV column header changes based on the selected condition

Table rates are set per WEBSITE.
```
