```
app/design/frontend/Vendor/ThemeName/
    Magento_Sales/
        email/
            order_new.html          <- overrides order confirmation
    Magento_Customer/
        email/
            account_new.html        <- overrides new account email
```

> **Exam focus:** The folder inside the theme is always `email/` (not `emails/`). The filename must **exactly match** the original module's email template filename.

---

### 5.6 Custom Email Template in a Module (Non-Theme)

```xml
<!-- File: app/code/Vendor/Module/etc/email_templates.xml -->
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:module:Magento_Email:etc/email_templates.xsd">
    <template id="vendor_module_custom_order"
              label="Custom Order Email"
              file="custom_order.html"
              type="html"
              module="Vendor_Module"
              area="frontend"/>
</config>
```

```
Template file location:
app/code/Vendor/Module/view/frontend/email/custom_order.html
```

```xml
<!-- Register in system.xml so it appears in Admin config dropdown -->
<!-- File: app/code/Vendor/Module/etc/adminhtml/system.xml -->
<field id="email_template" ...>
    <source_model>Magento\Config\Model\Config\Source\Email\Template</source_model>
</field>
```

> **Exam focus:** Custom email templates **must be registered** in `email_templates.xml` before they appear in the Admin configuration dropdown. The `id` attribute must be unique across all modules.

---

### 5.7 Sending a Custom Transactional Email Programmatically

```php
<?php
namespace Vendor\Module\Model;

use Magento\Framework\Mail\Template\TransportBuilder;
use Magento\Framework\Translate\Inline\StateInterface;
use Magento\Store\Model\StoreManagerInterface;

class EmailSender
{
    public function __construct(
        private TransportBuilder $transportBuilder,
        private StateInterface $inlineTranslation,
        private StoreManagerInterface $storeManager
    ) {}

    public function sendEmail(string $toEmail, string $toName, array $templateVars): void
    {
        $this->inlineTranslation->suspend();

        try {
            $transport = $this->transportBuilder
                ->setTemplateIdentifier('vendor_module_custom_order') // template id
                ->setTemplateOptions([
                    'area'  => \Magento\Framework\App\Area::AREA_FRONTEND,
                    'store' => $this->storeManager->getStore()->getId(),
                ])
                ->setTemplateVars($templateVars)
                ->setFromByScope('sales')   // uses sales email identity from config
                ->addTo($toEmail, $toName)
                ->getTransport();

            $transport->sendMessage();
        } finally {
            $this->inlineTranslation->resume();
        }
    }
}
```

> **Exam focus:** `TransportBuilder` is the correct service for sending transactional emails in Magento 2. Always `suspend()` inline translation before sending and `resume()` after (use try/finally). The old `setFrom()` method is deprecated — use `setFromByScope()` instead.

---

### 5.8 Email Header and Footer Templates

Email templates use a **container template** system:

```
design_email_header_template   <- wraps all emails (top)
        |
        v
[Your email content template]
        |
        v
design_email_footer_template   <- wraps all emails (bottom)
```

Config paths:
- `design/email/header_template`
- `design/email/footer_template`
- `design/email/logo`
- `design/email/logo_alt`
- `design/email/logo_width` / `logo_height`

> **Exam focus:** To change the email logo, go to **Content -> Design -> Configuration -> [Store View] -> Transactional Emails section**. The logo is shared across all transactional emails via the header template. Default logo fallback width is 180px (not 200px).

### 7.1 Common Weak Topics by Candidate Profile

Based on typical AD0-E708 exam results, these are the most commonly weak areas:

| Weak Topic | Why Candidates Miss It | Key Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Configurable product stock logic | Assume parent has stock | Remember: ONLY children have stock |
| Payment action + order state combo | Confuse state vs. status | Memorize the state transition table |
| `complete` vs `closed` state | Think cancel = closed | `closed` = credit memo; `canceled` = cancel |
| Email template hierarchy | Miss DB override priority | DB template always wins over filesystem |
| Bundle price types | Confuse dynamic vs fixed discount rules | Fixed = rule on bundle; Dynamic = rule on children |
| Grouped product order behavior | Think parent appears on order | Only children appear as order line items |
| `holded` reversibility | Think it's permanent | Unhold returns to previous state |

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Product Types
- [ ] **Simple** — single SKU, own stock, own price, shippable
- [ ] **Virtual** — separate product type (not a flag); no shipping; skips shipping step if cart is all-virtual
- [ ] **Downloadable** — has links (shareable: yes/no/use config) and samples; can limit downloads; extends **Virtual** (always virtual, never requires shipping)
- [ ] **Configurable** — parent has NO stock; stock is on child simples; super attributes must be global dropdown/swatch and user-defined (eligibility is automatic, no toggle)
- [ ] **Grouped** — has its own SKU but no price, no stock on parent; children are independent; order shows only child SKUs
- [ ] **Bundle** — dynamic price (rule on children) vs. fixed price (rule on bundle); ship separately or together
- [ ] **Custom options** — do NOT create SKUs, do NOT affect inventory; different from configurable attributes
- [ ] Downloadable extends **Virtual**; Configurable, Grouped, Bundle extend **AbstractType** directly

### Payment Actions
- [ ] **Authorize Only** — hold placed; NO invoice auto-created; merchant must manually invoice to capture; order goes to `processing` on success
- [ ] **Authorize and Capture** — immediate capture; invoice auto-created; refund requires credit memo, NOT void
- [ ] **Order** (PayPal Express only) — allows multi-capture against one order authorization
- [ ] After "Authorize and Capture", cancellation requires **credit memo**, not simple cancel
- [ ] After "Authorize Only" (no invoice yet), cancellation **voids** the authorization

### Order States & Statuses
- [ ] 8 core states: `new`, `pending_payment`, `processing`, `complete`, `closed`, `canceled`, `holded`, `payment_review`
- [ ] States are **hardcoded**; statuses are **configurable** labels mapped to states
- [ ] `complete` = order can no longer be invoiced AND can no longer be shipped (StateResolver.php)
- [ ] `closed` = full credit memo issued (refund)
- [ ] `canceled` = order canceled (items still had qty to invoice)
- [ ] `holded` is the ONLY reversible state (unhold returns to prior state via holdBeforeState/holdBeforeStatus)
- [ ] Custom statuses must be assigned to a core state via `assignState($state, $isDefault, $visibleOnFront)`
- [ ] Cannot cancel an order where all items are fully invoiced — must credit memo instead
- [ ] Admin path: **Stores -> Settings -> Order Status** (not directly under Stores)

### Transactional Email Customization
- [ ] Override hierarchy: **DB template > Theme file > Module default**
- [ ] Admin-created templates stored in **database** (`email_template` table) — highest priority
- [ ] Theme override path: `app/design/frontend/<V>/<T>/Magento_Sales/email/order_new.html`
- [ ] Module email templates registered in `etc/email_templates.xml`
- [ ] Template variables use `{{var ...}}` syntax, not PHP
- [ ] `{{trans "..."}}` for translations, `{{block class="..." template="..."}}` for block output
- [ ] `{{depend ...}}` for conditionals in email templates
- [ ] Must assign custom template in **Stores -> Config** after creating it in Admin
- [ ] Use `TransportBuilder` with `setFromByScope()` to send emails programmatically
- [ ] Always `suspend()` inline translation before sending, `resume()` after
- [ ] Email logo/header/footer configured under **Content -> Design -> Configuration -> Transactional Emails**
- [ ] Email header template wraps ALL transactional emails; default logo width fallback is 180px

### Exam Strategy
- [ ] "Core Features / General Configuration" domain = **46% of exam** — highest weight, most questions
- [ ] Score each section separately to identify specific weak areas
- [ ] Write wrong-answer reasoning in your own words (not copied from answer key)
- [ ] Flag top 5 weak topics explicitly for Week 2 reinforcement

flashcards.question: What is the heaviest-weighted domain on the AD0-E708 exam?
flashcards.answer: Core Features / General Configuration at 46%. This covers product types, admin panel, import/export, cart & checkout, shipping, CMS/Page Builder, order lifecycle, gifting, transactional emails, and B2B self-service.
flashcards.hint: Nearly half of the exam focuses on one domain.

flashcards.question: What type class does the Downloadable product type extend in Magento's code, and what is the practical implication?
flashcards.answer: Downloadable extends Virtual (not Simple or AbstractType). This means downloadable products are inherently virtual — they always skip the shipping step and never require weight, because they inherit Virtual's isVirtual()=true behavior.
flashcards.hint: Check the PHP class hierarchy — the parent class reveals the shipping behavior.

flashcards.question: How do Custom Options on a Simple product differ from Configurable product attributes?
flashcards.answer: Custom Options do NOT create new SKUs and do NOT affect inventory tracking. Configurable attributes create child Simple products, each with their own SKU and stock. Custom options are non-inventory-tracked selections at the product level.
flashcards.hint: One creates separate inventory-tracked variants, the other is just a selection with no inventory impact.

flashcards.question: In the order, what happens to the grouped product parent when items from a Grouped product are purchased?
flashcards.answer: On the order, grouped product associations are lost. The order line items show only the individual simple product SKUs, not the grouped parent. The grouped product is purely a storefront presentation container.
flashcards.hint: The parent is just for display — it disappears once the order is placed.

flashcards.question: For Dynamic Price bundles, where do catalog price rules apply — on the bundle parent or on the children?
flashcards.answer: For Dynamic Price bundles, catalog price rules apply to the child simple products. For Fixed Price bundles, catalog price rules apply to the bundle itself.
flashcards.hint: The pricing model determines which entity receives the discount.

flashcards.question: What are the three possible values for a downloadable link's 'shareable' setting?
flashcards.answer: Yes (shareable, URL never expires, no login needed), No (non-shareable, customer must be logged in), and Use Config (follows the global Downloadable Product Options setting). These correspond to values 1, 0, and 2 internally.
flashcards.hint: There is a per-link option that can also defer to a system-wide setting.

flashcards.question: What happens to an order in payment_review state when the admin accepts vs. denies the payment?
flashcards.answer: Accept moves the order to 'processing' state (payment confirmed). Deny moves the order to 'canceled' state. This applies when a payment gateway flags a transaction for manual review.
flashcards.hint: The admin makes a binary decision that determines whether the order proceeds or stops.

flashcards.question: After an 'Authorize and Capture' payment, can you simply cancel the order to return the customer's money?
flashcards.answer: No. Because funds have already been captured, you cannot void the transaction. You must create a Credit Memo to initiate a refund. Simple cancellation is only possible when items still have qty to invoice.
flashcards.hint: Once money has been captured, the reversal process is different.

flashcards.question: Is the 'Order' payment action available for all payment methods in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: No. The 'Order' payment action is only available for PayPal Express specifically. It allows multiple authorizations and captures against a single order. Braintree and other payment methods do NOT support it.
flashcards.hint: This multi-capture action is exclusive to one specific payment integration.

flashcards.question: What initial order state does a successful 'Authorize Only' payment action produce?
flashcards.answer: A successful online authorization (e.g., credit card) puts the order directly in 'processing' state — it does NOT pass through 'pending_payment' first. The pending_payment state is for offline methods or async payment confirmations.
flashcards.hint: A successful authorization is confirmed immediately, so it skips the waiting state.

flashcards.question: When can an order be canceled in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: An order can only be canceled if there are still items with quantity left to invoice. Once all items are fully invoiced, cancellation is blocked and you must use a Credit Memo instead. The canCancel() method checks each item's getQtyToInvoice().
flashcards.hint: The ability to cancel depends on whether invoicing has already occurred.

flashcards.question: What two MSI Source Selection Algorithms does Magento provide for determining which warehouse fulfills an order?
flashcards.answer: Priority (PriorityBasedAlgorithm) ships from sources in configured priority order and is the default. Distance Priority (DistanceBasedAlgorithm) ships from the source closest to the shipping address. Admin can also manually override during shipment creation.
flashcards.hint: One is order-based, the other is geography-based.

flashcards.question: Where are custom order statuses created and assigned in the admin?
flashcards.answer: At Stores > Settings > Order Status > Create New Status. Custom statuses must be assigned to an existing core state (e.g., 'processing') before they can be used. Status codes are immutable after creation.
flashcards.hint: You can create new labels, but they must attach to one of the eight existing states.

flashcards.question: Which commonly weak area trips up most AD0-E708 exam candidates regarding configurable products?
flashcards.answer: Candidates often assume the parent configurable product has its own stock. The correct concept is that ONLY child simple products have stock. The parent's stock quantity field is ignored by the inventory system.
flashcards.hint: The stock misconception about parent vs. child is the most common trap.

# Magento 2 EE: Gifting Options & B2B Loyalty/Self-Service
## Comprehensive Study Notes — Week 2, Day 5 (Jan 19)

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Gift Cards (EE)](#1-gift-cards-ee)
2. [Gift Wrapping (EE)](#2-gift-wrapping-ee)
3. [Gift Messages](#3-gift-messages)
4. [Gift Registry (EE)](#4-gift-registry-ee)
5. [Reward Points (EE)](#5-reward-points-ee)
6. [Store Credit (EE)](#6-store-credit-ee)
7. [Loyalty Program Design](#7-loyalty-program-design)
8. [B2B Self-Service (EE)](#8-b2b-self-service-ee)
9. [Requisition Lists (B2B)](#9-requisition-lists-b2b)
10. [Tax Interaction & Order Calculation Tricky Points](#10-tax-interaction--order-calculation-tricky-points)
11. [Hands-On Configuration Walkthrough](#11-hands-on-configuration-walkthrough)
12. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Gift Cards (EE)

### 1.1 Overview

Gift Cards are an **Adobe Commerce (EE) exclusive** product type that allows customers to purchase and send monetary value redeemable in the store. They are treated as a distinct product type in the catalog, separate from Simple, Virtual, Configurable, etc.

> **Exam focus:** Gift Cards are **EE-only** — not available in Magento Open Source.

### 1.2 Gift Card Types

| Type | Delivery | Physical Shipping | Use Case |
|------|----------|-------------------|----------|
| **Virtual** | Email only | No | Online-only redemption |
| **Physical** | Mail/post | Yes | In-store or online redemption |
| **Combined** | Both email + mail | Yes | Maximum flexibility |

```
+------------------+         +------------------+        +------------------+
|    VIRTUAL       |         |    PHYSICAL      |        |    COMBINED      |
|                  |         |                  |        |                  |
| Delivered via    |         | Mailed as a      |        | Delivered BOTH   |
| email only       |         | physical card    |        | by email AND     |
| No shipping      |         | Requires ship.   |        | physical mail    |
+------------------+         +------------------+        +------------------+
```

> **Exam focus:** Only **Physical** and **Combined** gift cards require a shipping address and incur shipping costs. Virtual gift cards do **not** require a shipping address.

### 1.3 Gift Card Product Configuration

Navigate to: **Catalog > Products > Add Product > Gift Card**

#### Key Configuration Fields

```
Gift Card Product Settings
|
+-- Amounts (fixed denominations, e.g. $25, $50, $100)
|   OR Open Amount (customer specifies value within a min/max range)
|   (Open Amount, Min, Max are product-level attributes, not global config)
|
+-- Gift Card Type: Virtual / Physical / Combined
|
+-- Allow Message: Yes/No
|
+-- Email Template (for Virtual/Combined delivery)
|
+-- Lifetime (days until card expires)
|   0 = never expires
|
+-- Is Redeemable: Yes/No (can balance be added to account?)
```

#### Gift Card Lifetime

- Configured per product under **Gift Card Information** tab
- Value in **days** from purchase date; `0` = never expires
- The expiration date is displayed in the customer's account under **Gift Card** section

> **Exam focus:** Lifetime is set in **days**. A value of `0` means the card never expires. Expiry is calculated from the **date of purchase**, not the date the card is sent or activated.

### 1.4 Email Delivery Configuration

Path: **Stores > Configuration > Sales > Gift Cards**

| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Gift Card Notification Email Sender | Store identity used for email (`giftcard/email/identity`) |
| Gift Card Notification Email Template | Template for delivery email (`giftcard/email/template`) |
| Generate Gift Card Account when Order Item is | Controls when the account/code is generated (e.g., "Invoiced" or "Ordered") |

> **Correction:** There is no simple "Send Gift Card Email when Order is Placed" toggle. The actual field is `order_item_status` — it controls when the gift card account is generated (at order or at invoice), which in turn triggers email delivery.

> **Exam focus:** For **Virtual** gift cards, the email is the delivery mechanism. The timing depends on the `order_item_status` configuration.

### 1.5 Redemption on Account Balance

Customers can:
1. **Redeem at checkout** — enter code in the "Gift Card" field; value applied as a discount
2. **Add to account balance** — go to **My Account > Gift Card** and apply code to their store account balance (which works like Store Credit)

```
Customer Receives Gift Card Code
           |
           v
    +------+----------+
    |                 |
    v                 v
Redeem at          Add to Account
Checkout           Balance (Store Credit)
(one-time use      (persists across
 at payment step)   multiple orders)
```

> **Exam focus:** When a customer redeems a Gift Card **to their account balance**, it becomes **Store Credit**. The original Gift Card code is then voided/used.

### 1.6 Global Gift Card Configuration

Path: **Stores > Configuration > Sales > Gift Cards** (section=`giftcard`, tab=`sales`)

```xml
<!-- Key config fields (module-gift-card/etc/adminhtml/system.xml) -->
<section id="giftcard">
    <group id="general">
        <!-- Is Redeemable (can add to account balance) -->
        <field id="is_redeemable">1</field>  <!-- showInDefault=1 only -->
        <!-- Lifetime in days (0 = no expiry) -->
        <field id="lifetime">0</field>  <!-- showInDefault=1 only -->
        <!-- Allow Message -->
        <field id="allow_message">1</field>
        <!-- Message Max Length -->
        <field id="message_max_length">255</field>
        <!-- Generate Account When Order Item Is -->
        <field id="order_item_status">9</field>
    </group>
    <group id="email">
        <field id="identity">...</field>  <!-- showIn: Default, Website, Store -->
        <field id="template">...</field>  <!-- showIn: Default, Website, Store -->
    </group>
</section>
```

> **Correction:** The fields `allow_open_amount`, `open_amount_min`, and `open_amount_max` are **product-level attributes** (defined in catalog_attributes.xml), not global system configuration. They are set per product, not globally. The field `allow_redeem` does not exist — the actual field is `is_redeemable`.

### 1.7 Admin Management of Gift Card Accounts

Path: **Marketing > Promotions > Gift Card Accounts**

- Admin can **create** gift card codes manually (without purchasing a product)
- Admin can **view balance**, **deactivate**, or **delete** cards
- Mass actions: delete, update balance
- Each account shows: code, balance, status (active/used/expired), expiry date

> **Correction:** Gift Card Accounts is under Marketing > **Promotions** > Gift Card Accounts (parent=`Magento_CatalogRule::promo`), not directly under Marketing.

> **Exam focus:** Gift Card Accounts can be created **directly by admin** without going through the purchase flow — useful for promotions, customer service credits, etc.

---

## 2. Gift Wrapping (EE)

### 2.1 Overview

Gift Wrapping allows customers to select a wrapping style (with an optional fee) for their order. It can be applied:
- **Per order** — single wrapping for the whole shipment
- **Per item** — individual wrapping for each product

> **Exam focus:** Gift Wrapping is **EE-only** and can be configured at **both the item level AND the order level** simultaneously. Each wrapping design has its own price and image.

### 2.2 Configuration

Path: **Stores > Configuration > Sales > Gift Options** (section=`sales`, group=`gift_options`)

| Setting | Field ID | Scope |
|---------|----------|-------|
| Allow Gift Wrapping on Order Level | `wrapping_allow_order` | Default + Website |
| Allow Gift Wrapping for Order Items | `wrapping_allow_items` | Default + Website |
| Allow Gift Receipt | `allow_gift_receipt` | Default + Website |
| Allow Printed Card | `allow_printed_card` | Default + Website |
| Default Price for Printed Card | `printed_card_price` | Default + Website |

## 5. Reward Points (EE)

### 5.1 Overview

Reward Points is an **EE loyalty feature** enabling a points-based system where customers earn points for actions (purchases, registrations, reviews) and spend points as a discount at checkout.

> **Exam focus:** Reward Points are **EE-only**. Exchange rates for earning and spending are managed separately at **Stores > Other Settings > Reward Exchange Rates**.

### 5.2 Global Configuration

Path: **Stores > Configuration > Customers > Reward Points** (section=`magento_reward`, tab=`customer`)

```
Reward Points Global Config (group=general)
|
+-- Enable Reward Points Functionality: Yes/No (field: is_enabled)
|
+-- Rewards Points Balance Redemption Threshold (field: min_points_balance)
|   (customer must have at least X points to use them)
|
+-- Cap Reward Points Balance At (field: max_points_balance)
|
+-- Reward Points Expire in (days) (field: expiration_days, 0 = never expire)
|
+-- Expiry Warning Before (days) (field: expiry_day_before)
|   - Send reminder X days before expiry
|
+-- Landing Page (informational page about the program)
```

> **Exam focus:** The **minimum points balance** setting prevents customers from using reward points until they accumulate a threshold. This is separate from per-order caps.

### 5.3 Exchange Rate Configuration

Path: **Stores > Other Settings > Reward Exchange Rates** (admin action: `adminhtml/reward_rate`)

> **Correction:** Exchange rates are managed as rate records in a separate admin grid (Stores > Other Settings > Reward Exchange Rates), NOT as config fields under Stores > Configuration. They are database records, not system.xml settings.

Two rates must be configured:

```
+----------------------------------+----------------------------------+
|  EARNING RATE                    |  SPENDING RATE                   |
|                                  |                                  |
|  X currency units spent          |  X points redeemed               |
|  = Y points earned               |  = Y currency discount           |
|                                  |                                  |
|  Example:                        |  Example:                        |
|  $1 spent = 10 points            |  100 points = $1 discount        |
+----------------------------------+----------------------------------+
```

> **Exam focus:** Exchange rates are configured as **two separate rates** — earning and spending. They do NOT have to be symmetrical. For example, earning $1 = 10 points but redeeming 100 points = $0.50 (not $1) is perfectly valid and common for margin protection.

### 5.4 Earning Actions

Path: **Stores > Configuration > Customers > Reward Points** (group=`points`, label="Actions for Acquiring Reward Points")

Actions that can earn points:

| Earning Action | Field ID | Description |
|----------------|----------|-------------|
| **Purchase** | `order` | Points based on order subtotal (via exchange rate) |
| **Registration** | `register` | One-time points for creating an account |
| **Newsletter Signup** | `newsletter` | Points for subscribing |
| **Review Submission** | `review` | Points when review is approved |
| **Invitation (converted to customer)** | `invitation_customer` | Points when invited person registers |
| **Invitation (converted to order)** | `invitation_order` | Points when invited person makes a purchase |

> **Correction:** There is **no Birthday earning action** in the codebase. The six actions above are the only ones defined (Reward.php action constants: REWARD_ACTION_REGISTER=2, REWARD_ACTION_NEWSLETTER=3, REWARD_ACTION_INVITATION_CUSTOMER=4, REWARD_ACTION_INVITATION_ORDER=5, REWARD_ACTION_REVIEW=6, REWARD_ACTION_ORDER_EXTRA=8).

> **Exam focus:** Points for **purchases** are only added to the customer's balance **after the order is invoiced/paid** (OrderCompleted observer checks `_isOrderPaidNow()`). Points from reviews are added **after the review is approved**.

### 5.5 Spending Rules (Redemption)

- Customers opt in at **checkout** to apply reward points
- The system calculates how much monetary value the points represent
- Points are deducted from balance upon **order placement** (RedeemForOrder observer on `sales_model_service_quote_submit_before`)
- If order is **refunded**, points can be optionally returned to the customer's balance

```
Checkout Payment Step
        |
        v
[ ] Apply Reward Points (checkbox)
    Balance: 500 points (= $5.00 discount)
    [Apply]
        |
        v
    Points deducted from balance
    Discount applied to order total
```

### 5.6 Points Lifetime / Expiry Policy

```
Expiration Days = 0        --> Points NEVER expire
Expiration Days = 365      --> Points expire 365 days after they were EARNED
```

> **Exam focus (UX/tricky):** Each **batch of points** has its own expiry date based on when they were earned — it's not a rolling reset of the entire balance. Points expiry is communicated via email (configurable reminder days before expiry via `expiry_day_before` field). **Clearly communicating the expiry policy is a critical UX concern** — customers who don't know their points expire will be frustrated when they lose them.

### 5.7 Points Balance Management (Admin)

Path: **Customers > All Customers > Edit Customer > Reward Points**

Admin can:
- **Manually add/deduct** points with a comment
- View full **points history** (earned, spent, expired, adjusted)
- Set individual customer's points to expire/not expire

```php
// Admin manual adjustment creates a history entry like:
[
    'points_delta'  => 500,      // positive = add, negative = deduct
    'comment'       => 'Goodwill gesture for late delivery',
    'is_expired'    => false,
    'expires_at'    => 'YYYY-MM-DD 23:59:59',
]
```

### 5.8 Reward Points on the Storefront

- Customers see their balance in **My Account > Reward Points**
- Full history with earn/spend/expire entries
- Notifications configurable: balance updates, expiry reminders

Store Credit is an **EE feature** that maintains a **monetary balance** (in store currency) associated with a customer account. Unlike Reward Points (which have an exchange rate), Store Credit is **1:1 with currency**.

> **Exam focus:** Store Credit is **EE-only**, denominated in **store currency**, and is **1:1** with the currency (no exchange rate). Reward Points have an exchange rate; Store Credit does not.

### 6.2 Sources of Store Credit

```
Store Credit Balance Sources
|
+-- 1. Admin Manual Credit
|       (Customers > Edit > Store Credit > Update Balance)
|
+-- 2. Refund to Store Credit
|       (Admin processes refund --> credits account instead of original payment)
|
+-- 3. Gift Card Redemption to Account
|       (Customer redeems gift card code to their account balance)
```

### 6.3 Admin Management

Path: **Customers > All Customers > Edit > Store Credit** (tab added by module-customer-balance)

```
Store Credit Panel
|
+-- Current Balance: $XX.XX
+-- Update Balance: [amount field] + [comment field]
+-- History: list of all credits/debits with dates and comments
```

When processing a credit memo:

```

        |
        v
Refund Options:
[ ] Refund to Original Payment Method (credit card refund)
[x] Refund to Store Credit (adds to customer account balance)
```

## 7. Loyalty Program Design

### 7.1 Combining EE Features for a Loyalty Program

A comprehensive loyalty program in Adobe Commerce EE combines multiple features:

```
LOYALTY PROGRAM ARCHITECTURE
|
+-- TIER IDENTIFICATION
|   Customer Segments (EE) — define Gold/Silver/Bronze tiers
|   based on lifetime spend, order count, etc.
|
+-- EARNING MECHANISM
|   Reward Points — points per purchase, registration, reviews
|
+-- SPENDING MECHANISM
|   Reward Points redemption at checkout
|   Store Credit for refunds
|
+-- EXCLUSIVE PRICING
|   Customer Group Pricing (special prices per group)
|   Catalog Price Rules scoped to segments/groups
|
+-- ENGAGEMENT
|   Gift Cards for gifting between customers
|   Gift Registry for event-based shopping
```

### 7.2 Customer Segments + Reward Points

**Customer Segments** (EE) allow dynamic grouping based on:
- Lifetime order value
- Number of orders
- Products purchased
- Wishlisted items
- Cart contents

```
Segment: "Gold Tier"
Conditions:
  - Lifetime spend >= $1000
  - Orders count >= 5

Applied Loyalty Benefits:
  - Cart Price Rule: 10% discount (Gold Tier customers)
  - Reward Points Exchange Rate: 1.5x earning rate (not natively
    per-segment, but achievable via cart price rule bonus points)
  - Exclusive Dynamic Block content shown to segment
```

> **Exam focus:** **Customer Segments** are **EE-only** and are **dynamic** (automatically update as customers meet/fail conditions). Customer **Groups** (Open Source) are static — admin assigns manually. Segments can target Cart Price Rules, Catalog Price Rules, and Dynamic Blocks (CMS content).

> **Correction:** Customer Segments admin path is **Customers > Segments** (title="Segments", parent=`Magento_Customer::customer`), not "Marketing > Customer Segments".

### 7.3 Special Prices Strategy

| Mechanism | Scope | Use Case |
|-----------|-------|----------|
| **Tier Pricing** | Product-level, quantity breaks | Buy more = pay less |
| **Group Price** | Customer group | Wholesale vs. retail |
| **Catalog Price Rule** | Dynamic, rule-based | Time-limited loyalty discounts |
| **Cart Price Rule** | Cart-level | Free shipping, % off cart |
| **Reward Points** | Account-level | Long-term loyalty earn/spend |

### 7.4 Sample Loyalty Program Configuration Flow

```bash
# Step 1: Create Customer Groups
# Admin > Customers > Customer Groups
# Create: Bronze, Silver, Gold

# Step 2: Create Customer Segments (EE)
# Customers > Segments
# "Gold Segment": Lifetime Spend >= $1000

# Step 3: Configure Reward Points Exchange Rates
# Stores > Other Settings > Reward Exchange Rates
# Earning: $1 = 10 points
# Spending: 100 points = $1 discount

# Step 4: Create Catalog Price Rules for each tier
# Marketing > Catalog Price Rules
# Rule: Customer Group = Gold --> 10% off all products

# Step 5: Set Reward Points Lifetime
# Stores > Config > Customers > Reward Points > expiration_days = 365
# (communicate clearly in program T&Cs)
```

```
+-- Company Users (buyers)

|   +-- Role: Senior Buyer (approve up to $5000 without approval)
|   +-- Role: Manager (full purchase authority)
|
+-- Company Structure (org chart)
    |
    +-- Departments/Divisions (hierarchical)
```

The Company Admin creates **custom roles** with granular permissions:

```
|
+-- Checkout Permissions
|   - Place orders: Yes/No
|   - Approve orders: Yes/No
|   - View orders: Own / Department / Company
|
+-- Quote Permissions

```

> **Exam focus:** The **Company Admin** is a **storefront role**, not a Magento admin role. Company Admins operate entirely within the storefront "My Account" area. They do NOT have access to the Magento backend.

### 8.4 Purchase Approval Workflows

Path (Storefront): **My Account > Approval Rules**

The Company Admin sets rules governing when orders need approval:

| Rule Type | Condition Key | Description |
|-----------|---------------|-------------|
| **Order Total** | `grand_total` | Orders exceeding $X require approval |
| **Shipping Cost** | `shipping_incl_tax` | Shipping cost exceeding $X requires approval |
| **Number of SKUs** | `number_of_skus` | Orders with more than N SKUs require approval |

```
Order Approval Workflow
        |
        v
Buyer places order
        |
        v
[Rule Check] Does order exceed approval threshold?
        |
   Yes  |  No
        |   +----> Order placed normally
        v
Order status: "Pending Approval"
        |
        v
Approver notified (email)
        |

   |         |
Approve    Reject
   |         |
   v         v
Order     Buyer notified
placed    order rejected
```

> **Exam focus:** Orders pending approval are in **"Pending Approval"** status. The buyer **cannot** proceed without approval. The approver is determined by the company org structure — the user's manager in the hierarchy.

- Set **per user** or **per role** by the Company Admin
- **Monthly spending limit** — resets monthly
- **Annual spending limit** — resets annually
- Limits are independent of approval workflows (a user can have both a spending limit AND an approval rule)

```
|

```

## 10. Tax Interaction & Order Calculation Tricky Points

### 10.1 Gift Card Tax Behavior

> **Exam focus (CRITICAL TRICKY POINT):** Gift Cards reduce the order subtotal **BEFORE tax is calculated** in most configurations. This means tax is calculated on the **net amount after gift card discount**, resulting in lower tax collected.

```
ORDER TOTAL CALCULATION (typical flow with Gift Card)
|
Step 1: Calculate Subtotal
        Product subtotal: $100.00
|
Step 2: Apply Gift Card Discount
        Gift Card applied: -$25.00
        Adjusted subtotal: $75.00
|
Step 3: Calculate Tax (on $75.00, NOT $100.00)
        Tax (10%): $7.50
|
Step 4: Add Shipping
        Shipping: $5.00
|
Step 5: Grand Total
        $75.00 + $7.50 + $5.00 = $87.50
```

Compare to a scenario where gift card is applied AFTER tax:
```
WITHOUT gift-card-before-tax behavior:
Tax calculated on $100.00 = $10.00
Grand Total = $100 - $25 + $10 + $5 = $90.00
            (customer pays more tax)
```

> **Exam focus:** The **default Magento EE behavior** is that Gift Cards (and also Reward Points discounts and Store Credit) are applied as **discounts to the subtotal BEFORE tax**. This is the most common configuration but it CAN be changed via tax configuration.

### 10.2 Reward Points Tax Interaction

Same behavior as Gift Cards:
- Reward points discount is applied to subtotal **before** tax in default config
- Tax configuration setting: **Stores > Config > Sales > Tax > Calculation Settings > Apply Customer Tax** (Before/After Discount) (field: `tax/calculation/apply_after_discount`)

> **Correction:** The "Apply Customer Tax" field is under **Calculation Settings** (`tax/calculation` group), not "Shopping Cart Display Settings".

### 10.3 Order of Discount Application

```
FULL ORDER CALCULATION SEQUENCE (default)
|
1. Product base price
2. Tier/group prices applied
3. Catalog Price Rules applied
4. Cart Price Rules applied (coupon codes)
5. Reward Points discount applied
6. Gift Card discount applied
7. Store Credit applied
         |
         v
   [SUBTOTAL after all discounts]
         |
8. Tax calculated on discounted subtotal
9. Shipping added
10. Gift Wrapping fees added (taxed separately if configured)
         |
         v
   [GRAND TOTAL]
```

> **Exam focus:** Understanding the **order of operations** for discounts, tax, and fees is frequently tested. Gift Cards, Reward Points, and Store Credit all reduce the taxable subtotal when the default tax configuration is used.

### 10.4 Gift Wrapping Tax

- Gift Wrapping has its own **Tax Class** setting: "Tax Class for Gift Options" (`tax/classes/wrapping_tax_class`)
- Can be configured to use same tax class as products or a different one
- Gift Wrapping fees are **added** to the order, not subtracted — so they increase the taxable amount
