## 5. Google Tag Manager

### GTM Overview

Google Tag Manager (GTM) acts as a **tag management system** — instead of hardcoding analytics/marketing scripts, you deploy a single GTM container snippet and manage all tags from the GTM UI.

```
Browser Request
      |
      v
Magento Page loads GTM Container Snippet
      |
      v
GTM reads dataLayer events
      |
      v
GTM fires configured Tags (GA4, Facebook Pixel, etc.)
```

### GTM Configuration in Magento

> **Note:** In Adobe Commerce EE, GTM is NOT a separate config section. It shares the same `google/analytics` group as Google Analytics. When the "Account type" field is set to "Google Tag Manager", the Container Id field appears and the Account Number field is hidden. This is controlled by the `module-google-tag-manager` module (EE-only).

```
Stores → Configuration → Sales → Google API → Google Analytics
  → Account type: Google Tag Manager
  → Container Id: GTM-XXXXXXX
```

The container snippet is injected into:
- `<head>` — main GTM snippet
- `<body>` — noscript fallback iframe

### The Data Layer

The **data layer** (`window.dataLayer`) is a JavaScript array that Magento populates with structured eCommerce event data, which GTM reads and forwards to configured analytics tags.

#### Data Layer Structure

```javascript
// Initial page load — product detail page
window.dataLayer = [{
  'pageType': 'product',
  'ecommerce': {
    'detail': {
      'actionField': {'list': 'Product Page'},
      'products': [{
        'id': 'MH01-XS-Black',
        'name': 'Chaz Kangeroo Hoodie',
        'price': '52.00',
        'brand': 'Magento',
        'category': 'Tops/Hoodies & Sweatshirts',
        'variant': 'XS-Black'
      }]
    }
  }
}];
```

#### Key eCommerce Events in GTM Data Layer

| Page/Action | dataLayer Event | Trigger Type in GTM |
|---|---|---|
| Category Page | `productImpression` | Custom Event |
| Product Detail Page | `productDetail` | Custom Event |
| Add to Cart | `addToCart` | Custom Event |
| Remove from Cart | `removeFromCart` | Custom Event |
| Checkout Step 1 | `checkout` (step: 1) | Custom Event |
| Purchase Complete | `purchase` | Custom Event |

#### Example: Add to Cart Data Layer Push

```javascript
window.dataLayer.push({
  'event': 'addToCart',
  'ecommerce': {
    'currencyCode': 'USD',
    'add': {
      'products': [{
        'name': 'Breathable Running Jacket',
        'id': 'WJ05',
        'price': '149.99',
        'brand': 'Magento',
        'category': 'Women/Tops/Jackets',
        'variant': 'Blue-M',
        'quantity': 1
      }]
    }
  }
});
```

### GTM vs Native GA Integration

| Aspect | Native GA Integration (CE) | GTM Integration (EE) |
|---|---|---|
| Setup complexity | Low (just Account Number) | Medium (Container ID + GA tag in GTM) |
| Flexibility | Limited to Magento config options | Highly flexible — add any tag |
| Tag Management | None | Full GTM interface |
| Debug capability | Limited | GTM Preview/Debug mode |
| Recommended for | Simple setups | Enterprise/production |

**Exam focus:**
- GTM is configured under the **same Google Analytics section** — the Account type field switches between UA and GTM mode.
- GTM uses the **data layer** (`window.dataLayer`) to receive eCommerce event data.
- GTM and native GA should NOT both track the same events — this causes **double-tracking**.
- The `module-google-tag-manager` is **EE-only** (proprietary license).

## 6. Shopping Feeds & Google Shopping

### Google Shopping / Merchant Center

Adobe Commerce supports integration with **Google Merchant Center** to enable Product Listing Ads (PLAs) via product feeds.

### Feed Tools in Adobe Commerce

> **Note:** There is **no** "Marketing → Shopping Feed" menu item in the standard Adobe Commerce 2.4.8-p3 codebase. Google Shopping feed functionality requires a **third-party extension** (e.g., Google Shopping Feed by Magefan, Amasty, etc.) or custom implementation. Adobe Commerce Channel Manager is a separate SaaS extension.

### Required Google Product Feed Attributes

```
id           -> Product SKU
title        -> Product Name
description  -> Product Description
link         -> Product URL
image_link   -> Base Image URL
price        -> Final Price + Currency
availability -> in stock / out of stock
condition    -> new / used / refurbished
brand        -> Manufacturer attribute
gtin         -> Barcode/EAN/UPC attribute (recommended)
mpn          -> Manufacturer Part Number
```

### Feed Format (XML)

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rss version="2.0" xmlns:g="http://base.google.com/ns/1.0">
  <channel>
    <title>My Store</title>
    <link>https://mystore.com</link>
    <description>Product Feed</description>
    <item>
      <g:id>WJ05-Blue-M</g:id>
      <g:title>Breathable Running Jacket</g:title>
      <g:description>Lightweight running jacket...</g:description>
      <g:link>https://mystore.com/breathable-running-jacket.html</g:link>
      <g:image_link>https://mystore.com/media/catalog/product/w/j/wj05.jpg</g:image_link>
      <g:price>149.99 USD</g:price>
      <g:availability>in stock</g:availability>
      <g:condition>new</g:condition>
      <g:brand>Magento</g:brand>
    </item>
  </channel>
</rss>
```

### Adobe Commerce Channel Manager (SaaS)

Adobe Commerce also offers **Channel Manager** (a SaaS extension) for managing sales channels including:
- **Amazon Sales Channel** — list and sell on Amazon

**Exam focus:**
- Google Shopping feed functionality is **not built into** the standard Adobe Commerce admin — it requires third-party extensions.
- Google Shopping feed requires specific attributes: `id`, `title`, `price`, `availability`, `image_link`.
- Feed format is RSS/XML compatible with Google Merchant Center specifications.
- Product attributes in Magento must be **mapped** to Google feed attributes.

## 7. Tricky Exam Scenarios

### Scenario 1: URL Key Change Creates Automatic 301 Redirect

**Setup:** A product with URL key `old-jacket.html` is renamed to `new-jacket.html`.

**What Magento does:**

```
1. Admin saves product with new URL key: new-jacket.html
2. "Create Permanent Redirect for old URL" checkbox = Yes (default)
3. Magento inserts into url_rewrite table:
   request_path:  old-jacket.html
   target_path:   new-jacket.html (or canonical target path)
   redirect_type: 301
4. Old URL still works: 301 redirect to new URL
5. SEO equity (link juice) is preserved via 301
```

**Common trap:** If the checkbox is **unchecked**, no redirect is created, and old bookmarks/links return **404**.

```sql
-- Verify redirect exists:
SELECT request_path, target_path, redirect_type
FROM url_rewrite
WHERE request_path = 'old-jacket.html';

-- Expected result:
-- request_path: old-jacket.html
-- target_path: new-jacket.html
-- redirect_type: 301
```

**Exam focus:**
- Redirect is **301 (permanent)** not 302 (temporary).
- Redirect creation is controlled by a **checkbox that defaults to checked**.
- This applies to **products, categories, and CMS pages**.

---

### Scenario 2: Canonical URL Issues with Configurable Product Variants

**The problem:**

```
Configurable Product:  /mens-hoodie.html
Simple child products:
  - /mens-hoodie/blue-xs.html
  - /mens-hoodie/red-m.html
  - /mens-hoodie/black-xl.html

Without canonical tags:
  Google indexes ALL URLs as separate pages
  -> Thin content / duplicate content penalty
  -> Link equity split across all variants
```

**The solution with canonical tags enabled:**

```html
<!-- On /mens-hoodie/blue-xs.html -->
<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/mens-hoodie.html" />

<!-- Google understands: -->
<!-- "This page's authoritative version is mens-hoodie.html" -->
<!-- All ranking signals consolidated to parent URL -->
```

**Additional complexity — layered navigation:**

```
/mens/jackets.html?color=blue     <- filter applied
/mens/jackets.html?price=50-100   <- filter applied
/mens/jackets.html?p=2            <- pagination

Canonical points to: /mens/jackets.html
-> Prevents filter parameter pages from being indexed separately
```

**Exam focus:**
- Enabling canonical for products on a configurable product setup **canonicals child simple products to the parent configurable URL**.
- Without canonical tags, configurable variants can cause **duplicate content penalties**.
- Layered navigation filter URLs (query strings) also benefit from canonical handling.
- This is a **known and documented SEO challenge** in Magento 2.

---

### Scenario 3: Changing URL Suffix Regenerates All Rewrites

**Setup:** Store changes product URL suffix from `.html` to `` (empty).

```
Before: /breathable-jacket.html
After:  /breathable-jacket

Impact:
1. ALL product URL rewrites regenerated
2. Old .html URLs get 301 redirects to new non-suffix URLs
3. For large catalogs: can be a SLOW operation
4. Temporary storefront performance impact during regeneration
```

**Exam focus:**
- URL suffix change is a **store-wide setting** — it changes ALL URLs simultaneously.
- Plan this change during **low-traffic periods**.

---

### Scenario 4: Double Tracking — GTM + Native GA Both Enabled

```
Config mistake:
  Native Google Analytics: Enabled (G-XXXXXXXXXX)
  Google Tag Manager: Enabled (GTM-XXXXXXX)
  GTM has GA4 tag configured inside it

Result:
  Every page triggers GA4 TWICE
  Inflated pageview counts
  Inaccurate purchase event data
  Double revenue reported in GA4

Fix:
  Disable native GA in Magento config
  Manage GA4 ONLY through GTM
```

**Exam focus:**
- If using GTM, **disable the native GA integration** to prevent double-tracking.
- GTM is the preferred method for enterprise setups as it offers more control.

```bash
# Key admin paths for SEO audit:

1. Stores → Config → Catalog → Catalog → Search Engine Optimization
   - Use Canonical Link Meta Tag For Categories: Yes
   - Use Canonical Link Meta Tag For Products: Yes
   - Product URL Suffix: .html
   - Category URL Suffix: .html
   - Create Permanent Redirect for URLs if URL Key Changed: Yes
   - Use Categories Path for Product URLs: Yes/No (important!)

2. Stores → Config → Catalog → XML Sitemap
   - All frequency/priority settings
   - Generation cron settings

3. Stores → Config → Sales → Google API
   - Google Analytics settings
   - Google Tag Manager settings (EE — same group as GA)

4. Marketing → SEO & Search → URL Rewrites
   - Audit existing rewrites
   - Create manual rewrites

5. Marketing → SEO & Search → Site Map
   - Generate / view existing sitemaps
```

### Use Categories Path for Product URLs

This setting deserves special attention:

```
Setting: "Use Categories Path for Product URLs"
Path: Stores → Config → Catalog → Catalog → SEO
Field ID: product_use_categories (default: No)

Yes:
  /mens/jackets/breathable-jacket.html
  (changes URL when category changes)

No (default):
  /breathable-jacket.html
  (URL is independent of category structure)
```

**Exam focus:**
- `Use Categories Path for Product URLs = No` is the **default** and is **generally recommended** for SEO stability — product URLs don't change when category structure changes.
- When set to `Yes`, moving a product creates additional redirect chains.

### Checking URL Rewrites via CLI/Database

```bash
# Query directly:
mysql -u root -p magento_db -e "
SELECT 
  url_rewrite_id,
  entity_type,
  request_path,
  target_path,
  redirect_type,
  store_id,
  is_autogenerated
FROM url_rewrite 
WHERE request_path LIKE '%jacket%'
ORDER BY url_rewrite_id DESC
LIMIT 20;
"
```

### Regenerate URL Rewrites

> **Note:** There is **no** `catalog:urls:reindex` CLI command in Magento 2. URL rewrites are generated via event observers in `module-catalog-url-rewrite` (triggered on product/category save). To regenerate all URL rewrites, use the standard indexer:

```bash
# Reindex URL rewrites via the standard indexer
php bin/magento indexer:reindex catalog_url_rewrite
php bin/magento indexer:reindex catalog_category_product

# Flush cache after
php bin/magento cache:flush
```

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Native SEO Features
- [ ] Meta title/description configurable per **product**, **category**, and **CMS page** individually
- [ ] Blank meta title falls back to **entity name** (product name, category name, page title)
- [ ] URL keys auto-generated from name; can be manually edited per entity
- [ ] URL keys must be unique per **store view**
- [ ] Default URL suffix is `.html` for both products and categories
- [ ] URL suffix configured at **store view scope** under Catalog → Catalog → SEO
- [ ] Changing URL key **automatically creates a 301 redirect** (checkbox defaults to enabled)
- [ ] URL rewrites stored in `url_rewrite` database table
- [ ] `redirect_type = 0` = internal transparent rewrite; `301` = permanent redirect
- [ ] Moving a product to different category creates **automatic 301 redirects**
- [ ] Manual URL rewrites created at **Marketing → SEO & Search → URL Rewrites**
- [ ] Canonical URL tags configured under Catalog → Catalog → SEO
- [ ] Canonical tags prevent duplicate content from **multi-category assignments**, **layered navigation filters**, and **configurable product variants**
- [ ] `Use Categories Path for Product URLs = No` (default) recommended for SEO URL stability

### XML Sitemaps
- [ ] Sitemap generated at **Marketing → SEO & Search → Site Map**
- [ ] Includes Products, Categories, and CMS Pages (each configurable)
- [ ] Frequency and priority configurable per entity type; all default to "daily"
- [ ] Max 50,000 URLs per file — large catalogs produce **indexed sitemaps** with multiple files
- [ ] Product images can be included in sitemap (default: All)
- [ ] Cron job `sitemap_generate` handles automated scheduled generation
- [ ] Submit to Google via **Google Search Console** or reference in `robots.txt`

### Hreflang & Multi-Store SEO
- [ ] Magento does **not** natively generate hreflang tags — requires extension or custom module
- [ ] Store View locale set under General → General → Locale Options
- [ ] `hreflang="x-default"` should point to default fallback store
- [ ] Store code in URL is optional (`Add Store Code to Urls` setting)

### Google Analytics
- [ ] GA configured at **Stores → Configuration → Sales → Google API → Google Analytics**
- [ ] CE module: basic GA (Enable, Account Number, Anonymize IP)
- [ ] EE module (google-tag-manager): adds Account Type, GA4, and GTM Container ID support
- [ ] No "Content Experiments" field exists in current AC 2.4.8
- [ ] Enhanced Ecommerce tracks: impressions, clicks, detail views, add/remove cart, checkout, purchase
- [ ] `purchase` event fires on **order success page**

### Google Tag Manager (EE)
- [ ] GTM is in the **same config group** as Google Analytics — not a separate section
- [ ] Account type field switches between UA, GTM, and GA4 modes
- [ ] Uses **Container ID** format: `GTM-XXXXXXX`
- [ ] Data layer `window.dataLayer` passes eCommerce event data to GTM
- [ ] Enabling both native GA and GTM with GA4 tag causes **double tracking**
- [ ] `module-google-tag-manager` is **EE-only** (proprietary license)
- [ ] Key data layer events: `addToCart`, `removeFromCart`, `checkout`, `purchase`, `productDetail`, `productImpression`

### Shopping Feeds
- [ ] Google Shopping feed is **not built into** standard AC admin — requires third-party extension
- [ ] Required feed attributes: `id`, `title`, `description`, `link`, `image_link`, `price`, `availability`
- [ ] Feed format: RSS/XML compliant with Google Merchant Center spec
- [ ] Product attributes must be **mapped** to Google taxonomy fields

### Tricky Exam Scenarios
- [ ] URL key change = **301 redirect auto-created** if checkbox enabled (default YES)
- [ ] Unchecked redirect checkbox on URL key change = old URLs return **404**
- [ ] Configurable product variants without canonical = **duplicate content** risk
- [ ] Layered navigation filter URLs (query strings) need canonical pointing to base category
- [ ] Suffix change regenerates **ALL** URL rewrites — plan for performance impact
- [ ] Double tracking: GTM + native GA both enabled = **inflated analytics data**
- [ ] `Use Categories Path for Product URLs = Yes` → product URL changes when category moves

flashcards.question: What happens when you change a product's URL key in Magento 2 with the redirect checkbox enabled?
flashcards.answer: Magento automatically creates a 301 (permanent) redirect from the old URL to the new URL. The redirect is stored in the url_rewrite database table. The 'Create Permanent Redirect for old URL' checkbox defaults to enabled. If unchecked, no redirect is created and old bookmarks/links return 404.
flashcards.hint: A specific HTTP redirect type is created by default, stored in a specific database table.

flashcards.question: What is the default URL suffix for products and categories in Magento 2, and at what scope is it configured?
flashcards.answer: The default URL suffix is .html for both products and categories. It is configured at Store View scope (showInDefault=1, showInWebsite=1, showInStore=1) under Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Search Engine Optimization. Changing the suffix triggers mass URL rewrite regeneration for ALL affected entities.
flashcards.hint: It is a store-wide setting with a significant impact when changed.

flashcards.question: What does redirect_type = 0 mean in the url_rewrite table?
flashcards.answer: A redirect_type of 0 means it is an internal rewrite (transparent to the user), not an actual HTTP redirect. The URL is rewritten server-side without the browser seeing a redirect. A value of 301 means permanent redirect, and 302 means temporary redirect.
flashcards.hint: Zero does not mean 'no entry' — it means a specific type of URL handling.

flashcards.question: How do canonical URLs help with configurable product variants in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: When 'Use Canonical Link Meta Tag For Products' is enabled, simple product pages that are children of a configurable product will canonicalize back to the parent configurable product URL. This prevents duplicate content penalties from each variant being indexed as a separate page and consolidates link equity.
flashcards.hint: Child product pages point search engines to the parent URL.

flashcards.question: What is the 'Use Categories Path for Product URLs' setting, and what is its default?
flashcards.answer: When set to Yes, product URLs include the category path (e.g., /mens/jackets/product.html). When set to No (the default), product URLs are independent of category structure (e.g., /product.html). No is recommended for SEO stability because product URLs won't change when category structure changes.
flashcards.hint: The default prioritizes URL stability over descriptive category paths.

flashcards.question: What entities are included in an XML Sitemap, and what is the maximum number of URLs per file?
flashcards.answer: XML Sitemaps include Products, Categories, and CMS Pages (each configurable). The maximum is 50,000 URLs per file — larger catalogs produce indexed sitemap files (e.g., sitemap.xml as index, sitemap-1-1.xml for products). Product images can be included in the sitemap (default: All images).
flashcards.hint: There is a specific URL limit per file that triggers automatic splitting.

flashcards.question: Does Magento 2 / Adobe Commerce natively generate hreflang tags for multi-language stores?
flashcards.answer: No, Magento does NOT natively generate hreflang tags — this requires a third-party extension or custom module. The store view locale is set under General > General > Locale Options. The hreflang x-default should point to the default/fallback store view.
flashcards.hint: Multi-language SEO requires something beyond the core platform.

flashcards.question: Where is Google Analytics configured in Adobe Commerce, and what is the key difference between CE and EE?
flashcards.answer: GA is configured at Stores > Configuration > Sales > Google API > Google Analytics. CE has basic GA (Enable, Account Number, Anonymize IP). EE's module-google-tag-manager adds Account Type selector (Universal Analytics, GTM, GA4), GTM Container ID, and enhanced data layer events. GTM integration is EE-only.
flashcards.hint: Both editions share the same config section, but one adds extra account type options.

flashcards.question: What happens if both native Google Analytics and Google Tag Manager with a GA4 tag are enabled simultaneously?
flashcards.answer: This causes double-tracking: every page triggers GA4 twice, resulting in inflated pageview counts, inaccurate purchase event data, and double revenue reported in GA4. The fix is to disable native GA in Magento config and manage GA4 ONLY through GTM.
flashcards.hint: Running two tracking systems simultaneously creates a data accuracy problem.

flashcards.question: Is Google Shopping feed functionality built into the standard Adobe Commerce admin?
flashcards.answer: No, Google Shopping feed functionality is NOT built into the standard Adobe Commerce admin. It requires a third-party extension or custom implementation. The feed format is RSS/XML compliant with Google Merchant Center specifications and requires mapping product attributes to Google taxonomy fields.
flashcards.hint: This capability requires something beyond the core platform.

flashcards.question: What is the data layer (window.dataLayer) in the context of Google Tag Manager, and what eCommerce events does it track?
flashcards.answer: The data layer is a JavaScript array that Magento populates with structured eCommerce event data, which GTM reads and forwards to configured analytics tags. Key events include: productImpression, productDetail, addToCart, removeFromCart, checkout, and purchase. The purchase event fires on the order success page.
flashcards.hint: It is a client-side data structure that acts as a bridge between the store and analytics.

flashcards.question: What is a Search Term Redirect in Magento 2, and how does it differ from search synonyms?
flashcards.answer: A Search Term Redirect sends the user directly to a specific URL when they search a particular term, bypassing the search engine entirely. Synonyms map related terms so they produce the same search results. Redirects are configured under Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Terms.
flashcards.hint: One changes what results are shown; the other takes the user to a completely different page.

flashcards.question: What happens to a blank Meta Title field on a product in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: If Meta Title is left blank on a product, Magento falls back to the product name as the page title. If Meta Description is blank, Magento may auto-generate from the short description (behavior varies by theme). Meta Keywords are supported in the UI but have no ranking impact in modern search engines.
flashcards.hint: There is an automatic fallback to another product attribute.

flashcards.question: Where are manual URL rewrites created in Adobe Commerce, and what fields are required?
flashcards.answer: Manual URL rewrites are created at Marketing > SEO & Search > URL Rewrites > Add URL Rewrite. Required fields include Request Path (the incoming URL), Target Path (the destination URL or internal route), Redirect Type (301 permanent, 302 temporary, or No redirect), Store, and Description.
flashcards.hint: They are under the Marketing menu, not Stores or Content.

flashcards.question: What canonical URL challenges exist with layered navigation in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Layered navigation filter URLs with query strings (e.g., ?color=blue, ?price=50-100, ?p=2) create potential duplicate content issues. When canonical tags are enabled, these filtered pages canonical back to the base category URL, preventing filter parameter pages from being indexed as separate pages by search engines.
flashcards.hint: URL parameters from filtering can multiply the number of indexable pages.

studyNotes.content:
# Adobe Commerce EE vs Open Source & Add-on Services
### Comprehensive Study Notes — Week 2, Jan 23

---

   - [MSI — Multi-Source Inventory](#41-msi--multi-source-inventory)
   - [Page Builder (Free Extension for CE)](#42-page-builder-free-extension-for-ce)
5. [Hosting Options](#5-hosting-options)
   - [Adobe Commerce Cloud Pro](#51-adobe-commerce-cloud-pro)
   - [Cloud Starter](#52-cloud-starter)
   - [On-Premises (Self-Hosted)](#53-on-premises-self-hosted)
6. [SaaS Add-On Services](#6-saas-add-on-services)
   - [Live Search](#61-live-search)
   - [Product Recommendations](#62-product-recommendations)
   - [Payment Services](#63-payment-services)
   - [Catalog Service](#64-catalog-service)
7. [Adobe Commerce as a Service — Headless & Emerging Options](#7-adobe-commerce-as-a-service--headless--emerging-options)
8. [Admin Panel Comparison: EE vs CE](#8-admin-panel-comparison-ee-vs-ce)
9. [Tricky Exam Topics & Common Misconceptions](#9-tricky-exam-topics--common-misconceptions)
10. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Overview: Edition Landscape

Adobe Commerce (formerly Magento) is offered in two primary **code editions** and multiple **deployment/hosting models**.

```
+-----------------------------------------------+
|          Adobe Commerce Ecosystem              |
|                                                |
|  +------------------+  +--------------------+ |
|  | Open Source (CE) |  |  Commerce (EE)     | |
|  | Free / Community |  |  Licensed / Paid   | |
|  +------------------+  +--------------------+ |
|           |                    |               |
|           +--------+-----------+               |
|                    |                           |
|         Deployment / Hosting Options           |
|   +----------+  +-----------+  +-----------+  |
|   |  Cloud   |  |  Cloud    |  | On-Prem   |  |
|   |   Pro    |  |  Starter  |  | Self-Host |  |
|   +----------+  +-----------+  +-----------+  |
|                                                |
|     SaaS Add-Ons (available to both editions) |
|   Live Search | Product Recs | Payment Svcs   |
|   Catalog Service                              |
+-----------------------------------------------+
```

### Key Terminology

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **CE** | Community Edition / Open Source — free, no license fee |
| **EE** | Enterprise Edition / Adobe Commerce — paid license, feature-rich |
| **Cloud Pro** | Adobe-managed hosting on AWS/Azure, high availability |
| **Cloud Starter** | Lighter Adobe-managed hosting, lower cost |
| **SaaS Add-ons** | Services delivered via Adobe's SaaS infrastructure, connected via API keys |
| **B2B Suite** | B2B module set included with EE — business-to-business selling features |

> **Exam focus:** Adobe Commerce EE and CE share the same core codebase. EE adds features via licensed modules on top of the base platform. CE is **not** a "stripped-down" version — it is fully functional for B2C.

---

## 2. Feature Comparison Matrix

This is the most exam-critical table. Study every row.

| Feature | Open Source (CE) | Commerce (EE) | Notes |
|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| Standard Catalog & Cart | ✅ | ✅ | Core platform |
| CMS Pages & Blocks | ✅ | ✅ | Core platform |
| Page Builder | ✅ (ext.) | ✅ (native) | EE ships it out-of-box; CE installs free extension |
| Multi-Source Inventory (MSI) | ✅ | ✅ | Included in both since 2.3 |
| Live Search (SaaS) | ✅ (SaaS add-on) | ✅ (SaaS add-on) | License key required; works with both |
| Product Recommendations | ✅ (SaaS add-on) | ✅ (SaaS add-on) | Sensei AI powered |
| Content Staging & Preview | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| B2B Suite | ❌ | ✅ | Requires EE license; B2B modules ship with EE |
| Customer Segments | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| Related Product Rules | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| Gift Cards | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| Gift Wrapping | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| Reward Points | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| Store Credit | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| RMA (Returns) | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| Visual Merchandiser | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| Catalog Permissions | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| Advanced Reporting | ✅ | ✅ | module-analytics is CE (OSL-3.0); Reports > Business Intelligence menu exists in both editions. Full Adobe Commerce Intelligence (MBI) is a separate paid service. |
| Async Order Management | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| Scheduled Import/Export | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| Targeted Promotions (Segments) | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| Private Sales / Invitations | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only |
| Google Tag Manager (built-in) | ❌ | ✅ | EE-only native integration |
| Payment Services (SaaS) | ✅ (SaaS add-on) | ✅ (SaaS add-on) | Works with both editions |
| Catalog Service (SaaS) | ✅ (SaaS add-on) | ✅ (SaaS add-on) | Works with both editions |

> **Exam focus:** MSI is available in **both** CE and EE. This is one of the most common trick questions. Do not confuse "multi-store" (both) with "multi-source inventory" (both) — neither is EE-only.

> **Exam focus:** Live Search is a **SaaS add-on** — it is available to **both** CE and EE merchants who subscribe to it. It is not exclusive to EE.

---

## 3. EE-Exclusive Features Deep Dive

### 3.1 Content Staging & Preview

**What it is:** A native workflow for scheduling changes to content, products, categories, promotions, CMS pages, and blocks — with a visual timeline and preview capability.

```
Content Staging Timeline (EE Only)
------------------------------------
Jan 1          Jan 15         Feb 1
  |                |             |
  +---[Campaign A]-+             |
  |    (active)                  |
  +-----------------------------[Campaign B]-->
  |              |
  [Preview at any future date]
```

**Key capabilities:**
- Create *campaigns* that group content changes together
- Schedule start and end dates for campaigns
- Preview storefront as it will look at any future date/time
- Roll back or modify campaigns without touching live content

**Staging-aware entities:**
- Products (price, name, images)
- Categories (name, description, assignment)
- CMS Pages and Blocks
- Cart Price Rules
- Catalog Price Rules
- Dynamic Blocks (module-banner-staging)

> **Exam focus:** Content Staging is **EE-only**. CE has no native staging mechanism. The staging dashboard is accessed at **Content > Content Staging > Dashboard** (module-staging/etc/adminhtml/menu.xml).

> **Exam focus:** Content Staging operates on a *timeline* model. Each scheduled campaign creates a *snapshot* of entity state. Overlapping campaigns are merged, with later campaigns having higher priority.

### 3.2 B2B Suite

The B2B Suite is a **module set included with Adobe Commerce EE**, providing features for manufacturer → distributor → retailer selling models. B2B modules ship in the EE codebase and are enabled via Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features (section=btob).

**Core B2B modules and features:**

| B2B Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| **Company Accounts** | Single parent company account with child buyer accounts, roles & permissions |
| **Shared Catalogs** | Custom catalogs with custom pricing per company |
| **Quick Order** | Order by SKU list or CSV upload |
| **Requisition Lists** | Saved shopping lists (like wishlists for B2B) |
| **Purchase Orders** | Formal PO workflow with approval rules |
| **Payment on Account** | Net 30/60/90 payment terms |
| **Negotiated Quotes** | Sales rep ↔ buyer quote negotiation workflow |
| **Company Credit** | Credit limits and balance tracking per company |

```
B2B Company Hierarchy (EE + B2B Module)
-----------------------------------------
Company Account (Admin)
  |
  +-- Division A (Sub-unit)
  |     +-- Buyer 1 (Purchaser role)
  |     +-- Buyer 2 (Viewer role)
  |
  +-- Division B (Sub-unit)
        +-- Buyer 3 (Manager role)
        +-- Buyer 4 (Purchaser role)
```

> **Exam focus:** B2B modules are included in the Adobe Commerce (EE) codebase. They are enabled via configuration at Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features. Each feature (Company Accounts, Shared Catalogs, Negotiable Quotes, Quick Order, Requisition Lists) has its own enable toggle. CE cannot use B2B Suite.

> **Exam focus:** **Shared Catalogs** are a B2B Suite feature (EE). They allow different product catalogs and tier pricing for each company. The default public catalog still exists for guest/non-company customers.

> **Exam focus:** **Negotiated Quotes** is the B2B feature that enables a sales rep to modify pricing during checkout negotiation. This is distinct from standard cart price rules.

### 3.3 Customer Segments & Related Product Rules

**Customer Segments (EE-only)**

Dynamically group customers based on real-time conditions:

```php
// Example segment conditions (configured in Admin, not code):
// Customer Segment: "VIP Shoppers"
// Condition: 
//   - Customer Group = "Wholesale"
//   - Total Orders >= 10
//   - Total Spent >= $5000
//   - Last Order <= 90 days ago
```

**What segments power:**
- Targeted banner displays
- Cart price rules (apply only to segment)
- Related product rules
- Private sales access
- Content personalization

**Related Product Rules (EE-only)**

Automate the display of Related Products, Up-sells, and Cross-sells on product pages using rule-based conditions instead of manual assignment.

```
Rule: "Electronics Cross-Sell"
  IF product attribute: Category = "Laptops"
  THEN show products where: Category = "Laptop Accessories"
  AND: Price <= current product price * 0.5
  Sort by: Newest first
  Display position: Cross-sells
```

> **Exam focus:** CE has *manual* related products, up-sells, and cross-sells — an admin manually assigns them per product. EE has **Related Product Rules** that automate this via conditions. This is a key CE vs EE distinction.

> **Exam focus:** Customer Segments are **real-time** — they evaluate conditions dynamically at the time of the customer's visit, not batch-processed. A customer can enter/leave a segment mid-session.

### 3.4 Gift Cards, Wrapping, Reward Points & Store Credit

All four of these are **EE-exclusive loyalty and gifting features**.

#### Gift Cards (EE-only)

Three types of gift cards:

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| **Virtual** | Delivered by email only; no physical product |
| **Physical** | Shipped as a physical card; code printed/included |
| **Combined** | Both email delivery and physical shipping |

- Gift card amounts can be fixed or customer-defined (within min/max bounds)
- Gift card codes are stored in the gift card account pool
- Can be used as partial or full payment

> **Exam focus:** Gift Cards are a **product type** in EE (like Simple, Configurable, etc.). They appear as a separate product type in the catalog.

#### Gift Wrapping (EE-only)

- Offered at checkout for individual items or the entire order
- Multiple gift wrapping designs with separate prices
- Can include gift receipts and printed gift messages
- Configurable per website (showInDefault=1, showInWebsite=1, showInStore=0)

#### Reward Points (EE-only)

```
Reward Points Flow:
  Purchase -> Earn Points -> Points Balance
                                  |
                            Spend at Checkout
                                  |
                         Discount Applied
```

- Configurable earn/spend rates per store (e.g., $1 spent = 10 points; 100 points = $1 discount)
- Points can expire (configurable expiry period)
- Admins can manually adjust point balances
- Restrictions: min/max points per order, max discount percentage

> **Exam focus:** Reward Points require a customer to be **logged in** — they are tied to customer accounts, not guest sessions.

#### Store Credit (EE-only)

- Manual or automated credit applied to customer accounts
- Used for refunds-as-credit instead of payment reversals
- Configurable whether customers can use store credit at checkout
- Admins can add/subtract credit manually
- Distinct from Gift Cards — Store Credit is account-based, Gift Cards are code-based

> **Exam focus:** **Store Credit** (EE) ≠ **Gift Cards** (EE). Store Credit is tied to a customer account; Gift Cards use redemption codes and can be given to anyone. Both are EE-only.

### 3.5 Page Builder (Native)

Page Builder is Adobe Commerce's drag-and-drop content editor for CMS Pages, CMS Blocks, Category descriptions, and Product descriptions.

**Native in EE** — ships out-of-the-box with zero installation required.

```
Page Builder Content Types:
+----------------------------+
| Layout                     |
|  - Row                     |
|  - Column                  |
|  - Tab                     |
+----------------------------+
| Elements                   |
|  - Text                    |
|  - Heading                 |
|  - Buttons                 |
|  - Divider                 |
|  - HTML Code               |
+----------------------------+
| Media                      |
|  - Image                   |
|  - Video                   |
|  - Banner                  |
|  - Slider                  |
|  - Map                     |
+----------------------------+
| Add Content                |
|  - Block                   |
|  - Dynamic Block           |
|  - Products                |
+----------------------------+
```

> **Exam focus:** **Dynamic Blocks** in Page Builder (EE) can be targeted to **Customer Segments** — they display different content to different customer segments. This is an EE+Page Builder combination feature. CE's Page Builder extension does not have Dynamic Blocks or Segment targeting.

### 3.6 Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA)

EE provides a built-in RMA workflow for managing product returns.

```
RMA Workflow:
  Customer Request --> Admin Review --> Authorize/Reject
        |                                    |
        v                                    v
  Return Label              [Authorized] -- Items Received
  Generated                                  |
                                     Refund / Exchange
                                     Store Credit / Repair
```

**Key RMA features:**
- Customers submit return requests from their account dashboard
- Admin can authorize, partially authorize, or reject
- Multiple RMA attributes configurable (reason, condition, resolution)
- Return shipping label integration
- Each authorized return generates an RMA number

> **Exam focus:** RMA in EE is **not the same** as issuing a credit memo (which CE can do). CE can process refunds via credit memos on orders but has no formal *return request workflow* for customers. RMA is the structured workflow.

### 3.7 Visual Merchandiser

A drag-and-drop tool within the **Category admin page** (EE-only) that allows merchandisers to control the display order of products in a category. Visual Merchandiser does **not** have its own admin menu item — it is embedded within category edit pages.

**Key capabilities:**
- Drag products into exact position order
- Pin specific products to always appear at top
- Auto-sort by rules: price, new arrivals, revenue, quantity, etc.
- See product thumbnails while sorting (visual grid)
- Smart Category rules: automatically add products matching attribute conditions

```

| $29.99|  | $49.99|  | $19.99|
|  PIN  |  |       |  |       |
+-------+  +-------+  +-------+
+-------+  +-------+  +-------+
|  [P4] |  |  [P5] |  |  [P6] |
| $99.99|  | $14.99|  | $39.99|
+-------+  +-------+  +-------+

[Add Products by Rule: Sort by "Price: High to Low"]
```

> **Exam focus:** Visual Merchandiser is found at **Catalog > Categories > [Select Category] > Products in Category** tab — it's embedded in the category edit page, not a separate admin section. There is no standalone "Visual Merchandiser" menu item in the Catalog menu.

> **Exam focus:** Visual Merchandiser configuration is at **Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Visual Merchandiser** (section=visualmerchandiser, tab=catalog). Settings include visible attributes for category rules, minimum stock threshold, and color attribute configuration.

> **Exam focus:** The **"Smart Category"** functionality (auto-populate category by attribute rules) is part of Visual Merchandiser (EE-only). CE requires manual product-to-category assignment only.

### 3.8 Catalog Permissions

Allows restricting catalog access (categories and products) based on **Customer Group**.

```
Permission Matrix Example:
                    | Guest | General | Wholesale | VIP |
--------------------|-------|---------|-----------|-----|
Category: "Public"  |  YES  |   YES   |    YES    | YES |
Category: "Trade"   |  NO   |   NO    |    YES    | YES |
Category: "VIP Only"|  NO   |   NO    |    NO     | YES |
Product Prices      | HIDE  |  SHOW   |    SHOW   |SHOW |
```

**Configuration:**
- Enabled globally at Stores > Configuration > Catalog > **Category Permissions** (the config group label is "Category Permissions", not "Catalog Permissions" — section=catalog, group=magento_catalogpermissions)
- Set per-category (overriding global defaults)
- Can hide categories entirely, show without prices, or show fully
- Can redirect restricted visitors to a login page or custom CMS page

> **Important:** When enabling Category Permissions, a warning is displayed: "By default this feature restricts all categories." You must explicitly configure permissions per category or set global defaults to avoid accidentally locking out all visitors.

> **Exam focus:** Catalog Permissions (EE) restrict by **Customer Group**, not by individual customer. B2B Shared Catalogs (EE + B2B) take this further by providing entirely separate product and pricing catalogs per company.

> **Exam focus:** When Catalog Permissions restricts a category, that category is also **removed from navigation menus** and **search results** for unauthorized groups — not just blocked when accessed directly.

### 3.9 Advanced Reporting

Adobe Commerce provides **Advanced Reporting** via the module-analytics module (Reports > Business Intelligence menu).

**Report categories:**
- **Products reports:** Best sellers, ordered quantities, low stock
- **Sales reports:** Orders, tax, invoiced, shipped, refunded, coupons
- **Customer reports:** Order totals, order counts, new vs. returning
- **Marketing:** Shopping cart abandonment, search terms

**Reports > Business Intelligence menu** (module-analytics):
- Advanced Reporting — opens external reporting dashboard
- BI Essentials — signup for full Commerce Intelligence service

> **Important correction:** The module-analytics module that provides the Reports > Business Intelligence menu is licensed as **OSL-3.0 (Open Source)**, meaning the Advanced Reporting menu and basic BI integration are available in **both CE and EE**. The full **Adobe Commerce Intelligence (MBI)** platform with advanced dashboards, data warehousing, and custom reporting is a separate paid service.

> **Exam focus:** Standard reports (Orders, Sales, Customers, Catalog) are available in **both CE and EE**. The Advanced Reporting menu (Reports > Business Intelligence > Advanced Reporting) is also in both editions. The distinction is that the full Commerce Intelligence (MBI) data warehouse service is a separate paid offering.

### 3.10 Async Order Management

For high-traffic EE merchants, Adobe Commerce EE supports **asynchronous order placement**.

```
Synchronous (CE default):
  Customer Checkout -> Order Processing -> DB Write -> Confirmation
  [Customer waits for all steps to complete]

Asynchronous (EE):
  Customer Checkout -> Queue Entry -> Confirmation
                            |
                    [Background Worker]
                            |
                    Order Processing -> DB Write
  [Customer gets instant confirmation; processing is queued]
```

**Technical implementation:**
- Uses **Message Queue Framework** (RabbitMQ or MySQL-based)
- Async APIs: `POST /async/V1/orders`
- Reduces checkout response time under load
- Requires message queue consumer processes running

```bash
# Start the async order consumer (example)
php bin/magento queue:consumers:start placeOrderProcessor
```

> **Exam focus:** Async Order is part of the **Bulk API / Async API** feature set in EE. CE does not include async order processing natively. The async APIs use the prefix `/async/` or `/bulk/` in REST endpoints.

## 4. Shared Features: What CE Also Gets

### 4.1 MSI — Multi-Source Inventory

**Critical exam topic:** MSI is available in **both CE and EE** since Adobe Commerce / Magento Open Source 2.3.

```
MSI Architecture:
+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
|   Source 1       |     |   Source 2       |     |   Source 3       |
|  (Warehouse LA)  |     |  (Warehouse NY)  |     |  (Store London)  |
|  Stock: 50 units |     |  Stock: 30 units |     |  Stock: 20 units |
+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
         \                       |                        /
          \                      v                       /
           +-----------> Stock (Pool) <----------------+
                         (Total: 100)
                              |
                    Sales Channel Assignments
                         /         \
                        v           v
                 Website 1      Website 2
```

**Key MSI concepts:**

| Concept | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Source** | Physical location holding inventory (warehouse, store, dropshipper) |
| **Stock** | Aggregated pool of sources; assigned to sales channels (websites) |
| **Source Item** | The quantity of a specific SKU at a specific source |
| **Salable Quantity** | Total available quantity minus reservations |
| **Reservation** | Quantity held during checkout (before order placement) |
| **Source Selection Algorithm (SSA)** | Logic for which source fulfills an order |

**Available SSAs:**
- `Distance Priority` — ships from nearest source to customer
- `Source Priority` — ships from sources in configured priority order

> **Exam focus:** MSI **is available in both CE and EE**. This is a top trick question. Many candidates assume advanced inventory is EE-only. MSI has been in Open Source since 2.3.

> **Exam focus:** The **Default Stock** and **Default Source** cannot be deleted in MSI. They serve as fallback for merchants who haven't configured multi-source. Simple/virtual products on single-source use the default source.

```bash
php bin/magento setup:upgrade
```

## 5. Hosting Options

### 5.1 Adobe Commerce Cloud Pro

The premium, enterprise-grade Adobe-managed hosting solution built on **AWS and Azure**. Adobe Commerce Cloud is available for **Adobe Commerce (EE) only** — Magento Open Source (CE) cannot be deployed on Adobe Commerce Cloud.

```
Cloud Pro Architecture:
+=============================================+
|            PRODUCTION CLUSTER              |
|  +----------+  +----------+  +----------+ |
|  | Web Node |  | Web Node |  | Web Node | |  <- Auto-scaling
|  +----------+  +----------+  +----------+ |
|       |              |              |      |
|  +----------------------------------------+|
|  |          Load Balancer (Fastly CDN)    ||
|  +----------------------------------------+|
|  +----------+  +----------+               |
|  | DB Master|  | DB Slave |               |  <- MySQL HA
|  +----------+  +----------+               |
|  +----------+  +----------+               |
|  | Redis    |  |Elastic   |               |
|  | (Cache)  |  |Search    |               |
|  +----------+  +----------+               |
+=============================================+
         |
+=============================================+
|           STAGING CLUSTER                  |
|  (Mirror of production, isolated)          |
+=============================================+
         |
+=============================================+
|      INTEGRATION ENVIRONMENTS (x3)         |
|  (Development branches, smaller footprint) |
+=============================================+
```

**Cloud Pro key specs:**

| Component | Detail |
|---|---|
| **CDN** | Fastly (included, configurable) |
| **Search** | Elasticsearch / OpenSearch |
| **Cache** | Redis (session + full-page cache) |
| **DB** | MySQL with Master/Slave replication |
| **Environments** | Production + Staging + 3 Integration |
| **Deployment** | Git-based CI/CD via Adobe Cloud CLI |
| **SLA** | 99.99% uptime for production |
| **Scaling** | Vertical (resize) and horizontal (add nodes) |
| **WAF** | Included (Fastly WAF) |
| **DDoS** | Fastly DDoS protection included |

> **Exam focus:** Cloud Pro includes a **dedicated Staging environment** that mirrors production — this is separate from development Integration environments. Staging is for QA and UAT before production deploy.

> **Exam focus:** The deployment workflow in Cloud Pro is **Git-push-to-deploy**. Developers push to a branch, which triggers a build pipeline. The `master`/`production` branch deploys to production.

```bash
# Cloud CLI deployment workflow (example)
magento-cloud environment:push
magento-cloud environment:merge staging
magento-cloud environment:deploy
```

### 5.2 Cloud Starter

A more affordable, simpler Adobe-managed hosting tier. Like Cloud Pro, it is available for **Adobe Commerce (EE) only**.

**Cloud Starter vs Cloud Pro:**

| Aspect | Cloud Starter | Cloud Pro |
|---|---|---|
| **Architecture** | Single-cluster, shared | Multi-cluster, dedicated |
| **Environments** | Master + 3 branches | Prod + Staging + 3 Integration |
| **Dedicated Staging** | ❌ (branches only) | ✅ (dedicated cluster) |
| **Auto-scaling** | Limited | Full horizontal scaling |
| **SLA** | Lower | 99.99% |
| **Target merchant** | SMB, lower traffic | Mid-market to Enterprise |
| **Price** | Lower | Higher |
| **HA** | Basic | Full HA |

> **Exam focus:** Cloud **Starter** does **NOT** have a dedicated staging cluster. It uses branch environments (similar to integration environments in Pro) for staging. Cloud **Pro** has a proper dedicated staging cluster.

### 5.3 On-Premises (Self-Hosted)

Merchants deploy and manage Adobe Commerce themselves on their own infrastructure or chosen cloud provider (AWS, Azure, GCP — not managed by Adobe). This is the **only deployment option for Magento Open Source (CE)**.

**Installation methods:**

```bash
# Composer installation (recommended)
composer create-project --repository-url=https://repo.magento.com/ \
    magento/project-enterprise-edition <install-dir>

# Setup via CLI
php bin/magento setup:install \
    --db-host=localhost \
    --db-name=magento \
    --db-user=magento \
    --db-password=secret \
    --admin-email=admin@example.com \
    --admin-user=admin \
    --admin-password=Admin@123 \
    --base-url=https://example.com/ \
    --backend-frontname=admin
```

**Merchant responsibilities in on-premises:**
- Server provisioning and scaling
- Security patching (OS, PHP, MySQL)
- SSL certificate management
- Backup strategy
- CDN configuration
- Performance tuning
- Elasticsearch/OpenSearch setup

> **Exam focus:** On-premises merchants must manage their own **security patches** and **version upgrades**. Adobe Commerce Cloud (Pro/Starter) handles infrastructure security but merchants still apply application patches.

## 6. SaaS Add-On Services

SaaS services are **separate from the Adobe Commerce application** — they run on Adobe's infrastructure and connect to any edition (CE or EE) via **API keys and module installation**.

```
SaaS Add-On Architecture:
+---------------------------+         +---------------------------+
| Adobe Commerce Store      |  <--->  | Adobe SaaS Infrastructure |
| (CE or EE, any hosting)   |  API    | - Live Search             |
|                           |  Keys   | - Product Recommendations |
| Installed connector       |         | - Catalog Service         |
| modules                   |         | - Payment Services        |
+---------------------------+         +---------------------------+
                                      Data synced via:
                                      - SaaS Data Export module
                                      - Catalog sync (product data)
```

### 6.1 Live Search

A **SaaS-based search replacement** for the native Elasticsearch/OpenSearch search in Adobe Commerce.

**Key features:**

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| **Instant search popover** | Real-time results as user types (no page reload) |
| **Faceted filtering** | AI-ranked facets in search results |
| **Synonyms management** | Admin-managed via SaaS dashboard |
| **Search rules** | Pin/boost/bury products in search results |
| **Query expansion** | Handles misspellings, partial matches |
| **GraphQL API** | Search powered via GraphQL queries |
| **Analytics** | Search term analytics, zero-result tracking |

```
Live Search Architecture:
  Storefront -> GraphQL -> Adobe SaaS (Live Search) -> Indexed Results
                                   ^
                                   |
                          Product Data Sync
                          (catalog export cron)
```

**Installation:**

Live Search is a SaaS add-on that is **not bundled in the base EE codebase**. It requires a separate Composer package installation and SaaS subscription. API keys are configured at Stores > Configuration > Services > Commerce Services Connector (section=services_connector, tab=service).

> **Exam focus:** Live Search **replaces** the Elasticsearch-based search entirely. It uses **GraphQL** on the frontend, not standard PHP search adapters. If Live Search is enabled, native search is disabled.

> **Exam focus:** Live Search is available for **both CE and EE** merchants — it is a SaaS subscription, not an EE-exclusive feature. However, it does require a paid SaaS subscription.

> **Exam focus:** Live Search product data is synced to Adobe's SaaS via the **SaaS Data Export** module and catalog sync jobs. There is a delay between product changes and search index updates (near real-time, not instant).

### 6.2 Product Recommendations

AI-powered product recommendation widgets driven by **Adobe Sensei** (Adobe's AI/ML framework).

**Recommendation types:**

| Type | Logic |
|---|---|
| `recommended-for-you` | Based on shopper's browsing/purchase history |
| `most-viewed` | Most viewed products site-wide |
| `most-purchased` | Best sellers |
| `most-added-to-cart` | Most added to cart |
| `viewed-viewed` | "Customers who viewed this also viewed" |
| `viewed-bought` | "Customers who viewed this also bought" |
| `bought-bought` | "Customers who bought this also bought" |
| `more-like-this` | Similar products by attributes |
| `visual-similarity` | Visually similar products (image AI) |
| `trending` | Rising popularity |

**Placement locations:** Home page, category pages, product pages, cart page, checkout page, order confirmation page.

> **Exam focus:** Product Recommendations require **behavioral data** to be effective. A new store with no history will use fallback logic (popularity-based) until enough data is collected. Adobe recommends 1,000+ events before AI recommendations activate.

> **Exam focus:** Product Recommendations uses the same **SaaS Data Export** and **Commerce Services Connector** as Live Search. Both are configured with the same API keys.

### 6.3 Payment Services

Adobe's own **payment gateway SaaS**, built on PayPal's infrastructure but delivered as an Adobe-branded service.

**Key features:**
- Hosted payment fields (PCI-compliant, no card data on merchant server)
- Apple Pay / Google Pay / Venmo
- Credit/debit card payments
- PayPal payment options (Pay Later, PayPal Credit)
- Order management within Adobe Commerce Admin (no PayPal dashboard needed)
- Financial reporting built into Commerce Admin
- Sandbox testing environment

```
Payment Services Flow:
  Customer -> Hosted Fields (iFrame) -> Adobe Payment Services SaaS
                                                  |
                                         PayPal Processing
                                                  |
                                       Settlement to Merchant
                                                  |
                                   Reports in Commerce Admin
```

> **Exam focus:** Payment Services is available for **both CE and EE**. It is a SaaS subscription service, not EE-exclusive. It competes with (and can replace) third-party payment extensions.

### 6.4 Catalog Service

A **high-performance read-only catalog API** (GraphQL) optimized for storefront product display — separate from the core Commerce GraphQL API.

**Why it exists:**
- Core Commerce GraphQL calls the database synchronously — slower under load
- Catalog Service pre-indexes data into an optimized SaaS data store
- Returns product data faster for headless/PWA storefronts

**Data served:**
- Product details (name, price, images, attributes)
- Product variants (configurable options)
- Category data
- Pricing (including complex tier pricing)

```graphql
# Catalog Service GraphQL query (example)
query GetProducts {
  products(skus: ["SKU-001", "SKU-002"]) {
    sku
    name
    prices {
      regular { amount currency }
      final { amount currency }
    }
    images { url label }
  }
}
```

> **Exam focus:** Catalog Service is designed for **headless storefronts** and **PWA Studio** deployments where performance is critical. It is NOT a replacement for the admin catalog management — it is a *read-only* storefront data API.

Adobe is actively evolving Commerce toward a **composable commerce / headless** architecture.

```
Traditional (Monolithic):
  +------------------------------------------+
  |  Adobe Commerce (PHP Application)         |
  |  Frontend (Luma theme) + Backend + APIs   |
  +------------------------------------------+

Headless / Composable:
  +------------------+    +-----------------+

         |                         |
         v                         v
  +------------------+    +-----------------+
  | SaaS Services    |    | SaaS Services   |
  | - Live Search    |    | - Catalog Svc   |
  | - Product Recs   |    | - Payment Svcs  |
  +------------------+    +-----------------+
```

**Key headless/composable technologies:**

> **Exam focus:** Adobe's direction is toward **SaaS/composable commerce** where even the Commerce backend becomes a managed service. "Commerce as a Service" is an evolving/emerging positioning — expect exam questions about the *direction* not specific GA features.

> **Exam focus:** **PWA Studio** produces a **Progressive Web App** storefront that consumes Commerce's GraphQL API. It is separate from the Luma/Blank themes and requires separate build/deployment. It is compatible with both CE and EE.

## 9. Tricky Exam Topics & Common Misconceptions

### Misconception Summary Table

| Misconception | Reality |
|---|---|
| "MSI is EE-only" | ❌ **MSI is in both CE and EE** since 2.3 |
| "Page Builder requires EE" | ❌ **CE can install Page Builder as a free extension**; EE ships it natively |
| "Live Search is EE-only" | ❌ **Live Search is a SaaS add-on** available to both CE and EE |
| "Product Recommendations is EE-only" | ❌ **SaaS add-on**, available to both |
| "Advanced Reporting is EE-only" | ❌ **module-analytics is CE (OSL-3.0)**; the Reports > Business Intelligence menu exists in both editions. Full Adobe Commerce Intelligence (MBI) is a separate paid service |
| "Cloud Starter runs CE" | ❌ **Both Cloud Pro and Cloud Starter are for Adobe Commerce (EE) only**. They are deployment tiers, not edition-specific. CE runs on self-hosted infrastructure only |
| "Catalog Permissions = Shared Catalogs" | ❌ **Catalog Permissions** (EE) restricts category access by customer group; **Shared Catalogs** (EE + B2B) provides entirely separate product/price catalogs per company |
| "Store Credit = Gift Cards" | ❌ **Store Credit** is account-tied; **Gift Cards** use redemption codes. Both are EE-only but different features |
| "Async Order works via admin" | ❌ **Async Order** is an API-level feature for developers; it uses the `/async/` REST endpoint prefix, not the admin |

### Edition Decision Quick Rules

```
Ask: "Does this feature personalize by customer/segment?"
  YES -> Likely EE (Segments, Related Product Rules, Dynamic Blocks, Catalog Permissions)

Ask: "Does this feature manage a complex B2B workflow?"
  YES -> Likely EE + B2B (Quotes, POs, Company Accounts, Shared Catalogs)

Ask: "Does this feature involve loyalty/gifting?"
  YES -> Likely EE (Reward Points, Store Credit, Gift Cards, Gift Wrapping)

Ask: "Does this feature manage returns formally?"
  YES -> EE (RMA)

Ask: "Does this feature schedule/preview future content?"
  YES -> EE (Content Staging)

Ask: "Does this feature use AI-powered search or recommendations?"
  -> SaaS Add-On (Live Search, Product Recommendations) - available to both editions

Ask: "Does this feature manage inventory across locations?"
  -> MSI - available to BOTH editions
```
