- [ ] **Product Recommendations** — SaaS add-on (Sensei AI), works with CE and EE
- [ ] **Payment Services** — SaaS add-on, works with CE and EE
- [ ] **Catalog Service** — SaaS add-on, works with CE and EE
- [ ] **Standard Reports** — Sales, Customer, Catalog reports in both editions
- [ ] **Advanced Reporting (Reports > Business Intelligence)** — module-analytics is CE; full Commerce Intelligence (MBI) is separate paid service
- [ ] **PWA Studio / GraphQL** — works with both editions
- [ ] **Cart and Catalog Price Rules** — both editions
- [ ] **Customer Groups** — both editions

### Hosting Models
- [ ] **Cloud Pro** — Adobe-managed (EE only), HA, dedicated Staging + Production clusters, Fastly CDN, 99.99% SLA
- [ ] **Cloud Starter** — Adobe-managed (EE only), simpler, no dedicated staging, branch environments, lower cost
- [ ] **On-Premises** — self-managed, both CE and EE, merchant responsible for infrastructure, security, scaling

### Cloud Pro Key Facts
- [ ] Environments: Production + Staging + 3 Integration environments
- [ ] Deploy via Git push (branch-based CI/CD)
- [ ] Includes Fastly CDN, Redis, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, MySQL HA
- [ ] Staging is a **separate dedicated cluster** (mirrors production)
- [ ] Auto-scaling supported (horizontal node addition)

### SaaS Add-Ons — Key Facts
- [ ] Connected via **Commerce Services Connector** (API key pair: production + sandbox, configured at Stores > Configuration > Services > Commerce Services Connector)
- [ ] Data sync via **SaaS Data Export** modules (cron-based catalog sync)
- [ ] **Live Search** — replaces native search; uses GraphQL; requires catalog sync delay
- [ ] **Product Recommendations** — needs behavioral event data; uses Adobe Sensei AI
- [ ] **Catalog Service** — read-only GraphQL API optimized for headless storefronts
- [ ] **Payment Services** — hosted fields (PCI); PayPal infrastructure; financial reporting in Admin

### Key Distinctions to Know for Exam
- [ ] **MSI ≠ EE-only** (top trick question)
- [ ] **Live Search ≠ EE-only** (SaaS subscription, available to CE)
- [ ] **Advanced Reporting ≠ EE-only** (module-analytics is CE; full MBI is separate paid service)
- [ ] **Catalog Permissions ≠ Shared Catalogs** (EE vs EE + B2B)
- [ ] **Store Credit ≠ Gift Cards** (both EE, but different mechanisms)
- [ ] **Cloud Pro and Starter ≠ CE hosting** (both are EE-only deployment tiers)
- [ ] **Page Builder CE extension ≠ EE native** (CE lacks Dynamic Blocks, Segments, Staging integration)
- [ ] **Visual Merchandiser location**: Catalog > Categories > [Category] > Products in Category tab (no standalone menu item)
- [ ] **Content Staging location**: Content > Content Staging > Dashboard
- [ ] **Customer Segments location**: Customers > Segments (NOT Marketing)
- [ ] **Dynamic Blocks location**: Content > Elements > Dynamic Blocks (NOT Marketing > Banners)
- [ ] **Email Reminders location**: Marketing > Communications > Email Reminders

flashcards.question: Is Multi-Source Inventory (MSI) an EE-exclusive feature?
flashcards.answer: No, MSI is available in BOTH CE (Open Source) and EE since Magento 2.3. This is one of the most common trick questions on the exam. MSI includes Sources (physical locations), Stocks (aggregated pools assigned to websites), Reservations, and Source Selection Algorithms (Distance Priority and Source Priority).
flashcards.hint: An advanced inventory feature that many candidates incorrectly assume is EE-only.

flashcards.question: What is Content Staging & Preview in Adobe Commerce EE?
flashcards.answer: Content Staging is an EE-only workflow for scheduling changes to products, categories, CMS pages/blocks, cart/catalog price rules, and dynamic blocks. It uses a timeline model with campaigns that have start/end dates. You can preview the storefront at any future date. Overlapping campaigns are merged with later campaigns having higher priority.
flashcards.hint: It provides a future-dated preview capability for multiple entity types.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Catalog Permissions (EE) and Shared Catalogs (B2B)?
flashcards.answer: Catalog Permissions restrict category/product visibility by Customer Group (hide categories, show without prices, or show fully). Shared Catalogs (EE + B2B) provide entirely separate product catalogs with custom pricing per company. Catalog Permissions work at the group level; Shared Catalogs work at the company level.
flashcards.hint: One restricts visibility; the other creates entirely separate product/price experiences.

flashcards.question: Is Live Search exclusive to Adobe Commerce EE?
flashcards.answer: No, Live Search is a SaaS add-on available to BOTH CE and EE merchants who subscribe to it. It replaces the native Elasticsearch/OpenSearch search entirely, uses GraphQL on the frontend, and is powered by Adobe Sensei AI. Product data is synced via the SaaS Data Export module. You cannot run both Live Search and native search simultaneously.
flashcards.hint: It is a subscription service, not an edition-locked feature.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Cloud Pro and Cloud Starter hosting for Adobe Commerce?
flashcards.answer: Cloud Pro has dedicated Production and Staging clusters with full HA, auto-scaling, 99.99% SLA, and 3 integration environments. Cloud Starter has no dedicated staging cluster (uses branch environments), limited scaling, and a lower SLA. Both are EE-only — CE/Open Source cannot be deployed on Adobe Commerce Cloud.
flashcards.hint: One has a true separate staging cluster; the other simulates it with branches.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between RMA (Returns) in EE and Credit Memos in CE?
flashcards.answer: RMA in EE provides a structured return request workflow where customers submit return requests from their account, admin can authorize/reject, and return shipping labels can be generated. CE can only process refunds via credit memos on orders but has no formal customer-facing return request workflow.
flashcards.hint: One is a customer-facing workflow; the other is an admin-only refund process.

flashcards.question: How does Page Builder availability differ between CE and EE?
flashcards.answer: EE ships Page Builder natively with zero installation required. CE can install it as a free Composer package (magento/module-page-builder). However, the CE version lacks Dynamic Blocks, Customer Segment targeting, and Content Staging integration — all of which require EE.
flashcards.hint: Both get the tool, but one edition gets extra personalization features with it.

flashcards.question: What are the five core B2B features that can be toggled in Adobe Commerce EE?
flashcards.answer: The five toggleable B2B features are: Company Accounts (company_active), Shared Catalogs (sharedcatalog_active), B2B Quotes/Negotiable Quotes (negotiablequote_active), Quick Order (quickorder_active), and Requisition Lists (requisition_list_active). All are configured at Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features.
flashcards.hint: Each has its own enable toggle under a shared configuration section.

flashcards.question: What SaaS add-on services are available to both CE and EE merchants?
flashcards.answer: Live Search, Product Recommendations, Payment Services, and Catalog Service are all SaaS add-ons available to both CE and EE. They connect via API keys through the Commerce Services Connector and sync data via the SaaS Data Export module. They are not bundled in the base codebase — they require separate installation and subscription.
flashcards.hint: These services run on Adobe's infrastructure and connect to any edition.

flashcards.question: What is Async Order Management in Adobe Commerce EE?
flashcards.answer: Async Order Management is an EE-only feature that uses a message queue (RabbitMQ or MySQL-based) to process orders asynchronously. Customers get instant confirmation while order processing happens in the background. It uses the /async/ REST API endpoint prefix and requires message queue consumer processes to be running.
flashcards.hint: It separates the customer-facing confirmation from the backend processing.

flashcards.question: When Catalog Permissions is enabled in EE, what happens by default?
flashcards.answer: When enabling Catalog Permissions, a warning is displayed: 'By default this feature restricts all categories.' You must explicitly configure permissions per category or set global defaults to avoid accidentally locking out all visitors. Restricted categories are also removed from navigation menus and search results for unauthorized groups.
flashcards.hint: Enabling it without configuration locks everything down, not opens it up.

flashcards.question: What is the Catalog Service SaaS add-on, and what is it designed for?
flashcards.answer: Catalog Service is a high-performance read-only catalog API (GraphQL) optimized for storefront product display, separate from the core Commerce GraphQL API. It pre-indexes data into an optimized SaaS data store for faster performance. It is designed for headless storefronts and PWA deployments, not for admin catalog management.
flashcards.hint: It is a performance optimization for a specific type of storefront architecture.

flashcards.question: Is Advanced Reporting (Reports > Business Intelligence) an EE-exclusive feature?
flashcards.answer: No, the module-analytics module that provides the Reports > Business Intelligence menu (Advanced Reporting, BI Essentials) is licensed as OSL-3.0 (Open Source), meaning it is available in both CE and EE. The full Adobe Commerce Intelligence (MBI) platform with advanced dashboards and data warehousing is a separate paid service.
flashcards.hint: The basic reporting menu is in both editions; the premium service is separate.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between single Wish Lists (CE) and Multiple Wish Lists (EE)?
flashcards.answer: CE provides a single Wish List per customer with social sharing features. EE provides Multiple Wish Lists (module-multiple-wishlist) allowing customers to create multiple named wishlists. Gift Registry (EE-only) is a separate feature with event context. Requisition Lists (B2B) serve a similar purpose but for procurement.
flashcards.hint: The number of lists a customer can create differs by edition.

flashcards.question: Where is the Customer Segments admin menu located in Adobe Commerce EE?
flashcards.answer: Customer Segments is found at Customers > Segments (not under Marketing). Dynamic Blocks are at Content > Elements > Dynamic Blocks (not Marketing > Banners). Visual Merchandiser has no standalone menu item — it is embedded in category edit pages. Email Reminders are under Marketing > Communications.
flashcards.hint: Several EE features have admin locations that differ from what many study guides suggest.

studyNotes.title: Day 14 — Practice Test #2 + Review
studyNotes.content:
# Adobe Commerce (Magento) Certified Professional — Practice Test #2 Study Notes
## Week 2: Core Features — CMS, B2B Loyalty & Merchandising

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Exam Overview & Scoring Strategy](#1-exam-overview--scoring-strategy)
2. [Section 2: Merchandising — Deep Dive](#2-section-2-merchandising--deep-dive)
3. [Section 3: Digital Marketing — Deep Dive](#3-section-3-digital-marketing--deep-dive)
4. [EE vs CE Feature Matrix](#4-ee-vs-ce-feature-matrix)
5. [CMS Core Concepts](#5-cms-core-concepts)
6. [B2B & Loyalty Features](#6-b2b--loyalty-features)
7. [Promotions — Sandbox Scenarios](#7-promotions--sandbox-scenarios)
8. [Common Wrong-Answer Traps](#8-common-wrong-answer-traps)
9. [Week 1 vs Week 2 Score Tracker](#9-week-1-vs-week-2-score-tracker)
10. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Exam Overview & Scoring Strategy

### Exam Structure (Adobe Commerce Business Practitioner Expert AD0-E708)

| Category | % of Exam |
|---|---|
| Section 1: Core Features/General Configuration | ~46% |
| Section 2: Merchandising | ~10% |
| Section 3: Digital Marketing | ~4% |
| Section 4: Add-on Modules | ~18% |
| Section 5: Systems Architecture | ~10% |
| Section 6: Compliance/Security | ~12% |
| **Total** | **100%** |

> **Note:** Adobe periodically updates exam blueprints. Verify current section weights at [Adobe's exam guide](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/docs/). The section names and weights above reflect the AD0-E708 Business Practitioner Expert blueprint.

### Timed Test Strategy
- **60 questions / 105 minutes** → ~1 min 45 sec per question
- Flag and skip questions requiring > 90 seconds on first pass
- Review flagged questions in remaining time
- **Never leave a question blank** — no penalty for guessing

**Exam focus:**
- Passing score is typically **68%** (≈41 correct)
- Questions are scenario-based — look for the *most correct* answer, not just a *correct* answer
- Eliminate clearly wrong answers first (usually 2 can be eliminated immediately)

---

## 2. Section 2: Merchandising — Deep Dive

### 2.1 Visual Merchandiser (EE Only)

The Visual Merchandiser is an **Enterprise Edition exclusive** drag-and-drop tool for manually sorting products within categories.

```
Category Page (Visual Merchandiser)
+----------------------------------+
|  [Product A]  [Product B]  [C]  |  <- Drag to reorder
|  [Product D]  [Product E]  [F]  |
+----------------------------------+
       |
       v
  Sort Order saved to
  category_product table
  (position column)
```

#### Sorting Rules Available in Visual Merchandiser

There are 13 sort options in Visual Merchandiser (Sorting.php:24-38):

| Rule | Description |
|---|---|
| None | No automatic sorting |
| Move low stock to top | Prioritizes low-stock items |
| Move out of stock to bottom | Deprioritizes OOS items |
| Special price to top | Products with special price first |
| Special price to bottom | Products with special price last |
| Newest products first | By creation date |
| Sort by color | By color attribute value |
| Name: A - Z | Alphabetical ascending |
| Name: Z - A | Alphabetical descending |
| SKU: Ascending | SKU sort ascending |
| SKU: Descending | SKU sort descending |
| Price: High to low | Descending price sort |
| Price: Low to high | Ascending price sort |

**Exam focus:**
- Visual Merchandiser is **EE only** — CE does not have it
- You can **mix** manual positioning with automatic rules
- Products pinned manually are not overridden by automatic rules
- Pin icon "locks" a product position regardless of rule recalculation
- Visual Merchandiser has **no standalone admin menu item** — it is accessed at Catalog > Categories > [Category] > Products in Category tab

### 2.2 Category Merchandising Settings

Navigate to: **Catalog > Categories > [Select Category] > Display Settings**

```php
// Category display mode options (actual constant values)
'display_mode' => [
    'PRODUCTS',           // "Products only" (DM_PRODUCT)
    'PAGE',               // "Static block only" (DM_PAGE)
    'PRODUCTS_AND_PAGE'   // "Static block and products" (DM_MIXED)
]
```

**Exam focus:**
- `PRODUCTS_AND_PAGE` is the option when you need *both* a CMS block AND a product grid on a category page
- **Anchor** categories aggregate products from subcategories into layered navigation
- Setting "Is Anchor" = **Yes** on a parent category enables layered nav filters to show child category products

### 2.3 Layered Navigation

Layered navigation (faceted search) allows customers to filter by attributes.

#### Requirements for Attribute to Appear in Layered Nav

1. `Use in Layered Navigation` = **Filterable (with results)** OR **Filterable (no results)**
2. Attribute must be used in a product assigned to the category
3. Attribute input type must be compatible (Dropdown/Select, Multiple Select, Price, or Yes/No — NOT text/textarea)

**Exam focus:**
- **Filterable (with results)** — only shows filter option if products match
- **Filterable (no results)** — always shows the filter option even with zero results
- `Text` field attributes **cannot** be used in layered navigation
- Price ranges in layered nav are configured under: **Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Layered Navigation**

#### Layered Navigation Price Step Configuration

```
Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Layered Navigation
  |
  +-- Price Navigation Step Calculation
        |-- Automatic (equalize price ranges) [DEFAULT — value "auto"]
        |-- Automatic (equalize product counts) [value "improved"]
        |-- Manual [specify $X increments]
```

> **Note:** The default is "Automatic (equalize price ranges)" (auto), NOT "equalize product counts" (improved). Verified in module-layered-navigation/etc/config.xml:12.

### 2.4 Product Attributes for Merchandising

#### Attribute Scope Levels

| Scope | Description | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| Global | Same value across all stores/websites | SKU, Weight |
| Website | Different per website | Price, Status |
| Store View | Different per store view | Name, Description, Visibility |

**Exam focus:**
- **Price** is website-scoped by default
- **Status** is website-scoped (can enable/disable per website)
- **Visibility** is store-view-scoped (can differ per store view)
- **Name** and **Description** are store-view scoped (enables translation)
- Changing scope from Store View → Global **merges** values (takes the default store value)

### 2.5 Product Types — Merchandising Implications

```
Product Types
|
+-- Simple         (single SKU, no options)
+-- Configurable   (parent + child simples; customer selects option)
+-- Grouped        (displayed together, ordered individually)
+-- Bundle         (customer builds their own package)
+-- Virtual        (no shipping required — services, warranties)
+-- Downloadable   (digital files / links)
+-- Gift Card (EE) (virtual, physical, or combined)
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Configurable** products: The parent SKU itself has **no stock**; stock lives on child simples
- **Grouped** products: Each item in the group keeps its own price — no single "grouped price"
- **Bundle** products: Can be **fixed price** or **dynamic price**
- **Virtual** products do NOT trigger shipping step at checkout
- **Gift Card** is an **EE-only** product type

### 2.6 Related Products, Up-sells & Cross-sells

| Feature | Where it Displays | Assignment Location |
|---|---|---|
| Related Products | Product Detail Page (below main content) | Product > Related Products tab |
| Up-sells | Product Detail Page (replaces related on some themes) | Product > Up-sells tab |
| Cross-sells | Shopping Cart Page | Product > Cross-sells tab |

**Exam focus:**
- **Up-sells** are shown *instead of* or *alongside* the product being viewed (alternatives)
- **Cross-sells** appear on the **cart page** — "You might also like"
- In EE, **Related Products Rules** (automated) can replace or supplement manual assignments
- Manual relationships are one-directional — Product A related to B does NOT make B related to A

---

## 3. Section 3: Digital Marketing — Deep Dive

### 3.1 Cart Price Rules (Promotions)

**Path:** Marketing > Promotions > Cart Price Rules

#### Rule Structure

```
Cart Price Rule
|
+-- General Information
|     |-- Active (Yes/No)
|     |-- Websites
|     |-- Customer Groups
|     |-- Coupon (No Coupon / Specific Coupon / Auto-generated)
|     |-- Uses Per Coupon
|     |-- Uses Per Customer
|     |-- Priority (lower number = higher priority)
|     |-- Discard subsequent rules (Yes/No)
|
+-- Conditions
|     |-- Cart subtotal, item qty, customer segment (EE), etc.
|
+-- Actions
      |-- Discount type
      |-- Discount amount
      |-- Apply to Shipping (Yes/No)
      |-- Free Shipping
      |-- Discard subsequent rules
```

> **Note:** The field is called "Discard subsequent rules" (field name `stop_rules_processing`) in both the General Information and Actions sections. There is NO separate field called "Stop Further Rules Processing" — it is the same field.

#### Discount Types

| Action Type | Formula | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Percent of product price discount | `price × (discount/100)` | 20% off → saves $20 on $100 item |
| Fixed amount discount | `price - discount_amount` | $15 off cart |
| Fixed amount discount for whole cart | Applied to entire cart | $25 off order |
| Buy X get Y free (discount amount is Y) | Buy X, get Y items at discount | Buy 2 get 1 free |

**Exam focus:**
- **"Buy X Get Y"**: the *discount amount* field = **Y** (the number of FREE items, not X)
- **Priority**: Lower number = processed FIRST (Priority 0 runs before Priority 1)
- **"Discard subsequent rules"** stops any lower-priority rules (higher priority numbers) from applying after this one fires
- Coupon codes are **case-sensitive** by default — "SAVE10" and "save10" are treated as different codes (ValidateCouponCode.php performs direct equality comparison with no case conversion)

#### Auto-generated Coupons (Available in Both CE and EE)

```
Marketing > Promotions > Cart Price Rules > [Edit Rule]
  |
  +-- Coupon = "Auto Generated"
        |-- Code Length
        |-- Code Format (Alphanumeric / Alphabetical / Numeric)
        |-- Code Prefix
        |-- Code Suffix
        |-- Dash Every X Characters
```

> **Important correction:** Auto-generated coupon codes are available in **both CE and EE** — the Generate controller exists in the base module-sales-rule (Controller/Adminhtml/Promo/Quote/Generate.php). The "Manage Coupon Codes" section appears in the cart price rule form (sales_rule_form.xml:552). There is no separate "Coupon Codes" menu item — coupon management is done within the cart price rule form itself.

### 3.2 Catalog Price Rules

**Path:** Marketing > Promotions > Catalog Price Rule (singular title)

These apply **before** the product is added to the cart — they change the displayed price.

```
Catalog Price Rule
|
+-- Conditions (based on product attributes, categories)
+-- Actions
      |-- Apply (by percentage / by fixed amount / to fixed / orig. fixed)
      |-- Discount Amount
      |-- Discard subsequent rules (Yes/No)
```

> **Note:** There is **no** "Apply to Subproducts" field in catalog price rules. This field does not exist in the catalog_rule_form.xml. The actions section contains only: simple_action (Apply), discount_amount, and stop_rules_processing (Discard subsequent rules).

**Exam focus:**
- Catalog price rules do **NOT** use coupon codes
- They apply to the **listed price** in catalog, not at checkout
- Rules must be **Applied/Re-indexed** after changes (or wait for cron job)

#### Catalog Price Rule vs Cart Price Rule — Key Differences

| Feature | Catalog Price Rule | Cart Price Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Coupon code | No | Yes (optional) |
| Applies at | Catalog/browse time | Cart/checkout |
| Customer group | Yes | Yes |
| Conditions on cart contents | No | Yes |
| Requires reindex | Yes | No |

### 3.3 Email Marketing & Newsletters

**Path:** Marketing > Communications > Newsletter Subscribers

```
Newsletter Subscription Flow
  Customer opts in
       |
       v
  Confirmation email sent (if "Need to Confirm" = Yes)
       |
       v
  Added to subscribers list
       |
       v
  Marketing > Communications > Newsletter Templates
       |
       v
  Marketing > Communications > Newsletter Queue (scheduled send)
```

**Exam focus:**
- `Need to Confirm` setting is at: **Stores > Config > Customers > Newsletter > Subscription Options** (section=newsletter, tab=customer, group=subscription)
- Unsubscribe link is **mandatory** in newsletter templates
- Newsletter queue entries can be **paused** or **resumed**

### 3.4 URL Rewrites

**Path:** Marketing > SEO & Search > URL Rewrites

```
Request Path  -->  Target Path
/old-category/old-product  -->  /new-category/product-name.html
        |
        v
  Redirect Type:
    301 (Permanent) -- search engines update their index
    302 (Temporary) -- search engines keep old URL
    No redirect     -- just an alias
```

**Exam focus:**
- **301** redirect is preferred for SEO (permanent moves)
- Auto URL rewrites are created when you change a product/category URL key
- **"Create Permanent Redirect for old URL"** checkbox appears on product/category save when changing the URL key. The related system config field label is "Create Permanent Redirect for URLs if URL Key Changed" (catalog/seo/save_rewrites_history)
- Custom URL rewrites are **manual** overrides that take precedence

### 3.5 Sitemap & SEO

**Path:** Marketing > SEO & Search > Site Map

```xml
<!-- Generated sitemap.xml structure -->
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/product-name.html</loc>
    <lastmod>YYYY-MM-DD</lastmod>
    <changefreq>daily</changefreq>
    <priority>1.0</priority>
  </url>
</urlset>
```

**Exam focus:**
- Sitemap can be configured to include: **Products, Categories, CMS Pages**
- Generation can be **manual** or **scheduled via cron**
- `robots.txt` can be edited at: **Content > Design > Configuration > [Store] > Edit > Search Engine Robots** (the "Edit custom instruction of robots.txt File" field is in the "Search Engine Robots" fieldset, not directly under "HTML Head")
- Meta robots (`noindex`, `nofollow`) for specific pages: set at page/category level

### 3.6 Search & Elasticsearch

**Path:** Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog Search

| Feature | CE | EE |
|---|---|---|
| Elasticsearch / OpenSearch | Yes (required in 2.4+) | Yes |
| Live Search (SaaS) | Add-on | Add-on |
| Search Synonyms | Yes | Yes |
| Search Terms Management | Yes | Yes |

> **Important correction:** MySQL Full-text Search was **removed** in Adobe Commerce 2.4. Only Elasticsearch or OpenSearch is available as the search engine. There is no MySQL search option in the admin configuration.

**Exam focus:**
- Adobe Commerce 2.4.x **requires** Elasticsearch (or OpenSearch) — MySQL search has been removed
- **Search Synonyms**: Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Synonyms (One-way vs two-way synonyms)
- **Search Terms**: Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Terms — shows popular terms, allows redirect
- Configuring a search term redirect: Assign a URL to the search term so customers typing it go directly to a page

---

## 4. EE vs CE Feature Matrix

This is one of the **highest-yield** areas of the exam. Memorize this table.

### 4.1 EE-Only Features (Critical List)

| Feature | Where in Admin | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Visual Merchandiser** | Catalog > Categories > [Category] > Products in Category | Drag-and-drop product sorting (no standalone menu) |
| **Customer Segments** | Customers > Segments | Target content/rules by segment |
| **Gift Registry** | Stores > Config > Customers | Customer wish-list variant |
| **Reward Points** | Stores > Config > Customers > Reward Points | Loyalty program |
| **Store Credit** | Customer Account | Admin can add credit to customer account |
| **Gift Cards** | Product type | Virtual/Physical/Combined |
| **Related Products Rules** | Marketing > Promotions > Related Products Rules | Automated cross/upsell rules |
| **Staging & Preview** | Content > Content Staging > Dashboard | Schedule future content changes |
| **Page Builder** | Content > Pages | Drag-and-drop CMS (Note: CE has Page Builder as free extension in 2.4, but without Dynamic Blocks/Segments) |
| **B2B Module** | Stores > Config > General > B2B Features | Company accounts, quotes, etc. (included with EE) |
| **Private Sales / Events** | Marketing > Private Sales | Invite-only sales |
| **Multiple Wish Lists** | Customer account | Multiple named wishlists (module-multiple-wishlist, proprietary) |
| **RMA (Returns)** | Sales > Returns | Return Merchandise Authorization |
| **Scheduled Import/Export** | System > Data Transfer | Cron-based data sync |
| **Dynamic Blocks** | Content > Elements > Dynamic Blocks | Segment-targeted content blocks |

> **Note corrections from original:**
> - "Auto-generated Coupons" removed from EE-only list — they are available in **both CE and EE**
> - Dynamic Blocks admin path is **Content > Elements > Dynamic Blocks**, not "Content > Banners"
> - Customer Segments is under **Customers > Segments**, not Marketing

> **Note:** Page Builder was introduced to CE in version 2.4.x but with fewer features than EE. Always check the question's context.

**Exam focus:**
- If a question mentions **Customer Segments** → that's EE
- If a question mentions **Reward Points** → that's EE
- If a question mentions **Staging & Preview** (scheduling) → that's EE
- **Wish Lists** exist in both CE and EE, but **multiple wish lists** is EE only
- **Store Credit** (admin-added) is EE; **Gift Card** balance is also EE

### 4.2 Features Available in BOTH CE and EE

| Feature | Notes |
|---|---|
| Cart Price Rules (with coupon codes) | Both — **including** auto-generated coupon codes |
| Catalog Price Rules | Both |
| Layered Navigation | Both |
| CMS Pages & Blocks | Both |
| Newsletter | Both |
| Basic Wish List (single list) | Both |
| URL Rewrites | Both |
| Sitemaps | Both |
| Search Terms & Synonyms | Both |
| Product Reviews | Both |
| Inventory Management | Both (MSI in 2.3+) |
| Advanced Reporting (Reports > BI) | Both — module-analytics is CE (OSL-3.0) |

---

## 5. CMS Core Concepts

### 5.1 CMS Pages

**Path:** Content > Elements > Pages

```
CMS Page Structure
|
+-- Title (used for browser tab / heading)
+-- URL Key (used in URL: /your-url-key)
+-- Store View (which stores show this page)
+-- Status (Enabled/Disabled)
+-- Content (HTML / Page Builder blocks)
+-- Design (layout — 1 column, 2 column, etc.)
+-- Meta Data (title, keywords, description)
```

**Exam focus:**
- CMS page URL key is used directly as the URL path — CMS pages do **not** use a URL suffix like .html. The product/category URL suffix configuration does not apply to CMS pages. The CMS router matches the request path directly against the page identifier.
- A disabled CMS page returns a **404** error to visitors

### 5.2 CMS Blocks (Static Blocks)

**Path:** Content > Elements > Blocks

Blocks are **reusable content snippets** that can be embedded in:
- CMS Pages (via widget or directive)
- Category pages
- Product pages
- Email templates
- Layout XML

```
Embedding a Block in a CMS Page (using directive):
{{block class="Magento\Cms\Block\Block" id="my-block-identifier"}}

OR using widget insertion:
{{widget type="Magento\Cms\Block\Widget\Block" template="widget/static_block/default.phtml" block_id="my-block-identifier"}}
```

> **Note:** In the block directive, the parameter is `id=` (not `block_id=`). In the widget directive, the parameter is `block_id=`. Both accept the block's **string identifier** (e.g., "my-block-identifier"), not the numeric database ID.

**Exam focus:**
- Static blocks do **not** have a URL — they cannot be accessed directly
- Block `identifier` is what you reference in directives
- Blocks can be store-view specific

### 5.3 Widgets

**Path:** Content > Elements > Widgets

Widgets are **dynamic content** components that can be placed in CMS pages, blocks, or layout positions.

#### Common Widget Types

| Widget Type | Description |
|---|---|
| CMS Static Block | Embeds a static block |
| CMS Page Link | Link to a CMS page |
| Catalog Category Link | Link to a category |
| Catalog Product Link | Link to a specific product |
| Catalog New Products List | Shows newest products |
| Catalog Products List | Shows products matching conditions (note: "Products" plural) |
| Orders and Returns | Self-service order lookup form |
| Recently Compared Products | Customer's comparison history |
| Recently Viewed Products | Customer's browsing history |

**Exam focus:**
- Widgets have **Layout Update XML** that controls where they render (handle, block reference, method)
- Widget instances are **theme-agnostic** (they persist across theme changes)
- To place a widget in a specific page: use **Display On = Specific Page** and select the page

### 5.4 Page Builder (EE Full Feature / CE Basic)

Page Builder Sections:
```
Page Builder Toolbar
|
+-- Layout (Row, Column, Tab)
+-- Elements (Text, Heading, Buttons, Divider, HTML Code)
+-- Media (Image, Video, Banner, Slider, Map)
+-- Add Content (Block, Dynamic Block, Products)
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Dynamic Block** (formerly Banner) in Page Builder is EE only
- Rows can have **full-width**, **full-bleed**, or **contained** appearance settings (three options)
- Page Builder content is stored as **HTML with data-pb-style attributes** in the database

### 5.5 Design Configuration & Themes

**Path:** Content > Design > Configuration

```
Design Hierarchy (most specific wins):
Store View > Website > Global Default
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Transactional email design** (header/footer logo) is configured per store view in Design Configuration
- Design exceptions: Override theme for specific user agents
- `Search Engine Robots` section contains robots.txt editing
- `HTML Head` section contains: default meta description, keywords, demo store notice, scripts/CSS

## 6. B2B & Loyalty Features

### 6.1 B2B Module Overview (EE)

B2B modules are included with the Adobe Commerce (EE) license. They are enabled via configuration at Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features (section=btob).

```
B2B Features Hierarchy
|
+-- Company Management
|     |-- Company Admin
|     |-- Company Users (sub-accounts)
|     |-- Roles & Permissions (within company)
|     |-- Company Credit
|
+-- Shared Catalog
|     |-- Custom pricing per company
|     |-- Restricted product visibility
|
+-- Negotiable Quotes
|     |-- Customer requests quote from cart
|     |-- Admin negotiates price
|     |-- Quote converted to order
|
+-- Purchase Orders (PO)
|     |-- Approval workflows
|     |-- PO number on checkout
|
+-- Quick Order
      |-- Order by SKU (bulk entry)
      |-- Upload CSV of SKUs
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Shared Catalog** — Can set custom prices AND hide products from non-B2B customers
- There is a **Public Shared Catalog** (default, for all) and **Custom Shared Catalogs** (per company)
- **Negotiable Quotes** require the B2B module — NOT available in CE or standard EE without B2B enabled
- Company Admin can create sub-users and assign roles/permissions within the company

### 6.2 Reward Points (EE Only)

**Path:** Stores > Configuration > Customers > Reward Points (section=magento_reward, tab=customer)

```
Reward Points Flow
  Customer Action (purchase, registration, review, etc.)
       |
       v
  Points Earned (based on exchange rate)
       |
       v
  Points Balance (in customer account)
       |
       v
  Points Redeemed at checkout
       |
       v
  Points = Dollar Discount (based on redemption rate)
```

#### Reward Point Exchange Rates

Configured at: **Stores > Other Settings > Reward Exchange Rates** (not under Marketing)

| Rate Type | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Points to Currency | 100 pts = $1 | Redemption value |
| Currency to Points | $1 spent = 10 pts | Earning rate |

**Exam focus:**
- Reward points have an **expiration** date (configurable via `expiration_days` field, not `points_lifetime`)
- Points can be earned for: **Purchase, Registration, Newsletter Signup, Writing a Review, Sending Invitations (customer), Converting Invitations to Order** — 6 earning actions total, NO birthday action
- Points are applied at checkout as a **payment method** (partial or full)
- Admin can manually **add/deduct** points from a customer account
- Points **balance** is visible in the customer's My Account section

### 6.3 Store Credit (EE Only)

**Path:** Customer Account (Admin View) > Store Credit tab (module-customer-balance, section=customer, group=magento_customerbalance)

```
Store Credit Actions
  Admin adds credit to customer account
       |
       v
  Customer sees credit balance in My Account
       |
       v
  Customer applies credit at checkout
  (checkbox "Use Store Credit" appears in payment step)
       |
       v
  Order charged remaining balance to another payment method
```

**Exam focus:**
- Store Credit does **not** expire (unlike reward points which can)
- Credit is **website-scoped** (per website, not global)
- When a refund is issued as store credit, it appears in the Store Credit tab
- Store credit is different from a **gift card balance** (though both show in payment step)

### 6.4 Customer Groups & Tier Pricing

**Path:** Customers > Customer Groups

Default groups:
- **NOT LOGGED IN** (guests)
- **General**
- **Wholesale**
- **Retailer**

**Tier Pricing** allows quantity-based discounts:

```
Product > Advanced Pricing > Tier Prices
  |
  +-- Website: All / Specific
  +-- Customer Group: All / Specific
  +-- Quantity: (minimum qty to trigger)
  +-- Price: (specific price OR percent discount)
```

**Exam focus:**
- Tier prices are configured **per product** (or via catalog price rules for bulk)
- A tier price **replaces** the regular price when qty threshold is met (it's not a discount off the top)
- **Group Price** was deprecated — use Tier Price with qty=1 for group-specific pricing
- Customer group assignment affects: tier pricing, tax class, catalog price rules, cart price rules

### 6.5 Private Sales & Events (EE Only)

**Path:** Marketing > Private Sales (parent defined in module-enterprise)

```
Private Sale Setup
  1. Create Event (start/end date, category)
  2. Create Invitation(s) -- send to existing customers or email list
  3. Invited customers get special access
  4. "Allow Invites" -- customers can invite others (configurable)
```

**Exam focus:**
- Private sales require the customer to be **logged in**
- Categories linked to events show a countdown timer
- `Stores > Config > General > General > Website Restrictions` controls site-wide access restriction (module-website-restriction, section=general, group=restriction)

## 7. Promotions — Sandbox Scenarios

### 7.1 Scenario: "Buy X Get Y Free" Setup

This is a **commonly missed** question type. Here is the exact configuration:

**Goal:** Buy 3 items, get 1 free (from the same product)

```
Cart Price Rule Configuration:
  Name: Buy 3 Get 1 Free
  Coupon: No Coupon (automatic)

  Conditions: (leave blank to apply to all products)

  Actions:
    Apply: Buy X get Y free (discount amount is Y)
    Discount Amount: 1       <-- Y = 1 (the FREE item)
    Maximum Qty Discount is Applied To: 1
    Discount Qty Step (Buy X): 3   <-- X = 3 (buy this many)
    Apply to Shipping Amount: No
    Discard subsequent rules: No
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Discount Amount = Y** (number of FREE items)
- **Discount Qty Step = X** (number that must be purchased to trigger free items)
- The discount applies at each item's own price based on quantity ratio calculations — it does **NOT** sort by cheapest item (BuyXGetY.php:27-50)
- If cart has 6 items and rule is Buy 3 Get 1, customer gets **2** free items (2 cycles of Buy3Get1)

### 7.2 Scenario: Tiered Percentage Discounts by Customer Group

**Goal:** Wholesale customers get 15% off all Category X products

```
Catalog Price Rule:
  Name: Wholesale 15% - Category X
  Status: Active
  Websites: Main Website
  Customer Groups: Wholesale

  Conditions:
    If ALL of these conditions are TRUE:
      Category is [X]

  Actions:
    Apply: By Percentage of the Original Price
    Discount Amount: 15
```

```bash
# After saving, apply the rule:
# Admin: Marketing > Catalog Price Rules > Apply Rules button
# OR via CLI (use correct indexer IDs):
php bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogrule_rule
php bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogrule_product
php bin/magento indexer:reindex catalog_product_price
php bin/magento cache:flush
```

> **Note:** The correct indexer IDs are `catalogrule_rule` and `catalogrule_product` (no underscore between "catalog" and "rule"). There are NO indexer IDs called `catalog_rule_product` or `catalog_rule_product_price`.

**Exam focus:**
- Catalog price rules require **reindexing** to take effect
- The "Apply Rules" button in Admin triggers this reindex for catalog rules only
- Changes to Cart Price Rules do **not** require reindex

### 7.3 Scenario: Coupon Code with Usage Limits

**Goal:** Single-use coupon "WELCOME10" for 10% off first order, new customers only

```
Cart Price Rule:
  Name: New Customer Welcome 10%
  Coupon: Specific Coupon
  Coupon Code: WELCOME10
  Uses Per Coupon: 1         <-- total uses across all customers
  Uses Per Customer: 1       <-- per individual customer

  Conditions:
    Customer Group is [NOT LOGGED IN] -- or create a "New Customers" segment (EE)
    -- OR --
    Total Number of Orders is less than 1  <-- CE-compatible approach

  Actions:
    Apply: Percent of product price discount
    Discount Amount: 10
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Uses Per Coupon**: Total redemptions allowed globally
- **Uses Per Customer**: How many times one customer can use it
- Setting `Uses Per Coupon = 1` makes it a true single-use code globally
- In EE, use **Customer Segments** to target "New Customers" more precisely
- The `Total Number of Orders` condition is under **Conditions > Customer Address / Customer** (not cart conditions)

### 7.4 Scenario: Free Shipping Threshold

**Goal:** Free shipping on orders over $75

**Method 1: Cart Price Rule**
```
Cart Price Rule:
  Name: Free Shipping Over $75
  Coupon: No Coupon

  Conditions:
    Subtotal >= 75

  Actions:
    Apply: Percent of product price discount
    Discount Amount: 0
    Free Shipping: For matching items only
                   -- OR --
                   For shipment with matching items
```

**Method 2: Shipping Method Configuration (Recommended)**
```
Stores > Config > Sales > Shipping Methods > Free Shipping:
  Enabled: Yes
  Minimum Order Amount: 75
  Include Tax to Amount: Before Tax / After Tax
```

> **Note:** The config section label is "Shipping Methods" (not "Delivery Methods").

**Exam focus:**
- The **shipping method approach** is simpler and more performant
- Cart Price Rule approach for free shipping is used when you need **conditional logic** (specific products, coupon required, etc.)
- **"For matching items only"** = free shipping on items that met the rule conditions (other items still paid)
- **"For shipment with matching items"** = entire shipment is free if any item matches

## 8. Common Wrong-Answer Traps

### 8.1 Traps in Merchandising Questions

| Trap | Correct Understanding |
|---|---|
| "Tier price is a discount off regular price" | Tier price **IS** the price when qty met — not a percentage off |
| "Visual Merchandiser available in CE" | EE ONLY |
| "Grouped product has its own price" | Grouped product displays child prices; no single "grouped price" |
| "Setting a product inactive hides it from search" | Yes — but the product URL still resolves (shows unavailable) |
| "Anchor = No on parent still shows child products" | Child products still appear, but layered nav won't aggregate filters |

### 8.2 Traps in Digital Marketing Questions

| Trap | Correct Understanding |
|---|---|
| "Catalog price rules take effect immediately after save" | Require **reindex** (or Apply Rules button) |
| "Buy X Get Y — discount amount = X" | Discount Amount = **Y** (free items), Step = **X** (trigger qty) |
| "Buy X Get Y discounts the cheapest item" | Discount applies at each item's own price — does NOT sort by cheapest |
| "301 and 302 both update search engine indexes" | Only **301** signals permanent change to search engines |
| "Auto-generated coupon codes require EE" | Auto-generated coupons are available in **both CE and EE** |
| "Discard Subsequent Rules stops all rules" | Only stops rules with **higher priority number** (lower priority). Lower number = higher priority = runs first |
| "Coupon codes are case-insensitive" | Coupon codes are **case-sensitive** by default — no case conversion on validation |

### 8.3 Traps in EE vs CE Questions

| Feature Question | Common Wrong Answer | Correct Answer |
|---|---|---|
| "Which feature allows customer segment targeting?" | Customer Groups (CE) | **Customer Segments** (EE) |
| "What provides B2B quote negotiation?" | Cart Price Rule | **Negotiable Quotes** (B2B module) |
| "How to schedule content changes?" | Cron + custom code | **Staging & Preview** (EE) |
| "Multiple wish lists available in CE?" | Yes, it's a standard feature | No — **single wish list** in CE; **multiple** in EE |
| "RMA available in CE?" | Yes, in Sales menu | No — **EE only** |

### 8.4 Scope & Configuration Traps

```
Price scope default = Website
Name scope default = Store View
Status scope default = Website
Visibility scope default = Store View

Common trap: "Changing product price changes it globally"
Correct: Price is website-scoped, not global (unless scope changed in config)
```

**Exam focus:**
- When you change price at website level, it does NOT affect other websites
- `Stores > Config > Catalog > Catalog > Price > Catalog Price Scope` can be changed to Global — then one price for all

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Merchandising
- [ ] Visual Merchandiser = **EE only**; drag-and-drop product ordering within categories (no standalone menu item)
- [ ] Pin icon in Visual Merchandiser = locks product position, not overridden by rules
- [ ] Category **Anchor = Yes** → child category products roll up into layered nav
- [ ] Category Display Mode: `PRODUCTS_AND_PAGE` shows both grid and CMS block
- [ ] Layered Nav requires attribute: Use in Layered Navigation ≠ No; input type must be Dropdown/Select/Price/Yes/No
- [ ] "Filterable (with results)" hides filter if no products match; "Filterable (no results)" always shows filter
- [ ] Price Navigation Step default: "Automatic (equalize price ranges)" — NOT equalize product counts
- [ ] Configurable product: **no stock on parent**, stock on child simples
- [ ] Grouped product: no single price; each child keeps own price
- [ ] Bundle: can be **fixed** or **dynamic** pricing
- [ ] Virtual product: skips shipping at checkout
- [ ] Gift Card product = **EE only**
- [ ] Cross-sells display on the **cart page**
- [ ] Up-sells display on the **product detail page**
- [ ] Related product rules (automated) = **EE only**
- [ ] Price is **website-scoped**; Name/Description are **store-view-scoped**
- [ ] Status is **website-scoped**; Visibility is **store-view-scoped**

### Digital Marketing & Promotions
- [ ] Cart Price Rule priority: **lower number = higher priority** (runs first)
- [ ] "Discard subsequent rules" = stop lower-priority rules from firing (only field name — no "Stop Further Rules Processing")
- [ ] Buy X Get Y: **Discount Amount = Y** (free items); **Step = X** (trigger); does NOT sort by cheapest
- [ ] Auto-generated bulk coupon codes = available in **both CE and EE**
- [ ] Coupon codes are **case-sensitive** by default
- [ ] Catalog Price Rules: **no coupon codes**, apply at browse time, require **reindex**
- [ ] Catalog Price Rules: no "Apply to Subproducts" field exists
- [ ] Cart Price Rules: **no reindex needed**, apply at checkout
- [ ] Cart Price Rules can use coupon codes (CE and EE)
- [ ] Correct catalog rule indexer IDs: `catalogrule_rule`, `catalogrule_product` (NOT `catalog_rule_product`)
- [ ] 301 redirect = permanent (SEO passes value); 302 = temporary
- [ ] URL Rewrite: Request Path → Target Path; type is 301, 302, or No Redirect
- [ ] Newsletter "Need to Confirm" = double opt-in setting (Stores > Config > Customers > Newsletter)
- [ ] Search term redirect = sends customer directly to a URL when they search a term
- [ ] Adobe Commerce 2.4 requires Elasticsearch/OpenSearch (**MySQL search removed**)
- [ ] Free shipping via shipping method = minimum order amount setting (simpler approach)
- [ ] CMS pages use URL key directly — **no URL suffix** applied

### EE vs CE — EE-Exclusive Features
- [ ] Visual Merchandiser
- [ ] Customer Segments (admin: Customers > Segments)
- [ ] Reward Points
- [ ] Store Credit (admin-added to customer account)
- [ ] Gift Card product type
- [ ] Related Products Rules (automated)
- [ ] Content Staging & Preview (scheduling)
- [ ] Dynamic Blocks (Content > Elements > Dynamic Blocks, targeted by segment)
- [ ] Multiple Wish Lists (CE = single only)
- [ ] RMA / Returns Management
- [ ] Private Sales & Events (Marketing > Private Sales)
- [ ] Scheduled Import/Export (System > Data Transfer)
- [ ] B2B features: Company Accounts, Shared Catalogs, Negotiable Quotes, Purchase Order Approval Workflows

### CMS
- [ ] CMS Page URL key does NOT include `.html` — and CMS pages have **no URL suffix** at all
- [ ] Disabled CMS page = **404** for visitors
- [ ] Static block = no direct URL, referenced by `identifier`
- [ ] Block directive: `{{block class="..." id="identifier"}}` (uses `id=`, not `block_id=`)
- [ ] Widget directive: `{{widget type="..." block_id="identifier"}}` (uses `block_id=` with string identifier)
- [ ] Widgets = dynamic, theme-agnostic, placed via Layout Update XML
- [ ] Page Builder Dynamic Block = **EE only**
- [ ] Design hierarchy: Store View > Website > Global (most specific wins)

### B2B & Loyalty
- [ ] Shared Catalog = custom pricing AND product visibility restrictions per company
- [ ] Public Shared Catalog = visible to all (guest/general); Custom = per company
- [ ] Negotiable Quotes = B2B module only, customer requests quote from cart
- [ ] Reward Points: 6 earning actions — purchase, registration, review, newsletter, invitation_customer, invitation_order — NO birthday
- [ ] Reward Points: have **expiration dates** (configurable via `expiration_days`); Store Credit does **not** expire
- [ ] Reward Exchange Rates: configured at Stores > Other Settings > Reward Exchange Rates (NOT under Marketing)
- [ ] Tier pricing: replaces the price at qty threshold (not a discount off the top)
- [ ] Group price deprecated → use Tier Price with qty=1 for group-specific pricing
- [ ] Customer group affects: tier prices, tax class, price rules, catalog visibility (shared catalog)
- [ ] "NOT LOGGED IN" is a customer group (for guest pricing/rules)
- [ ] Reward Points redeemed at checkout as a payment method
- [ ] Store Credit is website-scoped; applied at checkout payment step

### Sandbox Verification Steps
- [ ] Tested Buy X Get Y rule: confirmed Discount Amount=Y, Step=X fields
- [ ] Verified catalog price rule requires reindex after save
- [ ] Confirmed cross-sells appear on cart page (not product page)
- [ ] Verified Anchor category behavior in layered nav
- [ ] Checked tier price behavior — price replaces, not discounts

flashcards.question: In a Buy X Get Y Free cart price rule, what does the 'Discount Amount' field represent?
flashcards.answer: The Discount Amount field represents Y — the number of FREE items the customer receives. The 'Discount Qty Step (Buy X)' field represents X — the number of items the customer must buy to trigger the free items. The discount applies at each item's own price and does NOT sort by cheapest item.
flashcards.hint: The field name is misleading — it is the free quantity, not a dollar amount.

flashcards.question: What is the AD0-E708 exam passing score, and how many questions are there?
flashcards.answer: The exam has 60 questions with a 105-minute time limit, giving approximately 1 minute 45 seconds per question. The passing score is typically 68% (approximately 41 correct answers). Questions are scenario-based — look for the most correct answer, not just a correct answer.
flashcards.hint: You need roughly two-thirds of the answers correct.

flashcards.question: What is the default scope for product Price, Name, Status, and Visibility attributes?
flashcards.answer: Price is website-scoped. Name and Description are store-view-scoped (enabling translation). Status is website-scoped (can enable/disable per website). Visibility is store-view-scoped (can differ per store view). These scope defaults are frequently tested.
flashcards.hint: Some attributes vary by language (store view); others vary by regional pricing (website).

flashcards.question: What is the key difference between a Configurable, Grouped, and Bundle product type?
flashcards.answer: Configurable: parent + child simples where customer selects options (stock on children only). Grouped: products displayed together but ordered individually, each with its own price. Bundle: customer builds their own package, can have fixed price or dynamic price. Virtual products skip the shipping step at checkout.
flashcards.hint: Consider where stock lives, how pricing works, and how the customer interacts.

flashcards.question: How do coupon codes handle case sensitivity in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: Coupon codes are case-sensitive by default. 'SAVE10' and 'save10' are treated as different codes because the validation performs a direct equality comparison with no case conversion. This is important when communicating coupon codes to customers.
flashcards.hint: The system does not normalize the input before comparing.

flashcards.question: Do CMS pages use a URL suffix like .html, similar to products and categories?
flashcards.answer: No, CMS pages do NOT use a URL suffix. The product/category URL suffix configuration does not apply to CMS pages. The CMS router matches the request path directly against the page identifier/URL key. For example, a CMS page with URL key 'about-us' is accessed at /about-us, not /about-us.html.
flashcards.hint: CMS page URL handling is different from product/category URL handling.

flashcards.question: What is the correct admin path for configuring Reward Points exchange rates?
flashcards.answer: Exchange rates are managed at Stores > Other Settings > Reward Exchange Rates, not under Stores > Configuration or Marketing. They are database records (admin grid), not system.xml configuration fields. Two rates must be configured: an earning rate (currency to points) and a spending rate (points to currency).
flashcards.hint: The rates are managed as records in a grid, not as config values.

flashcards.question: What is the Newsletter subscription 'Need to Confirm' setting, and where is it configured?
flashcards.answer: The 'Need to Confirm' setting enables double opt-in for newsletter subscriptions — when enabled, customers must confirm their subscription via email before being added to the subscribers list. It is configured at Stores > Config > Customers > Newsletter > Subscription Options.
flashcards.hint: It adds an extra verification step to the subscription process.

flashcards.question: What are the Shared Catalog types in Adobe Commerce B2B, and what is the distinction?
flashcards.answer: There is a Public Shared Catalog (default, visible to all guest and general customers) and Custom Shared Catalogs (per company). Shared Catalogs can set custom prices AND hide products from non-B2B customers. They are a B2B Suite feature, included with the EE license, not available in CE.
flashcards.hint: One is the default for everyone; the other is company-specific.

flashcards.question: What is the key fact about tier pricing that is commonly misunderstood?
flashcards.answer: Tier price IS the price when the quantity threshold is met — it is NOT a discount off the regular price. It replaces the effective price entirely. Group Price was deprecated in Magento 2 and is now achieved using Tier Price with qty=1 for the target customer group.
flashcards.hint: It is a replacement, not a reduction.

flashcards.question: What are the three free shipping action options available within a Cart Price Rule?
flashcards.answer: No (no free shipping from this rule), For matching items only (waives shipping cost for qualifying items only), and For shipment with matching items (waives shipping for the entire shipment if any item matches). The 'For shipment' option is the most generous.
flashcards.hint: The options range from none to partial to full shipment coverage.

flashcards.question: What is the 'Discard subsequent rules' field, and does it exist under a different name?
flashcards.answer: The field is called 'Discard subsequent rules' (field name: stop_rules_processing) in both catalog and cart price rules. There is NO separate field called 'Stop Further Rules Processing' — some documentation uses this alternate name, but the actual admin UI label is 'Discard subsequent rules'.
flashcards.hint: The field has one official label, though study materials sometimes use an alternate name.

flashcards.question: What happens when a disabled CMS page is accessed by a visitor?
flashcards.answer: A disabled CMS page returns a 404 error to visitors. This is different from a disabled CMS Block, which renders nothing silently (no error) wherever it is embedded. Understanding this distinction is important for managing content availability.
flashcards.hint: Two types of disabled CMS content behave differently on the frontend.

flashcards.question: What is Private Sales in Adobe Commerce EE, and what does Website Restrictions control?
flashcards.answer: Private Sales (Marketing > Private Sales) enables invite-only sale events with countdown timers on categories. Website Restrictions (Stores > Config > General > General > Website Restrictions) controls site-wide access restriction. Private sales require customers to be logged in. Categories linked to events show a countdown timer.
flashcards.hint: One is event-based access; the other is site-wide access control.

flashcards.question: Where is robots.txt editing configured in Adobe Commerce admin?
flashcards.answer: The robots.txt file is edited at Content > Design > Configuration > [Store] > Edit > Search Engine Robots. The field is in the 'Search Engine Robots' fieldset, not directly under 'HTML Head'. This is also where you can set meta robots directives (noindex, nofollow) for specific page types.
flashcards.hint: It is under the Design area, within a specific fieldset that is easy to overlook.

studyNotes.title: Day 15 — B2B: Company & Shared Catalog
studyNotes.content:
# Adobe Commerce B2B: Company & Shared Catalog — Study Notes

## Table of Contents
1. [B2B Module Overview](#1-b2b-module-overview)
2. [Company Accounts Architecture](#2-company-accounts-architecture)
3. [Company Status Lifecycle](#3-company-status-lifecycle)
4. [Company Admin User & User Management](#4-company-admin-user--user-management)
5. [Company Credit: Limits & Terms](#5-company-credit-limits--terms)
6. [Shared Catalog: Core Concepts](#6-shared-catalog-core-concepts)
7. [Shared Catalog Types: Public vs Custom](#7-shared-catalog-types-public-vs-custom)
8. [Shared Catalog Pricing & Indexing](#8-shared-catalog-pricing--indexing)
9. [Company → Shared Catalog Assignment](#9-company--shared-catalog-assignment)
10. [Product Visibility Rules (The Tricky Part)](#10-product-visibility-rules-the-tricky-part)
11. [Hands-On Walkthrough](#11-hands-on-walkthrough)
12. [Common Pitfalls & Exam Traps](#12-common-pitfalls--exam-traps)
13. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

## 1. B2B Module Overview

Adobe Commerce B2B is a **suite of modules** available exclusively in **Adobe Commerce (Enterprise Edition)**. It is *not* available in Magento Open Source. B2B modules ship with the EE codebase and are enabled via configuration.

### Key B2B Modules

| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Magento_Company` | Company accounts, hierarchy, users, roles |
| `Magento_SharedCatalog` | Custom pricing and product visibility per company |
| `Magento_NegotiableQuote` | Quote negotiation workflow |
| `Magento_QuickOrder` | SKU-based rapid ordering |
| `Magento_RequisitionList` | Requisition lists (saved shopping lists) |
| `Magento_CompanyCredit` | Net payment terms and credit limits |
| `Magento_PurchaseOrder` | Purchase order approval workflows |

> **Note:** The requisition list module is `Magento_RequisitionList` (not `Magento_Requisition`). This is confirmed in module-requisition-list/etc/module.xml.

> **Exam focus:** B2B modules are **Adobe Commerce EE only**. The `Magento_SharedCatalog` module and `Magento_Company` module are separate but deeply integrated — you need *both* enabled to fully leverage company-scoped pricing.

### Enabling B2B

```bash
# Enable B2B modules (Company must be enabled before SharedCatalog — it's a config dependency)
bin/magento module:enable Magento_Company
bin/magento module:enable Magento_SharedCatalog
bin/magento module:enable Magento_CompanyCredit
bin/magento module:enable Magento_PurchaseOrder
bin/magento setup:upgrade
bin/magento setup:di:compile
bin/magento cache:flush
```

**Admin path to enable B2B features:**
`Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features` (section=btob)

```
B2B Features Panel
------------------
Enable Company:                [Yes / No]
Enable Shared Catalog:         [Yes / No]  <-- only visible when Company = Yes
Enable B2B Quote:              [Yes / No]
Enable Quick Order:            [Yes / No]
Enable Requisition List:       [Yes / No]
```

> **Important:** The "Enable Shared Catalog" field has a `<depends>` on `company_active=1` — it only appears when Company is enabled. Also, enabling Shared Catalog **automatically enables Category Permissions** for all stores (per the system.xml comment). This is a significant side effect.

> **Exam focus:** Enabling **Shared Catalog** automatically forces product visibility to be managed through catalog assignment. This has **immediate storefront impact** — products disappear from guests if not in a Public catalog.

---

## 2. Company Accounts Architecture

### Hierarchical Structure

```
+------------------------------------------+
|           Parent Company (Root)          |
|   Company Admin User                     |
|   +------------------------------------+ |
|   |  Division / Sub-Unit A             | |
|   |    Team Lead User                  | |
|   |    +------------------------------+| |
|   |    |  Sub-Unit A1 (nested)        || |
|   |    |    Regular User 1            || |
|   |    |    Regular User 2            || |
|   |    +------------------------------+| |
|   +------------------------------------+ |
|   +------------------------------------+ |
|   |  Division / Sub-Unit B             | |
|   |    Regular User 3                  | |
|   +------------------------------------+ |
+------------------------------------------+
```

### Key Entities

- **Company Account** — The top-level organizational record in the Admin
- **Parent Company** — The root of the company hierarchy
- **Sub-units (Teams / Divisions)** — Organizational groupings under the parent
- **Company Admin** — A special customer account designated as the company's administrator
- **Company Users** — Regular customer accounts attached to the company

> **Exam focus:** A company account is **separate from a regular customer account**. The Company Admin is a *customer account* flagged with elevated B2B permissions. Sub-units do NOT have separate credit limits — credit is managed at the **company level**.

### Database Tables

| Table | Description |
|---|---|
| `company` | Core company record |
| `company_advanced_customer_entity` | Links customer accounts to a company |
| `company_structure` | Stores the parent/child hierarchy tree |
| `company_team` | Team/sub-unit records |
| `company_roles` | Defined roles within a company |
| `company_permissions` | Permissions per role |
| `company_credit` | Credit limit and balance per company (module-company-credit) |

### Company Fields (Admin Form)

```
Company Information
-------------------
Company Name:          *required
Company Legal Name:
Company Email:         *required (contact email, not admin user email)
VAT/TAX ID:
Reseller ID:
Comment:

Company Admin
-------------
Job Title:
Email:                 *required (creates/links customer account)
First Name / Last Name:
Gender:

Company Legal Address
---------------------
Street, City, State, Zip, Country, Phone

Company Settings
----------------
Sales Representative:  (Admin user assigned to manage this company)

Advanced Settings
-----------------
Customer Group / Shared Catalog:
Allow to Exceed Credit Limit: [Yes / No]
Credit Currency:
Credit Limit:
```

---

## 3. Company Status Lifecycle

A company account moves through a defined set of statuses.

```
  [Registration Submitted]
           |
           v
       +-------------------+
       | Pending Approval   |  <-- default on creation from storefront
       +-------------------+
           |
     Admin Reviews
           |
     /-----+------\
    /               \
   v                 v
+--------+      +----------+
| Active |      | Rejected |  <-- permanent denial
+--------+      +----------+
    |
    |  Admin can block
    v
+---------+
| Blocked |  <-- temporary suspension, can be re-activated
+---------+
```

### Status Definitions

| Status | Constant | Value | Description | User Can Log In? | Orders Possible? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Pending Approval** | STATUS_PENDING | 0 | Awaiting admin review | No | No |
| **Active** | STATUS_APPROVED | 1 | Fully operational | Yes | Yes |
| **Rejected** | STATUS_REJECTED | 2 | Registration denied | No | No |
| **Blocked** | STATUS_BLOCKED | 3 | Temporarily suspended | No | No |

> **Note:** The UI label is "Active" but the internal constant is `STATUS_APPROVED`. The UI label for Pending is "Pending Approval" (not just "Pending"). These labels are defined in Model/Company/Source/Status.php.

> **Exam focus:** There are exactly **4 company statuses**: Pending Approval, Active, Rejected, Blocked. "Inactive" is *not* a valid company status. A **Blocked** company can be re-activated; **Rejected** is permanent (though an admin can change the status back manually if needed). Users of a Blocked/Rejected/Pending company **cannot log in**.

### Status Change Email Notifications

| Event | Email Sent To |
|---|---|
| Company created (Pending) | Company Admin + Store Admin |
| Status → Active | Company Admin |
| Status → Rejected | Company Admin |
| Status → Blocked | Company Admin |

---

## 4. Company Admin User & User Management

### Company Admin

- One **Company Admin** per company (can be changed by the store admin)
- The Company Admin is a **customer account** — it appears in `Customers > All Customers`
- Has access to the **My Company** section in the storefront
- Can manage: company users, roles, permissions, company profile, credit info (view only)

> **Exam focus:** The Company Admin manages the company from the **storefront**, not the Admin panel. Store admins manage companies from `Customers > Companies` in the Admin.

### Roles and Permissions

The Company Admin can create roles with granular permissions:

```
Default Roles (out of box)
--------------------------
Default User  -- minimal permissions
```

**Permission Tree Structure (examples):**

```
Company                         [Allow/Deny]
  |- Account Information        [Allow/Deny]
  |- Users & Structure          [Allow/Deny]
  |- Payment Information        [Allow/Deny]
  |- Credit Information         [Allow/Deny]
  |- Purchase Order Approval    [Allow/Deny]

Quotes                          [Allow/Deny]

Order History                   [Allow/Deny]
  |- View All Orders            [Allow/Deny]
  |- View Own Orders            [Allow/Deny]

Requisition Lists               [Allow/Deny]
```

### Hierarchical Purchase Order Approval

When **Purchase Orders** are enabled:

```
User (submits PO)
      |
      v
Supervisor in hierarchy (approves/rejects)
      |
      v (if above limit)
Company Admin (final approval)
      |
      v
Order placed
```

> **Exam focus:** Approval rules are based on **order amount thresholds** (grand_total, shipping_incl_tax, number_of_skus) and **company hierarchy position**. A user higher in the hierarchy can approve orders from users below them. Approval rules are configured by the Company Admin in the storefront.

---

## 5. Company Credit: Limits & Terms

Company Credit allows B2B companies to purchase on **Net terms** (pay later).

### Credit Configuration

**Admin path:** `Customers > Companies > [Edit Company] > Company Credit`

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Credit Currency | Currency for the credit account |
| Credit Limit | Maximum outstanding balance allowed |
| Allow to Exceed Credit Limit | Override flag (Yes/No) |
| Available Credit | Credit Limit - Outstanding Balance |
| Outstanding Balance | Sum of unpaid invoices |

### Credit Operations

```
Credit Limit = $10,000
      |
      |-- Purchase on Account ($2,000 order)
      v
Outstanding Balance = $2,000
Available Credit    = $8,000
      |
      |-- Payment Received ($2,000)
      v
Outstanding Balance = $0
Available Credit    = $10,000
```

### Payment Terms (Net Terms)

- Companies can pay using **Payment on Account** method (payment code: `companycredit`)
- This is the B2B equivalent of **Net 30 / Net 60** terms
- **Admin path:** `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > Payment on Account` (section=payment, group=companycredit)
- Default: disabled (`active=0`), payment action: `authorize_capture`, offline payment method

> **Exam focus:** Company credit is a **company-level** concept — all users in a company share the same credit pool. Individual users cannot have separate credit limits. Credit reimbursement (partial payments) is tracked in `Customers > Companies > [Company] > Credit History`.

---

## 6. Shared Catalog: Core Concepts

A **Shared Catalog** is a scoped product catalog that defines:
1. **Which products** a company can see and purchase
2. **What prices** (custom tier pricing) those products carry

> **Exam focus:** Shared Catalog controls **both visibility AND pricing**. A product not in a company's shared catalog is **completely invisible** — it returns no search results, doesn't appear in categories, and cannot be accessed by direct URL. It is not merely "unpriced."

### How Shared Catalog Works

```
Standard Catalog (All Products)
         |
         | filtered by
         v
  Shared Catalog
  +----------------------------+
  | Assigned Products          |  <-- subset of catalog
  | Custom Prices per product  |  <-- overrides standard prices
  | Assigned Categories        |  <-- controls navigation visibility
  +----------------------------+
         |
         | assigned to
         v
  Company Account(s)
         |
         v
  Company Users see ONLY these products at THESE prices
```

### Admin Path

```
Catalog > Shared Catalogs
```

---

## 7. Shared Catalog Types: Public vs Custom

This is one of the **most tested** areas. Understanding the distinction is critical.

### The Two Types

| Attribute | Public Shared Catalog (TYPE_PUBLIC=1) | Custom Shared Catalog (TYPE_CUSTOM=0) |
|---|---|---|
| **Who sees it** | All guests + logged-in non-company customers | Only assigned company/companies |
| **Quantity** | Exactly **one** Public catalog (system-wide, enforced by validation) | Unlimited Custom catalogs |
| **Replaces** | The standard B2C default catalog | N/A — adds a B2B layer |
| **Deletion** | Cannot be deleted | Can be deleted |
| **Default pricing** | Uses standard catalog prices | Uses custom B2B prices |
| **Scope** | Global (all non-company users) | Per-company |

> **Note:** If you try to create a second Public catalog, the admin shows a confirmation: "A public shared catalog already exists. If you proceed, the existing public shared catalog will be converted to a custom catalog." (SharedCatalogValidator.php, shared_catalog_form.xml)

### Public Shared Catalog = The B2C Storefront

```
When Shared Catalog is ENABLED:

  Guest / Regular Customer             Company User
  +-------------------------+          +---------------------------+
  | Sees: Public Catalog    |          | Sees: Custom Catalog      |
  | (IS the default catalog)|          | (assigned to their company|
  | Prices: standard/tier   |          | Prices: custom B2B prices |
  +-------------------------+          +---------------------------+
```

> **Exam focus:** The **Public Shared Catalog IS the default catalog** for all non-B2B visitors. When Shared Catalog is enabled, if you remove a product from the Public catalog, **guests cannot see it either**. This is a critical production consideration.

### Custom Shared Catalog = B2B Restricted View

- Created per business relationship
- Assigned to one or more companies
- A company can only be assigned to **one** shared catalog at a time
- Products outside the custom catalog are **completely invisible** to that company's users

> **Exam focus:** If a company has no shared catalog assigned, they default to the **Public shared catalog**. You must explicitly assign a Custom catalog to restrict them.

### Creating a Shared Catalog (Admin Flow)

```
Catalog > Shared Catalogs > Add Shared Catalog

Step 1: General Details
  Name:           "Acme Corp Pricing"
  Type:           Custom          <-- or Public
  Customer Tax Class: [Tax Class]
  Description:    optional

Step 2: Set Pricing and Structure
  (Assign categories and set custom prices)

Step 3: Assign Companies
  (Link to one or more company accounts)
```

> **Note:** "Set Pricing and Structure" and "Generate Catalog" are the exact UI labels confirmed in the codebase (Actions.php, pricing.js).

---

## 8. Shared Catalog Pricing & Indexing

### Custom Price Configuration

Prices in a custom shared catalog can be set in two ways:

1. **Flat custom price** — absolute dollar amount per product
2. **Percentage discount** — X% off the original price

```
Product: SKU-001
Original Price: $100.00

Custom Catalog Pricing Options:
  Option A: Fixed Price = $75.00
  Option B: 25% discount = $75.00 (calculated)
```

You can also set **tier prices** within a shared catalog:

```
Qty 1+:   $75.00
Qty 10+:  $65.00
Qty 50+:  $55.00
```

> **Exam focus:** Shared catalog **custom prices override** standard tier prices for assigned companies. The company user will NEVER see the standard storefront price — they see only the shared catalog price.

### Indexing for Shared Catalogs

Shared Catalog does **not** have its own dedicated indexer. Instead, it integrates with existing indexers via mview subscriptions (module-shared-catalog/etc/mview.xml):

| What Changes | Triggers Indexer | Via Table Subscription |
|---|---|---|
| Product assignments to catalog | `catalogpermissions_product` | `shared_catalog_product_item` |
| Category assignments to catalog | `catalogpermissions_category` | `sharedcatalog_category_permissions` |
| Product assignments (search) | `catalogsearch_fulltext` | `shared_catalog_product_item` |
| Custom pricing changes | `catalog_product_price` | Via customer group tier prices |

**Database tables** (module-shared-catalog/etc/db_schema.xml):

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `shared_catalog` | Shared catalog entity (name, type, customer_group_id, etc.) |
| `shared_catalog_product_item` | Product SKU assignments per catalog (customer_group_id, sku) |
| `sharedcatalog_category_permissions` | Category permission overrides per catalog |

```bash
# After shared catalog changes, reindex the relevant indexers:
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogpermissions_category
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogpermissions_product
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalog_product_price
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogsearch_fulltext
bin/magento cache:flush

# Or reindex everything:
bin/magento indexer:reindex
```

> **Important correction:** There is NO `sharedcatalog_product_price` indexer. The notes' original claim about a separate shared catalog price indexer was incorrect. Shared catalog pricing flows through the standard `catalog_product_price` indexer via customer group tier prices, and product visibility flows through the `catalogpermissions_product` and `catalogpermissions_category` indexers.

### Price Resolution Order (for Company Users)

```
When a company user views a product price:

1. Is Shared Catalog enabled?           NO --> Standard price logic
                |
               YES
                |
2. Does user's company have a 
   Custom catalog assigned?             NO --> Use Public catalog prices
                |
               YES
                |
3. Is this product in the custom catalog?  NO --> Product INVISIBLE (404)
                |
               YES
                |
4. Does the catalog have a custom price?   NO --> Use product's original price
                |
               YES
                |
5. Display custom catalog price (tier rules apply)
```

### Category Visibility in Shared Catalogs

A shared catalog also controls **category navigation**:

- Categories can be **included or excluded** from a shared catalog
- If a category has NO products assigned to the catalog, **the category is hidden** from navigation
- Even if a category is "assigned," only its catalog-assigned products are visible within it

> **Exam focus:** Assigning a **category** to a shared catalog does NOT automatically assign all its products. Products must be assigned **individually** (or via mass action). A category with zero assigned products will not appear in the company user's navigation.

---

## 9. Company → Shared Catalog Assignment

### Assignment Methods

**Method 1: From the Shared Catalog**
```
Catalog > Shared Catalogs > [Edit Catalog] > Assign Companies
  - Search for companies
  - Select and Save
```

**Method 2: From the Company Record**
```
Customers > Companies > [Edit Company] > Advanced Settings
  - Customer Group / Shared Catalog: [dropdown]
  - Select catalog > Save
```

> **Exam focus:** Company-to-Catalog assignment is **bidirectional** — you can set it from either the company record or the shared catalog record. The result is identical. Under the hood, this updates the company's **customer group** assignment.

### Shared Catalog and Customer Groups

This is a key architectural detail:

```
When you create a Shared Catalog, a corresponding 
Customer Group is automatically created.

Shared Catalog "Acme Corp Pricing"
    |
    +-- auto-creates Customer Group "Acme Corp Pricing"
    |       (via CustomerGroupManagement::createCustomerGroupForSharedCatalog)
    |
    v
Company users are assigned to this Customer Group
    |
    v
Price rules, tax rules use Customer Group as usual
```

> **Exam focus:** **Every shared catalog has a 1:1 corresponding customer group**. This is how pricing scoping works internally — the shared catalog wraps the customer group concept. You can see these customer groups in `Customers > Customer Groups`. They will be labeled with the catalog name. Do NOT delete these groups manually — delete the shared catalog itself to clean up properly.

### What Happens When You Assign a Custom Catalog to a Company

```
Before Assignment:
  Company "Acme Corp"
  Customer Group: General (default)
  Sees: Public Shared Catalog products

After Assigning "Acme Corp Pricing" Custom Catalog:
  Company "Acme Corp"
  Customer Group: "Acme Corp Pricing" (auto-switched)
  Sees: ONLY products in "Acme Corp Pricing" catalog
  Price: Custom B2B prices from catalog
```

---

## 10. Product Visibility Rules (The Tricky Part)

This section covers the exam traps around product visibility.

### Core Rule

> A product **not assigned** to a company's shared catalog is **completely invisible** to that company — it does not appear in search, categories, or via direct URL. It is not "visible but unpriced." It is **gone**.

### Visibility Behavior Matrix

| Product Status | In Public Catalog | In Custom Catalog (Company) | Guest Sees? | Company User Sees? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enabled | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Enabled | Yes | No | Yes | **No** |
| Enabled | No | Yes | **No** | Yes |
| Enabled | No | No | No | No |
| Disabled | Any | Any | No | No |

> **Exam focus:** Row 3 is the key B2B pattern — a product can be **B2B exclusive** by putting it in a Custom catalog but NOT in the Public catalog. Guests/regular customers cannot see it; only the assigned company can.

### The "Direct URL" Trap

```
Product URL: https://store.com/catalog/product/view/id/42

Company User (custom catalog, product NOT assigned):
  --> 404 Not Found (or redirect to homepage)
```
