```
  --> NOT a "403 Forbidden" — the product simply doesn't exist
      in their catalog context
```

> **Exam focus:** Direct URL access to a product not in a company's catalog returns a **404**, not a price-less page. This is tested conceptually — products are **invisible**, not merely unpriced.

### Shared Catalog vs Category Permissions

| Feature | Shared Catalog | Category Permissions |
|---|---|---|
| Availability | Adobe Commerce B2B only | Adobe Commerce EE only (both are EE) |
| Scope | Per company (via shared catalog) | Per customer group |
| Product level control | Yes | No (category level only) |
| Custom pricing | Yes | No |

> **Important correction:** Category Permissions is **EE-only** (module-catalog-permissions has proprietary license), NOT available in all editions. Both Shared Catalog and Category Permissions require Adobe Commerce EE. In fact, enabling Shared Catalog **automatically enables Category Permissions** as a dependency.

> **Exam focus:** Shared Catalog is more **granular** than standard Category Permissions. You get product-level visibility AND custom pricing, scoped per company.

---

## 11. Hands-On Walkthrough

### Step 1: Enable B2B Features

```
Admin > Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features
  Enable Company:        Yes
  Enable Shared Catalog: Yes   (only visible after Company = Yes)
  Save Config
```

> **Important:** Enabling Shared Catalog also enables Category Permissions for all stores. This is an automatic side effect.

```bash
bin/magento cache:flush
bin/magento indexer:reindex
```

### Step 2: Create a Company

```
Admin > Customers > Companies > Add New Company

Company Name:  "Acme Corporation"
Company Email: contact@acme.com

Company Admin:
  Email:      john.doe@acme.com
  First Name: John
  Last Name:  Doe

Status: Active  <-- set immediately for testing

Save Company
```

**Verify:** Check `Customers > All Customers` — John Doe should appear as a customer with company association.

### Step 3: Create a Custom Shared Catalog

```
Admin > Catalog > Shared Catalogs > Add Shared Catalog

Name:             "Acme B2B Catalog"
Type:             Custom
Customer Tax Class: Retail Customer
Description:      Custom pricing for Acme Corp

Save
```

### Step 4: Assign Categories and Products

```
Catalog > Shared Catalogs > [Edit "Acme B2B Catalog"] 
  > Set Pricing and Structure

Left panel: Category tree
  - Check "Electronics" category          <-- includes category
  - Uncheck "Clothing" category           <-- restricts category

Right panel: Product list for selected category
  - Select specific SKUs to include
  - Or: Select All in category

Click "Next: Set Pricing"
```

### Step 5: Set Custom Prices

```
For each assigned product:
  Method: Discount (%)
  Value:  20          <-- 20% off list price

Or per-product override:
  SKU-001: $85.00 fixed
  SKU-002: $120.00 fixed

Click "Generate Catalog"
```

### Step 6: Assign Company to Catalog

```
Catalog > Shared Catalogs > [Edit "Acme B2B Catalog"]
  > Assign Companies

Search: "Acme"
Select: Acme Corporation
Click: Save
```

### Step 7: Reindex

```bash
# Reindex relevant indexers (no sharedcatalog_product_price — use these):
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogpermissions_product
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogpermissions_category
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalog_product_price
bin/magento cache:flush
```

### Step 8: Verify from Company User Perspective

1. Open a **private/incognito browser window**
2. Navigate to your store
3. Log in as `john.doe@acme.com`
4. Browse to Electronics category — should see only assigned products at B2B prices
5. Browse to Clothing category — should be **invisible** in navigation
6. Attempt direct URL to a Clothing product — should get 404
7. Verify prices show the custom B2B discount

```
Expected Navigation (Company User):
  Home > Electronics > [only assigned products]
  (no Clothing link visible)

Expected Navigation (Guest):
  Home > Electronics > [all enabled products]
         > Clothing  > [all enabled products]
```

### Step 9: Test Price Override

```
Product: SKU-001
Standard Price: $100.00
Custom B2B Price: $80.00 (20% off)

Guest sees:    $100.00
Acme user sees: $80.00
```

---

## 12. Common Pitfalls & Exam Traps

### Pitfall 1: Forgetting to Reindex After Catalog Changes

```bash
# Reindex the relevant indexers after shared catalog changes:
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogpermissions_product
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogpermissions_category
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalog_product_price
bin/magento cache:flush
```

> **Note:** There is no `sharedcatalog_product_price` indexer. Shared catalog pricing is handled through the standard `catalog_product_price` indexer via customer group tier prices. Product visibility is handled through `catalogpermissions_product` and `catalogpermissions_category`.

### Pitfall 2: Thinking Products Are "Unpriced" Rather Than "Invisible"

```
WRONG assumption: "The company user sees the product but can't buy it"
CORRECT:          "The company user cannot see the product at all"
```

### Pitfall 3: Confusing Public Catalog with "All Products"

```
WRONG: "Guests see all products when Shared Catalog is enabled"
CORRECT: "Guests see only products in the Public Shared Catalog"

If you enable Shared Catalog and don't add products to Public catalog,
guests see NOTHING.
```

### Pitfall 4: Assigning Categories ≠ Assigning Products

```
WRONG: "Assigning Electronics category adds all Electronics products"
CORRECT: Categories and products must be assigned separately.
         An empty category (no assigned products) won't appear in nav.
```

### Pitfall 5: Assuming One Shared Catalog Per Store

```
WRONG: "There can only be one shared catalog"
CORRECT: One PUBLIC catalog (system limit, enforced by SharedCatalogValidator)
         Unlimited CUSTOM catalogs
         But each company can only be assigned ONE catalog at a time
```

### Pitfall 6: Manually Deleting Customer Groups

```
WRONG: Deleting the auto-generated customer group for a shared catalog
CORRECT: Delete the shared catalog itself; it will clean up its group
         Manual group deletion = broken catalog pricing
```

### Pitfall 7: Company Status Confusion

```
WRONG: "A Blocked company's orders are cancelled"
CORRECT: Blocking prevents future logins. Existing orders are unaffected.

WRONG: "Rejected is the same as Blocked"
CORRECT: Rejected = permanent denial (can be manually changed)
         Blocked  = temporary suspension (easily re-activated)
```

### Pitfall 8: Company Admin vs Store Admin

```
WRONG: "Company Admin logs into the Magento Admin panel"
CORRECT: Company Admin manages their company from the STOREFRONT
         Only store admins use the Admin panel for company management
```

### Pitfall 9: Forgetting Shared Catalog Enables Category Permissions

```
WRONG: "Shared Catalog only affects B2B users"
CORRECT: Enabling Shared Catalog also enables Category Permissions for ALL stores.
         This affects the entire storefront, not just B2B users.
```

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### B2B Module Basics
- [ ] B2B is **Adobe Commerce EE only** — not available in Open Source
- [ ] Enable order: `Magento_Company` must be enabled before `Magento_SharedCatalog`
- [ ] B2B enabled via `Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features` (section=btob)
- [ ] Requisition list module is `Magento_RequisitionList` (not `Magento_Requisition`)
- [ ] Enabling Shared Catalog **also enables Category Permissions** for all stores

### Company Account
- [ ] 4 statuses: **Pending Approval** (0), **Active** (1), **Rejected** (2), **Blocked** (3)
- [ ] Internal constant for Active is `STATUS_APPROVED`; UI label is "Active"
- [ ] Pending Approval = default on storefront registration; Active = fully operational
- [ ] Rejected = permanent (manual override possible); Blocked = temporary
- [ ] Blocked/Rejected/Pending users **cannot log in**
- [ ] Company Admin manages company from **storefront**, not Admin panel
- [ ] Sub-units and teams nest under the parent company
- [ ] Credit limit is **company-level**, not per-user
- [ ] All users in a company share one credit pool

### Company User Management
- [ ] Roles and permissions are created by the **Company Admin** in the storefront
- [ ] Hierarchical approval rules: higher-positioned users approve POs from below
- [ ] Approval rules based on order **amount thresholds** (grand_total, shipping_incl_tax, number_of_skus)

### Shared Catalog Types
- [ ] **Public** (TYPE_PUBLIC=1) = exactly one, system-wide, IS the default B2C/guest catalog
- [ ] **Custom** (TYPE_CUSTOM=0) = unlimited, assigned to specific companies, B2B only
- [ ] Enabling Shared Catalog without populating Public catalog = guests see nothing
- [ ] Each company can only be assigned to **one** shared catalog at a time
- [ ] Unassigned company defaults to **Public shared catalog**

### Product Visibility (Critical)
- [ ] Product NOT in a company's shared catalog = **completely invisible (404)**, not unpriced
- [ ] Products can be **B2B-exclusive** (in Custom catalog but not Public catalog)
- [ ] Assigning a **category** does NOT auto-assign its products
- [ ] A category with zero assigned products is **hidden from navigation**

### Pricing
- [ ] Shared catalog prices **override** standard tier prices for assigned companies
- [ ] Two pricing methods: **fixed price** or **percentage discount**
- [ ] Tier pricing is supported within shared catalogs

### Indexing (Corrected)
- [ ] There is **NO** `sharedcatalog_product_price` indexer — this does not exist
- [ ] Product visibility: `catalogpermissions_product` and `catalogpermissions_category` indexers (via mview subscriptions)
- [ ] Pricing: Standard `catalog_product_price` indexer (via customer group tier prices)
- [ ] Search: `catalogsearch_fulltext` indexer (subscribed to `shared_catalog_product_item`)
- [ ] Must reindex after any shared catalog pricing or assignment changes
- [ ] Database tables: `shared_catalog`, `shared_catalog_product_item`, `sharedcatalog_category_permissions`

### Customer Groups Integration
- [ ] Every shared catalog has a **1:1 auto-generated customer group**
- [ ] Assigning company to catalog = switching company's customer group
- [ ] Do NOT manually delete shared-catalog-generated customer groups

### Assignment
- [ ] Company-to-catalog assignment: via Shared Catalog > Assign Companies OR Company > Advanced Settings
- [ ] Both paths produce the same result
- [ ] After reassignment, **flush cache** and **reindex**

### Hands-On Verification
- [ ] Create company → set status Active
- [ ] Create Custom shared catalog → assign categories and products → set prices
- [ ] Assign company to catalog
- [ ] Reindex (catalogpermissions_product, catalogpermissions_category, catalog_product_price) + cache flush
- [ ] Verify in incognito as company user: restricted categories invisible, custom prices shown
- [ ] Verify guest user: unaffected (sees Public catalog)
- [ ] Test direct URL to restricted product: expect 404

flashcards.question: What editions of Adobe Commerce support B2B modules?
flashcards.answer: B2B modules are available exclusively in Adobe Commerce Enterprise Edition (EE). They are NOT available in Magento Open Source. B2B modules ship with the EE codebase and are enabled via configuration at Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features.
flashcards.hint: Think about the licensing tier that includes enterprise features.

flashcards.question: What happens automatically when you enable the Shared Catalog feature in Adobe Commerce B2B?
flashcards.answer: Enabling Shared Catalog automatically enables Category Permissions for all stores. This is a significant side effect because it immediately affects product visibility on the storefront — products not assigned to the Public catalog become invisible to guests.
flashcards.hint: There is an automatic dependency that impacts the entire storefront, not just B2B users.

flashcards.question: What are the four valid company statuses in Adobe Commerce B2B, and which ones prevent users from logging in?
flashcards.answer: The four statuses are Pending Approval (0), Active (1), Rejected (2), and Blocked (3). Users of Pending, Rejected, and Blocked companies cannot log in. Only Active company users can log in and place orders. 'Inactive' is NOT a valid company status.
flashcards.hint: There are exactly four statuses, and only one allows full storefront access.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between a Blocked and a Rejected company status in B2B?
flashcards.answer: Blocked is a temporary suspension that can be easily re-activated by changing the status back to Active. Rejected is a permanent denial of the company registration, though an admin can still manually change the status back to Active if needed. Both prevent users from logging in.
flashcards.hint: One is temporary, the other is intended to be permanent (but technically reversible).

flashcards.question: Where does a Company Admin manage their company — in the Admin panel or on the storefront?
flashcards.answer: The Company Admin manages their company from the storefront, not the Admin panel. They access the 'My Company' section in their customer account on the storefront. Only store admins (merchants) use the Admin panel to manage companies at Customers > Companies.
flashcards.hint: The Company Admin is a customer-level role, not an admin-panel role.

flashcards.question: How many types of Shared Catalog exist, and what are their key differences?
flashcards.answer: There are two types: Public (TYPE_PUBLIC=1) and Custom (TYPE_CUSTOM=0). There is exactly one Public catalog system-wide — it serves as the default catalog for guests and non-company customers. Custom catalogs are unlimited and assigned to specific companies for B2B pricing.
flashcards.hint: One type replaces the default guest catalog; the other creates private B2B views.

flashcards.question: What happens to a product that is NOT in a company's assigned Shared Catalog?
flashcards.answer: The product is completely invisible to that company's users — it does not appear in search results, category navigation, or via direct URL (returns 404). It is NOT merely 'unpriced' or shown without a price. The product simply does not exist in their catalog context.
flashcards.hint: Products are not just unpriced — they are entirely hidden from all access points.

flashcards.question: What is the relationship between a Shared Catalog and a Customer Group?
flashcards.answer: Every Shared Catalog has a 1:1 auto-generated Customer Group. When a company is assigned to a Shared Catalog, the company's customer group is automatically switched to the catalog's group. This is how pricing scoping works internally. You should never manually delete these auto-generated customer groups.
flashcards.hint: The Shared Catalog wraps an existing Magento concept to deliver scoped pricing.

flashcards.question: Does assigning a category to a Shared Catalog automatically include all its products?
flashcards.answer: No. Assigning a category to a Shared Catalog does NOT automatically assign all its products. Products must be assigned individually or via mass action. A category with zero assigned products will not appear in the company user's navigation.
flashcards.hint: Categories and products are separate assignments — one does not imply the other.

flashcards.question: How can you create a B2B-exclusive product that is invisible to guests but visible to a specific company?
flashcards.answer: Add the product to a Custom Shared Catalog assigned to the company, but do NOT add it to the Public Shared Catalog. Guests and regular customers (who see the Public catalog) will not see the product, but the assigned company's users will see it at custom B2B prices.
flashcards.hint: Control visibility by which catalog types include the product.

flashcards.question: How is company credit managed in B2B — at the user level or company level?
flashcards.answer: Company credit is managed at the company level, not per individual user. All users in a company share the same credit pool. Individual users cannot have separate credit limits. Credit reimbursement is tracked in Customers > Companies > [Company] > Credit History.
flashcards.hint: Think about credit as a shared resource for the entire organization.

flashcards.question: What are the two pricing methods available when setting custom prices in a Shared Catalog?
flashcards.answer: Prices can be set as a flat custom price (absolute dollar amount per product) or as a percentage discount (X% off the original price). Additionally, tier prices (quantity-based price breaks) can be configured within the shared catalog.
flashcards.hint: One method is absolute, the other is relative to the original price.

flashcards.question: Which module must be enabled before you can enable Shared Catalog in B2B configuration?
flashcards.answer: The Magento_Company module must be enabled before Magento_SharedCatalog. The 'Enable Shared Catalog' toggle in admin only appears when Company is set to Yes. This is a configuration dependency defined in system.xml with a <depends> on company_active=1.
flashcards.hint: There is a parent module that must be active first for the catalog feature to appear.

flashcards.question: What happens if you enable Shared Catalog but do not add any products to the Public catalog?
flashcards.answer: Guests and non-company customers will see NO products on the storefront. The Public Shared Catalog IS the default catalog for all non-B2B visitors, so if it contains no products, the storefront appears empty for guests.
flashcards.hint: The Public catalog replaces the standard product visibility for everyone not assigned to a custom catalog.

flashcards.question: How can company-to-catalog assignment be configured in the admin?
flashcards.answer: Assignment is bidirectional — you can set it from either direction: from the Shared Catalog record (Catalog > Shared Catalogs > Assign Companies) or from the Company record (Customers > Companies > Advanced Settings > Customer Group/Shared Catalog dropdown). Both methods produce the same result.
flashcards.hint: There are two equally valid admin paths to achieve the same assignment.

studyNotes.title: Day 16 — B2B: Negotiable Quotes, Requisition Lists & Quick Order
studyNotes.content:
# B2B: Negotiable Quotes, Requisition Lists & Quick Order
## Adobe Commerce B2B — Comprehensive Study Notes

---

## Table of Contents

1. [B2B Module Overview](#1-b2b-module-overview)
2. [Negotiable Quotes — Deep Dive](#2-negotiable-quotes--deep-dive)
   - [What Is a Negotiable Quote?](#what-is-a-negotiable-quote)
   - [Initiating a Quote](#initiating-a-quote)
   - [Quote States (Lifecycle)](#quote-states-lifecycle)
   - [Seller Actions in a Quote](#seller-actions-in-a-quote)
   - [Quote Expiry Dates](#quote-expiry-dates)
   - [Quote Comments and History](#quote-comments-and-history)
   - [Negotiable Quotes vs. Shared Catalog Pricing](#negotiable-quotes-vs-shared-catalog-pricing)
3. [Requisition Lists](#3-requisition-lists)
   - [What Is a Requisition List?](#what-is-a-requisition-list)
   - [Creating and Managing Lists](#creating-and-managing-lists)
   - [Adding Items to a Requisition List](#adding-items-to-a-requisition-list)
   - [Converting to Cart](#converting-to-cart)
4. [Quick Order](#4-quick-order)
   - [SKU-Based Entry](#sku-based-entry)
   - [CSV Upload Option](#csv-upload-option)
5. [Purchase Order Approval Workflows](#5-purchase-order-approval-workflows)
   - [Company Rules and Roles](#company-rules-and-roles)
   - [Approval Matrix](#approval-matrix)
6. [Full Negotiable Quote Flow — Hands-On Walkthrough](#6-full-negotiable-quote-flow--hands-on-walkthrough)
7. [Tricky Concepts & Exam Traps](#7-tricky-concepts--exam-traps)
8. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. B2B Module Overview

Adobe Commerce B2B is an **add-on module suite** available exclusively on **Adobe Commerce (Enterprise Edition)**. It is NOT available on Magento Open Source.

### Core B2B Features Enabled Per Module

| Feature | Module | UI Dependency (depends) |
|---|---|---|
| Company Accounts | `Magento_Company` | — |
| Shared Catalog | `Magento_SharedCatalog` | Company |
| Negotiable Quotes | `Magento_NegotiableQuote` | Company |
| Requisition Lists | `Magento_RequisitionList` | — (no `depends` on Company in system.xml) |
| Quick Order | `Magento_QuickOrder` | — |
| Purchase Orders | `Magento_PurchaseOrder` | Company |
| Payment on Account | `Magento_CompanyCredit` | Company |

> **Exam focus:** Negotiable Quotes, Shared Catalog, and Purchase Orders require the **Company** module to be enabled — their admin toggles only appear when Company is active. Requisition Lists and Quick Order can be enabled independently.

### Enabling B2B Features

```xml
<!-- app/etc/config.php excerpt (modules enabled) -->
'Magento_B2b' => 1,
'Magento_NegotiableQuote' => 1,
'Magento_RequisitionList' => 1,
'Magento_QuickOrder' => 1,
'Magento_PurchaseOrder' => 1,
```

**Admin path:** `Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features` (section id=`btob`, tab=`general`)

```
B2B Features Panel (group: website_configuration)
--------------------------------------------------
Enable Company:          [Yes]
Enable Shared Catalog:   [Yes]   (only visible when Company = Yes)
Enable B2B Quote:        [Yes]   (only visible when Company = Yes)
Enable Quick Order:      [Yes]
Enable Requisition List: [Yes]

Order Approval Configuration (separate group: order_approval)
--------------------------------------------------------------
Enable Purchase Orders:  [Yes]   (only visible when Company = Yes)
```

> **Note:** "Enable Purchase Orders" is in its own **"Order Approval Configuration"** group under the same B2B Features section, separate from the other toggles. It is NOT listed alongside the other toggles in the main panel.

> **Exam focus:** Each B2B feature has its own toggle in `Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features`. Shared Catalog **requires** Company to be enabled (its toggle only appears when Company is active). Enabling Shared Catalog also **automatically enables Category Permissions** for all stores.

---

## 2. Negotiable Quotes — Deep Dive

### What Is a Negotiable Quote?

A **Negotiable Quote** is a formal price negotiation mechanism where a **buyer** (company user) requests a custom price agreement from a **seller** (merchant/admin). The resulting agreed price can be **lower than any catalog price**, including shared catalog prices.

```
  BUYER                        SELLER (Admin)
  ------                       --------------
  Cart -> Request Quote        Receives Quote in Admin
        |                             |
        v                             v
  Quote Created (Draft)         Reviews & Adjusts
        |                       - Line item prices
        v                       - Shipping discount
  Submitted to Seller          - Overall discount %
        |                       - Expiry date
        v                             |
  Seller Responds <-----------  Sends Back to Buyer
        |
        v
  Buyer Reviews & Accepts
        |
        v
  Converts to ORDER
```

> **Exam focus:** A negotiable quote is NOT a regular cart. It is a **separate quote entity** stored in `negotiable_quote` and related tables (which extend the standard `quote` table via foreign key), not the standard `quote` table alone.

---

### Initiating a Quote

A buyer can initiate a negotiable quote from **two places**:

#### 1. From the Shopping Cart
```
My Cart > [Request a Quote] button
```
- Buyer adds items to cart
- Clicks **"Request a Quote"**
- Optionally adds a comment/message to the seller
- Quote is created in `Draft` state briefly, then moves to `Submitted`

#### 2. From a Saved Quote (Re-submission)
- Buyer can reopen a previously `Declined` or `Expired` quote
- Modify items or comments
- Re-submit for a new round of negotiation

> **Exam focus:** The **"Request a Quote"** button only appears if:
> - The buyer is logged in as a **company user**
> - The B2B Quote feature is **enabled**
> - The company has **"Allow Quotes"** enabled (this is a **company-level configuration toggle** set in admin under Customers > Companies > [Company] > Settings, NOT an ACL role permission)

---

### Quote States (Lifecycle)

This is one of the **most heavily tested** areas of B2B. The buyer sees **9 distinct frontend labels**, though internally Magento uses **11 status constants** (some share the same frontend label).

```
                    +----------+
      Buyer         |  DRAFT   |  (transient, rarely seen)
      Initiates     +----+-----+
                         |
                         v
                    +----+-----+
      Buyer sends   |SUBMITTED |  <-- Buyer has sent, waiting on seller
                    +----+-----+
                         |
               +---------+---------+
               |                   |
               v                   v
         +-----+----+        +-----+----+
         |  PENDING |        | DECLINED |  <-- Seller rejects
         +-----+----+        +----------+
               |
               v
         +-----+-----+
         |   OPEN    |  <-- Seller is actively editing
         +-----+-----+
               |
               v
         +-----+-----+
         |  UPDATED  |  <-- Seller has responded, waiting on buyer
         +-----+-----+
               |
         +-----+-----+
         |  (Buyer   |
         |  Reviews) |
         +-----+-----+
               |
       +-------+--------+
       |                |
       v                v
 +-----+-----+    +-----+------+
 |  ORDERED  |    |   CLOSED   |
 +-----------+    +------------+
                       ^
                       |
                  +----+----+
                  | EXPIRED |  <-- Past expiry date, not converted
                  +---------+
```

#### Complete State Reference Table

| Frontend Label | Internal Status Constant(s) | Who Acts | Meaning | Buyer Can Act? | Seller Can Act? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Draft** | `STATUS_DRAFT_BY_ADMIN`, `STATUS_DRAFT_BY_CUSTOMER` | System/Buyer | Quote created, not yet submitted | Yes (edit) | No |
| **Submitted** | `STATUS_CREATED`, `STATUS_SUBMITTED_BY_CUSTOMER` | Buyer | Buyer has sent quote request | No | Yes |
| **Pending** | `STATUS_PROCESSING_BY_ADMIN` | System | Seller is reviewing (shown as "Pending" to buyer) | No | Yes |
| **Open** | `STATUS_PROCESSING_BY_CUSTOMER` | Seller | Buyer is reviewing seller's response (shown as "Open" to buyer) | Yes | No |
| **Updated** | `STATUS_SUBMITTED_BY_ADMIN` | Seller | Seller responded, sent back to buyer | Yes | No |
| **Ordered** | `STATUS_ORDERED` | System | Quote converted to order | No | No (terminal) |
| **Closed** | `STATUS_CLOSED` | Buyer/Seller | Manually closed, no order | No | No (terminal) |
| **Declined** | `STATUS_DECLINED` | Seller | Seller rejected the quote | Buyer can duplicate | No (terminal) |
| **Expired** | `STATUS_EXPIRED` | System (cron) | Passed expiry date | Buyer can re-request | No (terminal) |

> **Note:** Internally there are **11 status constants** in `NegotiableQuoteInterface.php` (plus `STATUS_TEMPLATE_QUOTE` for quote templates). Multiple internal statuses map to the same frontend label — e.g., both `STATUS_CREATED` and `STATUS_SUBMITTED_BY_CUSTOMER` display as "Submitted" on the storefront. The backend admin sees different labels (e.g., `STATUS_CREATED` shows as "New" in admin but "Submitted" on storefront).

> **Exam focus:** **Terminal states** are `Ordered`, `Closed`, `Declined`, and `Expired`. A quote in a terminal state **cannot be re-opened** — but a buyer CAN duplicate/re-submit a declined or expired quote as a **new** quote.

> **Exam focus:** The `Pending` state (internal: `STATUS_PROCESSING_BY_ADMIN`) is the state where the **seller has the quote for review**. Shown as "Open" in the admin backend but "Pending" to the buyer.

---

### Seller Actions in a Quote

When a seller opens a submitted quote in the Admin (`Sales > Quotes`), they can perform the following adjustments:

#### 1. Line Item Price Adjustments
```
For each product in the quote, three discount types:
- Percentage Discount (type 1): Apply a percentage off the catalog price
- Amount Discount (type 2): Apply a fixed dollar amount discount
- Proposed Price (type 3): Set a specific proposed price per line item
- Remove items from the quote
```

#### 2. Shipping Adjustments
```
- Propose a specific shipping price
- Offer free shipping
- Select a shipping method for the buyer
```

#### 3. Quote-Level Discount
```
Three discount types (same as line items):
- Percentage Discount (type 1): Percentage discount applied to entire quote subtotal
- Amount Discount (type 2): Fixed amount discount on the quote
- Proposed Total (type 3): Set a specific proposed total for the entire quote
  (Note: Using Proposed Total at quote level disables individual line item discounts)
```

#### 4. Expiry Date
```
- Set a date after which the quote automatically expires
- Displayed prominently to buyer on storefront
```

#### 5. Comments
```
- Internal notes (not visible to buyer)
- External comments (visible to buyer in conversation thread)
```

#### Seller Response Actions

| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| **Send** | Sends quote back to buyer (`Updated` state) |
| **Save as Draft** | Saves seller edits without sending |
| **Decline** | Rejects quote (`Declined` state) |
| **Close** | Closes quote (`Closed` state) |

> **Exam focus:** A seller can set a **proposed shipping price** in a negotiable quote. This overrides the standard shipping rate calculation for that quote. Both line-item and quote-level discounts support **three types**: Percentage, Amount, and Proposed Price/Total.

---

### Quote Expiry Dates

- Set by the **seller** during negotiation
- Stored as `expiration_period` on the `negotiable_quote` record
- A **cron job** runs daily at midnight to check expiry dates
- When the current date passes the expiry date, the quote state changes to **`Expired`**
- The buyer receives a **notification email** when a quote expires

```
Admin: Sales > Quotes > [Quote] > Expiration Date field
                                    |
                          +----------v-----------+
                          | Date Picker (e.g.,   |
                          | YYYY-MM-DD)          |
                          +---------------------+
                          Visible to buyer on
                          storefront quote detail
```

> **Exam focus:** Expired quotes **cannot be directly re-activated**. The buyer must **create a new quote** or **duplicate** the expired one. Duplication copies items but creates a fresh quote in `Draft` state.

> **Exam focus:** Quote expiry is enforced by the **`backend_expire_date`** cron job (class `Magento\NegotiableQuote\Cron\ExpireQuote`, runs daily at midnight). If cron is not running, quotes will not auto-expire.

---

### Quote Comments and History

#### Comment Thread
Negotiable Quotes have a **conversation history** similar to a support ticket:

```
Quote Detail Page (Storefront / Admin)
--------------------------------------
[Buyer - Jan 10]  "Can you offer a better price on 50 units?"
[Seller - Jan 11] "We can offer $45/unit for orders over 50."
[Buyer - Jan 12]  "Accepted. Please confirm by Jan 20."
```

- Both buyer and seller see the **full conversation**
- Each comment is **timestamped** with the author
- Comments are stored in `negotiable_quote_comment` table

#### History Log
- Every **state change** is logged in the quote history
- Price changes are tracked
- Audit trail visible in Admin under the quote record

```
History Tab in Admin Quote Detail:
-----------------------------------
Jan 10 10:00  Status changed to: Submitted
Jan 11 09:30  Price updated for SKU-001: $60 -> $45
Jan 11 09:30  Status changed to: Updated
Jan 12 14:00  Status changed to: Ordered
```

> **Exam focus:** The quote history provides a complete **audit trail** of all changes. Sellers can add **internal-only comments** visible only in the admin, separate from buyer-visible comments.

---

### Negotiable Quotes vs. Shared Catalog Pricing

This is the **trickiest concept** in the entire B2B suite.

#### Price Hierarchy (Normal B2B)
```
Tier Price
    |
    v
Shared Catalog Price  <-- Set per customer group/company
    |
    v
Regular Catalog Price (MSRP)
```

#### Price Hierarchy With Negotiable Quote
```
Negotiable Quote Price  <-- CAN GO BELOW ALL OF THE ABOVE
    |
    v
Tier Price
    |
    v
Shared Catalog Price
    |
    v
Regular Catalog Price
```

**Key Principle:** A negotiable quote creates a **unique, one-time price agreement** that is **not constrained by any catalog pricing rule**, including:
- Shared catalog prices
- Tier prices
- Cart price rules
- Customer group discounts

> **Exam focus:** This is explicitly called out as a "tricky" concept. A quote price **bypasses all catalog pricing**. The seller can set any price — even $0 — for a line item in a negotiable quote. This is by design, allowing for fully custom B2B price negotiations.

> **Exam focus:** When a negotiable quote is converted to an order, the **negotiated prices are locked in** for that order. They do NOT re-validate against current catalog prices at checkout.

#### How It Works Technically
- Negotiable quote prices are stored in `negotiable_quote_item` table (columns: `original_price`, `negotiated_price_type`, `negotiated_price_value`)
- When the quote is converted to order, these prices are passed directly to the order/invoice
- Standard price processors are **bypassed** for quote-originated orders

---

## 3. Requisition Lists

### What Is a Requisition List?

A **Requisition List** is a **saved shopping list** that allows B2B buyers to store frequently purchased items for quick re-ordering. Think of it as a **named favorite/bookmark list for products**.

**Key characteristics:**
- A single buyer can have **multiple** requisition lists
- Default maximum: **999 lists per buyer** (configurable)
- Lists persist indefinitely (not cart-based, not session-based)
- Items in a list do NOT reflect current pricing — price is only calculated when added to cart

> **Exam focus:** Requisition Lists are **not carts**. They do not hold pricing or inventory until items are moved to the cart. Multiple lists per buyer are supported.

---

### Creating and Managing Lists

#### Storefront Navigation
```
My Account > My Requisition Lists
    |
    +-- [Create New List] --> Name (required), Description (optional)
    |
    +-- List: "Office Supplies"     [Edit] [Delete] [Add to Cart]
    +-- List: "Lab Equipment"       [Edit] [Delete] [Add to Cart]
    +-- List: "Monthly Consumables" [Edit] [Delete] [Add to Cart]
```

#### Admin Configuration
```
Stores > Configuration > Customers > Requisition Lists
(section=requisitionlist, tab=customer, group=general)
------------------------------------------------------
Number of Requisition Lists: [999]
```

> **Exam focus:** The number of requisition lists is **configurable** in admin (field label: "Number of Requisition Lists"). The default is **999**, minimum is **2**. A buyer can rename or delete lists but **cannot share lists** with other company users (lists are per-buyer via `customer_id`, not per-company).

---

### Adding Items to a Requisition List

Items can be added to a requisition list from **multiple locations**:

#### 1. Product Detail Page (PDP)
```
Product Page
    |
    +-- Select options (size, color, qty)
    +-- [Add to Requisition List v]
             |
             +-- Create New List
             +-- Office Supplies
             +-- Lab Equipment
```

#### 2. Category/Search Results Page
- Similar dropdown available on product listing tiles

#### 3. Previous Orders
```
My Account > My Orders > [Order Detail]
    |
    +-- [Add to Requisition List] on individual items or entire order
```

#### 4. Existing Cart
```
Shopping Cart > [Add All to Requisition List]
    or
Individual cart item > [Move to Requisition List]
```

#### 5. Another Requisition List
- Items can be **copied** between requisition lists

> **Exam focus:** Adding items from **previous orders** to a requisition list is a key B2B re-order workflow. This allows buyers to quickly rebuild recurring orders.

---

### Converting to Cart

```
My Requisition Lists > [List Name]
    |
    +-- Select items (checkboxes) or "Select All"
    +-- [Add to Cart]
         |
         v
    Items added to shopping cart
    with current pricing applied
         |
         v
    Standard checkout flow
         OR
    Request as Negotiable Quote
```

**Important behaviors:**
- Adding a requisition list to cart **does not remove** items from the list
- Items are **copied** to cart, not moved
- If a SKU is no longer available, the system will notify the buyer but skip that item

> **Exam focus:** Converting a requisition list to cart **does not empty the list**. The list remains intact for future use. This is different from a wishlist-to-cart behavior that some might assume.

---

## 4. Quick Order

### SKU-Based Entry

**Quick Order** allows buyers to bypass browsing and directly enter SKUs and quantities to place an order. Designed for buyers who **know exactly what they want**.

```
Storefront: Quick Order (link in header/navigation)
---------------------------------------------------
| SKU                | Qty | Status              |
|--------------------|-----|---------------------|
| SKU-001            |  5  | In Stock - $45.00   |
| SKU-XYZ            |  2  | In Stock - $120.00  |
| INVALID-SKU        |  1  | SKU not found (!)   |
| SKU-OUT            |  3  | Out of Stock (!)    |
|--------------------|-----|---------------------|
[Add More Rows]
[Add to Cart]  [Add to Requisition List]
```

**Features:**
- Real-time SKU validation as you type
- Inline error display for invalid/unavailable SKUs
- Can add multiple rows simultaneously
- Results can go to **Cart** or directly to a **Requisition List**

> **Exam focus:** Quick Order validates SKUs **in real time** via AJAX as the buyer types or tabs out of the SKU field. Invalid SKUs are flagged inline, not at submission.

> **Exam focus:** The **Quick Order** page is accessible to **both company users AND individual registered customers** (it does NOT require company membership, unlike Negotiable Quotes). However, it requires the Quick Order feature to be enabled.

---

### CSV Upload Option

For large orders, buyers can upload a **CSV file** instead of typing SKUs manually.

#### CSV Format
```csv
sku,qty
SKU-001,10
SKU-002,5
SKU-003,25
WIDGET-BLUE-LG,100
```

**Requirements:**
- File must be `.csv` format
- Column headers: `sku` and `qty` (case-sensitive, validated in `Magento\AdvancedCheckout\Model\Import`)
- One product per row
- Maximum rows: configurable (default allows large lists)

#### Upload Workflow
```
Quick Order Page
    |
    +-- [Upload CSV] tab/button
    +-- Browse for file > Upload
    +-- System validates each SKU
    +-- Invalid SKUs highlighted
    +-- [Add to Cart] / [Add to Requisition List]
```

> **Exam focus:** The CSV headers must be exactly `sku` and `qty`. The CSV upload is **not** a bulk import tool — it's a **buyer-facing** front-end feature to populate the quick order form.

> **Exam focus:** After uploading a CSV, the buyer still sees the **same validation interface** as manual entry. They can remove invalid rows or fix quantities before adding to cart.

---

## 5. Purchase Order Approval Workflows

### Company Rules and Roles

Adobe Commerce B2B supports a **Purchase Order (PO) approval workflow** that enforces spending controls at the company level.

#### How It Works — Overview
```
Buyer Places Order
       |
       v
  Is PO Approval Required?
  (Based on company rules)
       |
  +----+----+
  |         |
  No        Yes
  |         |
  v         v
Order    PO Created
Placed   (Pending Approval)
             |
             v
         Approver Reviews
         (Manager/Admin)
             |
         +---+---+
         |       |
      Approve  Reject
         |       |
         v       v
       Order   PO Rejected
       Placed  (Buyer notified)
```

#### Company User Roles
Company users are assigned **roles** with **permissions**:

```
Company Admin
    |
    +-- Sales Manager Role
    |       +-- Can approve POs up to $10,000
    |       +-- Can create quotes
    |
    +-- Buyer Role
    |       +-- Can create POs (requires approval > $500)
    |       +-- Can use Quick Order
    |
    +-- Viewer Role
            +-- Read-only access to orders
```

> **Exam focus:** Company **roles** control what users can **do**. Company **approval rules** control when **approvals are required**. These are two separate concepts.

---

### Approval Matrix

The approval matrix defines **when** a PO requires approval and **who** can approve it.

#### Rule Types

| Rule Type | Internal Key | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Order Total** | `grand_total` | Approval required if order exceeds amount | Orders > $1,000 need approval |
| **Shipping Cost** | `shipping_incl_tax` | Approval required if shipping exceeds amount | Shipping > $50 needs approval |
| **Number of SKUs** | `number_of_skus` | Approval required if SKU count exceeds limit | More than 10 SKUs needs approval |

#### Configuring Approval Rules

Approval rules are primarily managed by the **company admin on the storefront**, not in the merchant admin panel:

```
Storefront: My Account > Approval Rules (Company Admin only)

Rule: "Large Order Approval"
- Apply if: Order Total > $1,000.00
- Requires approval from: [Role: Sales Manager]
- OR requires approval from: [Specific User: john.manager@company.com]
```

> **Note:** The merchant admin panel does NOT have a "Purchase Order Approval Rules" section inside the company edit form. The merchant admin enables/disables Purchase Orders globally (`Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features > Order Approval Configuration`) and per-company (Customers > Companies > [Company] > Advanced Settings). The **company admin** creates and manages the actual approval rules on the **storefront**.

#### Approval Flow Example
```
Jane (Buyer) creates PO for $1,500
              |
              v
System checks approval rules
              |
              v
Rule matched: "Large Order Approval" (> $1,000)
              |
              v
PO Status: "Pending Approval"
John (Sales Manager) receives email notification
              |
              v
John logs in > My Account > Purchase Orders > Approval Required
              |
         +----+----+
         |         |
      Approve    Reject with comment
         |
         v
PO converts to Order automatically
(via message queue: purchaseorder.toorder)
Jane receives approval confirmation email
```

> **Exam focus:** When a PO is **approved**, it is **automatically converted to an order** via message queue — no further buyer action is needed. When **rejected**, the buyer receives a notification with the rejection comment and can **edit and resubmit** the PO.

> **Exam focus:** Company **Administrators** can always approve POs regardless of approval rule configuration. Approval rules apply to **non-admin company users**.

---

## 6. Full Negotiable Quote Flow — Hands-On Walkthrough

This section walks through the complete end-to-end negotiable quote process in Adobe Commerce EE.

### Step 1: Buyer — Initiate Quote Request

```
1. Log in as company buyer on storefront
2. Browse catalog and add items to cart:
   - SKU-001: Blue Widget x 50 @ $60.00 each
   - SKU-002: Red Widget x 25 @ $40.00 each
   Cart Total: $4,000.00

3. Navigate to Shopping Cart
4. Click "Request a Quote" button
5. In the quote form:
   - Name: "Q1 Bulk Order - Jan 2024"
   - Comment: "We are ordering 50+ units monthly.
                Can you offer volume pricing?
                Looking for ~20% discount."
6. Click "Send Request"

Result: Quote created, status = "Submitted"
        Buyer sees: "Your quote has been submitted."
        Admin notification email sent to seller.
```

### Step 2: Seller — Review and Respond in Admin

```
1. Admin logs in to Adobe Commerce backend
2. Navigate to: Sales > Quotes
3. Find quote: "Q1 Bulk Order - Jan 2024" (Status: New in admin / Submitted to buyer)
4. Open quote detail

--- Seller Reviews ---
Current prices (from shared catalog):
  SKU-001: $60.00 x 50 = $3,000.00
  SKU-002: $40.00 x 25 = $1,000.00
  Subtotal: $4,000.00

--- Seller Makes Adjustments ---
5. Line item: SKU-001
   Proposed Price: $48.00 (20% off $60)
   New line total: $2,400.00

6. Line item: SKU-002
   Proposed Price: $32.00 (20% off $40)
   New line total: $800.00

7. Shipping:
   Proposed Shipping Amount: $0.00 (Free shipping as incentive)

8. Quote-level discount: None (already discounted per-item)

9. Expiration Date: YYYY-MM-DD (30 days from today)

10. Seller Comment (visible to buyer):
    "Based on your monthly volume, we can offer 20% off
     and free shipping. This offer is valid for 30 days."

11. Click "Send" button

Result: Quote status changes to "Updated" (storefront) / "Submitted" (admin)
        Buyer receives email notification.
```

### Step 3: Buyer — Review Seller's Proposal

```
1. Buyer logs in to storefront
2. Navigates to: My Account > My Quotes
3. Opens quote: "Q1 Bulk Order - Jan 2024" (Status: Updated)

--- Buyer Reviews ---
Sees updated prices:
  SKU-001: $48.00 x 50 = $2,400.00  (was $3,000)
  SKU-002: $32.00 x 25 = $800.00    (was $1,000)
  Shipping: FREE                     (was $45)
  New Total: $3,200.00               (was $4,045)
  Savings: $845.00

Sees seller comment + expiry date: Feb 26, 2024

4. Buyer decides to negotiate further:
   Buyer Comment: "Thank you. Can we get SKU-001 at $45/unit
                   if we commit to a 3-month contract?"

5. Clicks "Submit" to send counter-offer

Result: Quote status: "Submitted" again
        Seller receives notification.
```

### Step 4: Seller — Final Counter-Offer

```
1. Seller opens quote again in Admin
2. Adjusts SKU-001 further:
   Proposed Price: $46.00 (best offer)
3. Adds internal note: "Cannot go below $46 — at margin floor"
4. Adds buyer-visible comment: "Our best price is $46/unit for SKU-001."
5. Clicks "Send"

Result: Quote status = "Updated" (storefront)
```

### Step 5: Buyer — Accept and Convert to Order

```
1. Buyer reviews final offer:
   SKU-001: $46.00 x 50 = $2,300.00
   SKU-002: $32.00 x 25 = $800.00
   Shipping: FREE
   Total: $3,100.00

2. Buyer clicks "Proceed to Checkout" on quote detail page
3. Checkout page pre-populated:
   - Items from quote (at negotiated prices)
   - Shipping = FREE (as set in quote)
   - Payment method selection
4. Buyer selects payment method
5. Buyer clicks "Place Order"

Result:
  - Quote status changes to "Ordered"
  - Order #100000042 created
  - Order items reflect NEGOTIATED prices ($46, $32)
  - Standard catalog prices NOT used
  - Quote is now in terminal "Ordered" state
```

### Step 6: Verification

```
Admin: Sales > Orders > Order #100000042
  Items:
    SKU-001: $46.00 x 50 = $2,300.00  (NOT the catalog price of $60)
    SKU-002: $32.00 x 25 = $800.00    (NOT the catalog price of $40)
  Shipping: $0.00
  Order Total: $3,100.00

  Note in order: "Created from Quote #Q-2024-0042"
```

> **Exam focus:** The converted order retains the **negotiated quote prices**. An admin looking at the order will see a reference back to the originating quote number.

---

## 7. Tricky Concepts & Exam Traps

### Trap 1: Quote Prices vs. Catalog Prices
```
WRONG assumption: "A negotiable quote price cannot go below the shared catalog price"
CORRECT:          "A negotiable quote price CAN go below ANY catalog price including
                   shared catalog prices — it is a fully custom agreement"
```

### Trap 2: Requisition List Pricing
```
WRONG assumption: "Items in a requisition list show the price at time of saving"
CORRECT:          "Items in a requisition list have NO price until added to cart.
                   The current catalog price applies when moved to cart."
```

### Trap 3: Quote States After Expiry
```
WRONG assumption: "An expired quote can be re-activated by the seller"
CORRECT:          "An expired quote is in a terminal state. The BUYER must
                   create a new quote (can duplicate the expired one)."
```

### Trap 4: Quick Order Accessibility
```
WRONG assumption: "Quick Order requires a company account"
CORRECT:          "Quick Order is available to any registered customer
                   (with the feature enabled). Company account NOT required."
```

### Trap 5: PO Approval Converts Automatically
```
WRONG assumption: "After PO approval, the buyer still needs to go through checkout"
CORRECT:          "When a PO is approved, it AUTOMATICALLY converts to an order
                   via message queue. No further buyer action is required."
```

### Trap 6: Requisition List to Cart Behavior
```
WRONG assumption: "Moving items from requisition list to cart removes them from the list"
CORRECT:          "Items are COPIED to cart. The requisition list remains unchanged."
```

### Trap 7: Who Can Initiate a Quote
```
WRONG assumption: "Any logged-in customer can request a negotiable quote"
CORRECT:          "Only company users whose company has 'Allow Quotes' enabled can
                   request quotes. The B2B Quote feature must also be globally enabled."
```

### Trap 8: Cron Dependency for Expiry
```
WRONG assumption: "Quotes expire immediately at midnight on the expiry date"
CORRECT:          "Quote expiry is processed by the 'backend_expire_date' cron job
                   (runs daily at midnight). If cron is delayed or not running,
                   quotes may not expire precisely on time."
```

### Trap 9: Requisition Lists Do NOT Require Company
```
WRONG assumption: "Requisition Lists require the Company module to be enabled"
CORRECT:          "The Requisition Lists toggle in admin has NO dependency on
                   Company. It can be enabled independently, unlike Negotiable
                   Quotes and Purchase Orders which require Company."
```

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Negotiable Quotes
- [ ] Quotes can be initiated from **cart** or **re-submitted from a prior quote**
- [ ] **9 frontend labels** (11 internal statuses): Draft, Submitted, Pending, Open, Updated, Ordered, Closed, Declined, Expired
- [ ] **Terminal states**: Ordered, Closed, Declined, Expired
- [ ] Seller can adjust: **line item prices, shipping cost, quote-level discount, expiry date**
- [ ] Discount types (line-item and quote-level): **Percentage, Amount, Proposed Price/Total**
- [ ] Quote price **bypasses all catalog pricing** — can go below shared catalog prices
- [ ] Expiry enforced by **`backend_expire_date` cron job** (daily at midnight) — not real-time
- [ ] Expired/Declined quotes cannot be re-opened — buyer must **create new or duplicate**
- [ ] Comments thread is visible to both parties; seller can add **internal-only notes**
- [ ] Quote history logs all **state changes and price edits**
- [ ] Converted order **retains negotiated prices** — does not re-validate catalog prices
- [ ] Requires **Company module** enabled and company must have **"Allow Quotes"** toggle enabled
- [ ] DB tables: `negotiable_quote`, `negotiable_quote_item`, `negotiable_quote_comment`

### Requisition Lists
- [ ] Multiple lists per buyer (default max: **999**, minimum: **2**)
- [ ] Lists are **per-buyer** (`customer_id`), not shared across company users
- [ ] Items can be added from: **PDP, category page, previous orders, cart, other lists**
- [ ] No pricing stored in list — price applied **when added to cart**
- [ ] Converting to cart **copies items** — does NOT remove from list
- [ ] Configured at: `Stores > Configuration > Customers > Requisition Lists` (section=requisitionlist)
- [ ] **Does NOT require Company module** — can be enabled independently

### Quick Order
- [ ] Available to **any registered customer** (not company-only)
- [ ] SKU validation occurs **in real-time** (AJAX)
- [ ] CSV upload format: columns `sku` and `qty`
- [ ] Results can go to **cart** OR **requisition list**
- [ ] Enabled at: `Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features`
- [ ] **Does NOT require Company module** — can be enabled independently

### Purchase Order Approvals
- [ ] Three rule types: **Order Total, Shipping Cost, Number of SKUs**
- [ ] When PO is approved → **automatically converts to order** (via message queue)
- [ ] When PO is rejected → buyer notified, can **edit and resubmit**
- [ ] Company **admin role** can always approve regardless of rules
- [ ] Approval rules configured by **company admin on storefront** (My Account > Approval Rules)
- [ ] Requires **Company module** enabled
- [ ] Config toggle in separate group: **"Order Approval Configuration"** under B2B Features

### B2B Module Dependencies
- [ ] All B2B features require **Adobe Commerce EE** (not Open Source)
- [ ] Negotiable Quotes require **Company module** (`depends` on `company_active`)
- [ ] Shared Catalog requires **Company module** (`depends` on `company_active`)
- [ ] Purchase Orders require **Company module** (`depends` on `company_active`)
- [ ] Requisition Lists and Quick Order have **no dependency** on Company
- [ ] Enabling Shared Catalog **automatically enables Category Permissions**
- [ ] Feature toggles in: `Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features` (section=btob)

### Key Admin Paths
- [ ] `Sales > Quotes` — manage negotiable quotes (title "Quotes", parent=sales_operation)
- [ ] `Customers > Companies` — manage company accounts and settings
- [ ] `Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features` — enable/disable features
- [ ] `Stores > Configuration > Customers > Requisition Lists` — configure list limits
- [ ] Purchase Order management is **storefront-only** (no dedicated admin menu)

flashcards.question: Which B2B features require the Company module to be enabled, and which can work independently?
flashcards.answer: Negotiable Quotes, Shared Catalog, and Purchase Orders require the Company module — their admin toggles only appear when Company is active. Requisition Lists and Quick Order can be enabled independently without the Company module.
flashcards.hint: Two B2B features stand alone; the rest depend on the organizational entity.

flashcards.question: What are the terminal states of a Negotiable Quote?
flashcards.answer: The four terminal states are Ordered, Closed, Declined, and Expired. A quote in any of these states cannot be re-opened. However, a buyer CAN duplicate a Declined or Expired quote as a new quote to restart the negotiation.
flashcards.hint: Four states end the quote lifecycle — but duplication offers a second chance for two of them.

flashcards.question: Can a Negotiable Quote price go below the Shared Catalog price?
flashcards.answer: Yes. A negotiable quote creates a unique, one-time price agreement that is NOT constrained by any catalog pricing rule. The seller can set any price — even below shared catalog prices, tier prices, or any other pricing mechanism. This is by design for fully custom B2B negotiations.
flashcards.hint: The negotiation process is unconstrained by existing pricing hierarchies.

flashcards.question: What three types of discounts can a seller apply to line items in a Negotiable Quote?
flashcards.answer: The three discount types are: Percentage Discount (type 1) — a percentage off the catalog price, Amount Discount (type 2) — a fixed dollar amount discount, and Proposed Price (type 3) — a specific proposed price per line item. These same three types are also available at the quote level.
flashcards.hint: Three ways to adjust price: relative percentage, absolute amount, or a completely new number.

flashcards.question: How is quote expiry enforced in Adobe Commerce?
flashcards.answer: Quote expiry is processed by the 'backend_expire_date' cron job (class ExpireQuote), which runs daily at midnight. When the current date passes the expiry date, the quote status changes to Expired and the buyer receives a notification email. If cron is not running, quotes will not auto-expire.
flashcards.hint: Expiry is not real-time — it depends on a scheduled background process.

flashcards.question: Do Requisition Lists store product prices?
flashcards.answer: No. Items in a Requisition List have NO price until they are added to the cart. The current catalog price is applied only when items are moved to the cart. This means prices may differ from when the item was originally added to the list.
flashcards.hint: Lists save product references, not pricing snapshots.

flashcards.question: What happens to a Requisition List when its items are added to the cart?
flashcards.answer: Items are COPIED to the cart, not moved. The Requisition List remains unchanged and intact for future use. This is a key difference from what users might assume — the list is a persistent reference, not consumed when used.
flashcards.hint: The list is designed for repeat purchasing, so it needs to persist.

flashcards.question: Can Requisition Lists be shared between company users?
flashcards.answer: No. Requisition Lists are per-buyer (stored via customer_id), not shared across company users. Each buyer maintains their own private lists. A single buyer can have up to 999 lists (configurable, minimum 2).
flashcards.hint: Lists are tied to individual customers, not to the company organization.

flashcards.question: Does the Quick Order feature require a company account?
flashcards.answer: No. Quick Order is available to any registered customer, not just company users. It does NOT require company membership. However, it does require the Quick Order feature to be enabled in the B2B configuration.
flashcards.hint: This feature is broader in accessibility than most B2B features.

flashcards.question: What is the required CSV format for Quick Order bulk upload?
flashcards.answer: The CSV must have columns named 'sku' and 'qty' (case-sensitive), with one product per row. After uploading, the buyer sees the same validation interface as manual entry and can remove invalid rows or fix quantities before adding to cart.
flashcards.hint: Two simple columns, case-sensitive headers, same validation as manual entry.

flashcards.question: What happens when a Purchase Order is approved?
flashcards.answer: When a PO is approved, it automatically converts to an order via message queue (purchaseorder.toorder) — no further buyer action is needed. The buyer receives an approval confirmation email. When rejected, the buyer is notified with the rejection comment and can edit and resubmit the PO.
flashcards.hint: Approval triggers an automatic conversion — no additional checkout step required.

flashcards.question: Who configures Purchase Order approval rules — the Magento Admin or the Company Admin?
flashcards.answer: Approval rules are configured by the Company Admin on the storefront (My Account > Approval Rules), NOT in the merchant admin panel. The merchant admin only enables/disables Purchase Orders globally and per-company. Company Administrators can always approve POs regardless of rule configuration.
flashcards.hint: The business organization controls its own approval policies from the front end.

flashcards.question: What are the three types of conditions available for Purchase Order approval rules?
flashcards.answer: The three condition types are: Order Total (grand_total) — approval required if order exceeds an amount, Shipping Cost (shipping_incl_tax) — approval required if shipping exceeds an amount, and Number of SKUs (number_of_skus) — approval required if SKU count exceeds a limit.
flashcards.hint: Three thresholds: money spent, shipping cost, and item variety.

flashcards.question: What conditions must be met for the 'Request a Quote' button to appear on the storefront?
flashcards.answer: Three conditions must all be met: the buyer must be logged in as a company user, the B2B Quote feature must be enabled globally, and the company must have 'Allow Quotes' enabled (a company-level configuration toggle set in admin under the company settings, NOT an ACL role permission).
flashcards.hint: Three gates: user type, global toggle, and company-level toggle.

flashcards.question: When a Negotiable Quote is converted to an order, do the prices re-validate against current catalog prices?
flashcards.answer: No. When a negotiable quote is converted to an order, the negotiated prices are locked in for that order. They do NOT re-validate against current catalog prices at checkout. Standard price processors are bypassed for quote-originated orders.
flashcards.hint: The agreed-upon prices are preserved as-is in the order.

studyNotes.title: Day 17 — MSI: Multi-Source Inventory
studyNotes.content:
# MSI: Multi-Source Inventory — Comprehensive Study Notes

## Table of Contents
1. [Overview & Architecture](#1-overview--architecture)
2. [Sources — Physical Locations](#2-sources--physical-locations)
3. [Stocks — Virtual Aggregations](#3-stocks--virtual-aggregations)
4. [Sales Channels](#4-sales-channels)
5. [Default Source & Default Stock](#5-default-source--default-stock)
6. [Source Items — Quantity Per Source](#6-source-items--quantity-per-source)
7. [Reservation System](#7-reservation-system)
8. [Salability — IsProductSalableInterface](#8-salability--isproductsalableinterface)
9. [Source Selection Algorithms (SSA)](#9-source-selection-algorithms-ssa)
10. [Shipment Creation](#10-shipment-creation)
11. [MSI in B2B](#11-msi-in-b2b)
12. [Common Traps & Misconceptions](#12-common-traps--misconceptions)
13. [Hands-On: Create Sources, Stock & Test Salability](#13-hands-on-create-sources-stock--test-salability)
14. [Database Schema Reference](#14-database-schema-reference)
15. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Overview & Architecture

Multi-Source Inventory (MSI) is a **core Magento Open Source (CE) feature** — not EE-exclusive — that replaced the legacy single-source inventory model introduced in Magento 2.3+.

```
+------------------+     assigned to     +------------------+
|    Source(s)     |-------------------->|     Stock        |
| (physical qty)   |                     | (virtual pool)   |
+------------------+                     +------------------+
                                                  |
                                          assigned to
                                                  |
                                          +------------------+
                                          |  Sales Channel   |
                                          |   (Website)      |
                                          +------------------+
```

### Key Module Structure

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|---------------|
| `Magento_Inventory` | Core Source/Stock CRUD |
| `Magento_InventorySalesApi` | Salability interfaces & reservations |
| `Magento_InventorySourceSelection` | SSA infrastructure (Priority SSA lives here) |
| `Magento_InventoryShipping` | Shipment source deduction & compensation |
| `Magento_InventoryBundleProduct` | Bundle-specific salability |
| `Magento_InventoryConfigurableProduct` | Configurable-specific salability |

> **Note:** There is no `Magento_InventoryB2b` module in the codebase. B2B/MSI integration is handled through the standard MSI salability APIs — no dedicated B2B-MSI module is needed.

> **Exam focus:** MSI is available in **both CE and EE** (license OSL-3.0). It is NOT an EE-exclusive feature. This is one of the most commonly tested misconceptions.

---

## 2. Sources — Physical Locations

A **Source** represents a real, physical location from which inventory is fulfilled.

### Characteristics
- Warehouse, retail store, drop-shipper, third-party fulfillment center
- Has a **unique `source_code`** (immutable once created)
- Stores latitude/longitude for Distance-Based SSA
- Can be **enabled or disabled** independently
- Each source tracks its own SKU quantities via **SourceItems**

### Source Attributes

| Attribute | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `source_code` | Unique string identifier (immutable, varchar 255) |
| `name` | Human-readable display name |
| `enabled` | Whether the source participates in sales (default=1) |
| `country_id`, `region_id`, `city`, `postcode` | Address for distance calculations |
| `latitude`, `longitude` | GPS coordinates for Distance SSA |
| `use_default_carrier_config` | Override shipping carrier settings |

### Creating a Source via API

```php
<?php
use Magento\InventoryApi\Api\Data\SourceInterfaceFactory;
use Magento\InventoryApi\Api\SourceRepositoryInterface;

/** @var SourceInterfaceFactory $sourceFactory */
/** @var SourceRepositoryInterface $sourceRepository */

$source = $sourceFactory->create();
$source->setSourceCode('warehouse_east');
$source->setName('East Coast Warehouse');
$source->setEnabled(true);
$source->setCountryId('US');
$source->setRegionId(43);  // NY
$source->setCity('New York');
$source->setPostcode('10001');
$source->setLatitude(40.7128);
$source->setLongitude(-74.0060);

$sourceRepository->save($source);
```

> **Exam focus:** The `source_code` is **immutable** — it cannot be changed after creation. Disabling a source does **NOT** delete its inventory data; quantities are preserved.

### Deactivating a Source

```
Enabled  -->  disabled
   |
   | Source items (qty) are PRESERVED in inventory_source_item table
   | Source is EXCLUDED from salability calculations
   | Source is EXCLUDED from SSA candidate pool
   v
NOT deleted, NOT zeroed out — just hidden from sales
```

> **Exam focus:** Deactivating a source stops it from being used for sales and SSA, but **inventory quantities are preserved**. This is a critical distinction for exam questions.

---

## 3. Stocks — Virtual Aggregations

A **Stock** is a virtual pool of inventory that aggregates one or more Sources.

### Characteristics
- Represents a **logical inventory view** for a sales channel
- One stock can aggregate many sources
- Stock-level quantity = **sum of eligible source quantities minus reservations**
- Assigned to one or more **Sales Channels (websites)**

### Stock-Source Assignment

```
+----------------------------+
|        Stock: "US Stock"   |
|  +----------------------+  |
|  | Source: Warehouse A  |  |  qty: 50
|  +----------------------+  |
|  | Source: Warehouse B  |  |  qty: 30
|  +----------------------+  |
|  | Source: Retail Store |  |  qty: 10
|  +----------------------+  |
|  Total Salable: 90 - reservations
+----------------------------+
         |
         | assigned to
         v
   Sales Channel: "US Website"
```

### Creating a Stock via API

```php
<?php
use Magento\InventoryApi\Api\Data\StockInterfaceFactory;
use Magento\InventoryApi\Api\StockRepositoryInterface;
use Magento\InventoryApi\Api\AssignSourcesToStockInterface;

/** @var StockInterfaceFactory $stockFactory */
$stock = $stockFactory->create();
$stock->setName('US East Stock');

/** @var StockRepositoryInterface $stockRepository */
$stockId = $stockRepository->save($stock);

/** @var AssignSourcesToStockInterface $assignSources */
$assignSources->execute(
    ['warehouse_east', 'retail_nyc'],
    $stockId
);
```

> **Exam focus:** The **Default Stock** (stock_id=1) always exists and cannot be deleted. At installation, only the Default Source is assigned to it. See the "Default Source & Default Stock" section for important details about source assignment.

## 4. Sales Channels

A **Sales Channel** links a Stock to a storefront/website.

### Types of Sales Channels

| Type | Constant | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| `website` | `SalesChannelInterface::TYPE_WEBSITE` | Magento website (most common) |

### Assigning a Stock to a Website

```php
<?php
use Magento\InventorySalesApi\Api\Data\SalesChannelInterfaceFactory;
use Magento\InventorySalesApi\Api\Data\SalesChannelInterface;
use Magento\InventoryApi\Api\StockRepositoryInterface;

$salesChannel = $salesChannelFactory->create();
$salesChannel->setType(SalesChannelInterface::TYPE_WEBSITE);
$salesChannel->setCode('us_website'); // website code, not ID

$extensionAttributes = $stock->getExtensionAttributes();
$extensionAttributes->setSalesChannels([$salesChannel]);
$stock->setExtensionAttributes($extensionAttributes);

$stockRepository->save($stock);
```

### The Lookup Chain

```
Customer browses Website "us_website"
         |
         v
System finds Stock assigned to "us_website"
         |
         v
System aggregates qty from all Sources in that Stock
         |
         v
Subtracts open Reservations
         |
         v
Returns Salable Quantity
```

> **Exam focus:** A website can only be assigned to **one stock** at a time. A stock can serve **multiple websites** (sales channels). This is enforced by the composite PK on `(type, code)` in `inventory_stock_sales_channel`.

## 5. Default Source & Default Stock

These exist for **backward compatibility** with pre-MSI Magento setups.

### Default Source

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| `source_code` | `default` (via `DefaultSourceProviderInterface`) |
| Purpose | Single-source merchants, backward compat |
| Deletable | **No** |
| Disableable | **No** |

### Default Stock

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| ID | `1` (via `DefaultStockProviderInterface`) |
| Purpose | Pre-configured stock for backward compatibility |
| Deletable | **No** |

### Backward Compatibility Flow

```
Pre-MSI product import (qty in cataloginventory_stock_item)
         |
         v
MSI migration maps qty --> Default Source inventory_source_item
         |
         v
Default Source is pre-assigned to Default Stock
         |
         v
Default Stock is assigned to the default website's sales channel
```

> **Important clarification:** The Default Stock does NOT automatically contain every source. Sources must be **explicitly assigned** to stocks via `inventory_source_stock_link`. At installation, only the Default Source (code=`default`) is linked to the Default Stock (id=1). If you create a new source and don't assign it to any stock, it is **orphaned** — it won't contribute to any stock's salable quantity until you explicitly link it.

> **Exam focus:** The Default Stock is a pre-configured stock with the Default Source assigned. To include additional sources in the Default Stock (or any stock), you must explicitly assign them via the admin (`Stores > Inventory > Stocks`) or API. Unassigned sources are not automatically part of any stock.

## 7. Reservation System

The reservation system is MSI's mechanism for tracking **"soft" inventory commitments** without locking rows.

### Design Philosophy

```
Traditional inventory:
  Place order --> UPDATE cataloginventory_stock_item SET qty = qty - 1
  (row-level lock, potential deadlock under load)

MSI Reservation:
  Place order --> INSERT INTO inventory_reservation (sku, qty, -1, metadata)
  (append-only, no lock contention)
```

### The `inventory_reservation` Table

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `reservation_id` | Auto-increment PK |
| `stock_id` | FK to stock |
| `sku` | Product SKU |
| `quantity` | **Negative** for deductions (e.g., `-1.0` when order placed) |
| `metadata` | JSON: event type, object type, object ID (varchar 255) |

### Reservation Lifecycle

```
1. Customer adds to cart
   --> No reservation yet

2. Customer places order
   --> INSERT reservation: qty = -2 (for qty 2 ordered)
   metadata: {"event_type":"order_placed","object_type":"order","object_id":"100042"}

3. Order ships (source deduction)
   --> Source item qty decremented (actual physical deduction)
   --> INSERT reservation: qty = +2 (compensation)
   metadata: {"event_type":"shipment_created"}

4. Net reservation effect: 0 (reservations cancel out)
   Physical qty reduced at the source level
```

### Calculating Salable Quantity

```
Salable Qty = SUM(source_item.quantity for sources in stock)
            + SUM(reservation.quantity for this stock+sku)

Example:
  Source A qty: 50
  Source B qty: 30
  Reservation (order placed): -5
  Salable Qty = 80 + (-5) = 75
```

### Compensation Events

| Trigger | SalesEvent Constant | Reservation Effect |
|---------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Order placed | `EVENT_ORDER_PLACED` | `-qty` (deduction) |
| Order shipped | `EVENT_SHIPMENT_CREATED` | `+qty` (compensation — source qty already decremented) |
| Order cancelled | `EVENT_ORDER_CANCELED` | `+qty` (reversal) |
| Order placement failed | `EVENT_ORDER_PLACE_FAILED` | `+qty` (reversal) |
| Credit memo created | `EVENT_CREDITMEMO_CREATED` | `+qty` (refund compensation) |

> **Note:** There is no `EVENT_ORDER_REJECTED` constant. The six defined event types in `SalesEventInterface` are: `order_placed`, `order_canceled`, `order_place_failed`, `shipment_created`, `creditmemo_created`, `invoice_created`.

> **Exam focus:** Reservations are **append-only** — records are never updated or deleted, only new rows added. This avoids row-level locks and enables high concurrency. The reservation quantity is **negative** when stock is committed. Source item quantity is decremented at **shipment creation**, not order placement.

## 8. Salability — IsProductSalableInterface

Salability is the **computed answer** to "can this product be sold right now?"

### The Interface

```php
<?php
namespace Magento\InventorySalesApi\Api;

interface IsProductSalableInterface
{
    /**
     * @param string $sku
     * @param int $stockId
     * @return bool
     */
    public function execute(string $sku, int $stockId): bool;
}
```

### The Extended Interface for Quantity

```php
<?php
namespace Magento\InventorySalesApi\Api;

interface IsProductSalableForRequestedQtyInterface
{
    /**
     * @param string $sku
     * @param int $stockId
     * @param float $requestedQty
     * @return \Magento\InventorySalesApi\Api\Data\ProductSalableResultInterface
     */
    public function execute(
        string $sku,
        int $stockId,
        float $requestedQty
    ): \Magento\InventorySalesApi\Api\Data\ProductSalableResultInterface;
}
```

> **Note:** The return type is `ProductSalableResultInterface` (not `ProductSalabilityErrorInterface[]` directly). Call `$result->getErrors()` to get the array of `ProductSalabilityErrorInterface` objects. Both interfaces are deprecated in favor of bulk APIs (`AreProductsSalableInterface`, `AreProductsSalableForRequestedQtyInterface`).

### Salability Check Chain

The default implementation uses a **chain of responsibility** pattern with 5 conditions (configured in `module-inventory-sales/etc/di.xml`):

```
IsProductSalable::execute($sku, $stockId)
    |
    +-> IsSetInStockStatusForCompositeProductCondition  (required)
    |       Checks: composite product stock status consistency
    |
    +-> IsAnySourceItemInStockCondition                 (required)
    |       Checks: at least one source_item has status=IN_STOCK
    |       for any enabled source in the stock
    |
    +-> BackOrderCondition                              (sort_order 10)
    |       If backorders enabled --> may return true even if qty <= 0
    |
    +-> ManageStockCondition                            (sort_order 20)
    |       If "Manage Stock" = No --> always salable
    |
    +-> IsSalableWithReservationsCondition               (sort_order 30)
            Checks: salable_qty > 0 considering reservations
```

### Backorder Interaction

| Backorder Setting | Salable When Qty <= 0? |
|------------------|------------------------|
| No Backorders | **No** — product goes out of stock |
| Allow Qty Below 0 | **Yes** — always salable |
| Allow Qty Below 0 + Notify Customer | **Yes** — salable with notification |

> **Exam focus:** `IsProductSalableInterface` uses a **chain of 5 conditions**: composite stock status, source item status, backorder settings, manage stock, and reservation-adjusted quantity. All required conditions must pass.

### Getting Stock ID for Current Website

```php
<?php
use Magento\InventorySalesApi\Api\StockResolverInterface;
use Magento\InventorySalesApi\Api\Data\SalesChannelInterface;
use Magento\Store\Model\StoreManagerInterface;

/** @var StoreManagerInterface $storeManager */
$websiteCode = $storeManager->getWebsite()->getCode();

/** @var StockResolverInterface $stockResolver */
$stock = $stockResolver->execute(
    SalesChannelInterface::TYPE_WEBSITE,
    $websiteCode
);
$stockId = $stock->getStockId();
```

## 9. Source Selection Algorithms (SSA)

An SSA determines **which source(s)** should fulfill a given order item.

### Available Algorithms

| Algorithm | Module | Logic |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| **Priority** | `Magento_InventorySourceSelection` | Deducts from sources in configured priority order |
| **Distance** | `Magento_InventoryDistanceBasedSourceSelection` | Selects nearest source to shipping address |
| **Custom** | Your module | Implement `SourceSelectionInterface` |

### Priority SSA (Default)

```
Sources assigned to Stock have a priority (integer, lower = higher priority):
  Source A: priority 1
  Source B: priority 2
  Source C: priority 3

Order: 15 units of SKU "ABC"

SSA Priority execution:
  Source A has 10 units --> assign 10 units to Source A
  Still need 5 more
  Source B has 8 units --> assign 5 units to Source B
  Done.

Result:
  [{ source: A, qty: 10 }, { source: B, qty: 5 }]
```

### Distance SSA

- Requires sources to have **latitude/longitude** configured
- Requires a **distance provider**: either **Google Maps API** (online) or **Offline** (uses imported GeoNames data with Haversine formula)
- Selects the geographically closest source first
- Falls back to priority if distances are equal

```php
<?php
// Distance SSA uses "google" or "offline" provider
// Config path: cataloginventory/source_selection_distance_based/provider
// Default: "google"
// Offline provider requires importing GeoNames data via CLI:
//   bin/magento inventory-geonames:import <country_code>
```

### Custom SSA Implementation

```php
<?php
namespace MyVendor\MyModule\Model\SourceSelection;

use Magento\InventorySourceSelectionApi\Api\Data\InventoryRequestInterface;
use Magento\InventorySourceSelectionApi\Api\Data\SourceSelectionResultInterface;
use Magento\InventorySourceSelectionApi\Model\SourceSelectionInterface;

class CustomAlgorithm implements SourceSelectionInterface
{
    public function execute(
        InventoryRequestInterface $inventoryRequest
    ): SourceSelectionResultInterface {
        // Custom logic: e.g., select source with highest qty,
        // or nearest to a specific region, or vendor-specific rules
    }
}
```

```xml
<!-- di.xml: Register the algorithm -->
<type name="Magento\InventorySourceSelectionApi\Model\SourceSelectionService">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="sourceSelectionMethods" xsi:type="array">
            <item name="my_custom_ssa" xsi:type="object">
                MyVendor\MyModule\Model\SourceSelection\CustomAlgorithm
            </item>
        </argument>
    </arguments>
</type>
```

> **Note:** Custom SSAs implement `SourceSelectionInterface` (NOT `SourceSelectionServiceInterface`). `SourceSelectionServiceInterface` is the API for *executing* algorithms by code — it dispatches to the correct `SourceSelectionInterface` implementation.

> **Exam focus:** The **Priority SSA is the default** (code `'priority'`) and ships with CE. Distance SSA requires GPS coordinates and a distance provider (Google Maps API or Offline with GeoNames data). Custom SSAs are registered via `di.xml`. The SSA returns a *recommendation* — the admin can override it during shipment creation.
