## 10. Shipment Creation

### Multi-Source Shipment Flow

```
Admin: Sales > Orders > View Order > Ship
         |
         v
System runs SSA to RECOMMEND source allocation
         |
         v
Admin sees "Sources" section per item:
  Item: Widget A (qty: 3)
    [Warehouse East: 2] [Retail NYC: 1]
         |
         v
Admin can OVERRIDE the recommendation
         |
         v
Admin clicks "Submit Shipment"
         |
         v
1. Shipment record created
2. SourceDeductionProcessor runs:
   a. SourceItems decremented per source (physical qty)
   b. Compensation reservations inserted (+qty)
3. Net reservation effect = 0
```

### Partial Shipments Across Sources

```
Order: 10x SKU "ABC"

Shipment 1 (today):
  Source A ships 6 units
  --> inventory_source_item: A.qty -= 6
  --> reservation: +6 (compensation)

Shipment 2 (tomorrow):
  Source B ships 4 units
  --> inventory_source_item: B.qty -= 4
  --> reservation: +4 (compensation)

Order fully shipped: total reservations compensated.
```

### Programmatic Shipment Source Selection

```php
<?php
use Magento\InventorySourceSelectionApi\Api\GetDefaultSourceSelectionAlgorithmCodeInterface;
use Magento\InventorySourceSelectionApi\Api\SourceSelectionServiceInterface;
use Magento\InventorySourceSelectionApi\Api\Data\InventoryRequestInterfaceFactory;
use Magento\InventorySourceSelectionApi\Api\Data\ItemRequestInterfaceFactory;

$algorithmCode = $getDefaultAlgorithm->execute(); // 'priority'

$requestItems = [];
foreach ($orderItems as $item) {
    $requestItem = $itemRequestFactory->create([
        'sku'      => $item->getSku(),
        'qty'      => $item->getQtyOrdered(),
    ]);
    $requestItems[] = $requestItem;
}

$inventoryRequest = $inventoryRequestFactory->create([
    'stockId' => $stockId,
    'items'   => $requestItems,
]);

$selectionResult = $sourceSelectionService->execute(
    $inventoryRequest,
    $algorithmCode
);

// $selectionResult->getSourceSelectionItems() --> array of [source_code, qty, qty_available]
```

> **Exam focus:** The SSA provides a **recommendation only**. The admin can modify source assignments before confirming the shipment. Partial shipments are fully supported — each partial shipment decrements the relevant source and posts a compensation reservation.

## 11. MSI in B2B

### Negotiable Quotes & MSI Salability

When B2B negotiable quotes interact with MSI:

```
Buyer requests quote for 100 units of SKU "XYZ"
         |
         v
Quote is negotiated (price changes, validity set)
         |
         v
Buyer converts quote to order
         |
         v
MSI salability check: IsProductSalableForRequestedQty
  - Uses stock assigned to buyer's website
  - Checks reservation-adjusted qty >= 100
         |
         v
If salable: order proceeds
If not salable: error (quantity changed since quote)
```

### Key Behaviors

| Scenario | MSI Behavior |
|----------|-------------|
| Quote contains product that goes OOS during negotiation | Salability check at order conversion may fail |
| Quote has reserved qty | **No** — quotes do NOT create reservations |
| Company account on different website | Uses stock for that website's sales channel |
| Shared catalog restricts products | MSI still checks physical availability |

> **Exam focus:** Negotiable quotes do **NOT** create MSI reservations. The salability check happens at **order conversion time**, not at quote creation. This means between quote approval and order placement, inventory could be depleted by other buyers.

## 12. Common Traps & Misconceptions

### Trap 1: MSI is EE-Only

```
WRONG: "MSI requires Magento Commerce (EE)"
RIGHT: MSI is available in Magento Open Source (CE) since 2.3
       Core modules are licensed OSL-3.0 (Open Source License).
```

### Trap 2: Disabling a Source Deletes Inventory

```
WRONG: "If I disable source 'warehouse_east', its inventory is gone"
RIGHT: Disabling a source:
  - Removes it from salability calculations
  - Removes it from SSA candidate pool
  - PRESERVES all inventory_source_item records
  - Re-enabling the source restores full functionality
```

### Trap 3: Default Stock Automatically Contains All Sources

```
WRONG: "The Default Stock covers all sources not assigned to any custom stock"
RIGHT: Sources must be EXPLICITLY assigned to stocks via inventory_source_stock_link.
  - At installation, only the Default Source (code='default') is linked to the Default Stock (id=1)
  - New sources created without stock assignments are ORPHANED — not part of any stock
  - You must manually assign sources to the Default Stock (or another stock) to include them
```

### Trap 4: Reservations Directly Reduce Source Qty

```
WRONG: "Placing an order reduces inventory_source_item.quantity"
RIGHT: 
  - Placing order: INSERT reservation (qty = -N) into inventory_reservation
  - Source item quantity is unchanged until SHIPMENT is created
  - Shipment creation DECREMENTS source item quantity
  - Shipment creation INSERTS compensation reservation (+N)
```

### Trap 5: One Stock Per Website (Bidirectional)

```
WRONG: "One stock can only serve one website"
RIGHT:
  - One WEBSITE can only be assigned to ONE stock
  - One STOCK can serve MULTIPLE websites (sales channels)
  (Enforced by composite PK on (type, code) in inventory_stock_sales_channel)
```

### Trap 6: SSA Makes the Final Shipment Decision

```
WRONG: "The SSA determines exactly which sources will ship"
RIGHT: SSA provides a RECOMMENDATION
  - Admins can override source selection in the shipment UI
  - SSA result is a starting point, not a lock
```

> **Exam focus:** All six traps above are prime exam question material. Memorize all of them.

// Create a simple test script or use a module's command

use Magento\InventorySalesApi\Api\IsProductSalableInterface;

## 14. Database Schema Reference

### Core MSI Tables

```
inventory_source
  source_code (PK, varchar 255)    name    enabled    country_id    latitude    longitude

inventory_stock
  stock_id (PK, auto_increment)    name

inventory_source_stock_link
  link_id (PK)    stock_id (FK)    source_code (FK)    priority
  UNIQUE(stock_id, source_code)

inventory_source_item
  source_item_id (PK)    source_code    sku    quantity (decimal 12,4)    status
  UNIQUE(source_code, sku)

inventory_reservation
  reservation_id (PK)    stock_id    sku    quantity (decimal 10,4)    metadata (varchar 255)

inventory_stock_sales_channel
  type + code (composite PK)    stock_id (FK)
```

### Relationship Diagram

```
inventory_source <---------+ inventory_source_stock_link +---------> inventory_stock
  (source_code)            |   (source_code, stock_id,  |              (stock_id)
                           |    priority)               |                   |
                           +----------------------------+                   |
                                                                            |
inventory_source_item                                    inventory_stock_sales_channel
  (source_code, sku, qty)                                  (stock_id, type, code)
                                                                    |
                                                             website "code"

inventory_reservation
  (stock_id, sku, quantity, metadata)  <-- append-only log
```

### Key Indexes for Performance

```sql
-- Salability query: sum reservations for stock+sku
SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM inventory_reservation
WHERE stock_id = ? AND sku = ?;
-- Index on (stock_id, sku) is critical

-- Source item lookup for stock
SELECT si.quantity FROM inventory_source_item si
JOIN inventory_source_stock_link ssl
  ON si.source_code = ssl.source_code
WHERE ssl.stock_id = ? AND si.sku = ? AND si.status = 1;
```

> **Exam focus:** Understanding the table structure helps answer questions about how salable quantity is computed and why the reservation system avoids locks (`INSERT` vs `UPDATE`).

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Core Concepts
- [ ] **MSI is CE + EE** — not EE-exclusive; available since Magento 2.3 (OSL-3.0 license)
- [ ] **Source** = physical location; has unique immutable `source_code`; stores lat/lng
- [ ] **Stock** = virtual pool aggregating 1+ sources
- [ ] **Sales Channel** = assignment of a stock to a website
- [ ] **Source Item** = `(source_code, sku, quantity, status)` — physical qty at a source
- [ ] **One website → one stock** (many websites can use the same stock)
- [ ] **One stock → many sources** (aggregation)

### Default Source & Stock
- [ ] Default Source code = `"default"`; cannot be deleted or disabled
- [ ] Default Stock ID = `1`; cannot be deleted
- [ ] Default Stock initially has only the Default Source assigned
- [ ] New sources must be **explicitly assigned** to stocks — they don't auto-roll into the Default Stock

### Reservation System
- [ ] Reservations are **append-only** — INSERT only, never UPDATE/DELETE
- [ ] Reservation quantity is **negative** when stock is committed (order placed)
- [ ] Order placed → `-qty` reservation; shipment created → `+qty` compensation
- [ ] Source item quantity is decremented at **shipment creation**, not order placement
- [ ] Salable qty = sum(source_item.qty) + sum(reservation.qty) for stock
- [ ] Six event types: `order_placed`, `order_canceled`, `order_place_failed`, `shipment_created`, `creditmemo_created`, `invoice_created`

### Salability
- [ ] `IsProductSalableInterface::execute(sku, stockId): bool`
- [ ] `IsProductSalableForRequestedQtyInterface::execute(sku, stockId, requestedQty): ProductSalableResultInterface`
- [ ] Chain of 5 conditions: composite stock status, source item in-stock, backorders, manage stock, reservation-adjusted qty
- [ ] Backorders enabled → can be salable even when physical qty = 0
- [ ] Both interfaces deprecated in favor of bulk `AreProductsSalable*` APIs

### Source Selection Algorithms
- [ ] **Priority SSA** = default (code `'priority'`); in `Magento_InventorySourceSelection`; deducts from sources in priority order
- [ ] **Distance SSA** = uses lat/lng + distance provider (Google Maps API or Offline/GeoNames); selects nearest source first
- [ ] **Custom SSA** = implements `SourceSelectionInterface`; registered via `di.xml` in `sourceSelectionMethods`
- [ ] SSA result is a **recommendation** — admin can override before confirming shipment

### Shipment
- [ ] Partial shipments across multiple sources are fully supported
- [ ] Each partial shipment decrements source item qty and inserts compensation reservation
- [ ] Admin UI allows overriding SSA source recommendations during shipment creation
- [ ] Shipment source deduction handled by `SourceDeductionProcessor` observer

### Disabling Sources
- [ ] Disabling a source: **stops it from being used for sales and SSA**
- [ ] Disabling a source: **preserves all inventory_source_item records**
- [ ] Re-enabling restores full functionality — no data is lost

### MSI + B2B
- [ ] Negotiable quotes do **NOT** create MSI reservations
- [ ] Salability is checked at **order conversion time**, not quote creation
- [ ] Inventory could be depleted between quote approval and order placement
- [ ] Stock used is determined by the buyer's company website assignment

### Common Exam Traps
- [ ] MSI ≠ EE exclusive (CE too!)
- [ ] Disabled source ≠ deleted inventory
- [ ] Default Stock ≠ auto-contains all sources (explicit assignment required)
- [ ] Order placement ≠ source qty decrement (shipment does that)
- [ ] SSA ≠ final decision (recommendation only)
- [ ] One stock can serve multiple websites; one website can only have one stock

### Admin Navigation Paths
- [ ] Sources: `Stores > Inventory > Sources`
- [ ] Stocks: `Stores > Inventory > Stocks`
- [ ] Product source qty: `Catalog > Products > [Product] > Sources tab`
- [ ] MSI indexer: `bin/magento indexer:reindex inventory`

flashcards.question: Is Multi-Source Inventory (MSI) exclusive to Adobe Commerce Enterprise Edition?
flashcards.answer: No. MSI is available in BOTH Magento Open Source (CE) and Adobe Commerce (EE). It is licensed under OSL-3.0 (Open Source License) and has been a core feature since Magento 2.3. This is one of the most commonly tested misconceptions.
flashcards.hint: Think about the license type — it is an open source license.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between a Source and a Stock in MSI?
flashcards.answer: A Source represents a physical location (warehouse, store, drop-shipper) from which inventory is fulfilled. A Stock is a virtual pool that aggregates one or more Sources and is assigned to a Sales Channel (website). Stock-level quantity equals the sum of eligible source quantities minus reservations.
flashcards.hint: One is physical and tangible; the other is a logical aggregation for a website.

flashcards.question: Can a Source Code be changed after a Source is created in MSI?
flashcards.answer: No. The source_code is immutable — it cannot be changed after creation. It is a unique string identifier (varchar 255) that permanently identifies the source. Only the source name and other attributes can be modified.
flashcards.hint: This identifier is set once and locked permanently.

flashcards.question: What happens to inventory data when you disable a Source in MSI?
flashcards.answer: Disabling a source does NOT delete its inventory data. Quantities are preserved in the inventory_source_item table. The source is simply excluded from salability calculations and the SSA candidate pool. Re-enabling the source restores full functionality with no data loss.
flashcards.hint: The source becomes invisible to sales, but its records remain intact.

flashcards.question: How does the MSI reservation system differ from traditional inventory management?
flashcards.answer: Traditional inventory uses UPDATE to decrement stock quantity at order time (causing row-level locks). MSI uses append-only INSERTs into the inventory_reservation table — reservations are never updated or deleted, only new rows are added. This avoids row-level locks and enables high concurrency.
flashcards.hint: INSERT-only operations versus UPDATE operations — think about database locking.

flashcards.question: When is the physical source item quantity actually decremented in MSI — at order placement or shipment creation?
flashcards.answer: Source item quantity is decremented at SHIPMENT creation, not order placement. At order placement, only a negative reservation is created. When the shipment is created, the source item qty is decremented AND a compensation reservation (+qty) is inserted to offset the original negative reservation.
flashcards.hint: The physical deduction waits for the fulfillment step, not the purchase step.

flashcards.question: What is the formula for calculating Salable Quantity in MSI?
flashcards.answer: Salable Qty = SUM(source_item.quantity for all enabled sources in the stock) + SUM(reservation.quantity for this stock and SKU). Reservations are negative when stock is committed (order placed) and positive when compensated (shipment, cancellation, credit memo).
flashcards.hint: Physical stock across all sources plus the net effect of all reservation entries.

flashcards.question: Does adding an item to the shopping cart create an MSI reservation?
flashcards.answer: No. Adding to cart does NOT create a reservation. Reservations are created only at ORDER PLACEMENT. This is one of the most common wrong-answer traps on the exam. The cart is merely a shopping intent, not an inventory commitment.
flashcards.hint: The commitment event is later in the checkout process than most people assume.

flashcards.question: What are the two built-in Source Selection Algorithms (SSA) in MSI?
flashcards.answer: Priority SSA (default) deducts from sources in configured priority order (lowest number = highest priority). Distance SSA selects the nearest source to the shipping address using GPS coordinates, requiring either the Google Maps API or Offline GeoNames data as a distance provider.
flashcards.hint: One is based on numerical ranking; the other uses geographic proximity.

flashcards.question: Is the SSA recommendation final for shipment source assignment?
flashcards.answer: No. The SSA provides a recommendation only. The admin can modify source assignments before confirming the shipment in the admin UI. The SSA result is a starting point, not a lock — admins can override which sources fulfill which items.
flashcards.hint: Think of the algorithm's output as a suggestion, not a command.

flashcards.question: How many stocks can a single website be assigned to in MSI?
flashcards.answer: A website can only be assigned to ONE stock at a time. However, a single stock can serve MULTIPLE websites (sales channels). This is enforced by a composite primary key on (type, code) in the inventory_stock_sales_channel table.
flashcards.hint: The relationship is many-to-one from websites to stock.

flashcards.question: Do Negotiable Quotes create MSI reservations?
flashcards.answer: No. Negotiable quotes do NOT create MSI reservations. The salability check happens at order conversion time, not at quote creation. This means inventory could be depleted by other buyers between quote approval and order placement.
flashcards.hint: The price negotiation process is separate from inventory commitment.

flashcards.question: Can the Default Source and Default Stock in MSI be deleted?
flashcards.answer: No. The Default Source (code='default') and Default Stock (stock_id=1) cannot be deleted or disabled. They exist for backward compatibility with pre-MSI single-source setups. Only the Default Source is pre-assigned to the Default Stock at installation.
flashcards.hint: These are system-protected entities for backward compatibility.

flashcards.question: Does the Default Stock automatically contain all sources in MSI?
flashcards.answer: No. Sources must be explicitly assigned to stocks via inventory_source_stock_link. At installation, only the Default Source is linked to the Default Stock. New sources created without stock assignments are orphaned and won't contribute to any stock's salable quantity.
flashcards.hint: Explicit assignment is always required — nothing is automatic.

flashcards.question: What are the five conditions in the IsProductSalable chain of responsibility?
flashcards.answer: The five conditions are: (1) IsSetInStockStatusForCompositeProductCondition, (2) IsAnySourceItemInStockCondition, (3) BackOrderCondition, (4) ManageStockCondition, and (5) IsSalableWithReservationsCondition. All required conditions must pass for a product to be considered salable.
flashcards.hint: Five checks covering composite products, source status, backorders, stock management, and reservation-adjusted quantity.

studyNotes.content:
# Adobe Commerce: BI, LiveSearch & Product Recommendations
## Study Notes — Week 3, Add-on Modules

---

## Table of Contents

   - [1.4 Custom Metrics](#14-custom-metrics)

   - [1.6 Data Warehouse Sync](#16-data-warehouse-sync)
2. [LiveSearch (SaaS)](#2-livesearch-saas)
   - [2.1 Overview & Architecture](#21-overview--architecture)
   - [2.2 LiveSearch vs Native Search](#22-livesearch-vs-native-search)
   - [2.3 Features: Facets, Synonyms & Rules](#23-features-facets-synonyms--rules)
   - [2.4 Relevance Ranking](#24-relevance-ranking)
   - [2.5 SaaS Data Export & Sync Delay](#25-saas-data-export--sync-delay)
   - [2.6 Configuration in Admin](#26-configuration-in-admin)
3. [Product Recommendations (Sensei)](#3-product-recommendations-sensei)
   - [3.1 Overview](#31-overview)
   - [3.2 Recommendation Types](#32-recommendation-types)
   - [3.3 Placement Options](#33-placement-options)
   - [3.4 Behavioral Data Requirements](#34-behavioral-data-requirements)
   - [3.5 Configuration & Admin Setup](#35-configuration--admin-setup)
4. [Integration Architecture: How the Three Services Connect](#4-integration-architecture-how-the-three-services-connect)
5. [Tricky Exam Concepts & Common Pitfalls](#5-tricky-exam-concepts--common-pitfalls)
6. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Adobe Commerce Intelligence (BI/MBI Essentials)

### 1.1 Overview & Access

Adobe Commerce Intelligence (formerly **Magento Business Intelligence / MBI**) is a cloud-based data analytics platform. It provides merchants with actionable insights by aggregating data from the Commerce database, external sources, and third-party integrations into a centralized **data warehouse**.

**Access Path:**
```
Admin Panel → Reports → Business Intelligence
  → Advanced Reporting  (opens externally, target="_blank")
  → BI Essentials       (opens externally to RJMetrics dashboard, target="_blank")
```

> Both menu items redirect to **external SaaS portals** — they open in new browser tabs, not within the Admin panel.

**Exam focus:**
- BI is accessed via **Admin → Reports → Business Intelligence**, not directly from the Commerce database.
- BI runs as a **SaaS** application — it is *not* an on-premise module.
- Formerly known as **MBI (Magento Business Intelligence)**; now called **Adobe Commerce Intelligence**.

**Important distinction — Advanced Reporting vs. Full BI:**

| Feature | Advanced Reporting | Adobe Commerce Intelligence (BI Essentials/Pro) |
|---|---|---|
| **Module** | `Magento_Analytics` (module-analytics) | Separate SaaS subscription |
| **License** | OSL-3.0 (**CE + EE**) | Adobe Commerce subscription required |
| **What it provides** | Basic analytics, menu link, data export to Adobe | Full data warehouse, custom metrics, dashboards, cohort analysis |
| **Config path** | Stores > Configuration > General > Advanced Reporting | External BI portal |

> **Note:** The `module-analytics` providing the "Reports > Business Intelligence" menu is **available in both CE and EE** (OSL-3.0 license). However, the **full BI SaaS platform** (data warehouse, custom metrics, scheduled dashboards, cohort analysis) requires an Adobe Commerce subscription. The module-analytics provides the integration bridge and basic Advanced Reporting.

**Admin config for Advanced Reporting:**
```
Stores > Configuration > General > Advanced Reporting
(section=analytics, tab=general)
  → Advanced Reporting Service: [Enabled/Disabled]  (showInDefault=1 only)
  → Time of day to send data: [time picker]
  → Industry: [select]  (showInDefault=1, showInWebsite=1)
```

---

### 1.2 Pre-Built Reports

BI ships with a library of **pre-built dashboards and reports** organized into functional categories:

| Category | Example Reports |
|---|---|
| **Revenue** | Total Revenue, Revenue by Channel, Revenue Over Time |
| **Customers** | New vs Returning Customers, Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) |
| **Products** | Revenue by Product, Top Products by Units Sold |
| **Orders** | Average Order Value (AOV), Orders by Status |
| **Cohort Analysis** | Retention by Cohort, Revenue by Acquisition Cohort |

**Exam focus:**
- Pre-built reports cover **revenue, customers, and products** — memorize these three pillars.
- Reports are rendered in the **BI SaaS portal**, not inside Admin directly.

---

### 1.3 Key Report Types

These are the four most exam-critical report types:

#### New vs Returning Customers
Segments customers into **first-time buyers** vs **repeat purchasers**. Useful for measuring acquisition vs retention effectiveness.

- New Customer = customer placing their **first-ever order**
- Returning Customer = customer with **2+ lifetime orders**

#### Cohort Analysis
Groups customers by a **shared characteristic at a point in time** (e.g., month of first purchase) and tracks their behavior over subsequent periods.

```
Cohort Example:
  Jan Cohort (customers who first bought in Jan)
    -> Month 1: 100 customers, $5,000 revenue
    -> Month 2:  40 customers, $2,200 revenue  (40% retention)
    -> Month 3:  25 customers, $1,400 revenue  (25% retention)
```

**Exam focus:**
- Cohort Analysis is used to measure **customer retention over time**.
- Cohorts are typically grouped by **acquisition month/quarter**.

#### Revenue by Product
Breaks down total revenue contribution per SKU or product category. Identifies top-performing and underperforming products.

#### Customer Lifetime Value (CLV / LTV)
Calculates the **total predicted or historical revenue** a customer generates across their entire relationship with the store.

```
CLV = Average Order Value x Purchase Frequency x Customer Lifespan
```

**Exam focus:**
- CLV is one of the most strategically important metrics in BI — expect scenario questions about which report to use for long-term customer value analysis.

---

### 1.4 Custom Metrics

Beyond pre-built reports, administrators can create **custom metrics** by defining:

1. **Metric name** — descriptive label
2. **Table** — the source database table (e.g., `sales_order`)
3. **Operation** — `SUM`, `COUNT`, `AVERAGE`, `MAX`, `MIN`
4. **Column** — the specific field to operate on (e.g., `grand_total`)
5. **Timestamp** — the date field for time-series analysis (e.g., `created_at`)
6. **Filters** — conditions to narrow the dataset (e.g., `status = 'complete'`)

**Example custom metric definition:**

```
Metric: "Completed Order Revenue"
Table:  sales_order
Operation: SUM
Column: grand_total
Timestamp: created_at
Filter: status = 'complete'
```

**Exam focus:**
- Custom metrics require selecting a **source table, operation type, and timestamp column**.
- Filters are optional but commonly used to exclude cancelled/refunded orders.

---

### 1.5 Dashboards

Dashboards are **collections of report tiles** that can be:
- **Shared** with other BI users (read-only or edit access)
- **Cloned** to create a private working copy
- **Scheduled** for email delivery (daily/weekly/monthly reports via email)

Key dashboard features:
- Each tile can display charts, tables, numbers, or maps
- **Global date filters** apply to all tiles simultaneously
- Tiles can be resized and repositioned via drag-and-drop

**Exam focus:**
- Dashboards support **scheduled email delivery** — this is a common exam scenario.
- Dashboards are **shared at the BI portal level**, not via Commerce Admin roles/permissions.

---

### 1.6 Data Warehouse Sync

The BI Data Warehouse is the engine that pulls data from your Commerce database and makes it available for reporting.

```
Commerce DB (MySQL)
       |
       v
  [Data Warehouse Manager]
       |
       v
  BI Data Warehouse (Hosted)
       |
       v
  Reports & Dashboards
```

**Key concepts:**

| Concept | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Sync Frequency** | Default: every hour; can be configured to more frequent cycles |
| **Full Re-sync** | Required after schema changes or table additions |
| **Data Warehouse Manager** | UI for selecting which tables/columns to sync |
| **Update Queue** | Tracks which records have changed since last sync |
| **Native Tables** | Commerce core tables synced by default |
| **Integration Tables** | Third-party source tables (e.g., Salesforce, Google Analytics) |

**Exam focus:**
- There is always a **sync delay** — BI data is **never real-time**.
- The **Data Warehouse Manager** is where you add/remove tables and columns from sync.
- After adding a **new custom attribute**, you must manually add it to the Data Warehouse sync.

---

## 2. LiveSearch (SaaS)

### 2.1 Overview & Architecture

**LiveSearch** is Adobe Commerce's SaaS-based search solution powered by **Adobe Sensei** (Adobe's AI/ML framework). It replaces the native OpenSearch-based search with a cloud-hosted service that provides:

- Real-time **search-as-you-type** (instant results on keystroke)
- AI-powered **relevance ranking**
- **Faceted navigation** with dynamic facet generation
- **Synonym management**
- **Merchandising rules** (boost, bury, pin, hide)

> **Note:** LiveSearch is a **separate SaaS package** (`magento/live-search`) that is NOT included in the base Adobe Commerce EE distribution. It must be installed separately via Composer.

**Architecture diagram:**

```
  Storefront Browser
        |
        | (search query - REST/GraphQL)
        v
  Commerce Storefront
        |
        | (API call - SaaS)
        v
  Adobe LiveSearch Service (Cloud)
        |
        +----> Adobe Sensei (AI Ranking)
        |
        +----> Synced Catalog Index
                    ^
                    |
          [SaaS Data Export Module]
                    |
          Commerce Catalog (DB)
```

**Exam focus:**
- LiveSearch is **powered by Adobe Sensei** — AI/ML drives relevance ranking.
- LiveSearch is a **SaaS service** — it runs in Adobe's cloud, not on the Commerce server.
- Requires an **API key** to connect Commerce to the LiveSearch service (via Commerce Services Connector).

---

### 2.2 LiveSearch vs Native Search

This comparison is **heavily tested**:

| Feature | LiveSearch (SaaS) | Native Search (OpenSearch/ES) |
|---|---|---|
| **Engine** | Adobe Sensei (cloud AI) | OpenSearch / Elasticsearch 8 (Deprecated) |
| **Configuration** | API key + SaaS data sync | `env.php` connection settings |
| **Search type** | Real-time as-you-type | Standard query-response |
| **Index location** | Adobe cloud infrastructure | Local/remote ES/OS cluster |
| **Facets** | Dynamic, AI-assisted | Manually configured layered nav |
| **Merchandising rules** | Built-in (boost/bury/pin/hide) | Not available natively |
| **Synonyms** | Built-in SaaS UI management | **Built-in** (Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Synonyms) |
| **Requires OpenSearch** | **No** for storefront search — but ES/OS still needed for catalog indexing and admin | Yes |
| **Behavioral data** | Collected and used for ranking | Not used |
| **License** | Adobe Commerce SaaS service | Included with Magento OS |

> **Important correction:** Native Magento search **does** support synonyms natively via the `Magento_Search` module. The admin path is **Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Synonyms**. This is a built-in CE feature, not an extension requirement. Both one-way and two-way synonyms are supported natively.

**Exam focus:**
- **LiveSearch works independently of OpenSearch/Elasticsearch for storefront search** — when LiveSearch is active, the ES/OS configuration is bypassed for customer-facing search queries.
- **However**, OpenSearch/ES is still used for **catalog indexing and admin search** even with LiveSearch active. It is not entirely eliminated.
- LiveSearch requires an **API key** via the Commerce Services Connector.
- Native search still uses the `env.php` `elasticsearch` or `opensearch` configuration block.

**env.php native search config (for reference — NOT used by LiveSearch for storefront):**
```php
'system' => [
    'default' => [
        'catalog' => [
            'search' => [
                'engine' => 'opensearch',
                'opensearch_server_hostname' => 'localhost',
                'opensearch_server_port' => '9200',
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
```

---

### 2.3 Features: Facets, Synonyms & Rules

#### Facets

Facets are the **filterable attributes** displayed in the search results sidebar. LiveSearch supports:

- **Pinned facets** — always displayed at the top (e.g., Price, Color)
- **Dynamic facets** — AI-selected based on query context
- **Intelligent faceting** — automatically selects relevant attributes

**Admin path (requires LiveSearch package installed):**
```
Admin → Marketing → LiveSearch → Facets
```

**Exam focus:**
- LiveSearch supports **dynamic facets** — these are AI-selected, unlike native layered navigation which requires manual attribute configuration.
- Facets must be **enabled as searchable/filterable** on the attribute level in the Commerce catalog.

#### Synonyms

Synonyms allow merchants to map alternate query terms to canonical terms:

| Synonym Type | Behavior | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **One-way** | Term A → results for Term B | "sofa" → shows "couch" results |
| **Two-way** | Term A ↔ Term B (bidirectional) | "shirt" ↔ "tee" — both map to each other |

**Admin path (LiveSearch):**
```
Admin → Marketing → LiveSearch → Synonyms
```

> **Note:** Native Magento also has synonym management at **Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Synonyms** (module-search). LiveSearch provides its own separate synonym management in its SaaS UI.

**Exam focus:**
- Know the difference between **one-way** and **two-way** synonyms.
- LiveSearch synonyms are managed in the **LiveSearch admin UI** (under Marketing > LiveSearch).
- Native synonyms are managed at **Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Synonyms**.

#### Merchandising Rules (Search Rules)

Rules allow merchants to **manually influence search results** for specific queries:

| Rule Action | Description |
|---|---|
| **Boost** | Increases ranking of specified product(s) for a query |
| **Bury** | Decreases ranking of specified product(s) for a query |
| **Pin** | Fixes a product at a specific position (e.g., position 1) in results |
| **Hide** | Completely removes a product from results for a query |

**Admin path (requires LiveSearch package):**
```
Admin → Marketing → LiveSearch → Rules
```

Rules support **conditions** (e.g., apply rule only when query contains "sale") and **date scheduling** (start/end dates).

**Exam focus:**
- **Pin** places a product at an *exact position* — distinct from Boost which only raises rank.
- **Hide** removes the product from results entirely — distinct from Bury which only lowers rank.
- Rules are **query-specific** — they apply to particular search terms, not globally.

---

### 2.4 Relevance Ranking

LiveSearch uses a multi-factor relevance model powered by Adobe Sensei:

```
Relevance Score Factors:
  +---------------------------+
  | Text Match Relevance      |  (title, description, SKU matches)
  | Behavioral Signals        |  (click-through rate, purchase rate)
  | Popularity                |  (overall sales volume)
  | Recency                   |  (recently added/updated products)
  | Merchandising Rules       |  (manual boost/bury overrides)
  +---------------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- LiveSearch ranking uses **behavioral data** (clicks, purchases) — this data must accumulate before AI ranking is fully effective.
- Merchants can override AI ranking via **merchandising rules**.

---

### 2.5 SaaS Data Export & Sync Delay

This is one of the **trickiest exam topics**.

#### How SaaS Data Export Works

LiveSearch does **not** query the Commerce database directly. Instead, the catalog must be **exported to Adobe's cloud infrastructure** via the SaaS Data Export module.

```
Step 1: Catalog data in Commerce DB
           |
           v
Step 2: SaaS Data Export module packages catalog
           |
           v  (HTTPS to Adobe API)
Step 3: Adobe LiveSearch Cloud Index updated
           |
           v
Step 4: Storefront search queries hit cloud index
```

**Key SaaS Data Export facts:**

| Fact | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Module** | `Magento_SaaSCommon` (module-saas-common) — provides `saas:resync` CLI command |
| **Trigger** | Runs on product save, price update, and scheduled cron |
| **Initial sync** | Full catalog export on first setup (can take hours for large catalogs) |
| **Incremental sync** | Delta updates for changed products |
| **Sync delay** | Minutes to hours — catalog changes are **NOT instantly searchable** |

**Resync command:**
```bash
# Force full catalog resync to SaaS service
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=products

# Check sync status (dry run without exporting)
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=products --dry-run

# Additional options:
#   --no-reindex         Re-submission only, no re-indexing
#   --cleanup-feed       Force cleanup of feed indexer table
#   --thread-count       Set synchronization thread count
#   --batch-size         Set synchronization batch size
#   --continue-resync    Continue from last position
```

**Available feeds:**
```bash
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=products
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=productattributes
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=variants
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=categories
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=prices
```

**Exam focus:**
- The **sync delay** means newly added products may not appear in LiveSearch results immediately.
- This is a **known architectural trade-off** of SaaS-based search.
- The `saas:resync` command forces a re-export of the catalog.
- LiveSearch uses its **own cloud index** — *not* the local OpenSearch/ES index.

---

### 2.6 Configuration in Admin

**Full LiveSearch setup checklist:**

1. **Install the LiveSearch module:**
```bash
composer require magento/live-search
bin/magento module:enable Magento_LiveSearch
bin/magento setup:upgrade
```

2. **Configure API credentials:**
```
Admin → Stores → Configuration → Services → Commerce Services Connector
  → API Keys: Public Key + Private Key
  → SaaS Environment: Production / Sandbox
```

> **Note:** The API key configuration is under the **"Services" tab** (tab=service) in the **"Commerce Services Connector"** section (section=services_connector). The group is "API Keys" (group=services_connector_integration). This is NOT a LiveSearch-specific config section — it is the shared Commerce Services Connector used by both LiveSearch and Product Recommendations.

3. **Trigger initial catalog sync:**
```bash
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=products
```

4. **Configure facets:**
```
Admin → Marketing → LiveSearch → Facets
```

5. **Configure synonyms:**
```
Admin → Marketing → LiveSearch → Synonyms
```

6. **Create merchandising rules:**
```
Admin → Marketing → LiveSearch → Rules
```

7. **Preview & test search:**
```
Admin → Marketing → LiveSearch → Performance
```

**Exam focus:**
- API key configuration is at **Stores → Configuration → Services → Commerce Services Connector** (shared connector, not LiveSearch-specific).
- LiveSearch has its **own section under Marketing** for facets, synonyms, and rules (part of the LiveSearch SaaS package, not in base EE codebase).

---

## 3. Product Recommendations (Sensei)

### 3.1 Overview

**Product Recommendations** is an Adobe Commerce SaaS module that uses **Adobe Sensei** behavioral data and AI to display personalized product suggestion widgets on the storefront. Like LiveSearch, it:

- Runs as a **SaaS service** in Adobe's cloud
- Requires **API key configuration** (same Commerce Services Connector)
- Requires **behavioral data** collected from shopper interactions
- Is available for **Adobe Commerce only** (not Magento Open Source)
- Is a **separate package** (`magento/product-recommendations`) — NOT included in the base EE distribution

```
Shopper Behavior (views, clicks, purchases)
           |
           v
  Adobe Sensei Behavioral Engine
           |
           v
  Recommendation Algorithm
           |
           v
  Recommendation Widget on Storefront Page
```

---

### 3.2 Recommendation Types

**Exam focus:** Memorize all recommendation types and their behavioral requirements.

| Recommendation Type | How It Works | Min Data Required |
|---|---|---|
| **Most Viewed** | Products most viewed across all shoppers | Low (view events) |
| **Most Purchased** | Products most frequently purchased | Medium (purchase events) |
| **Most Added to Cart** | Products most added to cart | Medium (cart events) |
| **Trending** | Products with rapidly increasing view velocity | Medium-High (time-series view events) |
| **Viewed This, Viewed That** | "Other customers who viewed this also viewed..." | High (co-view behavioral pairs) |
| **Viewed This, Bought That** | "Customers who viewed this ended up buying..." | High (view-to-purchase behavioral pairs) |
| **Bought This, Bought That** | "Customers who bought this also bought..." | High (co-purchase behavioral pairs) |
| **More Like This** | Content-based similarity (attributes, categories) | Low (catalog-based, no behavior needed) |
| **Visual Similarity** | Image-based product similarity via AI | Low (catalog images) |
| **Recently Viewed** | Last N products viewed by *this* shopper | Per-session (no global data needed) |

**Detailed behavioral notes:**

```
Data dependency spectrum:

  Low data required                     High data required
  |---------------------------------------------|
  Recently   More    Most     Most    Viewed/   Bought
  Viewed     Like    Viewed   Purchased Bought  This/
             This                      That     That
```

**Exam focus:**
- **"Viewed This, Bought That"** and **"Bought This, Bought That"** require the **most behavioral data** — they need sufficient co-occurrence pairs to generate meaningful recommendations.
- **"More Like This"** is **catalog-based**, not behavioral — it works even with no purchase/view history.
- **"Recently Viewed"** is **session-based** — works for individual shoppers with no global data.
- **Minimum impressions threshold**: Adobe requires a minimum number of impressions/events before a recommendation unit becomes active (to avoid showing low-confidence results).

---

### 3.3 Placement Options

Product Recommendations can be placed on multiple **page types**:

| Page Type | Common Use Cases |
|---|---|
| **Homepage** | Most Viewed, Trending, Most Purchased |
| **Product Detail Page (PDP)** | Viewed This/Bought That, More Like This, Visual Similarity |
| **Cart Page** | Bought This/Bought That, Most Added to Cart |
| **Category Page** | Most Viewed (within category), Trending |
| **Order Confirmation Page** | Most Purchased, Trending |
| **Custom Page** | Any type, merchant-configured |

**Admin path to configure placements (requires Product Recommendations package):**
```
Admin → Marketing → Product Recommendations → Create Recommendation
  → Page Type: [Homepage | Product | Cart | Category | Order Confirmation | Custom]
  → Recommendation Type: [select from list]
  → Recommendation Name: (internal label)
  → Number of Products: (how many to display)
  → Placement Position: (before/after main content)
```

**Exam focus:**
- **PDP (Product Detail Page)** is the most common placement for cross-sell types like "Viewed This, Bought That."
- **Cart page** is ideal for "Bought This, Bought That" (last-minute add-ons).
- You can have **multiple recommendation units per page** — each independently configured.

---

### 3.4 Behavioral Data Requirements

Product Recommendations requires **storefront events** to be collected before AI-driven types become active.

#### Event Collection Architecture

```
  Shopper Action (view/click/add-to-cart/purchase)
           |
           v
  Commerce Storefront (Event SDK / data layer)
           |
           v (JavaScript event firing)
  Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) Data Collection
           |
           v
  Adobe Sensei Behavioral Model
           |
           v
  Recommendation Scores Updated
```

#### Minimum Data Thresholds

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Minimum impressions** | Each recommendation type needs a minimum number of recorded events before it activates |
| **Training period** | New stores typically need **several weeks** of data before behavioral recommendations work well |
| **Catalog sync** | Products must be synced via SaaS Data Export before they can appear in recommendations |
| **Fallback behavior** | If insufficient data exists, Adobe may show popular/catalog-based results instead |

**Exam focus:**
- A newly installed Product Recommendations module will **not immediately show behavioral recommendations** — there is a data accumulation period.
- The **minimum impression threshold** is a common exam trap — behavioral rec types require minimum data before they go live.
- If behavioral data is insufficient, the system may **fall back to catalog-based** recommendations.

---

### 3.5 Configuration & Admin Setup

**Installation:**
```bash
composer require magento/product-recommendations
bin/magento module:enable Magento_ProductRecommendationsAdmin
bin/magento setup:upgrade
```

**Configuration path:**
```
Admin → Stores → Configuration → Services → Commerce Services Connector
  (same API key used by LiveSearch — shared connector)

Admin → Marketing → Product Recommendations
  → Create Recommendation
  → View existing recommendations + performance metrics
```

**Recommendation performance panel:**

The admin shows each recommendation unit with:
- **Impressions** — how many times the widget was displayed
- **Clicks** — how many times a recommended product was clicked
- **Revenue** — revenue attributed to recommendation clicks
- **CTR (Click-Through Rate)** — clicks / impressions

**Exam focus:**
- Product Recommendations and LiveSearch **share the same Commerce Services Connector API key**.
- Performance data (impressions, CTR, revenue) is visible per recommendation unit in the admin.

---

## 4. Integration Architecture: How the Three Services Connect

```
  +-----------------------------------------------------+
  |           Adobe Commerce Instance                    |
  |                                                     |
  |  [Catalog DB] --> [SaaS Data Export] ----+          |
  |                                          |          |
  |  [Storefront] --> [Event SDK] -------+   |          |
  |                                      |   |          |
  +------------------------------+-------+---+----------+
                                 |       |
                          Events |       | Catalog Data
                                 v       v
  +-----------------------------------------------------+
  |           Adobe Cloud / Sensei Services              |
  |                                                     |
  |  +------------------+   +------------------------+ |
  |  | LiveSearch Index |   | Behavioral Data Store  | |
  |  | (Catalog Data)   |   | (View/Purchase Events) | |
  |  +------------------+   +------------------------+ |
  |           |                        |               |
  |           v                        v               |
  |  +------------------+   +------------------------+ |
  |  | LiveSearch API   |   | Product Rec Engine     | |
  |  | (Search Results) |   | (Recommendation Units) | |
  |  +------------------+   +------------------------+ |
  |                                                     |
  |  +---------------------------------------------+   |
  |  | Adobe Commerce Intelligence (BI)            |   |
  |  | (Syncs from Commerce DB - separate pipeline)|   |
  |  +---------------------------------------------+   |
  +-----------------------------------------------------+
                    ^
                    |
          API Key (Commerce Services Connector)
          Shared by LiveSearch + Product Recommendations
```

**Key shared infrastructure:**
- LiveSearch and Product Recommendations both use the **Commerce Services Connector** (same API key, section=services_connector, tab=service)
- Both rely on **SaaS Data Export** for catalog synchronization (CLI: `bin/magento saas:resync`)
- Both have an inherent **sync delay**
- BI uses a **separate sync pipeline** (Data Warehouse Manager), not SaaS Data Export

---

## 5. Tricky Exam Concepts & Common Pitfalls

### 5.1 LiveSearch Independence from OpenSearch/Elasticsearch

> **This is one of the most commonly tested "gotcha" facts.**

When LiveSearch is installed and configured:
- The storefront search **bypasses OpenSearch/Elasticsearch entirely** for customer-facing queries
- The `catalog/search/engine` setting in `env.php` / Admin is **ignored for storefront search**
- OpenSearch/ES is still used for **catalog indexing and admin-side search** — it is NOT fully eliminated
- The available search engine options in admin are: **OpenSearch** and **Elasticsearch 8 (Deprecated)**

**Exam focus:**
- LiveSearch = **Adobe cloud** handles **storefront** search queries
- Native search = **local/remote OpenSearch/ES** handles search queries
- They are **mutually exclusive** for storefront search
- OpenSearch/ES is still needed for **backend catalog indexing** even with LiveSearch active

---

### 5.2 SaaS Sync Delay is a Known Limitation

| Scenario | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Merchant adds new product | Product **not immediately searchable** in LiveSearch |
| Merchant updates price | Price change may take **minutes** to reflect in search |
| Merchant disables product | Product may **still appear briefly** before sync |
| Initial setup | Full sync may take **hours** for large catalogs |

**Exam focus:** Sync delay affects **LiveSearch** and **Product Recommendations** equally — both depend on SaaS Data Export.

---

### 5.3 BI is NOT Real-Time

| System | Data Freshness |
|---|---|
| LiveSearch | Minutes delay (SaaS sync) |
| Product Recommendations | Minutes-hours delay (behavioral + catalog sync) |
| Commerce Intelligence (BI) | Hours delay (Data Warehouse sync cycle) |
| Native Admin Reports | Near real-time (direct DB query) |

**Exam focus:** If an exam question asks about **real-time reporting**, the answer is **NOT BI** — use Admin native reports for real-time data.

---

### 5.4 Minimum Impressions for Product Recommendations

- New recommendation units display a **"Not enough data"** or **"Collecting data"** status
- Adobe requires a **statistically significant** number of events before activating behavioral algorithms
- This prevents low-confidence recommendations from degrading shopper experience
- The threshold varies by recommendation type (behavioral types need more data)

---

### 5.5 API Key Setup is Prerequisite for Both LiveSearch and Recommendations

```
Admin → Stores → Configuration → Services → Commerce Services Connector
(section=services_connector, tab=service, group=services_connector_integration "API Keys")
```

Without a valid API key:
- LiveSearch will **fall back to native search**
- Product Recommendations will **not display any widgets**
- SaaS Data Export will **fail silently** or log errors

---

### 5.6 BI Custom Metrics — Operations Summary

| Operation | Use Case |
|---|---|
| `SUM` | Total revenue, total discount amount |
| `COUNT` | Number of orders, number of customers |
| `AVERAGE` | Average order value, average items per order |
| `MAX` | Highest single order value |
| `MIN` | Lowest single order value |
| `COUNT DISTINCT` | Unique customers, unique products ordered |

---

### 5.7 LiveSearch Rule Priority

When multiple rules apply to the same query:
1. **Pin** rules take highest priority (exact position overrides everything)
2. **Boost** / **Bury** adjust score within remaining positions
3. **Hide** removes products before ranking is applied
4. AI ranking applies to all remaining products

**Exam focus:** **Pin > Boost/Bury > Hide > AI Ranking** — pin always wins.

---

### 5.8 Native Search Synonym Support

> **Common misconception:** Many study resources incorrectly state that native Magento search does NOT support synonyms. This is WRONG.

Native Magento includes built-in synonym management:
- **Admin path:** Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Synonyms
- **Module:** `Magento_Search` (CE, available in both CE and EE)
- Supports both **one-way** and **two-way** synonyms
- The difference is that LiveSearch provides its **own separate** synonym system in its SaaS UI

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Adobe Commerce Intelligence (BI)
- [ ] Accessed via **Admin → Reports → Business Intelligence** (two sub-items: Advanced Reporting, BI Essentials)
- [ ] Both menu items open **externally** (target="_blank") — BI is a SaaS portal
- [ ] Formerly called **MBI (Magento Business Intelligence)**
- [ ] `module-analytics` (Advanced Reporting integration) is **CE + EE** (OSL-3.0 license)
- [ ] Full BI SaaS platform (data warehouse, custom metrics) requires **Adobe Commerce subscription**
- [ ] Advanced Reporting config: Stores > Configuration > General > Advanced Reporting (section=analytics)
- [ ] Pre-built report pillars: **Revenue, Customers, Products**
- [ ] Key reports: **New vs Returning Customers, Cohort Analysis, Revenue by Product, CLV**
- [ ] Cohort Analysis = grouping customers by **acquisition period** to measure retention
- [ ] CLV = **Average Order Value x Purchase Frequency x Customer Lifespan**
- [ ] Custom metrics require: **table, operation (SUM/COUNT/AVG), column, timestamp, optional filters**
- [ ] Dashboards support **scheduled email delivery**
- [ ] Data sync is **not real-time** — hourly sync cycles via Data Warehouse Manager
- [ ] **Data Warehouse Manager** = UI for selecting which tables/columns to sync
- [ ] Adding a new custom attribute requires **manually adding it to Data Warehouse sync**

### LiveSearch
- [ ] Powered by **Adobe Sensei** (AI/ML)
- [ ] **Separate SaaS package** — NOT in base EE codebase; install via `composer require magento/live-search`
- [ ] Requires **API key** via Commerce Services Connector (section=services_connector, tab=service)
- [ ] Bypasses OpenSearch/ES for **storefront search** — but ES/OS still needed for catalog indexing
- [ ] Provides **real-time search-as-you-type** on the storefront
- [ ] Requires **SaaS Data Export** to sync catalog to Adobe cloud (`bin/magento saas:resync`)
- [ ] There is always a **sync delay** after catalog changes
- [ ] Supports **dynamic facets** (AI-selected) and **pinned facets** (merchant-selected)
- [ ] Synonym types: **one-way** (A → B) and **two-way** (A ↔ B)
- [ ] Rule actions: **Boost** (raise rank), **Bury** (lower rank), **Pin** (exact position), **Hide** (remove)
- [ ] Rule priority: **Pin > Boost/Bury > Hide > AI Ranking**
- [ ] Merchandising rules are **query-specific** and support **date scheduling**
- [ ] Relevance factors: text match + behavioral signals + popularity + recency + rules
- [ ] CLI resync command: `bin/magento saas:resync --feed=products`
- [ ] Admin config paths: **Marketing → LiveSearch → [Facets / Synonyms / Rules]** (when package installed)

### Product Recommendations
- [ ] Powered by **Adobe Sensei** behavioral AI
- [ ] **Separate SaaS package** — NOT in base EE codebase; install via `composer require magento/product-recommendations`
- [ ] Shares **same API key** as LiveSearch (Commerce Services Connector)
- [ ] Available in **Adobe Commerce only**
- [ ] Requires **SaaS Data Export** for catalog sync
- [ ] Requires **behavioral event data** accumulation before AI types activate
- [ ] **"More Like This"** = catalog-based, **no behavioral data required**
- [ ] **"Recently Viewed"** = session-based, no global data required
- [ ] **"Bought This, Bought That"** and **"Viewed This, Bought That"** = highest data requirements
- [ ] **Minimum impressions threshold** must be met before behavioral recommendations go live
- [ ] New stores see **"Collecting data"** status until threshold is met
- [ ] Placement options: **Homepage, PDP, Cart, Category, Order Confirmation, Custom**
- [ ] PDP best for: **cross-sell types** (Viewed/Bought That)
- [ ] Cart page best for: **Bought This, Bought That**
- [ ] Multiple recommendation units **can coexist on the same page**
- [ ] Performance metrics per unit: **Impressions, Clicks, Revenue, CTR**
- [ ] Admin path: **Marketing → Product Recommendations → Create Recommendation** (when package installed)

### Cross-Module Integration
- [ ] LiveSearch + Product Recommendations share **Commerce Services Connector** API key
- [ ] Both services depend on **SaaS Data Export** (CLI: `bin/magento saas:resync`, module: `Magento_SaaSCommon`)
- [ ] Both have **sync delay** — not real-time
- [ ] BI uses a **separate sync pipeline** (Data Warehouse, not SaaS Export)
- [ ] For **real-time data**, use native Admin reports — **not BI**
- [ ] **Advanced Reporting** (module-analytics) available in **both CE and EE**
- [ ] **Full BI SaaS platform**, LiveSearch, and Product Recommendations are **Adobe Commerce subscription** services

### Native Search vs LiveSearch — Key Differences
- [ ] Native search supports synonyms **natively** (Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Synonyms)
- [ ] Native search uses **manually configured** layered navigation (not dynamic facets)
- [ ] Native search has **no merchandising rules** (boost/bury/pin/hide)
- [ ] Native search has **no behavioral ranking**
- [ ] Available native search engines: **OpenSearch**, **Elasticsearch 8 (Deprecated)**

flashcards.question: Where is Adobe Commerce Intelligence (BI) accessed in the admin, and how does it work?
flashcards.answer: BI is accessed via Admin > Reports > Business Intelligence, which opens externally in a new browser tab. BI is a SaaS (cloud-based) application — it does NOT run on the Commerce server. It syncs data from the Commerce database on a schedule (typically hourly).
flashcards.hint: The admin link opens a separate portal — the analytics run in the cloud, not locally.

flashcards.question: What is Cohort Analysis in Adobe Commerce BI and what does it measure?
flashcards.answer: Cohort Analysis groups customers by a shared characteristic at a point in time (e.g., month of first purchase) and tracks their behavior over subsequent periods. It measures customer retention over time. Cohorts are typically grouped by acquisition month/quarter, with Month 0 always being the 100% baseline.
flashcards.hint: It answers 'of the customers who first bought in January, how many came back in February?'

flashcards.question: What is the formula for Customer Lifetime Value (CLV)?
flashcards.answer: CLV = Average Order Value x Purchase Frequency x Customer Lifespan. CLV is one of the most strategically important metrics in BI, used for long-term customer value analysis and determining how much to invest in customer acquisition and retention.
flashcards.hint: Three multiplied factors: how much they spend per order, how often they buy, and how long they stay.

flashcards.question: What powers LiveSearch and how does it differ from native search?
flashcards.answer: LiveSearch is powered by Adobe Sensei (AI/ML framework) and runs as a SaaS service in Adobe's cloud. Unlike native OpenSearch/Elasticsearch which runs on the Commerce server, LiveSearch provides real-time search-as-you-type, AI-powered relevance ranking, dynamic facets, and merchandising rules (boost/bury/pin/hide).
flashcards.hint: Adobe's AI powers cloud-based search with features native search cannot provide.

flashcards.question: When LiveSearch is active, is OpenSearch/Elasticsearch still needed?
flashcards.answer: Yes. While LiveSearch bypasses OpenSearch/ES for storefront search queries, OpenSearch/ES is still needed for catalog indexing and admin-side search. LiveSearch handles customer-facing search; the underlying search engine handles backend operations.
flashcards.hint: The SaaS service replaces one function but not all functions of the search engine.

flashcards.question: What are the four merchandising rule actions available in LiveSearch?
flashcards.answer: Boost (increases product ranking for a query), Bury (decreases ranking), Pin (fixes a product at a specific position in results), and Hide (completely removes a product from results for a query). Pin takes highest priority, followed by Boost/Bury, then Hide, then AI ranking.
flashcards.hint: Four actions that let merchants manually override AI-driven search results.

flashcards.question: What is the key difference between 'Pin' and 'Boost' in LiveSearch merchandising rules?
flashcards.answer: Pin places a product at an EXACT position in search results (e.g., always position 1). Boost only raises the product's ranking relative to other results without guaranteeing a specific position. Pin always takes the highest priority of all rule actions.
flashcards.hint: One guarantees an exact slot; the other just pushes upward.

flashcards.question: Why might a newly added product not appear in LiveSearch results immediately?
flashcards.answer: LiveSearch uses SaaS Data Export to sync the catalog to Adobe's cloud infrastructure. There is always a sync delay (minutes to hours) between catalog changes and search availability. The initial full sync can take hours for large catalogs. The saas:resync CLI command can force a re-export.
flashcards.hint: Cloud-based search has an inherent data pipeline delay.

flashcards.question: What two types of synonyms does LiveSearch support, and how do they differ?
flashcards.answer: One-way synonyms expand in a single direction (e.g., 'sofa' shows 'couch' results, but 'couch' does NOT show 'sofa' results). Two-way synonyms are bidirectional — both terms map to each other (e.g., 'shirt' and 'tee' both show results for both terms).
flashcards.hint: One type is directional; the other is mutual.

flashcards.question: Which Product Recommendation types work immediately on a new store with no behavioral data?
flashcards.answer: Only 'Recently Viewed' (session-based, works from browser session) and 'More Like This' (catalog-based, uses product attribute similarity) work immediately. All behavioral types like 'Bought Together', 'Trending', and 'Viewed This, Bought That' require accumulated event data before they activate.
flashcards.hint: Two types bypass the cold start problem: one uses the browser session, the other uses catalog attributes.

flashcards.question: What infrastructure do LiveSearch and Product Recommendations share?
flashcards.answer: Both use the same Commerce Services Connector API key (configured at Stores > Configuration > Services > Commerce Services Connector) and both rely on SaaS Data Export for catalog synchronization (CLI: bin/magento saas:resync). Both have inherent sync delays.
flashcards.hint: They share the same authentication and the same data pipeline to Adobe's cloud.

flashcards.question: What are the five custom metric configuration elements in Adobe Commerce BI?
flashcards.answer: A custom metric requires: (1) Metric name, (2) Source table (e.g., sales_order), (3) Operation type (SUM, COUNT, AVERAGE, MAX, MIN), (4) Column to operate on (e.g., grand_total), and (5) Timestamp field for time-series analysis (e.g., created_at). Filters are optional.
flashcards.hint: Name what you measure, where the data lives, what math to apply, which field, and the time dimension.

flashcards.question: What system should you use for real-time reporting in Adobe Commerce — BI or native Admin reports?
flashcards.answer: Native Admin reports provide near real-time data because they query the database directly. BI data has hours of delay due to Data Warehouse sync cycles. For real-time reporting needs, the answer is always native Admin reports, not BI.
flashcards.hint: Direct database queries are immediate; cloud sync introduces delays.

flashcards.question: What happens if Product Recommendations has insufficient behavioral data for a recommendation type?
flashcards.answer: The recommendation unit shows a 'Not enough data' or 'Collecting data' status. Adobe requires a minimum number of impressions/events before activating behavioral algorithms to prevent low-confidence results. The system may fall back to showing popular or catalog-based results instead.
flashcards.hint: The AI waits for statistical confidence before serving recommendations.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between dynamic facets and pinned facets in LiveSearch?
flashcards.answer: Pinned facets are always displayed at a fixed position in the facet list regardless of the query (e.g., Price, Color). Dynamic facets are AI-selected based on the current query context — LiveSearch automatically determines which attributes are most relevant for each specific search.
flashcards.hint: One type is merchant-controlled; the other is AI-driven based on context.

studyNotes.title: Day 19 — Taxes, Duties & B2B Tax Configuration
studyNotes.content:
# Taxes, Duties & B2B Tax Configuration
### Adobe Commerce / Magento 2 — Week 3 Study Notes

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Tax Architecture Overview](#1-tax-architecture-overview)
2. [Tax Classes](#2-tax-classes)
3. [Tax Rates](#3-tax-rates)
4. [Tax Rules](#4-tax-rules)
5. [Tax Display Settings](#5-tax-display-settings)
6. [Origin-Based vs Destination-Based Tax](#6-origin-based-vs-destination-based-tax)
7. [Fixed Product Tax (FPT)](#7-fixed-product-tax-fpt)
8. [B2B Tax Configuration & Tax-Exempt Companies](#8-b2b-tax-configuration--tax-exempt-companies)
9. [VAT ID Validation & EU Reverse Charge](#9-vat-id-validation--eu-reverse-charge)
10. [Cross-Border Duties (DDP vs DDU/DAP)](#10-cross-border-duties-ddp-vs-ddusdap)
11. [Tax Calculation on Discounts (Tricky Math)](#11-tax-calculation-on-discounts-tricky-math)
12. [Tax Display Rounding & 1-Cent Discrepancies](#12-tax-display-rounding--1-cent-discrepancies)
13. [Third-Party Tax Integrations (Avalara, TaxJar)](#13-third-party-tax-integrations-avalara-taxjar)
14. [Hands-On: Configure a Tax Rule on EE](#14-hands-on-configure-a-tax-rule-on-ee)
15. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Tax Architecture Overview

Adobe Commerce uses a **layered tax engine** built from three foundational building blocks that combine into rules:

```
+------------------+     +---------------------+     +------------------+
|   Customer Tax   |     |    Product Tax       |     |    Tax Rate      |
|      Class       |  +  |      Class           |  +  | (Country/State/  |
|  (Who is buying) |     | (What is being sold) |     |  ZIP / %)        |
+------------------+     +---------------------+     +------------------+
          |                        |                         |
          +------------------------+-------------------------+
                                   |
                           +---------------+
                           |   TAX RULE    |
                           | (the trigger) |
                           +---------------+
```

- **Tax Classes** define *categories* of buyers and products.
- **Tax Rates** define *how much* tax applies in a given jurisdiction.
- **Tax Rules** *connect* the two: "When customer class X buys product class Y in jurisdiction Z, apply rate R."

> **Exam focus:** You cannot have a functioning tax system without all three components — class, rate, AND rule. Missing any one component means no tax is calculated.

---

## 2. Tax Classes

Tax classes are assigned to either **customers** or **products**.

### 2.1 Product Tax Classes

| Built-in Class | Typical Use Case |
|---|---|
| **Taxable Goods** | Standard physical goods (class_id 2, created by setup patch) |
| **Shipping** | Freight/shipping charges (must be manually created — not a built-in default) |

> **Note:** Only "Taxable Goods" is created by the default setup patch. A "None" option (class_id 0) is dynamically generated by the source model — it represents "no tax class assigned." The "Shipping" tax class must be created manually; by default the "Tax Class for Shipping" config field points to class_id 0 (None).

- Default tax classes configured at: **Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Tax Classes**
  - "Default Tax Class for Product" — **global scope only** (showInDefault=1, no website/store). Setting this at website scope has no effect.
  - "Tax Class for Shipping" — default + website scope (showInDefault=1, showInWebsite=1)
- Product tax class is set per product at: **Product > Tax Class** attribute (scope: SCOPE_WEBSITE)
- New product tax classes are created **inline within the Tax Rules form** — there is no separate "Stores > Taxes > Product Tax Classes" menu item. The Tax Rules form provides an AJAX-based interface to add new tax classes on the fly.

> **Exam focus:** "None" (class_id 0) is a special product tax class meaning the product is explicitly exempt from all tax calculation — not the same as "no class assigned."

### 2.2 Customer Tax Classes

| Built-in Class | Typical Use Case |
|---|---|
| **Retail Customer** | Standard B2C consumers (class_id 3, created by setup patch) |

> **Note:** Only "Retail Customer" is installed by default. A "Wholesale Customer" class must be created manually if needed for B2B scenarios.

- New customer tax classes are created **inline within the Tax Rules form** — there is no separate "Stores > Taxes > Customer Tax Classes" menu item.
- Customer group is assigned a tax class at: **Customers > Customer Groups > Tax Class**
- "Default Tax Class for Customer" is **global scope only** (showInDefault=1).
- The **logged-in customer's group** determines their tax class at checkout.

```
Customer Group "B2B Exempt"
       |
       v
Tax Class: "Wholesale" (or create "Tax Exempt")
       |
       v
Tax Rule: No matching rule for this class = $0 tax
```

> **Exam focus:** Tax exemption in Magento is achieved by assigning a customer group with a tax class that has **no matching tax rule** — there is no single "exempt" checkbox on a customer record in native Magento.

### 2.3 Class Assignment Flow

```bash
# Where tax classes are configured (Admin paths)
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Tax Classes
  - Default Tax Class for Customer: [Retail Customer]    # global scope only
  - Default Tax Class for Product: [Taxable Goods]       # global scope only
  - Tax Class for Shipping: [None] (default is None, class_id 0)  # default + website scope
```

---

## 3. Tax Rates

A **Tax Rate** defines the actual percentage for a specific geographic jurisdiction.

### 3.1 Rate Anatomy

| Field | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Tax Identifier** | Human-readable name | `US-CA-*-Rate 1` |
| **Country** | ISO 2-letter country code | `US` |
| **State/Province** | State dropdown or `*` for all | `California` |
| **ZIP/Post Code** | Specific ZIP, range, or `*` for all | `*` (all) |
| **Rate** | Percentage | `8.25` |
| **Zip/Post is Range** | Toggle for ZIP range matching | Yes / No |

### 3.2 Creating Tax Rates

```
Stores > Taxes > Tax Zones and Rates > Add New Tax Rate
```

- You can also **import/export** rates via CSV — critical for jurisdictions with hundreds of ZIP-level rates (e.g., US state + county + city combos).

```bash
# CSV import format example (header row)
Code,Country,State,Zip/Post Code,Rate,Zip/Post is Range,Range From,Range To
US-CA-*-8.25,US,CA,*,8.25,,,
US-NY-*-8.875,US,NY,*,8.875,,,
EU-DE-VAT-19,DE,*,*,19,,,
```

> **Exam focus:** The ZIP/Post Code field supports wildcards (`*`) and ranges. When multiple rates could match, Magento uses the **most specific match** (exact ZIP beats wildcard).

### 3.3 Compound / Combined Rates

For jurisdictions where state + county + city taxes stack:
- Create **separate rates** for each layer (state, county, city).
- Add all three rates to the **same Tax Rule** — Magento sums them.
- Or create a **single combined rate** (e.g., 8.25% = 6% state + 1.25% county + 1% city).

## 4. Tax Rules

A **Tax Rule** is the binding logic: it matches a customer tax class + product tax class + tax rate(s) to trigger calculation.

### 4.1 Tax Rule Configuration

```
Stores > Taxes > Tax Rules > Add New Rule
```

| Field | Options |
|---|---|
| **Name** | Descriptive label |
| **Customer Tax Class** | One or more customer tax classes |
| **Product Tax Class** | One or more product tax classes |
| **Tax Rate** | One or more rates (summed if multiple) |
| **Priority** | Integer; lower = applied first |
| **Calculate Off Subtotal Only** | If checked, compound taxes calculate off subtotal not on top of prior tax |
| **Sort Order** | Display order in invoices/receipts |

### 4.2 Priority & Compound Tax

```
Priority 0 (Standard VAT): 10% on $100 = $10  -> Subtotal becomes $110
Priority 1 (Surtax, compound=OFF): 2% on $100 = $2  -> Total: $112
Priority 1 (Surtax, compound=ON):  2% on $110 = $2.20 -> Total: $112.20
```

> **Exam focus:** **Priority** controls order of application. Same-priority rules are *added* together. **"Calculate Off Subtotal Only"** (compound tax) means each priority layer taxes the running total including prior tax — used in Quebec (QST+GST) and some EU scenarios.

### 4.3 Example Tax Rule Matrix

| Rule Name | Customer Class | Product Class | Rate Applied |
|---|---|---|---|
| US Retail Tax | Retail Customer | Taxable Goods | US-CA-8.25% |
| US Shipping Tax | Retail Customer | Shipping | US-CA-8.25% |
| B2B Exempt | Wholesale Customer | Taxable Goods | *(none — no rule)* |
| EU VAT B2C | Retail Customer | Taxable Goods | EU-DE-19% |

## 5. Tax Display Settings

Display settings control **how tax is shown to customers** — they do NOT change the tax amount calculated, only its presentation.

### 5.1 Configuration Location

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > (multiple sections)
```

### 5.2 Display Settings Breakdown

#### Tax Calculation Settings
```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Calculation Settings
```

| Setting | Options | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| Tax Calculation Method Based On | Unit Price / Row Total / Total | See rounding section |
| Tax Calculation Based On | Shipping Address / Billing Address / Shipping Origin | Jurisdiction determination |
| Catalog Prices | Excluding Tax / Including Tax | Whether catalog prices include tax |
| Shipping Prices | Excluding Tax / Including Tax | Whether shipping amounts include tax |
| Apply Customer Tax | Before Discount / After Discount | **Critical for discount math** |
| Apply Discount On Prices | Excluding Tax / Including Tax | Changes effective discount amount |
| Apply Tax On | Custom price (if available) / Original price only | Which price to use for tax calculation |
| Enable Cross Border Trade | Yes / No | Fixes price regardless of customer tax rate |

> **Scope note:** All Calculation Settings fields are available at **default + website scope only** (showInDefault=1, showInWebsite=1, no showInStore). You cannot set different calculation methods per store view — they silently have no effect at store view scope.

#### Shopping Cart Display Settings
```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Shopping Cart Display Settings
```

| Setting | Options |
|---|---|
| Display Prices | Excluding Tax / Including Tax / Including and Excluding Tax |
| Display Subtotal | Excluding Tax / Including Tax / Including and Excluding Tax |
| Display Shipping Amount | Excluding Tax / Including Tax / Including and Excluding Tax |
| Additionally Show Order Total Without Tax | Yes / No |
| Display Full Tax Summary | Yes / No |
| Display Zero Tax Subtotal | Yes / No |

#### Orders, Invoices, Credit Memos Display
```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Orders, Invoices, Credit Memos Display Settings
```

Same excl/incl options as cart — applies to **order confirmation, admin view, PDFs**.

> **Exam focus:** Display settings are available at **default, website, and store view** levels. A B2B store view can show prices excluding tax while a B2C view shows prices including tax — same products, same actual tax, different presentation. However, **Calculation Settings** are only configurable at default and website levels, not per store view.

### 5.3 Catalog Price: Excl. vs Incl. Tax

This is one of the most confusing settings:

```
If "Catalog Prices = Including Tax":
  - Price entered in admin ($119) INCLUDES the 19% VAT
  - Magento back-calculates: net = $119 / 1.19 = $100, VAT = $19
  - Displayed price to customer = $119 (incl.) or $100 (excl.) depending on display

If "Catalog Prices = Excluding Tax":
  - Price entered in admin ($100) EXCLUDES tax
  - Magento calculates: VAT = $100 * 0.19 = $19, total = $119
  - Displayed price to customer = $100 (excl.) or $119 (incl.) depending on display
```

> **Exam focus:** The EU standard is **Catalog Prices = Including Tax** (consumer-facing price is always tax-inclusive). US merchants typically use **Excluding Tax**. Changing this setting on a live store requires repricing all products.

## 6. Origin-Based vs Destination-Based Tax

### 6.1 Definitions

| Type | Description | Typical Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Origin-Based** | Tax calculated at seller's location | US states like Texas, Pennsylvania |
| **Destination-Based** | Tax calculated at buyer's shipping address | Most US states (majority), EU VAT |
| **Billing Address** | Uses billing address for tax jurisdiction | Less common, sometimes used for services |

### 6.2 Configuration

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Calculation Settings
  > Tax Calculation Based On: [Shipping Address] <-- most common (destination-based)
```

> **Note:** The option labels in Magento admin are "Shipping Address", "Billing Address", and "Shipping Origin" — not "Shipping Destination". The config value stored is `shipping` for the "Shipping Address" option.

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Default Tax Destination Calculation
  > Default Country: [US]
  > Default State: [CA]        <- used before customer enters address (catalog display)
  > Default Post Code: [*]
```

> **Exam focus:** The **Default Tax Destination** settings determine what tax is shown in the **catalog/product page** before a customer logs in or enters an address. They are NOT the actual tax — they are the *estimated* display tax. Actual tax is calculated at checkout with the real address.

### 6.3 Tax Origin Configuration (for Origin-Based)

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Shipping Settings > Origin
  > Country: United States
  > Region/State: Texas
  > ZIP/Postal Code: 78701
```

When Tax Calculation Based On = **Shipping Origin**, this address is used for all tax jurisdiction lookups.

## 7. Fixed Product Tax (FPT)

**Fixed Product Tax** (also called **eco-tax**, **WEEE** — Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment) is a flat fee added to specific products regardless of the order total.

### 7.1 Common Use Cases

- **WEEE directive** (EU): recycling fee on electronics
- **Eco-fees**: tire recycling fee (Canada), battery recycling
- **State-mandated flat fees**: California Electronic Waste Recycling Fee (eWaste)

### 7.2 Enabling FPT

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Fixed Product Taxes
  > Enable FPT: Yes
  > Display Prices In Product Lists: [4 options — see below]
  > Display Prices On Product View Page: [4 options — see below]
  > Display Prices In Sales Modules: [4 options — see below]
  > Display Prices In Emails: [4 options — see below]
  > Apply Tax To FPT: Yes / No    (whether sales tax applies to the FPT amount itself)
  > Include FPT In Subtotal: Yes / No
```

> **Note:** The FPT config section is in module-weee (group id=weee, under section=tax). "Enable FPT" and "Apply Tax To FPT" are simple Yes/No toggles. There is no "Apply Discounts to FPT" field and no "FPT Tax Configuration" dropdown in the native admin — these were Magento 1 concepts. In Magento 2, the FPT tax behavior is controlled solely by the "Apply Tax To FPT" Yes/No toggle.

> **Scope note:** All FPT fields are available at **default + website scope** (showInDefault=1, showInWebsite=1, no showInStore). FPT configuration cannot be varied per store view.

### 7.3 Setting FPT on a Product

After enabling FPT, a new attribute type `Fixed Product Tax` (internal type: `weee`) is available:

```
Products > [Edit Product] > [FPT attribute, e.g. "WEEE Tax"]
  > Country: Germany
  > State/Province: *
  > Tax: 5.00  (flat EUR amount)
```

- FPT values are **per country/state combination**.
- Multiple country rows can be added per product.

```
Product price:    $100.00
FPT (eWaste):      $12.00
Subtotal:         $112.00
Sales Tax (8%):     $8.00  (if "Apply Tax To FPT = No", tax is on $100 only)
Order Total:      $120.00
```

> **Exam focus:** FPT is a **flat fee per unit**, not a percentage. Whether sales tax applies to the FPT amount itself is controlled by the "Apply Tax To FPT" setting. When set to No, the sales tax base is the product price only, excluding the FPT.

### 7.4 FPT Display Options

The display fields (Product Lists, Product View, Sales Modules, Emails) each offer 4 options:

| FPT Display Option | What Customer Sees |
|---|---|
| Including FPT only | Base price + FPT combined (no breakdown) |
| Including FPT and FPT description | Base price + FPT + label like "Includes $12 WEEE" |
| Excluding FPT. Including FPT description and final price | Base price shown, plus FPT description and total |
| Excluding FPT | Base price only |
