## 8. B2B Tax Configuration & Tax-Exempt Companies

### 8.1 Adobe Commerce B2B Module Tax Flow

```
Company Account Created
        |
        v
Company assigned to Customer Group (e.g., "Wholesale" or "Tax Exempt")
        |
        v
Customer Group has Tax Class = "Wholesale" (no applicable tax rule)
        |
        v
Zero tax calculated at checkout for all company members
```

### 8.2 Creating a Tax-Exempt Customer Group

```
Customers > Customer Groups > Add New Customer Group
  > Group Name: B2B Tax Exempt
  > Tax Class: [Create new: "Tax Exempt Class" OR leave no matching rule]
```

The key is ensuring **no Tax Rule** exists that maps:
- `Customer Tax Class = "Tax Exempt"` + any product class → any rate

```
# Verification: Create rule with Tax Exempt class would ADD tax back
# Leave unmapped = $0 tax  <-- this is the correct approach
```

### 8.3 Assigning Tax Exemption to a Company

```
# Via Admin:
Customers > Companies > [Select Company] > Advanced Settings
  > Customer Group: B2B Tax Exempt

# All users belonging to this company inherit the group's tax class
```

> **Exam focus:** In B2B, tax exemption is managed at the **Company > Customer Group** level, not per individual customer account. All members of the company share the group's tax class.

### 8.4 Shared Catalog and Tax

Adobe Commerce B2B **Shared Catalogs** can show different prices to different companies. Tax display still follows the customer's group/tax class regardless of which shared catalog they are assigned to.

## 9. VAT ID Validation & EU Reverse Charge

### 9.1 What is the Reverse Charge Mechanism?

In EU B2B transactions:
- **B2C** (business to consumer): Seller charges local VAT of the buyer's country (post-2021 OSS rules)
- **B2B cross-border** (within EU): If the buyer has a valid **VAT ID** in their member state, the **seller charges 0% VAT** and the buyer self-accounts (reverse charge)

```
EU Seller (Germany, 19% VAT)
        |
        +-----> EU B2C buyer (France): Seller charges 20% French VAT (OSS)
        |
        +-----> EU B2B buyer (France, valid VAT ID): Seller charges 0% (reverse charge)
                Buyer accounts for French VAT themselves
```

### 9.2 VAT ID Validation in Magento

```
Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration
  > Create New Account Options
    > Enable Automatic Assignment to Customer Group: Yes
    > Default Group: General
    > Group for Valid VAT ID - Domestic: [Domestic Customers]
    > Group for Valid VAT ID - Intra-Union: [EU VAT Exempt]  <-- key setting
    > Group for Invalid VAT ID: [General]
    > Validation Error Group: [General]  <-- separate group for VIES service errors
    > Validate on Each Transaction: Yes / No
```

> **Note:** There is a separate "Validation Error Group" field (viv_error_group) that handles the case when the VIES service is down or returns an error — this is distinct from "Group for Invalid VAT ID" which handles VAT numbers that are confirmed invalid.

```
Stores > Configuration > General > General > Store Information
  > VAT Number: [Your company's VAT ID]  <- required for VIES validation
```

### 9.3 VIES Validation Flow

```
Customer enters VAT ID on account/checkout
         |
         v
Magento calls EU VIES web service (ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies)
         |
         +--[Valid, same country as store]----> Group: "Domestic VAT"
         |
         +--[Valid, different EU country]-----> Group: "EU VAT Exempt" (0% tax)
         |
         +--[Invalid]--------------------------> Group: "Invalid VAT ID" group
         |
         +--[VIES service unavailable/error]---> Group: "Validation Error Group"
```

> **Exam focus:** VAT ID validation uses the **VIES (VAT Information Exchange System)** service from the EU Commission. If the VIES service is **down or unavailable**, Magento assigns the customer to the separate "Validation Error Group" (not the "Invalid VAT ID" group). The validation is triggered on **account creation** and/or **each transaction** depending on configuration.

### 9.4 VAT ID Validation Configuration Checklist

```
1. Store VAT number set in: Stores > Config > General > General > Store Information
2. VIES validation enabled in: Customer Configuration > Create New Account Options
3. Customer groups created:
   - "EU VAT B2B Exempt" with Tax Class = [no taxable rule]
   - "EU B2C" with Tax Class = "Retail Customer"
4. Tax rules:
   - Rule for Retail Customer + Taxable Goods = respective country VAT rate
   - NO rule for the exempt group = 0% tax
```

### 9.5 Zero-Rated vs Exempt

| Term | Meaning | VAT Return Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Zero-rated** | Taxable supply at 0% rate | Must still be reported on VAT return |
| **Exempt** | Outside scope of VAT | Not reported as a taxable supply |
| **Reverse charge** | B2B cross-border; buyer accounts for tax | Seller reports as zero-rated cross-border |

> **Exam focus:** In Magento, both zero-rated and exempt are implemented the same way (no applicable rate), but they have different **legal/accounting meanings** in EU VAT. The exam may test your understanding that the *mechanism* is the same even though the *compliance* terminology differs.

## 10. Cross-Border Duties (DDP vs DDU/DAP)

### 10.1 Terminology

| Term | Full Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **DDP** | Delivered Duty Paid | Seller pays all import duties/customs; buyer sees final all-in price |
| **DDU** | Delivered Duty Unpaid | Buyer pays duties upon delivery (also called DAP) |
| **DAP** | Delivered At Place | Modern Incoterms equivalent of DDU |
| **Customs duty** | Import duty | Percentage or flat fee on declared goods value |
| **De minimis** | Minimum threshold | Value below which no duty is charged (varies by country) |

### 10.2 Native Magento Limitations

> **Exam focus:** Adobe Commerce does **NOT** natively calculate import duties or customs fees. This is a critical exam point — duties require **third-party integration**.

```
Native Magento:
  + Calculates sales tax (VAT, GST, state tax)
  - Does NOT calculate customs/import duties
  - Does NOT provide HS codes (Harmonized System tariff codes)
  - Does NOT do landed cost calculation
```

### 10.3 DDP Implementation Options

To offer **DDP** (all-inclusive checkout with duties):

| Solution | Approach |
|---|---|
| **Avalara AvaTax** | Real-time duty + tax calculation via API |
| **TaxJar** | US-focused, limited international duty support |
| **Zonos** | Specialized cross-border duty + landed cost |
| **Global-e** | Full cross-border commerce platform |
| **Customs duties field (manual)** | Hardcoded flat surcharge per country (not recommended) |

### 10.4 DDU/DAP Checkout Experience

If operating DDU:
- Inform customers at checkout that **additional fees may apply upon delivery**
- Common implementation: display a disclaimer in the checkout comments or via a custom CMS block
- No automatic calculation in native Magento

> **Exam focus:** On the certification exam, questions about duties will test whether you know that **import duties ≠ sales tax** and require third-party tooling. If asked "how do you add import duties to checkout?" the answer is **third-party extension/integration**, not native configuration.

## 11. Tax Calculation on Discounts (Tricky Math)

This is one of the most frequently tested "gotcha" areas.

### 11.1 The Two Settings That Matter

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Calculation Settings
  > Apply Customer Tax: Before Discount / After Discount
  > Apply Discount On Prices: Excluding Tax / Including Tax
```

### 11.2 Scenario: $100 product, 10% tax, 20% discount

#### Case A: Apply Customer Tax = BEFORE Discount

```
Product price:          $100.00 (excl. tax)
Tax (10%):               $10.00
Price incl. tax:        $110.00
Discount (20% on $110): -$22.00   <- discount applied to tax-inclusive amount
                        --------
Cart total:              $88.00
Tax included in $88:      $8.00   (back-calculated: $88 / 1.10 = $80 net)
```

#### Case B: Apply Customer Tax = AFTER Discount

```
Product price:          $100.00 (excl. tax)
Discount (20% on $100): -$20.00   <- discount applied to pre-tax amount
Discounted price:        $80.00
Tax (10% on $80):         $8.00
                        --------
Cart total:              $88.00
Tax:                      $8.00
```

> In this case, the **cart total is the same** ($88) but the **tax amount** and **discount amount** differ in their display.

#### Case C: Apply Customer Tax = BEFORE Discount + Apply Discount On Prices = Excluding Tax

```
Product price:          $100.00 (excl. tax)
Discount (20% on $100): -$20.00   <- discount on pre-tax
Discounted price:        $80.00
Tax (10% on $100):       $10.00   <- tax still calculated on ORIGINAL price
                        --------
Cart total:              $90.00   <- different total!
Tax:                     $10.00
```

> **Exam focus:** **Case C** is the "trap" case — the customer gets a 20% discount but pays tax on the original full price. This configuration exists for tax compliance in some jurisdictions where discounts don't reduce the taxable base. The final total is **$90**, not $88 as in Cases A and B.

### 11.3 Summary Table

| Apply Tax | Apply Discount On | Tax Base | Discount Base | Cart Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| After Discount | Excl. Tax | $80 | $100 (pre-tax) | $88 |
| Before Discount | Incl. Tax | $110 (then back-calc) | $110 (incl. tax) | $88 |
| Before Discount | Excl. Tax | $100 (full price) | $100 (pre-tax) | $90 |

> **Exam focus:** The combination of **"Before Discount" + "Excluding Tax"** means the customer pays tax on the **original undiscounted price** — not the discounted price. This is the most mathematically surprising combination and most likely to appear in exam scenario questions.

## 12. Tax Display Rounding & 1-Cent Discrepancies

### 12.1 Why Rounding Discrepancies Occur

```
Tax Calculation Method Based On: Unit Price (per unit)
  vs
Tax Calculation Method Based On: Row Total (all units)
  vs
Tax Calculation Method Based On: Total (order total)
```

#### Example: 3 items at $9.99, 10% tax

```
METHOD: Unit Price
  Per unit tax: $9.99 * 0.10 = $0.999 -> rounds to $1.00
  3 units: $1.00 * 3 = $3.00 displayed
  But actual: $29.97 * 0.10 = $2.997 -> "true" total tax = $3.00
  -> No discrepancy here by coincidence

Different example: 3 items at $9.98, 10% tax
  Per unit tax: $9.98 * 0.10 = $0.998 -> rounds to $1.00
  Displayed: $1.00 * 3 = $3.00
  Actual row: $29.94 * 0.10 = $2.994 -> rounds to $2.99
  DISCREPANCY: displayed $3.00 vs calculated $2.99
               -> Order total shows $2.99 but line items sum to $3.00
```

### 12.2 The 3 Calculation Methods Compared

| Method | Rounding Level | Typical Discrepancy Risk |
|---|---|---|
| **Unit Price** | Each unit rounded individually | High with multiple qty |
| **Row Total** | Each line item total rounded | Medium |
| **Total** | Entire order total rounded once | Lowest |

> **Exam focus:** **Unit Price** method causes the most 1-cent discrepancies on invoices because each unit is rounded *before* summing. The exam will test that you know **row-level rounding** vs **total-level rounding** produce different displayed amounts.

### 12.3 Rounding Configuration

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Calculation Settings
  > Tax Calculation Method Based On: [Unit Price | Row Total | Total]
```

> **Note:** The default Tax Calculation Method is **Total** (TOTAL_BASE_CALCULATION), not Unit Price. This is the safest default as it produces the fewest rounding discrepancies.

> **Exam focus:** Magento stores the **exact unrounded tax** in the database but **displays** rounded values. The "1-cent discrepancy" seen on invoices is a **display artifact**, not a calculation error. The order total is mathematically correct — the line items are individually rounded for display.

### 13.1 Why Third-Party Is Required

| Scenario | Native Magento | Third-Party Needed |

| US state sales tax (basic) | Yes (manual rates) | Optional (automation) |

- **AutoFile** feature for automated state tax return filing
- Less comprehensive for international duties vs Avalara
- Available as Adobe Commerce Marketplace extension

> **Exam focus:** The exam will NOT ask you to configure Avalara, but you **must know** that import duties/customs are **NOT calculated natively** and require a third-party solution. This is a common distractor question.

Test 2: Display Prices = Including Tax

Test 3: Display Prices = Including and Excluding Tax

1. Create Customer Group: "B2B Exempt"

2. Strategy A (Recommended):

3. Strategy B:

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Tax Architecture
- [ ] Tax system = **Tax Class** + **Tax Rate** + **Tax Rule** (all three required)
- [ ] Missing any component = no tax calculated
- [ ] **Product tax classes**: "Taxable Goods" (default); "None" generated dynamically by source model
- [ ] **Customer tax classes**: "Retail Customer" (default only — "Wholesale" must be created manually)
- [ ] Tax exemption = assign customer group with **no matching tax rule**
- [ ] Tax classes are created/managed **inline in the Tax Rules form** — no separate menu pages

### Tax Rates
- [ ] Tax Rate fields: Identifier, Country, State, ZIP, Percentage
- [ ] ZIP supports wildcards (`*`) and ranges
- [ ] Most specific ZIP match wins when multiple rates match
- [ ] Rates can be bulk imported/exported via CSV
- [ ] Multiple rates in one rule = summed together

### Tax Rules
- [ ] Tax Rule binds: Customer Class + Product Class + Rate(s)
- [ ] **Priority**: lower number applied first; same priority = added together
- [ ] **"Calculate Off Subtotal Only"** (compound) = taxes the running total including prior tax

### Tax Display Settings
- [ ] Display settings are **presentation only** — they do NOT change tax amount
- [ ] Display settings available at default, website, and **store view** levels
- [ ] **Calculation Settings** only available at default + **website** levels (NOT store view)
- [ ] **Catalog Prices = Including Tax** is EU standard; US uses Excluding Tax
- [ ] Default Tax Destination = controls catalog display before address is known
- [ ] Three display modes: Excluding / Including / Including and Excluding

### Origin vs Destination Tax
- [ ] **Destination-based** = most common, uses **Shipping Address** (label in admin)
- [ ] **Origin-based** = uses store's **Shipping Origin** address
- [ ] Configured at: Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Calculation Settings

### Fixed Product Tax (FPT)
- [ ] FPT = flat fee per unit (not percentage) — WEEE, eco-tax
- [ ] FPT is **per country/region** on the product
- [ ] **Apply Tax To FPT** — controls whether sales tax applies to FPT amount (Yes/No)
- [ ] 4 display options: Including FPT only / Including FPT and description / Excluding FPT with description and final price / Excluding FPT
- [ ] FPT scope: default + website only (not per store view)

### B2B Tax Exemption
- [ ] Managed via **Company > Customer Group** assignment
- [ ] All company members inherit the group's tax class
- [ ] Tax exemption = no tax rule exists for the customer's tax class

### VAT ID Validation
- [ ] Uses **VIES** (EU Commission web service) for validation
- [ ] Valid EU VAT ID + intra-Union = auto-assign to exempt group (0% VAT)
- [ ] VIES service down = customer assigned to **"Validation Error Group"** (separate from "Invalid VAT ID" group)
- [ ] Requires store's own VAT number configured in Store Information
- [ ] **Reverse charge**: EU B2B cross-border = seller charges 0%, buyer self-accounts

### Cross-Border Duties
- [ ] **DDP** = seller pays all duties (all-in price for buyer)
- [ ] **DDU/DAP** = buyer pays duties on delivery
- [ ] **Import duties are NOT native** in Magento — require third-party (Avalara, TaxJar, Zonos)
- [ ] Native Magento calculates **sales tax/VAT only**

### Tax on Discounts (Tricky)
- [ ] **"After Discount"** = tax base is discounted price (most common)
- [ ] **"Before Discount"** = discount applied to tax-inclusive amount
- [ ] **"Before Discount" + "Excl. Tax"** = customer pays tax on *original* undiscounted price (highest total)
- [ ] This combination is the most exam-tested "trap" scenario

### Tax Rounding
- [ ] **Unit Price** method: rounds per unit → highest discrepancy risk with qty > 1
- [ ] **Row Total** method: rounds per line → medium risk
- [ ] **Total** method: rounds once on order total → lowest discrepancy (and the **default**)
- [ ] Magento stores exact values in DB; discrepancies are **display-only**
- [ ] 1-cent discrepancy = line items sum ≠ order total (display artifact)

### Third-Party Integrations
- [ ] **Avalara AvaTax**: real-time US + international tax + duties (Marketplace extension, not core)
- [ ] **TaxJar**: US sales tax + AutoFile; limited duty support
- [ ] Import duties **always** require third-party — no exceptions in native Magento
- [ ] Avalara/TaxJar replace Magento's native tax calculation engine

### CLI / Cache
- [ ] `bin/magento cache:clean config full_page` after any tax config change
- [ ] `bin/magento indexer:reindex catalog_product_price` after catalog price mode change
- [ ] Config path: `tax/calculation/algorithm` = UNIT_BASE_CALCULATION | ROW_BASE_CALCULATION | TOTAL_BASE_CALCULATION
- [ ] Config path: `tax/display/type` = 1 (excl) | 2 (incl) | 3 (both)
- [ ] Config path: `tax/calculation/based_on` = shipping | billing | origin

flashcards.question: What three foundational components are needed for a functioning tax system in Adobe Commerce?
flashcards.answer: Tax Classes (categories of buyers and products), Tax Rates (percentage for specific jurisdictions), and Tax Rules (the binding logic connecting classes to rates). Missing any one of these three components means no tax is calculated.
flashcards.hint: Who is buying, how much tax applies, and what connects the two.

flashcards.question: How is tax exemption achieved for B2B customers in Adobe Commerce?
flashcards.answer: Tax exemption is managed at the Company > Customer Group level. You assign the company to a customer group with a tax class that has no matching tax rule. All members of the company inherit the group's tax class. There is no single 'exempt' checkbox on a customer record in native Magento.
flashcards.hint: The absence of a matching rule is what creates the exemption.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between origin-based and destination-based tax calculation?
flashcards.answer: Origin-based tax uses the seller's location (Shipping Origin) for jurisdiction determination. Destination-based tax uses the buyer's shipping address. Most US states and EU VAT use destination-based. The setting is configured at Stores > Configuration > Sales > Tax > Calculation Settings.
flashcards.hint: One uses where the goods ship FROM; the other uses where they ship TO.

flashcards.question: What is Fixed Product Tax (FPT) and how does it differ from regular sales tax?
flashcards.answer: FPT (also called eco-tax or WEEE) is a flat fee per unit added to specific products, NOT a percentage. Common use cases include electronics recycling fees and tire recycling fees. Whether sales tax applies to the FPT amount itself is controlled by the 'Apply Tax To FPT' toggle.
flashcards.hint: A flat dollar amount per item versus a percentage of the price.

flashcards.question: What is the EU reverse charge mechanism and how does Magento handle it?
flashcards.answer: In EU B2B cross-border transactions, if the buyer has a valid VAT ID in their member state, the seller charges 0% VAT and the buyer self-accounts. Magento validates VAT IDs via the VIES (EU Commission) web service and can auto-assign customers to a tax-exempt group when a valid intra-Union VAT ID is confirmed.
flashcards.hint: Valid business identification number in a different EU country triggers zero-rate treatment.

flashcards.question: What happens if the VIES VAT validation service is unavailable when a customer submits a VAT ID?
flashcards.answer: The customer is assigned to the 'Validation Error Group' — this is a separate group from the 'Group for Invalid VAT ID'. The Invalid VAT ID group handles confirmed-invalid numbers, while the Validation Error Group handles cases where the VIES service is down or returns an error.
flashcards.hint: Service errors and confirmed-invalid numbers are handled differently with separate groups.

flashcards.question: Does Adobe Commerce natively calculate import duties and customs fees?
flashcards.answer: No. Adobe Commerce does NOT natively calculate import duties, customs fees, HS codes, or landed costs. It only calculates sales tax (VAT, GST, state tax). Import duties always require a third-party integration such as Avalara AvaTax, TaxJar, or Zonos.
flashcards.hint: Native tax engine handles sales tax only — border fees require external tools.

flashcards.question: What is the tricky tax result when 'Apply Customer Tax = Before Discount' AND 'Apply Discount On Prices = Excluding Tax'?
flashcards.answer: The customer pays tax on the ORIGINAL undiscounted price. For a $100 product with 10% tax and 20% discount: discount is 20% of $100 = $20, but tax is 10% of $100 (full price) = $10. Cart total = $90, not $88. This is the most exam-tested 'trap' scenario.
flashcards.hint: Tax base ignores the discount; the discount ignores the tax.

flashcards.question: What are the three tax calculation methods and which causes the most rounding discrepancies?
flashcards.answer: Unit Price (rounds per individual unit), Row Total (rounds per line item), and Total (rounds once on the entire order total). Unit Price causes the most 1-cent discrepancies because each unit is rounded before summing. Total is the default and safest method with the fewest discrepancies.
flashcards.hint: More rounding operations means more chance for pennies to accumulate differently.

flashcards.question: What is the purpose of the Default Tax Destination settings in Magento?
flashcards.answer: Default Tax Destination settings (Default Country, Default State, Default Post Code) determine what tax is shown on catalog and product pages BEFORE a customer logs in or enters their address. They provide estimated display tax, not the actual tax — actual tax is calculated at checkout with the real address.
flashcards.hint: These are for pre-checkout price display, not for final tax calculation.

flashcards.question: At what scope levels can tax display settings be configured versus tax calculation settings?
flashcards.answer: Tax display settings (Shopping Cart Display, Orders/Invoices Display) are available at default, website, AND store view levels. However, Tax Calculation Settings are only available at default and website levels — NOT per store view. Setting calculation options at store view scope has no effect.
flashcards.hint: Presentation can vary per store view; the math is locked at the website level.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between DDP and DDU/DAP for cross-border commerce?
flashcards.answer: DDP (Delivered Duty Paid) means the seller pays all import duties and customs — the buyer sees a final all-in price. DDU/DAP (Delivered Duty Unpaid / Delivered At Place) means the buyer pays duties upon delivery. Native Magento cannot calculate either; DDP requires third-party duty calculation.
flashcards.hint: One puts the duty burden on the seller; the other on the buyer.

flashcards.question: Where are new product and customer tax classes created in the Adobe Commerce admin?
flashcards.answer: Tax classes are created INLINE within the Tax Rules form (Stores > Taxes > Tax Rules). There is no separate 'Product Tax Classes' or 'Customer Tax Classes' menu page. The Tax Rules form provides an AJAX-based interface to add new tax classes on the fly.
flashcards.hint: Look inside the rule creation form, not in the main menu.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between 'Catalog Prices = Including Tax' and 'Catalog Prices = Excluding Tax'?
flashcards.answer: With Including Tax (EU standard), the price entered in admin already includes tax — Magento back-calculates the net price. With Excluding Tax (US standard), the price entered is the net price and Magento adds tax on top. Changing this on a live store requires repricing all products.
flashcards.hint: EU merchants build tax into the sticker price; US merchants add it on top.

flashcards.question: How does the Tax Rule priority system work when multiple tax rules apply?
flashcards.answer: Priority is an integer where lower numbers are applied first. Same-priority rules are ADDED together (summed). The 'Calculate Off Subtotal Only' (compound tax) option controls whether each priority layer taxes the running total including prior tax — used in scenarios like Quebec QST+GST.
flashcards.hint: Same priority = sum; different priority = sequential application with optional compounding.

studyNotes.title: Day 20 — Tailored Pricing & Sensei Recommendations Deep Dive
studyNotes.content:
# Tailored Pricing & Sensei AI Recommendations — Deep Dive Study Notes

## Table of Contents
1. [B2B Tailored Pricing Overview](#1-b2b-tailored-pricing-overview)
2. [Shared Catalog & Tier Prices](#2-shared-catalog--tier-prices)
3. [Negotiable Quotes & Negotiated Prices](#3-negotiable-quotes--negotiated-prices)
4. [Customer Group Prices](#4-customer-group-prices)
5. [B2B Price Precedence Rules](#5-b2b-price-precedence-rules)
6. [Sensei AI Product Recommendations Overview](#6-sensei-ai-product-recommendations-overview)
7. [Training Data Requirements & Cold Start Problem](#7-training-data-requirements--cold-start-problem)
8. [Recommendation Unit Rendering](#8-recommendation-unit-rendering)
9. [Supported Recommendation Types In Detail](#9-supported-recommendation-types-in-detail)
10. [A/B Testing Recommendations](#10-ab-testing-recommendations)
11. [Performance Metrics for Recommendations](#11-performance-metrics-for-recommendations)
12. [Catalog Sync to Adobe SaaS](#12-catalog-sync-to-adobe-saas)
13. [Recommendations Dashboard — Admin Hands-On](#13-recommendations-dashboard--admin-hands-on)
14. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. B2B Tailored Pricing Overview

Adobe Commerce B2B introduces a layered pricing architecture that allows merchants to offer **highly customized pricing** to business buyers. Unlike standard B2C price rules, B2B pricing operates across three distinct mechanisms that stack and interact with one another:

| Mechanism | Scope | Where Configured |
|---|---|---|
| Shared Catalog Tier Prices | Per-company / per-group | Catalog > Shared Catalogs |
| Negotiable Quote Prices | Per-quote / per-buyer | Sales > Quotes |
| Customer Group Prices | Per customer group | Product Edit Page > Advanced Pricing |

- **Exam focus:** Know that B2B pricing is **additive in configuration** but **exclusive in application** — only one price wins at checkout, determined by precedence rules.
- **Exam focus:** B2B pricing features require the **B2B module to be enabled** and the company account feature to be active.

---

## 2. Shared Catalog & Tier Prices

### 2.1 What Is a Shared Catalog?

A **Shared Catalog** is a B2B feature that allows merchants to create custom product assortments and pricing for specific companies or groups of companies. It essentially wraps a custom price list around a subset of the product catalog.

```
+---------------------+
|   Master Catalog    |
|   (all products)    |
+---------------------+
         |
    +----+----+
    |         |
+--------+ +--------+
|Shared  | |Shared  |
|Cat A   | |Cat B   |
|(Co. X) | |(Co. Y) |
+--------+ +--------+
```

- There are two types of Shared Catalogs:
  - **Public** (TYPE_PUBLIC=1) — replaces the default catalog for guests and non-company customers. Only one Public catalog is allowed.
  - **Custom** (TYPE_CUSTOM=0) — assigned to specific companies

### 2.2 Tier Prices Within Shared Catalogs

Tier prices in a Shared Catalog are **quantity-based price breaks** defined per product, per catalog. They allow "buy more, pay less" pricing scoped to a specific company or group.

**Example configuration in Admin:**

```
Catalog > Shared Catalogs > [Select Catalog] > Configure > Set Pricing & Structure
Product: Widget A
  Qty 1+   → $50.00  (base price for this catalog)
  Qty 10+  → $45.00  (tier 1)
  Qty 50+  → $40.00  (tier 2)
  Qty 100+ → $35.00  (tier 3)
```

- **Exam focus:** Shared Catalog tier prices are **not the same as standard catalog tier prices** — they live inside the Shared Catalog configuration and **override** standard tier prices for the assigned company.
- **Exam focus:** When a product is added to a Shared Catalog, you can set a **custom price** using one of two types: a **fixed price** (PRICE_TYPE_FIXED) or a **percentage discount** (PRICE_TYPE_DISCOUNT) off the original price. Both types are stored in the same `catalog_product_entity_tier_price` table.

### 2.3 Shared Catalog & Customer Groups

Under the hood, every Shared Catalog is **backed by a Customer Group**. When you create a Shared Catalog, Adobe Commerce automatically creates a corresponding Customer Group.

```bash
# Shared Catalog → Customer Group mapping can be verified in the DB:
SELECT sc.name, sc.customer_group_id, cg.customer_group_code
FROM shared_catalog sc
JOIN customer_group cg ON sc.customer_group_id = cg.customer_group_id;
```

> **Note:** There is no `bin/magento customer:group:list` CLI command in Magento EE 2.4.8-p3. To list customer groups, query the database directly or use the admin at Customers > Customer Groups.

- **Exam focus:** Deleting a **Custom** Shared Catalog **also deletes its associated customer group**. However, deleting the **Public** Shared Catalog does NOT delete its customer group (an exception is thrown to prevent this).
- **Exam focus:** A company can be assigned to **only one Shared Catalog** at a time — enforced because each company has a single `customer_group_id`, and each Shared Catalog maps to one customer group.

---

## 3. Negotiable Quotes & Negotiated Prices

### 3.1 Negotiable Quote Workflow

Negotiable Quotes allow B2B buyers to **request a price negotiation** directly from their cart. This creates a structured back-and-forth negotiation process.

```
Buyer                          Seller (Admin)
  |                                |
  |--- Submit Quote Request ------>|
  |                                |--- Review & Counter-Offer ----|
  |<-- Receive Negotiated Quote ---|                               |
  |--- Accept / Counter / Decline  |<------------------------------|
  |                                |
  |--- Convert to Order ---------->|
```

### 3.2 How Negotiated Prices Work

| Action | Who | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Request quote | Buyer | Locks current cart items/quantities |
| Add discount | Seller | Can apply % discount, fixed discount, or propose new total per item |
| Add shipping | Seller | Can negotiate shipping cost |
| Add expiry | Seller | Quote expires on set date |
| Approve quote | Seller | Buyer can now checkout at negotiated price |

The three discount types are defined in `NegotiableQuoteInterface.php`:
- **NEGOTIATED_PRICE_TYPE_PERCENTAGE_DISCOUNT** (1) — percentage off the item price
- **NEGOTIATED_PRICE_TYPE_AMOUNT_DISCOUNT** (2) — fixed amount off the item price
- **NEGOTIATED_PRICE_TYPE_PROPOSED_TOTAL** (3) — proposed total price for the item

Each line item in a negotiable quote (`negotiable_quote_item` table) stores its own `negotiated_price_type` and `negotiated_price_value`, enabling per-item custom pricing.

- **Exam focus:** Negotiated prices are **stored per quote**, not per product or customer group — they only apply to that specific approved quote.
- **Exam focus:** A negotiated price in an **approved Negotiable Quote takes the highest precedence** of all B2B pricing mechanisms.
- **Exam focus:** Negotiable Quotes require the **`Magento_NegotiableQuote`** module and must be enabled per company in the company configuration ("Allow Quotes" toggle).

### 3.3 Discount Types Available in Negotiable Quotes

- **Percentage discount** off the quoted subtotal
- **Fixed amount discount** off the quoted subtotal
- **Proposed total** (seller proposes a specific total for the line item)
- Shipping price can also be negotiated separately

---

## 4. Customer Group Prices

Customer Group Prices are the **standard Magento price differentiation mechanism**, predating B2B. In a B2B context, they serve as the fallback when Shared Catalog pricing is not in play.

### 4.1 Configuration

```
Product Edit > Advanced Pricing > Customer Group Price
+---------------+----------+-------+----------+
| Website       | Group    | Qty   | Price    |
+---------------+----------+-------+----------+
| All Websites  | Wholesale| 1     | $42.00   |
| All Websites  | Retailer | 1     | $46.00   |
+---------------+----------+-------+----------+
```

- These prices are stored in the `catalog_product_entity_tier_price` table (yes, even non-tiered group prices use this table with `qty = 1`).

```sql
-- Customer group prices in the DB
SELECT * FROM catalog_product_entity_tier_price
WHERE customer_group_id != 0  -- 0 = ALL GROUPS (standard tier)
AND qty = 1.0000;             -- qty=1 = flat group price, not a volume tier
```

- **Exam focus:** Customer group prices and tier prices **share the same database table** (`catalog_product_entity_tier_price`). The difference is `qty` and `customer_group_id` values. Key columns: entity_id, all_groups, customer_group_id, qty, value, website_id, percentage_value.
- **Exam focus:** Customer Group Prices are **superseded by Shared Catalog pricing** for any company assigned to a Shared Catalog.

---

## 5. B2B Price Precedence Rules

This is the **most critical section for the exam**. When multiple pricing mechanisms could apply, Adobe Commerce follows a strict waterfall:

### 5.1 The Precedence Waterfall

```
HIGHEST PRIORITY
      |
      v
+-----------------------------------+
| 1. Negotiated Quote Price         |  <- Approved negotiable quote checkout
+-----------------------------------+
      |
      v
+-----------------------------------+
| 2. Shared Catalog Tier Price      |  <- Qty-based price in shared catalog
+-----------------------------------+
      |
      v
+-----------------------------------+
| 3. Standard Catalog Tier Price    |  <- Regular product tier pricing
+-----------------------------------+
      |
      v
+-----------------------------------+
| 4. Special Price                  |  <- Time-limited special price
+-----------------------------------+
      |
      v
+-----------------------------------+
| 5. Regular (Base) Price           |  <- Standard product price
+-----------------------------------+
      |
     LOWEST PRIORITY
```

> **Simplified exam mnemonic (without Negotiable Quote):**
> **"Shared Tier → Standard Tier → Special → Regular"**

### 5.2 Detailed Precedence Breakdown

| Priority | Price Type | Condition for Application |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Negotiated Quote Price | Active approved negotiable quote being checked out |
| 2 | Shared Catalog Tier Price | Buyer's company assigned to a Shared Catalog + qty threshold met |
| 3 | Standard Tier Price | Qty threshold met, no Shared Catalog override |
| 4 | Special Price | Time-based, not superseded by higher mechanism |
| 5 | Regular/Base Price | Default fallback |

- **Exam focus:** **Catalog Price Rules (Cart Price Rules)** operate **separately** from this B2B precedence chain — they apply as discounts on top of the winning price, but this interaction can be complex.
- **Exam focus:** The order given in official Adobe documentation for B2B (without Negotiable Quote) is: **SharedCatalog tier price → standard tier price → special price → regular price**.
- **Exam focus:** A **Special Price does NOT override a Shared Catalog tier price** — the shared catalog tier price wins.
- **Exam focus:** If a buyer's company has a Shared Catalog but their **purchase quantity doesn't meet any tier threshold**, the **base Shared Catalog price** (not standard tier) is used.

### 5.3 Why This Matters — A Worked Example

```
Product: Widget A
  Regular Price:              $100.00
  Special Price:              $85.00 (active)
  Standard Tier (10+):        $80.00
  Shared Catalog price:       $75.00 (base for Company X)
  Shared Catalog Tier (10+):  $65.00

Scenario A — Company X buyer orders qty 5:
  Result: $75.00 (Shared Catalog base price wins over special $85)

Scenario B — Company X buyer orders qty 15:
  Result: $65.00 (Shared Catalog Tier price for 10+)

Scenario C — Guest orders qty 15:
  Result: $80.00 (Standard Tier for 10+, no shared catalog)

Scenario D — Guest orders qty 3:
  Result: $85.00 (Special Price, no tier threshold met)
```

---

## 6. Sensei AI Product Recommendations Overview

> **Important codebase note:** Product Recommendations (`magento/product-recommendations`) is a **separate SaaS package** that is NOT included in the base Adobe Commerce EE 2.4.8-p3 distribution. It must be installed separately via Composer. Admin paths, GraphQL endpoints, and recommendation types described in this section are from the SaaS package documentation and cannot be verified against the base codebase.

Adobe Sensei is Adobe's AI and machine learning framework. **Product Recommendations** is a SaaS service powered by Sensei that delivers intelligent product suggestions on the storefront.

### 6.1 Architecture

```
+-------------------+     Catalog Sync      +----------------------+
|  Adobe Commerce   |---------------------->|  Adobe SaaS Data     |
|  (On-Premise/    |                        |  Space (cloud)       |
|   Cloud)          |<----------------------|  - Catalog index     |
|                   |   Recommendations     |  - Behavioral data   |
|  Storefront       |   API response        |  - ML models         |
+-------------------+                       +----------------------+
        |                                           ^
        | Shopper events                            |
        +-------------------------------------------+
          (page views, clicks, purchases, etc.)
```

### 6.2 Key Components

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `magento/product-recommendations` | Main composer package (separate SaaS add-on, not in base EE) |
| Data Connection module | Sends behavioral events to Adobe SaaS (separate package) |
| Catalog Sync | Syncs product data to SaaS Data Space (base EE has module-saas-common and data exporter modules) |
| Recommendation Units | Frontend widgets/blocks displaying results |
| Adobe Sensei ML models | Trained on your behavioral and catalog data |

```bash
# Install Product Recommendations (separate Composer package)
composer require magento/product-recommendations

# Verify sync status (saas:resync is in base EE via module-saas-common)
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=products
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=categories

# Check sync status
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=products --dry-run
```

- **Exam focus:** Product Recommendations is a **SaaS service** — it runs in Adobe's cloud, not on your Magento instance. Your instance sends data TO it and receives recommendations FROM it.
- **Exam focus:** Requires a valid **API key / SaaS Data Space** configured in `Stores > Configuration > Services > Commerce Services Connector` (section=services_connector, tab=service, group=services_connector_integration).

---

## 7. Training Data Requirements & Cold Start Problem

### 7.1 Minimum Data Requirements

Different recommendation types have different data requirements:

| Recommendation Type | Minimum Data Required | Training Needed? |
|---|---|---|
| Recently Viewed | Session data (client-side) | **No** |
| More Like This | Catalog attributes | Minimal (attribute-based) |
| Most Viewed | Page view events | Yes — impressions |
| Most Purchased | Order history | Yes — purchase events |
| Bought Together | Order history (co-purchase) | Yes — substantial order data |
| Trending | Recent activity spike data | Yes — recency-weighted events |
| Recommended for You | Full behavioral profile | Yes — heavy personalization |

- **Exam focus:** **"Recently Viewed"** is the only recommendation type that requires **no training data** — it works from the browser session immediately.
- **Exam focus:** **"Bought Together"** (Also Bought) requires **sufficient order history** — specifically, orders where multiple products were purchased together. Sparse order data produces poor results.

### 7.2 The Cold Start Problem

The **cold start problem** refers to the inability to make accurate recommendations when there is insufficient historical data.

```
New Store Launch
      |
      v
  Day 0: No impressions, no events, no order data
      |
      |--- "Most Viewed" recommendations: EMPTY / FALLBACK
      |--- "Bought Together" recommendations: EMPTY / FALLBACK
      |--- "Trending" recommendations: EMPTY / FALLBACK
      |--- "Recently Viewed": WORKS (session-based)
      |--- "More Like This": WORKS (attribute-based)
      v
  Weeks 1-4: Data accumulates...
      |
      v
  Sufficient data: ML models train, recommendations populate
```

**How the cold start problem manifests:**
- New stores see **empty recommendation units** for behavior-dependent types
- New products added to an existing store **don't appear in recommendations immediately** — they must go through catalog sync first AND then accumulate impressions
- The Recommendations dashboard will show units as "inactive" until training data thresholds are met

**Mitigation strategies:**
1. Use **"Recently Viewed"** and **"More Like This"** on new stores — they work immediately
2. Adobe provides **fallback behavior** — if a recommendation type has insufficient data, it may fall back to showing popular or random products
3. Run marketing campaigns to accelerate impression accumulation

- **Exam focus:** The cold start problem applies to **new catalogs** and **new products** — existing products that accumulate impressions don't face this for behavior-based types.
- **Exam focus:** **New products are NOT immediately available for recommendations** even after being added — they must complete **catalog sync to Adobe SaaS** first, which can take time.

---

## 8. Recommendation Unit Rendering

A **Recommendation Unit** is the container that displays recommended products on the storefront. There are two rendering methods:

### 8.1 Widget-Based Rendering (Default)

The widget approach uses Page Builder or layout XML to place recommendation blocks on specific page types.

```xml
<!-- layout XML placement example -->
<!-- view/frontend/layout/catalog_product_view.xml -->
<page>
    <body>
        <referenceContainer name="content.bottom">
            <block class="Magento\ProductRecommendationsLayout\Block\Renderer"
                   name="product.recommendations"
                   template="Magento_ProductRecommendationsLayout::renderer.phtml">
                <arguments>
                    <argument name="recommendation_id" xsi:type="string">
                        unit-id-from-admin
                    </argument>
                </arguments>
            </block>
        </referenceContainer>
    </body>
</page>
```

> **Note:** The block class `Magento\ProductRecommendationsLayout\Block\Renderer` is from the separate `magento/product-recommendations` package, not in the base EE codebase.

**Widget placement via Admin (requires Product Recommendations package):**
```
Marketing > Product Recommendations > Create Recommendation
  - Name: "You May Also Like"
  - Storefront Page Type: Product Detail Page
  - Recommendation Type: More Like This
  - Number of Products: 6
  - Placement: Below Product Description
```

> **Note:** The "Marketing > Product Recommendations" menu item does NOT exist in base EE — it is added by the `magento/product-recommendations` package.

### 8.2 API-Based Rendering (Headless)

For headless storefronts (PWA Studio, custom React/Vue frontends), recommendations are fetched via the **GraphQL API**.

```graphql
# Fetch recommendation units for a page type
query getRecommendations($currentSku: String, $pageType: PageType!) {
  recommendations(
    currentSku: $currentSku
    pageType: $pageType
    userPurchaseHistory: []
    userViewHistory: []
  ) {
    results {
      unitId
      unitName
      typeId
      products {
        name
        sku
        smallImage {
          url
        }
        priceRange {
          minimumPrice {
            finalPrice {
              value
              currency
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```javascript
// Sending behavioral events for headless (required for ML training)
// Uses @adobe/magento-storefront-events-sdk (separate npm package)
import { sendEvent } from '@adobe/magento-storefront-events-sdk';

// Track product view
sendEvent('productPageView', {
  productContext: {
    productId: 123,
    sku: 'WJ01',
    name: 'Stellar Solar Jacket',
    categories: ['Women', 'Tops'],
    pricing: { regularPrice: 75.00 }
  }
});

// Track recommendation click (critical for CTR measurement)
sendEvent('recommendationClick', {
  unitId: 'unit-abc-123',
  productId: 456,
  rank: 2
});
```

- **Exam focus:** Both rendering methods must still send **behavioral events** back to Adobe SaaS — without events, the ML models cannot train or measure performance.
- **Exam focus:** For headless, the merchant is responsible for implementing **event tracking** using the Adobe Storefront Events SDK — it is NOT automatic.
- **Exam focus:** API-based rendering uses **GraphQL** — not REST.

### 8.3 Supported Page Types for Placement

| Page Type | Typical Recommendation Types Used |
|---|---|
| Home Page | Most Viewed, Trending, Recommended for You |
| Category Page | Most Viewed in Category, Trending |
| Product Detail Page (PDP) | More Like This, Bought Together, Viewed-Bought |
| Cart Page | Bought Together, More Like This |
| Checkout Page | Last-resort upsell placements |
| 404 / Search No Results | Trending, Most Viewed |

---

## 9. Supported Recommendation Types In Detail

### 9.1 Complete Reference Table

| Type ID | Display Name | Data Source | Training Required | Cold Start Safe? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `more-like-this` | More Like This | Product attributes | No (attribute-based) | **Yes** |
| `recently-viewed` | Recently Viewed | Browser session | No | **Yes** |
| `trending` | Trending | Recent event spike | Yes (recent events) | No |
| `most-viewed` | Most Viewed | Page view events | Yes | No |
| `most-purchased` | Most Purchased | Order data | Yes | No |
| `bought-together` | Bought Together | Co-purchase orders | Yes (substantial) | No |
| `viewed-bought` | Viewed This, Bought That | View + purchase correlation | Yes | No |
| `recommended-for-you` | Recommended for You | Full behavioral profile | Yes (heavy) | No |

### 9.2 More Like This (Attribute-Based)

**How it works:** Recommends products with similar attribute values to the currently viewed product. It does NOT require any behavioral training — purely content-based filtering.

```
Current Product: Blue Denim Jacket
  Attributes: Color=Blue, Type=Jacket, Material=Denim, Gender=Mens, Size-range=S-XL

Similarity scoring:
  Product A: Blue Hoodie       -> Score: 0.72 (Color+Gender match)
  Product B: Black Denim Jeans -> Score: 0.65 (Material+Gender match)
  Product C: Blue Denim Shirt  -> Score: 0.85 (Color+Material match) <-- top result
  Product D: Red T-Shirt       -> Score: 0.20 (Gender match only)
```

**Key attributes used for similarity:**
- Category membership
- Price range proximity
- Configurable/custom attributes (color, size, material, brand)
- Product type

- **Exam focus:** "More Like This" is **purely attribute-based** — it does not consider purchase history or view history.
- **Exam focus:** Works on **Day 1** of a new store with no behavioral data.
- **Exam focus:** Quality of "More Like This" recommendations is **directly tied to the quality and completeness of product attribute data**.

### 9.3 Trending (Recent Activity Spike)

**How it works:** Identifies products experiencing a **sudden spike in activity** (views, add-to-cart, purchases) over a **recent short time window** (typically 24-72 hours). It is **recency-weighted** — a product with 1000 views last week but 5 today would NOT trend vs. one with 50 views but all in the last hour.

```
Time window: Last 24 hours
Product events:
  Widget A: 1200 events (flat, been popular for weeks) -> NOT trending
  Widget B: 800 events (sudden spike from social media) -> TRENDING
  Widget C: 300 events (up 400% from yesterday)        -> TRENDING
  Widget D: 50 events (new, normal rate)               -> NOT trending
```

- **Exam focus:** "Trending" is **not** "Most Popular" — it specifically requires a **recent spike**, not cumulative popularity.
- **Exam focus:** Requires **event data to be flowing** — does not work for cold start stores.

### 9.4 Recently Viewed (Session-Based)

**How it works:** Displays products the shopper has viewed **in their current session** (or across sessions if they're logged in). This data is stored **client-side in the browser / local storage** or server-side for authenticated users.

**Characteristics:**
- **No ML training required**
- Works on Day 1 for any store
- Personalized at the individual shopper level
- The one recommendation type that is **100% session/user-specific**
- If a shopper has viewed 0 products (e.g., lands on PDP directly), this unit may be empty

- **Exam focus:** "Recently Viewed" requires **no training data** and **no catalog sync delay** — it works immediately.
- **Exam focus:** This is the **most personalized** type for a new store since it reflects that individual shopper's behavior.

### 9.5 Bought Together (Co-Purchase)

**How it works:** Analyzes historical orders to find products **frequently purchased in the same order**. Uses **collaborative filtering** (item-item).

```
Order history analysis:
  Order #1001: [Widget A, Widget B, Widget C]
  Order #1002: [Widget A, Widget B]
  Order #1003: [Widget A, Widget C]
  Order #1004: [Widget B, Widget C]

Co-occurrence matrix:
         Widget A  Widget B  Widget C
Widget A    -         2         2
Widget B    2         -         2
Widget C    2         2         -

Result: Widget A page -> recommend Widget B & C (co-purchased 2x each)
```

**Data requirements:**
- Needs **meaningful order history** — Adobe recommends at minimum **hundreds to thousands of orders** for quality recommendations
- New stores will see empty/fallback results
- Results improve non-linearly as order data grows

- **Exam focus:** "Bought Together" requires **order history data** — it is one of the hardest types to deploy for new stores.
- **Exam focus:** "Bought Together" is **item-item collaborative filtering** — entirely different from "Recommended for You" (user-item).

---

## 10. A/B Testing Recommendations

### 10.1 What Can Be A/B Tested

Adobe Commerce Product Recommendations supports A/B testing to determine which recommendation type, placement, or configuration produces better business outcomes.

| Test Variable | Example |
|---|---|
| Recommendation type | "More Like This" vs. "Bought Together" on PDP |
| Number of products shown | 4 products vs. 8 products |
| Placement on page | Above fold vs. below description |
| Page type | Testing on PDP vs. Cart page |

### 10.2 A/B Test Setup in Admin

> **Note:** This admin interface is provided by the `magento/product-recommendations` SaaS package.

```
Marketing > Product Recommendations > [Recommendation Unit]
  > Test Settings
    - Enable A/B Test: Yes
    - Control: [Original recommendation config]
    - Variant: [New recommendation type/config]
    - Traffic Split: 50/50
    - Test Duration: 14 days (minimum recommended)
    - Primary Metric: Click-Through Rate | Revenue | Conversions
```

### 10.3 Statistical Significance

- Tests should run until **statistical significance is achieved** (typically 95% confidence)
- Minimum recommended test duration: **14 days** to capture weekly behavior cycles
- Low-traffic stores may need longer durations

### 10.4 Comparing Recommendation Types for Business Outcomes

```
Example A/B Test Results:
+----------------------+------+----------+---------+-----------+
| Recommendation Type  | CTR  | Rev/Unit | Impress | Lift vs   |
|                      |      |          |         | Baseline  |
+----------------------+------+----------+---------+-----------+
| More Like This (ctrl)|3.2%  | $1.45    | 10,000  | baseline  |
| Bought Together (var)|5.8%  | $2.90    | 10,200  | +100%     |
+----------------------+------+----------+---------+-----------+

Decision: Bought Together wins for this store/page type
```

- **Exam focus:** The **three key metrics** for A/B testing recommendations are **CTR (Click-Through Rate)**, **Revenue** (or Revenue per Unit), and **Impressions**.
- **Exam focus:** Revenue impact is typically more important than CTR — a high CTR recommendation that drives low-value purchases is inferior to a lower CTR that drives high-AOV purchases.

---

## 11. Performance Metrics for Recommendations

### 11.1 The Three Core Metrics

#### Click-Through Rate (CTR)
```
CTR = (Total Recommendation Clicks / Total Recommendation Impressions) x 100

Example:
  Impressions: 5,000
  Clicks: 175
  CTR = (175 / 5,000) x 100 = 3.5%
```

- Measures **engagement** with the recommendation unit
- Higher CTR = recommendation products are relevant to the shopper
- Benchmark: Industry average CTR for product recommendations is ~2-5%

#### Revenue
```
Revenue Attribution = Sum of order revenue from shoppers who clicked a recommendation

Revenue per Impression = Total Revenue Attributed / Total Impressions
Revenue per Click = Total Revenue Attributed / Total Clicks
```

- Revenue can be measured as **total attributed revenue** or **revenue per impression/click**
- Attribution window matters — typically last-click or time-window based

#### Impressions
```
Impression = 1 recommendation unit viewed by 1 shopper on 1 page load

Total Impressions = Sigma(all page loads where unit was rendered and visible)
```

- Impressions measure **reach** of the recommendation unit
- Low impressions = unit is on a low-traffic page or not rendering correctly
- Needed as the denominator for CTR calculation

### 11.2 Metrics Dashboard in Admin

> **Note:** This dashboard is part of the `magento/product-recommendations` SaaS package.

```
Marketing > Product Recommendations > [Unit Name] > View Metrics

Available metrics:
  - Impressions (last 7 / 30 days)
  - Clicks
  - Click-Through Rate (%)
  - Revenue Attributed
  - Revenue per Impression
  - Units Sold via Recommendations
```

- **Exam focus:** All three metrics — **CTR, Revenue, Impressions** — must be monitored together. CTR alone doesn't indicate business value; Revenue without Impressions context is misleading.
- **Exam focus:** A recommendation unit with **0 impressions** likely has a rendering problem or is on a page with no traffic — not a data training issue.

---

## 12. Catalog Sync to Adobe SaaS

### 12.1 Why Catalog Sync Is Critical

Product Recommendations runs entirely in **Adobe's SaaS infrastructure**. Your local Magento catalog must be **continuously synchronized** to Adobe SaaS for:
- New products to appear in recommendations
- Price/attribute changes to be reflected
- Inventory status to be considered

### 12.2 Sync Architecture

```
Adobe Commerce DB              Adobe SaaS Data Space
+------------------+          +----------------------+
| catalog_product  |          | Products Index       |
| entity tables    |--sync--->| (recommendation-     |
|                  |          |  ready format)       |
| price tables     |--sync--->| Price Index          |
|                  |          |                      |
| category tables  |--sync--->| Category Index       |
+------------------+          +----------------------+
                                        |
                                        v
                              +----------------------+
                              | Sensei ML Models     |
                              | (trained on this     |
                              |  synced data)        |
                              +----------------------+
```

### 12.3 Sync Commands

```bash
# Feeds confirmed in base EE (module-catalog-data-exporter):
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=products
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=productAttributes
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=categories

# Additional feeds may be available when Product Recommendations package is installed:
# --feed=categoryPermissions, --feed=productOverrides, --feed=prices
# (these feed names are NOT registered in base EE — they require the SaaS add-on packages)
```

> **Note:** The `saas:resync` command is provided by `module-saas-common` which IS in the base EE codebase. However, some feed names are only registered when additional SaaS packages are installed.

### 12.4 Sync Delay Timeline

```
Admin: "New Product Created & Saved"
  |
  | (indexing triggered)
  v
~5-15 minutes: Product indexed locally in Magento
  |
  | (cron job: catalog_data_exporter_products)
  v
~15-60 minutes: Product exported to SaaS feed queue
  |
  | (SaaS ingestion processing)
  v
~1-24 hours: Product available in Adobe SaaS Data Space
  |
  | (ML model re-training cycle)
  v
Hours to days: Product appears in recommendations
```

- **Exam focus:** **New products are NOT immediately available for recommendations** — there is a pipeline delay through catalog sync, SaaS ingestion, and model training.
- **Exam focus:** This sync delay is a **tricky exam topic** — "I just created a product, why isn't it showing in recommendations?" → catalog sync pipeline delay.

### 12.5 Common Sync Issues

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| New product not in recommendations | Sync delay or failed cron | Run `saas:resync`, check cron |
| Price not updated in recommendations | Price feed not synced | `saas:resync --feed=prices` (requires SaaS package) |
| Product appears but wrong attributes | Attribute feed stale | `saas:resync --feed=productAttributes` |
| No recommendations at all | API key misconfigured | Check Commerce Services Connector config |

```bash
# Check Commerce Services Connector configuration
# Actual config paths (verified in base EE):
# Section: services_connector
# Group: services_connector_integration
# Fields: production_api_key, production_private_key, sandbox_api_key, sandbox_private_key
```

---

## 13. Recommendations Dashboard — Admin Hands-On

> **Note:** The entire "Marketing > Product Recommendations" admin interface is provided by the separate `magento/product-recommendations` Composer package. It does NOT exist in the base Adobe Commerce EE installation. The following describes the interface once the package is installed.

### 13.1 Navigating to the Dashboard

```
Admin Panel Navigation (requires magento/product-recommendations package):
Marketing > Product Recommendations
  |
  +-> List view: All created recommendation units
  +-> [Create Recommendation] button
  +-> Each unit shows: Name, Type, Page, Status, Impressions, CTR
```

### 13.2 Creating a Recommendation Unit — Step by Step

```
Step 1: Name & Page Type
  Name: "Products You Might Like"
  Storefront Page Type: Product Detail Page

Step 2: Recommendation Type Selection
  Available types shown with status indicators:
  [READY]    More Like This
  [READY]    Recently Viewed
  [TRAINING] Most Viewed        <- insufficient data yet
  [TRAINING] Trending           <- insufficient data yet
  [NOT READY] Bought Together   <- needs more order history

Step 3: Number of Products
  Set: 4 to 8 (recommended range)

Step 4: Visual Filters (optional)
  - Exclude out-of-stock products: Yes
  - Price range filter: $0 - $500
  - Category restriction: Tops, Jackets

Step 5: Placement
  Content Block Position: Below product description

Step 6: Design (optional)
  - Custom CSS
  - Product card configuration

Step 7: Save & Activate
```

### 13.3 Recommendation Status Indicators

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Active | Unit is live, rendering on storefront |
| Inactive | Created but not yet activated |
| Training | Recommendation type lacks sufficient data |
| Not Ready | Recommendation type fundamentally unavailable (e.g., no orders for Bought Together) |
| Syncing | Catalog sync in progress |

### 13.4 Available Recommendation Types in EE Admin

When creating a recommendation in Adobe Commerce EE with Product Recommendations installed, the following types are available in the UI:

1. **Recommended for You** — personalized per-user
2. **Most Viewed** — site-wide or category-scoped
3. **Most Purchased** — by order frequency
4. **Most Added to Cart** — by add-to-cart events
5. **Trending** — recent activity spike
6. **Bought Together** — co-purchase analysis
7. **Viewed This, Bought That** — view-to-purchase correlation
8. **Viewed This, Viewed That** — view-to-view correlation
9. **More Like This** — attribute similarity
10. **Recently Viewed** — session/user history

- **Exam focus:** Types with (**Ready**) status on a new installation are typically only **"More Like This"** and **"Recently Viewed"** — all others require data accumulation.
- **Exam focus:** Adobe Commerce EE (Enterprise Edition) with the `magento/product-recommendations` package is required — this feature is **NOT available in Magento Open Source**.

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### B2B Tailored Pricing
- [ ] Three B2B pricing mechanisms: **Shared Catalog tier prices**, **Negotiable Quote prices**, **Customer Group prices**
- [ ] Price precedence (exam order): **Negotiated Quote → Shared Catalog Tier → Standard Tier → Special Price → Regular Price**
- [ ] Simplified exam order (without negotiable quote): **SharedCatalog tier → standard tier → special price → regular price**
- [ ] **Special Price does NOT override Shared Catalog tier price** — Shared Catalog wins
- [ ] Every Shared Catalog is backed by an **auto-created Customer Group**
- [ ] A company can be assigned to **only one Shared Catalog** (enforced by single customer_group_id)
- [ ] Deleting a **Custom** Shared Catalog deletes its customer group; deleting **Public** does NOT
- [ ] Customer group prices and tier prices share the **`catalog_product_entity_tier_price`** table
- [ ] Shared Catalog custom prices: **PRICE_TYPE_FIXED** or **PRICE_TYPE_DISCOUNT** (percentage)
- [ ] Negotiated Quote prices are **per-quote only**, not stored on the product
- [ ] Negotiable Quotes require **`Magento_NegotiableQuote`** module + "Allow Quotes" enabled per company

### Sensei AI Product Recommendations — Architecture
- [ ] Product Recommendations is a **SaaS service** (separate `magento/product-recommendations` package, not in base EE)
- [ ] Requires **Commerce Services Connector** with API key and SaaS Data Space (section=services_connector)
- [ ] Two rendering methods: **Widget-based** (default) and **API/GraphQL** (headless)
- [ ] Headless requires manual **behavioral event tracking** via Storefront Events SDK
- [ ] API-based rendering uses **GraphQL**, not REST

### Cold Start Problem
- [ ] Cold start = **insufficient data** for ML models to train recommendations
- [ ] Only **"Recently Viewed"** works with zero training data
- [ ] **"More Like This"** works with zero behavioral data (attribute-based)
- [ ] **"Bought Together"** requires the **most data** (substantial order history)
- [ ] New products face catalog sync delay — **not immediately available in recommendations**
- [ ] Mitigation: Use "Recently Viewed" and "More Like This" on new stores

### Recommendation Types — Must Know
- [ ] **More Like This**: attribute-based, no training needed, **cold-start safe**
- [ ] **Recently Viewed**: session-based, no training needed, **cold-start safe**, most personalized
- [ ] **Trending**: recent **spike** in activity (not cumulative popularity), requires event data
- [ ] **Bought Together**: co-purchase analysis, requires **substantial order history**
- [ ] **Recommended for You**: full behavioral profile, most data-intensive
- [ ] **Trending ≠ Most Popular** — recency-weighted spike detection

### Catalog Sync
- [ ] New products go through: **Magento index → SaaS feed queue → SaaS ingestion → ML training** before appearing
- [ ] Sync delay can be **hours to days** for new products
- [ ] Force resync: `bin/magento saas:resync --feed=products` (module-saas-common in base EE)
- [ ] Confirmed feed names in base EE: **products**, **productAttributes**, **categories**
- [ ] Failed catalog sync = products missing from recommendations

### Performance Metrics
- [ ] Three core metrics: **CTR**, **Revenue**, **Impressions**
- [ ] CTR = Clicks / Impressions x 100
- [ ] 0 impressions = rendering problem (not training problem)
- [ ] Revenue attribution is more important than CTR alone

### A/B Testing
- [ ] Can test: **recommendation type**, **number of products**, **placement**, **page type**
- [ ] Primary metrics: **CTR**, **Revenue**, **Impressions**
- [ ] Minimum recommended test duration: **14 days**
- [ ] Need statistical significance (~95%) before declaring winner
- [ ] Revenue per impression is a better holistic metric than CTR alone

### Availability
- [ ] Product Recommendations requires **Adobe Commerce EE** (not Magento Open Source)
- [ ] Requires `magento/product-recommendations` Composer package (separate from base EE)
- [ ] "Recently Viewed" and "More Like This" are typically **immediately deployable**
- [ ] All behavior-based types show **"Training"** status on new installations

flashcards.question: What is the B2B price precedence order from highest to lowest priority?
flashcards.answer: The order is: (1) Negotiated Quote Price, (2) Shared Catalog Tier Price, (3) Standard Catalog Tier Price, (4) Special Price, (5) Regular/Base Price. A Special Price does NOT override a Shared Catalog tier price — the Shared Catalog tier always wins.
flashcards.hint: Quote > Shared Tier > Standard Tier > Special > Regular — the negotiated deal always trumps.

flashcards.question: In the B2B pricing hierarchy, what price does a company buyer see if they order a quantity that does NOT meet any tier threshold in their Shared Catalog?
flashcards.answer: They see the base Shared Catalog price for that product (not the standard tier price, special price, or regular price). The Shared Catalog base price takes precedence over special prices and regular prices even without meeting a tier threshold.
flashcards.hint: The catalog-assigned base price applies even before volume discounts kick in.

flashcards.question: Where are Shared Catalog tier prices stored in the database?
flashcards.answer: Shared Catalog tier prices are stored in the catalog_product_entity_tier_price table — the SAME table used for standard tier prices and customer group prices. The auto-created customer group ID for the Shared Catalog is what differentiates the rows.
flashcards.hint: All three pricing mechanisms share a single database table, differentiated by customer group.

flashcards.question: What is the cold start problem in the context of Product Recommendations?
flashcards.answer: The cold start problem is the inability to make accurate behavioral recommendations when there is insufficient historical data. New stores have no impressions, clicks, or purchase events. Only 'Recently Viewed' (session-based) and 'More Like This' (attribute-based) work on Day 1.
flashcards.hint: AI needs data to learn from — without it, most recommendation types stay empty.

flashcards.question: How does the 'Trending' recommendation type differ from 'Most Viewed'?
flashcards.answer: Trending identifies products with a sudden SPIKE in activity over a recent short time window (24-72 hours) — it is recency-weighted. Most Viewed shows products with the highest cumulative view count. A product popular for weeks but flat today would NOT trend, but a product with a sudden surge would.
flashcards.hint: One measures velocity of change; the other measures total accumulation.

flashcards.question: What is the 'More Like This' recommendation type based on, and does it require behavioral data?
flashcards.answer: More Like This is purely attribute-based — it recommends products with similar attribute values (category, price range, color, material, brand) to the currently viewed product. It does NOT require any behavioral data (no purchase or view history needed) and works on Day 1 of a new store.
flashcards.hint: Catalog content, not shopper behavior, drives this recommendation type.

flashcards.question: What are the three core performance metrics for Product Recommendation units?
flashcards.answer: CTR (Click-Through Rate = clicks / impressions x 100), Revenue (total attributed revenue from recommendation clicks), and Impressions (number of times the recommendation unit was displayed). All three must be monitored together — CTR alone doesn't indicate business value.
flashcards.hint: Engagement rate, monetary impact, and reach — all three tell the complete story.

flashcards.question: What happens when you delete a Custom Shared Catalog versus the Public Shared Catalog?
flashcards.answer: Deleting a Custom Shared Catalog also deletes its auto-created customer group. Deleting the Public Shared Catalog is prevented — an exception is thrown because the Public catalog serves as the default for all non-B2B visitors.
flashcards.hint: One cleans up its linked entity; the other cannot be removed at all.

flashcards.question: Which recommendation types require the most behavioral data to function?
flashcards.answer: 'Bought This, Bought That' (co-purchase analysis) and 'Viewed This, Bought That' (view-to-purchase correlation) require the most data. They need sufficient co-occurrence pairs — orders where multiple products were purchased together — which requires hundreds to thousands of orders.
flashcards.hint: Correlating one product to another requires enough shared purchase events to find real patterns.

flashcards.question: What are the two rendering methods for Product Recommendations on the storefront?
flashcards.answer: Widget-based rendering (default) uses Page Builder or layout XML to place recommendation blocks on specific pages. API-based rendering (headless) fetches recommendations via GraphQL API for PWA/custom frontends. Both methods require behavioral event tracking to feed the ML models.
flashcards.hint: Traditional blocks or programmatic API calls — but both need event data flowing.

flashcards.question: Why might a newly created product not appear in Product Recommendations even after being added to the catalog?
flashcards.answer: New products must go through a multi-stage pipeline: Magento indexing (5-15 min), SaaS feed queue export (15-60 min), SaaS ingestion processing (1-24 hours), and ML model re-training (hours to days). This catalog sync delay means products are NOT immediately available for recommendations.
flashcards.hint: A four-stage pipeline introduces significant delay from creation to recommendation eligibility.

flashcards.question: How do Cart Price Rules interact with B2B price precedence?
flashcards.answer: Cart Price Rules operate SEPARATELY from the B2B price precedence chain. They apply as discounts on top of the winning price from the precedence hierarchy. The B2B precedence (Negotiated Quote > Shared Catalog Tier > Standard Tier > Special > Regular) determines the base price, and cart rules discount from there.
flashcards.hint: The precedence chain picks the base price; cart rules layer discounts on top.

flashcards.question: What is the minimum recommended duration for an A/B test on Product Recommendations?
flashcards.answer: The minimum recommended test duration is 14 days to capture weekly behavior cycles and achieve statistical significance (~95% confidence). Low-traffic stores may need longer durations. The primary comparison metrics are CTR, Revenue, and Impressions.
flashcards.hint: Two weeks captures the natural rhythm of shopping behavior.

flashcards.question: Why can a company only be assigned to one Shared Catalog at a time?
flashcards.answer: Each company has a single customer_group_id, and each Shared Catalog maps to one customer group. Since a customer can only belong to one customer group at a time, a company can only be assigned to one Shared Catalog. This is enforced architecturally.
flashcards.hint: The underlying customer group constraint creates a 1:1 limitation.

flashcards.question: What does a recommendation unit with zero impressions indicate?
flashcards.answer: Zero impressions indicates a rendering problem — the widget is not being displayed on the page. This is NOT a training data issue. Possible causes include the unit being on a low-traffic page, incorrect placement configuration, or a technical rendering failure. Training issues would show some impressions but poor CTR.
flashcards.hint: No views at all points to a display problem, not a data problem.

## 2. B2B Module — Complete Flow

The canonical B2B customer journey follows this path:

```
Company Account Created
        |
        v
Company Admin Assigns Roles & Users
        |
        v
Admin Assigns Shared Catalog to Company
        |
        v
Buyer Browses Catalog (custom prices visible)
        |
        v
Buyer Adds to Requisition List (optional)
        |
        v
Buyer Creates Cart --> Requests Negotiable Quote
        |
        v
Sales Rep Negotiates / Adjusts Quote
        |
        v
Buyer Accepts Quote --> Converts to Order
        |
        v
Purchase Order Approval Workflow (if enabled)
        |
        v
Order Placed --> Fulfillment
```

**Exam focus:** The exam often presents steps out of order and asks you to identify the *correct* sequence. Memorise: **Company → Shared Catalog → Negotiable Quote → Order**.

---

### 2.1 Company Management

#### Company Hierarchy

```
Parent Company Account
    |
    +-- Company Admin (dedicated admin user)
    |       |
    |       +-- Team A
    |       |     +-- Buyer 1
    |       |     +-- Buyer 2
    |       +-- Team B
    |             +-- Buyer 3
    |
    +-- (Sub-companies — Commerce 2.4.2+)
```

#### Key Configuration Paths

| Setting | Admin Path |
|---|---|
| Enable B2B Features | Stores > Config > General > B2B Features |
| Enable Company | B2B Features > Enable Company = Yes |
| Enable Shared Catalog | B2B Features > Enable Shared Catalog = Yes |
| Enable Negotiable Quote | B2B Features > Enable Negotiable Quote = Yes |
| Enable Purchase Orders | B2B Features > Enable Purchase Orders = Yes |

> **Exam focus:** You **must** enable Company *before* you can enable Shared Catalog or Negotiable Quote. These features have a dependency chain: Company → (Shared Catalog, Negotiable Quote, PO) — they do not activate independently.

#### Company Status Lifecycle

```
Pending Approval
      |
      v
    Active  <---> Blocked
      ^               
      |               
      v               
   Rejected           
```

- **Pending**: Default when company registers from storefront
- **Active**: Admin approves; company users can transact
- **Blocked**: Temporarily suspended; users cannot log in
- **Rejected**: Admin rejects company; however, a rejected company **can** be reactivated back to Active status by the admin (the code in `CompanyStatus.php` has an explicit email template `company_status_rejected_blocked_to_active_template` for this transition, and `SaveValidator/CompanyStatus.php` allows all four statuses as valid transitions)

**Exam focus:** Blocked vs. Rejected — both are *reversible*. Blocked temporarily prevents login; Rejected is a stronger denial but can still be reversed by the admin changing the status back to Active.

#### Company Roles & Permissions

```php
// Roles are purely ACL-based in B2B
// Defined in: Magento_Company::etc/company_acl.xml

// Key default roles:
// - Default User (base permissions)
// - Custom roles created by Company Admin
```

- Company Admin can create unlimited custom roles
- Permissions include: View Orders, Place Orders, View Quotes, Manage Users & Roles, Edit Account, View/Edit Address (defined in `company_acl.xml` — these are company-level permissions, **not** admin ACL permissions)
- Permissions are **not** inherited from Magento admin ACL

---

### 2.2 Shared Catalogs

#### Types of Shared Catalog

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| **Public** | Default catalog; available to all (including guests) |
| **Custom** | Private catalog; assigned to one or more companies |

> **Exam focus:** There is always **exactly one Public shared catalog**. You cannot delete it; you can only rename it. Creating a custom shared catalog does NOT remove the public one.

#### Shared Catalog Pricing

- Custom pricing is set **per product, per catalog** (not per customer group directly)
- Shared Catalog automatically creates a corresponding **Customer Group** with the same name
- Prices can be set as:
  - Fixed price
  - Percentage discount from original price

```
Custom Shared Catalog "Wholesale"
        |
        v (auto-creates)
Customer Group "Wholesale"
        |
        v (tier pricing stored in)
catalog_product_entity_tier_price table
```

**Exam focus:** Shared Catalog pricing is stored in the *tier price* table, not a separate table. The auto-created customer group is the mechanism by which prices are applied.

#### Assigning Products & Categories

1. Navigate to: **Catalog > Shared Catalogs > [Select] > Set Pricing & Structure**
2. Select categories/products to include
3. Set custom prices
4. Assign the catalog to company: **Catalog > Shared Catalogs > [Select] > Assign Companies**

> **Exam focus:** Products must be **explicitly included** in a custom shared catalog. A product not included will be invisible to that company's buyers — it does not appear as out-of-stock; it is completely hidden.
