### 2.3 Negotiable Quotes

#### Negotiable Quote State Machine

```
Draft (Buyer)
      |
      v (Buyer submits)
Submitted
      |
      v (Sales rep opens)
Pending
      |
      +-- Sales rep adjusts --> Open
      |                           |
      |                     (Rep sends back)
      |                           |
      +<--------------------------+
      |
      v (Buyer reviews)
      +-- Buyer accepts --> Ordered (terminal)
      +-- Buyer declines --> Closed (terminal)
      +-- Buyer counter-offers --> Submitted again
      |
      v (Admin expires or declines)
    Expired / Declined (terminal)
```

**Exam focus:** Know every terminal state: **Ordered**, **Closed**, **Expired**, **Declined**. Ordered is the only *positive* terminal state.

#### Quote Adjustments Available to Sales Rep

- Percentage or fixed discount on **individual line items** (stored per-item in `negotiable_quote_item` table as `negotiated_price_type` and `negotiated_price_value` — types include `PERCENTAGE_DISCOUNT`, `AMOUNT_DISCOUNT`, and `PROPOSED_TOTAL`)
- Custom shipping method and rate
- Expiry date on the quote
- Comments/attachments

> **Note:** Negotiable quote discounts are applied **per line item**, not as a blanket discount on the cart subtotal. The `negotiable_quote_item` table tracks the negotiated price type and value for each individual item in the quote.

#### Quote Conversion to Order

```
Buyer accepts quote
        |
        v
Quote status = "Ordered"
        |
        v
Cart is populated with quote items at negotiated prices
        |
        v
Normal checkout flow (address, payment)
        |
        v
Order created — negotiated prices locked
```

> **Exam focus:** A negotiable quote does **not** bypass checkout. The buyer still completes the checkout process after accepting the quote. The quote merely pre-populates the cart with negotiated prices.

---

### 2.4 Purchase Orders & Approval Workflows

#### Purchase Order Flow

```
Buyer creates PO (instead of normal order)
        |
        v
PO Status: Pending
        |
        v
Approval Rule evaluated
        +-- No rule matches OR auto-approved --> Status: Approved
        +-- Rule requires approval --> Status: Approval Required
                |
                v
        Approver reviews
        +-- Approves --> Status: Approved --> Order Placed
        +-- Rejects --> Status: Rejected (terminal)
```

#### Approval Rule Conditions

| Condition Type | Example |
|---|---|
| Order Total | PO total > $1,000 requires manager approval |
| Number of SKUs | More than 10 SKUs requires approval |
| Shipping Cost | Shipping > $100 requires approval |

**Exam focus:** Approval rules are configured by the **Company Admin** in the storefront, not by the Magento Admin. The Magento Admin only enables/disables the PO feature globally.

#### Purchase Order Statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Pending | Awaiting approval rule evaluation |
| Approval Required | Rule triggered; waiting for approver action |
| Approved | Cleared; ready for order placement |
| Approved - Pending Payment | Approved but payment not yet processed |
| Order in Progress | Order conversion underway |
| Order Placed | Successfully converted to Magento order |
| Order Failed | Order conversion failed (e.g. payment declined) |
| Rejected | Denied by approver |
| Canceled | Buyer canceled before approval |

> **Note:** There are **9 PO statuses** in total (defined in `PurchaseOrderInterface.php`), not 6. There is no "Converted" status — the final positive state is "Order Placed". The statuses `approved_pending_payment`, `order_in_progress`, `order_placed`, and `order_failed` track the granular order conversion lifecycle.

---

### 2.5 Requisition Lists & Quick Order

#### Requisition Lists

- Saved lists of products for repeat purchasing (like saved carts)
- **Not** shared across company users — private to each buyer
- Maximum lists per customer: configured in **Stores > Config > Customers > Requisition Lists > Number of Requisition Lists**
- Default maximum: **999**

> **Exam focus:** Requisition Lists are **NOT** the same as a Wish List. Wish Lists are B2C. Requisition Lists are B2B, support multiple named lists, and are designed for repeat B2B purchasing workflows.

#### Quick Order

- Allows buyers to paste SKUs (one per line or CSV upload) to add multiple items directly to cart
- Bypasses browse/search flow
- Configured at: **Stores > Config > General > B2B Features > Enable Quick Order**

> **Note:** Quick Order is under **General > B2B Features** (section `btob`, tab `general`), not under Sales > B2B Features.

### 2.6 B2B Credit & Payment on Account

#### Company Credit

- Admin sets a **Credit Limit** per company
- Buyers use "Payment on Account" payment method at checkout
- Credit is consumed on order placement; released on order cancellation/refund

```
Credit Limit: $10,000
Outstanding Balance: $3,000
Available Credit: $7,000
        |
        v (New order: $2,000)
Outstanding Balance: $5,000
Available Credit: $5,000
```

**Exam focus:** Payment on Account is only available to companies with company credit enabled. It is **not** available to guest or regular B2C customers.

## 3. MSI — Multi-Source Inventory

### 3.1 Core Architecture

#### Key Concepts

| Concept | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Source** | Physical location (warehouse, store, supplier) with inventory |
| **Stock** | Virtual aggregation of one or more Sources |
| **Sales Channel** | Website assigned to a Stock |
| **Source Item** | Quantity of a SKU at a specific Source |
| **Reservation** | Temporary hold on inventory quantity |

```
Source A (Warehouse East)  ---+
Source B (Warehouse West)  ---+--> Stock 1 --> Website 1 (US Store)
Source C (Store Chicago)   ---+

Source D (UK Warehouse)    -------> Stock 2 --> Website 2 (UK Store)

Default Source             -------> Default Stock --> Default Website
```

> **Exam focus:** Every Magento installation has a **Default Source** and **Default Stock** that cannot be deleted. Single-source merchants use only these. Multi-source requires creating additional Sources and Stocks.

---

### 3.2 Sources & Stocks

#### Creating a Source

```
Stores > Inventory > Sources > Add New Source

Required fields:
- Source Code (unique, immutable after save)
- Source Name
- Status (Enabled/Disabled)
- Country, State, City, ZIP, Street
- Latitude/Longitude (for Distance Priority algorithm)
```

> **Exam focus:** The **Source Code is immutable** — it cannot be changed after the source is saved. This is a common exam trap.

#### Assigning Sources to Stock

```
Stores > Inventory > Stocks > [Select Stock] > Sources tab

- Add sources via search
- Set priority (integer; lower number = higher priority)
- Priority used by Source Selection Algorithms
```

#### Stock-to-Sales-Channel Assignment

- Each Stock can be assigned to **one or more websites**
- One website can only be assigned to **one Stock** at a time
- Salable Quantity displayed on storefront = sum of **enabled** assigned source quantities minus reservations

**Exam focus:** The **Salable Quantity** formula:

```
Salable Qty = SUM(Source Item Qty for enabled sources) - SUM(Open Reservations)
```

---

### 3.3 Reservation Lifecycle

This is the **most heavily tested MSI topic**. Understand every event that creates or compensates a reservation.

#### Reservation Creation & Compensation Events

```
+--------------------------------------------------+
|           RESERVATION LIFECYCLE                  |
+--------------------------------------------------+

[1] Customer adds item to cart
         |
         v
    No reservation yet (cart is not a reservation)

[2] Customer PLACES ORDER
         |
         v
    Reservation CREATED: qty = -1 (negative)
    Table: inventory_reservation
    Comment: "Order #000001234"

[3a] Order SHIPPED (source deducted)
         |
         v
    Source Item Qty physically decremented
    Compensation reservation CREATED: qty = +1
    Net effect: reservation neutralized

[3b] Order CANCELED
         |
         v
    Compensation reservation CREATED: qty = +1
    Net effect: inventory returned to Salable Qty

[3c] Credit Memo (return)
         |
         v
    Compensation reservation CREATED: qty = +1
    (if "Return to Stock" = Yes)

+--------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Reservation Table Structure

```sql
-- inventory_reservation table (simplified)
SELECT * FROM inventory_reservation;

-- Columns:
-- reservation_id  (auto-increment)
-- stock_id        (which stock)
-- sku             (product SKU)
-- quantity        (negative = hold, positive = release)
-- metadata        (JSON: object_type, object_id)

-- Example rows for a single order:
-- | 1 | 1 | SKU-001 | -2.0000 | {"object_type":"order","object_id":"1234"} |
-- | 2 | 1 | SKU-001 | +2.0000 | {"object_type":"order_shipment","object_id":"567"} |
```

> **Exam focus:** Reservations are **append-only** — rows are never updated or deleted. Compensation works by inserting an equal and opposite quantity row. The net sum of all rows for a SKU + stock = current reservation hold.

**Exam focus:** The cart does **NOT** create a reservation. Reservations are created at **order placement** only. This is one of the most common wrong-answer traps.

#### Reservation Inconsistency & Cleanup

- CLI command to check for inconsistencies:

```bash
bin/magento inventory:reservation:list-inconsistencies
```

- CLI command to create compensating reservations:

```bash
bin/magento inventory:reservation:create-compensations
```

- Inconsistencies occur when: order is manipulated outside of Magento (direct DB edits), failed queue messages, etc.

---

### 3.4 Source Selection Algorithms

When an order is shipped, MSI uses an SSA to recommend which source(s) to deduct from.

#### Available Algorithms

| Algorithm | Key Logic |
|---|---|
| **Priority** (default) | Deducts from sources in order of Stock-Source priority (lowest number first) |
| **Distance** | Deducts from source geographically closest to shipping address |

```
Priority Algorithm Example:
Stock 1 Sources:
  Priority 1: Warehouse East  (qty: 5)
  Priority 2: Warehouse West  (qty: 100)
  Priority 3: Store Chicago   (qty: 10)

Order for qty 7 of SKU-001:
  --> Deduct 5 from Warehouse East (exhausted)
  --> Deduct 2 from Warehouse West
  --> Store Chicago not touched
```

> **Exam focus:** The Priority algorithm selects sources **greedily** from highest priority (lowest number). Distance algorithm requires latitude/longitude configured on sources and shipping address geocoding.

#### Custom SSA via Plugin

```php
// Implement interface:
// Magento\InventorySourceSelectionApi\Api\SourceSelectionServiceInterface

// Or create a new algorithm implementing:
// Magento\InventorySourceSelectionApi\Model\SourceSelectionInterface

// Register in di.xml:
```

```xml
<type name="Magento\InventorySourceSelectionApi\Model\GetSourceSelectionAlgorithmList">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="algorithms" xsi:type="array">
            <item name="custom_algorithm" xsi:type="object">
                Vendor\Module\Model\Algorithm\CustomAlgorithm
            </item>
        </argument>
    </arguments>
</type>
```

---

### 3.5 MSI & Order Management

#### Source Assignment During Shipment

```
Admin > Orders > [Order] > Ship
        |
        v
Source Selection panel appears
        |
        v
Algorithm suggests source(s) with quantities
        |
        v
Admin can OVERRIDE algorithm suggestion
        |
        v
Admin confirms > Shipment created
        |
        v
Source Item Qty decremented
Reservation compensated (+quantity)
```

#### Bulk Transfer & Assignment

```bash
# Bulk assign sources to products
# Done via: Catalog > Products > [Select] > Actions > Assign Inventory Source
```

> **Note:** There is no `bin/magento inventory:source-deduction:execute` CLI command. Source deductions happen automatically when shipments are created. For bulk inventory operations, use the admin mass actions (Catalog > Products grid) or direct API/import.

> **Exam focus:** When a source is **disabled**, it is excluded from **both** SSA recommendations **and** Salable Quantity calculations. The `SelectBuilder.php` in `module-inventory-indexer` filters sources by `enabled = 1` when computing salable quantity. A disabled source's inventory does **not** count toward salable quantity — to preserve that inventory's availability, reassign it to another source or re-enable the source before unlinking it from the stock.

## 4. Business Intelligence (BI)

### 4.1 Architecture & Data Pipeline

Adobe Commerce BI (formerly Magento BI / RJMetrics) is a **cloud-based** analytics platform that syncs data from your Commerce database.

#### Data Flow

```
Commerce Database (MySQL)
        |
        v (Encrypted replication / API sync)
BI Data Warehouse (hosted)
        |
        v
Data Transformation (ETL layer)
        |
        v
Report Builder
        |
        v
Dashboards & Email Reports
```

> **Exam focus:** BI is a **separate cloud service** — it does not run on your Commerce server. Data is synced on a schedule (typically hourly or daily). Reports are **not** real-time.

#### Sync Frequency

| Sync Type | Frequency |
|---|---|
| Standard Update Cycle | ~1 hour |
| Full Re-sync | On demand or scheduled |
| New Column Sync | After adding column in Data Warehouse Manager |

---

### 4.2 Key Metrics & Reports

#### Pre-Built Metrics (know these)

| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Revenue** | Sum of order totals (grand total) |
| **Orders** | Count of orders |
| **Average Order Value (AOV)** | Revenue / Orders |
| **Customer Lifetime Value (CLV/LTV)** | Total revenue per customer over lifetime |
| **Repeat Customer Rate** | % customers with >1 order |
| **Time Between Orders** | Avg days between first and second order |
| **New vs. Returning Customers** | Segmented order count |

> **Exam focus:** AOV, CLV, and Repeat Customer Rate are the three most commonly tested BI metrics. Know their *formulas*, not just their names.

#### Report Builder Types

| Builder | Use Case |
|---|---|
| **Visual Report Builder** | Point-and-click; time series, grouped data |
| **SQL Report Builder** | Custom SQL queries against DW; flexible but advanced |
| **Cohort Report Builder** | Retention analysis; groups customers by acquisition date |

**Exam focus:** The **Cohort Report Builder** is unique to BI and is the primary tool for customer retention and LTV analysis. It is not available in native Commerce reports.

---

### 4.3 Dashboards & Cohort Analysis

#### Cohort Analysis Explained

A cohort groups customers by a shared characteristic (typically first order month) and tracks behavior over time.

```
Cohort: Customers who first purchased in January 2024

Month 0 (Jan): 100 customers   (100% baseline)
Month 1 (Feb):  45 customers   (45% retention)
Month 2 (Mar):  28 customers   (28% retention)
Month 3 (Apr):  22 customers   (22% retention)
```

> **Exam focus:** Cohort analysis measures **retention rate**, not just repurchase count. The "Month 0" baseline is always 100%.

#### Email Report Scheduling

- Reports and dashboards can be scheduled as email summaries
- Formats: PDF, CSV, image (PNG)
- Configured per dashboard: **Share > Schedule Export**

## 5. Live Search

### 5.1 Architecture & Indexing

Adobe Live Search replaces the native Elasticsearch/OpenSearch-powered search with an **Adobe-hosted SaaS service**.

#### Architecture Overview

```
Commerce Backend
    |
    +-- Catalog Sync Service --> Adobe SaaS Environment
    |   (product data, prices,                |
    |    attributes, categories)              v
    |                               Search Index (Adobe hosted)
    |                                         |
Storefront (PWA / Luma)                       |
    |                                         |
    +-- GraphQL API Request ----------------->+
    |   (search query, filters)               |
    |                                         v
    +<-------- Search Results (JSON) ---------+
```

> **Exam focus:** Live Search does **not** use Elasticsearch for search. It uses Adobe's proprietary SaaS search index. Elasticsearch/OpenSearch remains installed and is used for **catalog indexing** (category pages, layered navigation on category browse) when Live Search is active — it is not fully replaced.

#### Prerequisites & Installation

Live Search is a **separate SaaS package** (`magento/live-search`) that must be installed via Composer. It is **not** included in the base Adobe Commerce EE installation. The "Marketing > Live Search" admin menus (Facets, Synonyms, Rules) are added by this package and do not exist in base EE.

```bash
# Install via Composer
composer require magento/live-search

# After install, configure API keys:
# Stores > Config > Services > Commerce Services Connector
# - Enter Production API Key / Private Key
# - Enter Sandbox API Key / Private Key
# - Select SaaS Data Space
```

**Exam focus:** Live Search requires a **Commerce Services Connector** with valid API keys. Without the connector configured, the module installs but does not function. The connector fields are in section `services_connector`, group `services_connector_integration`.

#### Catalog Sync & Indexing Latency

| Event | Sync Behavior |
|---|---|
| Product Save | Queued for sync; appears in Live Search within **~15 min** to **1 hour** |
| Full Catalog Sync | CLI trigger; syncs entire catalog |
| Price Change | Synced on next scheduled sync cycle |

```bash
# Force a full catalog sync
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=products

# Check sync status
bin/magento saas:resync --feed=products --dry-run
```

> **Exam focus:** Live Search indexing is **not instant**. New products or price changes have a sync delay. This is a common scenario question: "A product was added but doesn't appear in Live Search — why?"

---

### 5.2 Facets, Synonyms & Rules

#### Facets

Facets are the filterable attributes displayed in Live Search results.

| Facet Type | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Pinned** | Always displayed at a fixed position in facet list |
| **Dynamic** | Displayed based on relevance to current results |

- Maximum **8 pinned facets** at a time
- Only attributes marked as **filterable** in attribute configuration appear as facets
- Configured in: **Marketing > Live Search > Facets** (requires Live Search SaaS package installed)

> **Exam focus:** An attribute must be set to **"Use in Layered Navigation: Filterable (with results)"** AND be synced to Live Search to appear as a facet. Both conditions must be met.

#### Synonyms

Two types of synonym behavior:

| Type | Behavior | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Two-way** | Query A shows results for B, and query B shows results for A | "jacket" <-> "coat" |
| **One-way** | Query A shows results for B, but NOT vice versa | "pants" -> "trousers" (but "trousers" doesn't show "pants" results) |

```
Configured: "sofa" (two-way) "couch", "settee"

Search "sofa" --> returns sofa + couch + settee results
Search "couch" --> returns sofa + couch + settee results
Search "settee" --> returns sofa + couch + settee results
```

**Exam focus:** Two-way vs. one-way synonym direction is consistently tested. One-way is unidirectional — the expansion only goes from the *trigger term* to the *expanded terms*.

#### Merchandising Rules

Rules allow you to control search result ranking and display for specific queries.

| Rule Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Pin** | Force product to specific position in results |
| **Boost** | Move product higher in results (weighted) |
| **Bury** | Move product lower in results |
| **Hide** | Remove product from results entirely |

**Rule Priority:**

```
Pinned products (absolute position)
        |
        v
Boosted products (relative rank increase)
        |
        v
Default ranking (algorithm)
        |
        v
Buried products (relative rank decrease)
        |
        v
Hidden products (excluded)
```

> **Exam focus:** Rules are query-specific (triggered by a search term) or category-specific (triggered by category browse). A rule for "shoes" does NOT apply to "boots" unless explicitly configured.

---

### 5.3 GraphQL & Storefront Integration

Live Search exposes results via **GraphQL** exclusively on the storefront.

#### Key GraphQL Queries

```graphql
# Product Search
{
  productSearch(phrase: "running shoes", filter: [], pageSize: 10, currentPage: 1) {
    total_count
    items {
      product {
        sku
        name
        price_range {
          minimum_price {
            final_price {
              value
              currency
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
    facets {
      title
      attribute_code
      buckets {
        title
        count
      }
    }
    page_info {
      page_size
      current_page
      total_pages
    }
  }
}
```

```graphql
# Autocomplete / Popover suggestions
{
  productSearch(phrase: "run", pageSize: 5) {
    suggestions
    items {
      product {
        name
        sku
        small_image { url }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> **Exam focus:** Live Search uses the `productSearch` GraphQL query, **not** the native `products` query. This is an important distinction — integrations must use the Live Search endpoint.

#### Live Search Widgets (Storefront)

- **Search Popover**: Renders as-you-type suggestions
- **Search Results Page**: Full results with facets
- Both are React-based widgets served from Adobe CDN
- Can be customized via **Page Builder** or CSS overrides

## 7. Practice Test Strategy — Section 4

### Scoring by Sub-Topic

After Practice Test #3, categorize every wrong answer:

```
Wrong Answer Log Template:
+---------------------------+------------------+------------------+
| Question # | Sub-Topic    | My Answer        | Correct Answer   |
+---------------------------+------------------+------------------+
|     12     | B2B Flow     | Quote -> Company | Company -> Quote |
|     17     | MSI Reserv.  | Cart creates rsv | Order creates rsv|
|     23     | Live Search  | Uses Elasticsearch| Uses Adobe SaaS |
+---------------------------+------------------+------------------+
```

### Common Wrong-Answer Patterns

#### B2B Traps

| Wrong Assumption | Correct Fact |
|---|---|
| Shared Catalog creates new pricing table | Uses existing tier_price table |
| Negotiable Quote bypasses checkout | Buyer still completes full checkout |
| Rejected company cannot be reactivated | Rejected companies **can** be reactivated to Active by admin (code allows all status transitions) |
| PO rules set by Magento Admin | PO rules set by Company Admin in storefront |
| Requisition Lists are shared across company | Private to each individual buyer |

#### MSI Traps

| Wrong Assumption | Correct Fact |
|---|---|
| Cart creates a reservation | Reservation created at order placement |
| Reservations are updated in place | Append-only; compensated by new rows |
| Disabling a source only excludes it from SSA | Disabled sources excluded from **both** SSA **and** Salable Qty (SelectBuilder filters `enabled=1`) |
| Source Code can be changed after save | Source Code is immutable |
| Default Stock can be deleted | Default Stock and Default Source cannot be deleted |

#### Live Search Traps

| Wrong Assumption | Correct Fact |
|---|---|
| Live Search uses Elasticsearch | Uses Adobe SaaS; Elasticsearch remains for catalog indexing |
| New products appear immediately | ~15 min to 1 hour sync delay |
| Any attribute auto-becomes a facet | Must be filterable AND synced |
| Synonyms are always two-way | Two types: two-way and one-way |
| Live Search uses `products` GraphQL query | Uses `productSearch` query |

---

## 8. Sandbox Scenario Walkthroughs

### Scenario A — B2B Full Flow (30 min)

**Goal:** Trace the complete B2B flow from company creation to order.

```
Step 1: Create Company (Admin > Customers > Companies > Add Company)
  - Company Name: "Acme Corp"
  - Company Email: admin@acme.com
  - Company Admin: Set first/last name, email, password
  - Credit Limit: $5,000
  - Save

Step 2: Create Custom Shared Catalog
  (Catalog > Shared Catalogs > Add Shared Catalog)
  - Name: "Acme Wholesale"
  - Type: Custom
  - Set Pricing & Structure: select 5-10 products, set 10% discount
  - Assign to Company: "Acme Corp"

Step 3: Log in as Company Admin (storefront)
  - Verify only Shared Catalog products are visible
  - Verify custom prices show (10% less than regular)

Step 4: Add products to cart
  - Request a Negotiable Quote
  - Check admin notification

Step 5: Admin negotiates quote (Admin > Sales > Quotes)
  - Apply additional 5% discount on line items
  - Add expiry date (+7 days)
  - Send to buyer

Step 6: Log in as buyer
  - Accept the quote
  - Complete checkout
  - Verify order placed with negotiated prices

Step 7: Check MSI
  - Verify reservation created in inventory_reservation table
  - Check Salable Qty decreased
```

### Scenario B — MSI Reservation Trace (30 min)

**Goal:** Observe the full reservation lifecycle for one order.

```bash
# Before order - check reservation table
SELECT * FROM inventory_reservation WHERE sku = 'YOUR-SKU';
# Should show 0 rows (or balanced rows)

# Check salable quantity
SELECT * FROM inventory_stock_1 WHERE sku = 'YOUR-SKU';
```

```
Step 1: Place order for 2 units of SKU

Step 2: Check reservation table
  - Should see row: qty = -2.0000
  - metadata: order_id = [new order id]

Step 3: Check salable qty - should be 2 less than before

Step 4: Create shipment in admin
  - Select source
  - Submit shipment

Step 5: Check reservation table again
  - Should see NEW row: qty = +2.0000
  - metadata: order_shipment_id = [shipment id]

Step 6: Check source item table
  - Source physical qty should now be reduced by 2
  - SELECT * FROM inventory_source_item
    WHERE sku = 'YOUR-SKU' AND source_code = 'default';

Step 7: Cancel a SECOND test order
  - Check reservation table
  - Should see compensation row: qty = +2.0000
  - Source item qty should NOT change (never shipped)
```

---

## 9. Wrong-Answer Trace Templates

### B2B Wrong Answer Trace

```
WRONG ANSWER TRACE — B2B

Question: [Write question here]
My Answer: [What I chose]
Correct Answer: [What it should be]

Correct B2B Flow Trace:
1. Company created & approved (Admin)
2. Company Admin assigned
3. Custom Shared Catalog created
4. Products/pricing added to Shared Catalog
5. Shared Catalog assigned to Company
6. Buyer logs in, sees catalog
7. Buyer requests Negotiable Quote (from cart)
8. Sales rep negotiates (Admin > Sales > Quotes)
9. Quote sent back to buyer
10. Buyer accepts quote
11. Buyer completes checkout (quote pre-populates cart)
12. Order created with negotiated prices
13. PO workflow (if enabled): Pending -> Approval Required -> Approved -> Order Placed

Where in this flow did I go wrong?
[Write answer here]

Why is my wrong answer incorrect?
[Write answer here]

Memory hook for correct answer:
[Write your mnemonic/hook here]
```

### MSI Reservation Wrong Answer Trace

```
WRONG ANSWER TRACE — MSI RESERVATION

Question: [Write question here]
My Answer: [What I chose]
Correct Answer: [What it should be]

Correct Reservation Lifecycle:
Event                    | Reservation Effect
-------------------------|-------------------
Item added to cart       | NO reservation
Order placed             | -qty reservation created
Order shipped            | +qty compensation (source also decremented)
Order canceled           | +qty compensation (source NOT changed)
Credit memo (return to   | +qty compensation (source may or may not
stock)                   | be incremented depending on setting)

Key rules:
- Reservations are APPEND-ONLY
- Net sum = current hold
- Cart ≠ reservation trigger
- Shipment triggers BOTH source decrement AND reservation compensation

Where did I confuse the lifecycle?
[Write answer here]
```

### Live Search Wrong Answer Trace

```
WRONG ANSWER TRACE — LIVE SEARCH

Question: [Write question here]
My Answer: [What I chose]
Correct Answer: [What it should be]

Architecture reminder:
- NOT Elasticsearch (that's native Commerce)
- Adobe SaaS hosted index
- Catalog Sync Service pushes data
- GraphQL query = productSearch (not products)
- Sync delay = ~15min to 1hr
- Facets: must be filterable + synced
- Synonyms: two-way OR one-way (different behavior)
- Rules: Pin > Boost > Default > Bury > Hide

Which fact did I get wrong?
[Write answer here]
```

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### B2B Module

- [ ] **Enable order**: Company → then Shared Catalog, Negotiable Quote, PO (dependency chain)
- [ ] **Public Shared Catalog**: exactly one, cannot be deleted, always exists
- [ ] **Shared Catalog pricing**: stored in `catalog_product_entity_tier_price` via auto-created customer group
- [ ] **Products not in Shared Catalog**: completely hidden (not out-of-stock) for assigned company
- [ ] **Negotiable Quote terminal states**: Ordered, Closed, Expired, Declined
- [ ] **Quote → Order**: buyer still completes full checkout; quote pre-populates cart
- [ ] **Company statuses**: Pending → Active <-> Blocked; Rejected can be reactivated to Active by admin
- [ ] **PO Approval Rules**: configured by Company Admin in storefront, not Magento Admin
- [ ] **PO Statuses**: 9 total — Pending, Approval Required, Approved, Approved Pending Payment, Order in Progress, Order Placed, Order Failed, Rejected, Canceled
- [ ] **Requisition Lists**: private to individual buyer (not shared across company users)
- [ ] **Payment on Account**: B2B only; consumes company credit limit
- [ ] **Negotiable Quote discounts**: per-item only (not cart subtotal) — stored in negotiable_quote_item

### MSI

- [ ] **Default Source & Default Stock**: cannot be deleted
- [ ] **Source Code**: immutable after save
- [ ] **Salable Qty formula**: `SUM(enabled Source Item Qty) - SUM(Open Reservations)`
- [ ] **Cart does NOT create a reservation**: reservations created at order placement only
- [ ] **Reservation rows are append-only**: compensation = new opposite-sign row
- [ ] **Shipment**: decrements source item qty AND creates compensation reservation
- [ ] **Cancellation**: creates compensation reservation; does NOT change source qty
- [ ] **Disabled source**: excluded from **both** SSA **and** Salable Qty calculations (SelectBuilder filters enabled=1)
- [ ] **Priority SSA**: deducts from lowest-priority-number source first (greedy)
- [ ] **Distance SSA**: requires lat/long on sources; nearest source selected first
- [ ] **CLI inconsistency check**: `bin/magento inventory:reservation:list-inconsistencies`

### Business Intelligence (BI)

- [ ] **BI is cloud-hosted**: separate SaaS, not on Commerce server
- [ ] **Not real-time**: sync delay ~1 hour (standard update cycle)
- [ ] **AOV formula**: Revenue / Orders
- [ ] **CLV**: total revenue per customer over lifetime
- [ ] **Cohort Report Builder**: retention analysis; customers grouped by acquisition date
- [ ] **SQL Report Builder**: custom queries against data warehouse
- [ ] **Pre-built BI metrics**: Revenue, Orders, AOV, CLV, Repeat Customer Rate, New vs. Returning
- [ ] **Cohort Month 0**: always 100% baseline

### Live Search

- [ ] **NOT Elasticsearch**: Adobe SaaS index; Elasticsearch remains for catalog indexing
- [ ] **Separate SaaS package**: not in base EE; install via `composer require magento/live-search`
- [ ] **Requires Commerce Services Connector**: API keys must be configured (services_connector/services_connector_integration)
- [ ] **Sync delay**: ~15 min to 1 hour; products not instantly searchable after save
- [ ] **Force sync**: `bin/magento saas:resync --feed=products`
- [ ] **Facets**: attribute must be "Filterable (with results)" AND synced; max 8 pinned
- [ ] **Two-way synonym**: bidirectional expansion
- [ ] **One-way synonym**: trigger term expands to synonyms, not reverse
- [ ] **Rule priority**: Pin > Boost > Default Algorithm > Bury > Hide
- [ ] **Rules are query-specific**: a rule for "shoes" ≠ rule for "boots"
- [ ] **GraphQL query**: `productSearch` (NOT `products`)
- [ ] **B2B + Live Search**: respects Shared Catalog visibility for logged-in buyers

### Cross-Module

- [ ] **B2B orders use same MSI flow** as B2C: no separate inventory path
- [ ] **Live Search respects Shared Catalog** for logged-in B2B company users
- [ ] **B2B tables syncable to BI**: quotes, companies, purchase orders (not default; requires setup)

---

*Study notes generated for Adobe Commerce Professional Certification — Week 3, Practice Test #3 Review*
*Focus: Section 4 — Add-on Modules (B2B, MSI, BI, Live Search)*

flashcards.question: What is the correct sequence for the canonical B2B customer journey?
flashcards.answer: Company Account Created > Company Admin Assigns Roles & Users > Admin Assigns Shared Catalog to Company > Buyer Browses Catalog > Buyer Creates Cart > Requests Negotiable Quote > Sales Rep Negotiates > Buyer Accepts > Converts to Order > PO Approval (if enabled) > Order Placed.
flashcards.hint: Company first, then catalog, then negotiation, then order — always in that dependency order.

flashcards.question: In MSI, what is the complete reservation lifecycle from cart to shipment?
flashcards.answer: Cart = NO reservation. Order placed = negative reservation created (-qty). Order shipped = source item qty decremented AND compensation reservation (+qty) inserted. Order canceled = compensation reservation (+qty) inserted, source qty unchanged. Credit memo with return to stock = compensation reservation (+qty).
flashcards.hint: Cart is free, order commits, ship deducts physically and compensates the reservation.

flashcards.question: Does Live Search use Elasticsearch for storefront search queries?
flashcards.answer: No. Live Search uses Adobe's proprietary SaaS search index powered by Adobe Sensei. Elasticsearch/OpenSearch is bypassed for customer-facing search queries. However, ES/OS still remains installed and is used for catalog indexing and admin-side search.
flashcards.hint: The SaaS service handles the customer-facing search; the local engine handles backend indexing.

flashcards.question: Which GraphQL query does Live Search use — 'products' or 'productSearch'?
flashcards.answer: Live Search uses the 'productSearch' GraphQL query, NOT the native 'products' query. This is an important distinction for integrations — using the wrong query endpoint will bypass Live Search and fall back to native search.
flashcards.hint: The query name explicitly includes 'Search' in its name.

flashcards.question: What is the relationship between Shared Catalog pricing and the tier_price database table?
flashcards.answer: Shared Catalog pricing is stored in the catalog_product_entity_tier_price table — the same table used for standard tier prices. The auto-created customer group for each Shared Catalog is the mechanism by which prices are differentiated and applied. This is not a separate pricing table.
flashcards.hint: Same table, different customer group IDs — the catalog wraps existing infrastructure.

flashcards.question: What happens when a disabled MSI source is part of a stock's source assignments?
flashcards.answer: A disabled source is excluded from BOTH SSA recommendations AND Salable Quantity calculations. The inventory data is preserved but does not count toward what customers can buy. To restore availability, either re-enable the source or reassign its inventory to another enabled source.
flashcards.hint: Disabled means invisible to sales AND to quantity calculations — a double exclusion.

flashcards.question: Does a Negotiable Quote bypass the standard checkout process?
flashcards.answer: No. A Negotiable Quote does NOT bypass checkout. When the buyer accepts the quote, the cart is pre-populated with quote items at negotiated prices, and the buyer still completes the standard checkout process (address selection, payment method). The quote merely locks in the prices.
flashcards.hint: The quote sets the prices, but the buyer still walks through the full checkout steps.

flashcards.question: How many Purchase Order statuses exist in Adobe Commerce B2B?
flashcards.answer: There are 9 PO statuses: Pending, Approval Required, Approved, Approved Pending Payment, Order in Progress, Order Placed, Order Failed, Rejected, and Canceled. 'Converted' is NOT a valid status — the final positive state is 'Order Placed'.
flashcards.hint: Nine statuses track the full lifecycle from submission through payment and order conversion.

flashcards.question: For Live Search facets to appear, what two conditions must be met?
flashcards.answer: The product attribute must be set to 'Use in Layered Navigation: Filterable (with results)' in the attribute configuration AND the attribute must be synced to the Live Search SaaS service. Both conditions must be met — having only one is not sufficient.
flashcards.hint: Two gates: attribute configuration AND SaaS data synchronization.

flashcards.question: Does Live Search respect Shared Catalog visibility for B2B users?
flashcards.answer: Yes. Live Search respects customer group and Shared Catalog restrictions for logged-in B2B company users. Products NOT in a company's Shared Catalog are excluded from Live Search results for that company's buyers. Anonymous users see the public catalog.
flashcards.hint: The SaaS search service honors the same visibility rules as the on-premise catalog.

flashcards.question: What approximate percentage of the AD0-E708 exam covers add-on modules (B2B, MSI, BI, Live Search)?
flashcards.answer: Add-on modules represent approximately 18-22% of the exam — making it the single largest optional-feature block. The exam focuses on scenario-based questions about correct sequences, reservation events, pre-built vs custom metrics, and search indexing behavior.
flashcards.hint: Nearly one-fifth of the exam focuses on these enterprise features.

flashcards.question: What are the key B2B BI metrics that can be tracked when B2B tables are synced to the BI Data Warehouse?
flashcards.answer: Key B2B BI metrics include Quote-to-Order conversion rate, Average Negotiation Cycles, and PO approval time. These require syncing B2B-specific tables (quotes, companies, purchase orders) to the BI Data Warehouse — this is not configured by default and requires manual setup.
flashcards.hint: Three metrics track the efficiency of B2B sales processes from quote to fulfillment.

flashcards.question: Do B2B orders follow the same MSI reservation flow as B2C orders?
flashcards.answer: Yes. B2B orders go through the exact same MSI reservation flow as B2C orders — there is no separate B2B inventory path. Order placement creates a negative reservation, shipment decrements source qty and creates compensation, cancellation creates compensation without changing source qty.
flashcards.hint: The inventory system is channel-agnostic — B2B and B2C are treated identically.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Requisition Lists and Wish Lists in Adobe Commerce?
flashcards.answer: Requisition Lists are a B2B feature designed for repeat business purchasing — they support multiple named lists per buyer (up to 999), are private per buyer, and items are copied (not moved) to cart. Wish Lists are a B2C feature with different functionality and purpose.
flashcards.hint: One is for systematic business reordering; the other is for consumer product bookmarking.

flashcards.question: What CLI commands are available for diagnosing MSI reservation issues?
flashcards.answer: Two key commands: 'bin/magento inventory:reservation:list-inconsistencies' checks for reservation discrepancies, and 'bin/magento inventory:reservation:create-compensations' creates compensating reservations to fix those inconsistencies. These are needed when orders are manipulated outside of Magento.
flashcards.hint: One diagnoses; the other fixes — both deal with reservation balance problems.

studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2 Compliance: Roles, Permissions & Security
## Study Notes — Week 4: Systems Architecture, Compliance & Final Prep

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Admin Roles & Permissions](#1-admin-roles--permissions)
2. [Admin Users & Security Settings](#2-admin-users--security-settings)
3. [Customer Groups](#3-customer-groups)
4. [GDPR Compliance](#4-gdpr-compliance)
5. [PCI DSS Compliance](#5-pci-dss-compliance)
6. [Common Security Aspects](#6-common-security-aspects)
7. [Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)](#7-accessibility-wcag-21-aa)
8. [Tricky Exam Concepts](#8-tricky-exam-concepts)
9. [Hands-On: Creating a Restricted Admin Role (EE)](#9-hands-on-creating-a-restricted-admin-role-ee)
10. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Admin Roles & Permissions

### 1.1 Overview

Magento 2 uses a **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)** system to restrict admin users to only the areas and actions they need. This is configured under:

```
System > Permissions > User Roles
```

Each role contains a **Resource Tree** — a hierarchical list of every admin capability in the system. Access can be granted or denied at **any node level** in that tree.

---

### 1.2 The Resource Tree

The resource tree is a nested hierarchy. In the admin UI, selecting or deselecting a parent node **automatically cascades to all child nodes** — checking a parent selects all its children, and unchecking a parent deselects all its children (implemented via `_selectChildNodes` / `_deselectChildNodes` in `roles-tree.js`).

```
Admin Resources
|
+-- Dashboard
+-- Sales
|   +-- Orders
|   |   +-- View
|   |   +-- Edit
|   |   +-- Cancel
|   +-- Invoices
|   +-- Shipments
+-- Catalog
|   +-- Products
|   +-- Categories
+-- Customers
+-- Marketing
+-- Content
+-- Reports
+-- Stores
+-- System
    +-- Permissions
        +-- User Roles
        +-- Users
```

**Exam focus:**
- The resource tree is defined in each module's `acl.xml` file
- Selecting **"All"** as Resource Access grants full super admin access
- Selecting a parent node **automatically selects all child nodes** in the UI
- Deselecting a parent node **automatically deselects all child nodes** in the UI
- To grant access to a child without its parent's other children, you must manually check only the specific nodes you want

> **Note:** Although the UI cascades changes, the database stores individual allow/deny permissions per resource (each resource gets its own row in `authorization_rule`). This means the permission check at runtime evaluates each resource independently.

---

### 1.3 acl.xml — How Resources Are Declared

Each module declares its ACL resources in:

```
app/code/Vendor/Module/etc/acl.xml
```

Example structure:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Acl/etc/acl.xsd">
    <acl>
        <resources>
            <resource id="Magento_Backend::admin">
                <resource id="Magento_Catalog::catalog">
                    <resource id="Magento_Catalog::catalog_inventory"
                              title="Inventory"
                              sortOrder="50" />
                    <resource id="Magento_Catalog::products"
                              title="Products"
                              sortOrder="10">
                        <resource id="Magento_Catalog::products_attributes"
                                  title="Product Attributes"
                                  sortOrder="10" />
                    </resource>
                </resource>
            </resource>
        </resources>
    </acl>
</config>
```

**Exam focus:**
- Every ACL resource must be a child of `Magento_Backend::admin`
- The top-level ACL also includes `Magento_Backend::all` (title "Allow everything") above `Magento_Backend::admin`
- The `id` attribute is the unique identifier used in PHP checks
- `sortOrder` controls display order in the UI tree

---

### 1.4 Checking Permissions in PHP

```php
<?php
// In a controller
use Magento\Framework\AuthorizationInterface;

class MyController extends \Magento\Backend\App\Action
{
    /**
     * ACL resource constant — matches acl.xml resource id
     */
    const ADMIN_RESOURCE = 'Magento_Catalog::products';

    public function execute()
    {
        // isAllowed() uses the ADMIN_RESOURCE constant
        if (!$this->_isAllowed()) {
            // Magento will redirect to 403 page
        }
        // ... controller logic
    }
}
```

```php
<?php
// Programmatic check anywhere
/** @var AuthorizationInterface $authorization */
$isAllowed = $this->_authorization->isAllowed('Magento_Catalog::products');
```

**Exam focus:**
- `const ADMIN_RESOURCE` in a controller is what Magento uses to auto-check access
- If `ADMIN_RESOURCE` is not overridden, the default value `Magento_Backend::admin` from `AbstractAction.php` is used — which means **all** authenticated admin users can access it (since every admin user has the base `admin` resource)

---

### 1.5 Role Configuration in Admin UI

**Path:** `System > Permissions > User Roles`

Steps to create a role:
1. Click **Add New Role**
2. Enter **Role Name**
3. Enter **Current Admin Password** (security verification)
4. Click **Role Resources** tab
5. Set **Resource Access** to:
   - `All` — grants everything (super admin)
   - `Custom` — manually select specific resources
6. Check/uncheck individual resource nodes
7. Click **Save Role**

```
Role Information Tab:
  - Role Name: "Catalog Manager"
  - Current User Identity Verification: [password]

Role Resources Tab:
  - Resource Access: [Custom v]
  - [ ] All
    [ ] Dashboard
    [x] Catalog
      [x] Products
        [ ] Product Attributes
      [x] Categories
    [ ] Sales
    [ ] Customers
    ...
```

**Exam focus:**
- Setting **Resource Access = All** gives the role access to every resource = **super admin equivalent**
- The password field on role save is required for identity verification
- Roles apply to multiple users; changing a role affects **all users assigned to it**

---

## 2. Admin Users & Security Settings

### 2.1 Creating & Managing Admin Users

**Path:** `System > Permissions > All Users`

Key fields when creating an admin user:
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| User Name | Unique login username |
| First / Last Name | Display name |
| Email | Must be unique |
| Password | Must meet complexity requirements |
| Interface Locale | Language for admin UI |
| This Account is | Active / Inactive |
| User Role | Assign one role |

**Exam focus:**
- An admin user can only be assigned **one role**
- Setting the account to **Inactive** immediately revokes access without deleting the user
- The user's assigned role can be changed at any time

---

### 2.2 Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)

**Introduced in Magento 2.4.x** — 2FA is **required** and **cannot be disabled** via the admin UI in 2.4+.

**Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Security > 2FA`

Supported 2FA providers:
| Provider | Type |
|----------|------|
| Google Authenticator | TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) |
| Duo Security | Push/SMS/TOTP |
| Authy | TOTP |
| U2F (Yubikey and others) | Hardware key |

**Exam focus:**
- 2FA is **mandatory in Magento 2.4.x** — it ships enabled by default
- Each admin user configures their **own** 2FA device on first login
- 2FA can be disabled only via **CLI** (for development only, not recommended in production):

```bash
# Disable 2FA for development (NOT for production)
bin/magento module:disable Magento_TwoFactorAuth

# Reset 2FA for a specific user (if they lost their device)
bin/magento security:tfa:reset <username> <provider>

# Example: reset Google Authenticator for admin user
bin/magento security:tfa:reset admin google
```

- If a user loses their 2FA device, an admin with appropriate permissions can reset it via CLI

---

### 2.3 Admin Access Restrictions

Admin panel access can be restricted at the **web server level** (nginx/Apache configuration) to limit by IP address. This is the recommended approach for production environments.

> **Note:** Magento does NOT have an "Allow IPs" field under Admin > Security for admin panel access. The `dev/restrict/allow_ips` field under **Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Developer > Developer Client Restrictions** (`module-developer`) restricts access to **developer tools** (debug output, profiler, etc.), not the admin panel itself. Admin panel IP restriction should be configured at the web server level.

- Can also be configured via custom admin URL for layered security
- Often combined with custom admin URL (see Section 6.1)

**Exam focus:**
- IP restriction for admin panel = **web server configuration** (not a Magento admin setting)
- Developer IP restriction = Stores > Config > Advanced > Developer > Developer Client Restrictions
- Often combined with custom admin URL for layered security

---

### 2.4 Admin Security Configuration

**Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Admin > Security`

Fields from `module-backend/etc/adminhtml/system.xml` (admin section, security group):

| Setting | Field ID | Description |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| Recovery Link Expiration Period (hours) | `password_reset_link_expiration_period` | Time before password reset link expires |
| Add Secret Key to URLs | `use_form_key` | CSRF protection token in admin URLs |
| Login is Case Sensitive | `use_case_sensitive_login` | Username case sensitivity |
| Admin Session Lifetime (seconds) | `session_lifetime` | Session expiry (min 60, max 31536000) |

Additional fields from `module-user/etc/adminhtml/system.xml` (same group):

| Setting | Field ID | Description |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| Maximum Login Failures to Lockout Account | `lockout_failures` | Lockout threshold |
| Lockout Time (minutes) | `lockout_threshold` | Duration of lockout after failures |
| Password Lifetime (days) | `password_lifetime` | Force password change after N days |
| Password Change | `password_is_forced` | When to force password changes |

> **Note:** Admin password **complexity** requirements (minimum length, character classes) are enforced in code, not via separate admin config toggles. There are no individual "Password Requires Numeric" / "Password Requires Special Character" fields for admin passwords. For **customer** passwords, those settings exist under Customers > Customer Configuration > Password Options (`minimum_password_length`, `required_character_classes_number`).

---

## 3. Customer Groups

### 3.1 Default Customer Groups

Magento 2 ships with four default customer groups:

| Group ID | Group Name | Description |
|----------|------------|-------------|
| 0 | NOT LOGGED IN | Guest visitors (no account or not signed in) |
| 1 | General | Default group for registered customers |
| 2 | Wholesale | B2B wholesale buyers |
| 3 | Retailer | Retail business buyers |

**Exam focus:**
- Group ID `0` = **NOT LOGGED IN** — this is the guest group, always present
- **NOT LOGGED IN** cannot be deleted
- **General** is the default group assigned to new customer registrations
- Custom groups can be created (especially relevant in B2B/EE scenarios)

---

### 3.2 What Customer Groups Affect

Customer groups are a **central segmentation mechanism** that influence:

```
Customer Group
      |
      +-- Pricing (Tier Prices / Group Prices)
      |
      +-- Tax Class Assignment
      |
      +-- Shipping Method Availability
      |
      +-- Catalog Price Rules
      |
      +-- Cart Price Rules (Promotions)
      |
      +-- Customer Segments (EE only)
      |
      +-- Shared Catalogs (B2B EE)
```

#### Pricing
- **Tier prices** can be set per customer group on a product
- **Catalog Price Rules** can target specific groups
- B2B **Shared Catalogs** (EE) are linked to customer groups

#### Tax
- Each customer group has a **Tax Class** assigned
- Different groups can be taxed differently (e.g., Wholesale = tax-exempt)

```
Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration
  Default Group: [General v]

Customers > Customer Groups
  - Group Name: Wholesale
  - Tax Class: [Tax Exempt v]
```

> **Note:** Customer Groups are managed at **Customers > Customer Groups** (parent=`Magento_Customer::customer`), NOT under "Stores > Other Settings".

#### Shipping
- Some shipping methods can be restricted to certain customer groups via extensions
- Cart price rules (free shipping) can target groups

#### Promotions
- Cart price rules: "Customer Group is one of: [Wholesale, Retailer]"
- Catalog price rules: target specific groups for discounts

**Exam focus:**
- Customer groups affect: **pricing, shipping, tax classes, promotions** — know all four
- The group is evaluated at **cart/checkout time** for tax and shipping
- Changing a customer's group immediately affects their next session's pricing

---

### 3.3 Assigning Customers to Groups

Manually: `Customers > All Customers > Edit Customer > Account Information > Group`

> **Note:** Customer Segments (EE) do **not** auto-assign customers to customer groups. Segments are a separate targeting mechanism used for promotions, dynamic blocks, and reports — they group customers by behavior/conditions but do not change the customer's actual group assignment.

## 4. GDPR Compliance

### 4.1 Overview

The **General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)** applies to merchants selling to EU customers. Magento 2 (2.3.1+) includes built-in GDPR features.

**Key GDPR rights relevant to Magento:**

| Right | Description | Magento Implementation |
|-------|-------------|----------------------|
| Right to Erasure ("Right to be Forgotten") | Customer can request deletion of personal data | Anonymize customer data (not delete orders) |
| Right to Data Portability | Customer can request export of their data | Export customer data as CSV/JSON |
| Right to Access | Customer can view their personal data | My Account dashboard |
| Consent | Cookie consent, marketing opt-in | Cookie consent popup, newsletter opt-in |

---

### 4.2 Right to Erasure — Critical Exam Concept

> **IMPORTANT:** Right to erasure does **NOT** mean deleting order records. Orders must be **retained for legal/financial compliance**. Instead, Magento **anonymizes** the personal data associated with orders.

**What happens during erasure:**
- Customer account is **deleted**
- Personal data (name, email, address) in order records is **replaced with anonymized values** (e.g., "Anonymized", random hash)
- Order records themselves are **preserved** (required by accounting/tax law)
- Customer's **wishlist, reviews, and other data** are deleted

**Path:** `Customers > All Customers > Select Customer > Delete`

Or via customer's own request through the Privacy Policy page / My Account.

```
Before Erasure:
  Order #100001
    Customer: John Doe
    Email: john@example.com
    Address: 123 Main St, New York

After Erasure:
  Order #100001
    Customer: Anonymized
    Email: anon_5f4d8a3b2c@example.com
    Address: [Anonymized]
```

**Exam focus:**
- **GDPR right to erasure = ANONYMIZE order history, NOT delete it**
- This is a very common exam trap — "delete" is wrong
- Order records must be kept for legal/tax/financial compliance
- The customer account itself IS deleted; only order associations are anonymized

---

### 4.3 Data Export Request

Customers can request a copy of their data:

**Customer-facing:** My Account > Privacy Settings > Export Personal Data

**Admin-facing:** `Customers > All Customers > Export` or individual customer record

Exported data includes:
- Profile information
- Order history
- Addresses
- Wishlist items
- Product reviews
- Newsletter subscriptions

**Exam focus:**
- Data export is built into Magento 2.3.1+ natively
- Export format is typically **CSV**

---

### 4.4 Cookie Consent

Magento 2 includes a cookie consent notification:

**Path:** `Stores > Configuration > General > Web > Default Cookie Settings`

| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Cookie Lifetime | Seconds before cookie expires |
| Cookie Path | Path restriction for cookies |
| Cookie Domain | Domain restriction |
| Use HTTP Only | Prevent JS access to cookies |
| Cookie Restriction Mode | Enable/disable consent banner |

**Path for Cookie Restriction Mode:** `Stores > Configuration > General > Web > Default Cookie Settings > Cookie Restriction Mode = Yes`

When enabled:
- A banner appears notifying users of cookie usage
- Non-essential cookies are blocked until user consents
- Consent is stored as a cookie itself

**Exam focus:**
- Cookie Restriction Mode = **Yes** enables GDPR-compliant cookie consent
- When enabled, Magento blocks non-essential cookies until consent given

---

### 4.5 Privacy Policy CMS Page

**Requirement:** Magento requires a **Privacy Policy CMS page** to be configured.

**Path:** `Stores > Configuration > General > Store Information`

Or the CMS page:
- **Default identifier:** `privacy-policy-cookie-restriction-mode`
- **Page title:** Privacy and Cookie Policy

Magento links this page in:
- Cookie consent notification banner
- Customer registration form ("I agree to the Privacy Policy")
- Footer links

**Exam focus:**
- Privacy Policy page is a **CMS page** — not a static file
- It is required for GDPR cookie consent implementation
- The default CMS page identifier is `privacy-policy-cookie-restriction-mode`
- Must be linked from cookie consent banner

---

### 4.6 GDPR Features in Magento

> **Note:** There is no dedicated "Privacy" configuration section under Customers > Customer Configuration in the base Adobe Commerce 2.4.8-p3 codebase. GDPR compliance features (customer data deletion, export) are implemented as admin actions and customer account pages rather than through a central config toggle. Customer deletion (which triggers order data anonymization) is available via the standard Customers > All Customers > Delete action. Privacy-related customer account pages may be provided by additional extensions or Adobe Commerce Cloud features.

## 5. PCI DSS Compliance

### 5.1 Overview

**PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard)** is a security standard for merchants handling cardholder data. Key principle: **minimize cardholder data storage**.

---

### 5.2 Never Store CVV

> **RULE:** CVV/CVC codes must **NEVER** be stored — not in the database, not in logs, not in session.

This is a fundamental PCI DSS requirement (Requirement 3.2):
- CVV is the 3-4 digit security code on a card
- Must only be used for authorization, then discarded
- Magento's payment modules are designed to never persist CVV

**Exam focus:**
- Storing CVV = **immediate PCI DSS violation**
- Not even temporarily in a database field
- Logs must also never capture CVV

---

### 5.3 Tokenization (Vault)

Instead of storing card numbers, Magento uses **tokenization**:

```
Customer enters card number
         |
         v
Payment Gateway processes card
         |
         v
Gateway returns TOKEN (e.g., "tok_abc123xyz")
         |
         v
Magento stores TOKEN only (not card number)
         |
         v
Future purchases use token — card never re-entered
```

**Magento Vault** is the built-in tokenization system:

**Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > [Provider] > Vault`

```xml
<!-- Vault configuration in payment method config -->
<vault>
    <config_path>payment/braintree_cc_vault</config_path>
</vault>
```

**How Vault works:**
1. Customer pays and opts to "Save this card"
2. Gateway tokenizes the card and returns a payment token
3. Token is stored in `vault_payment_token` table
4. On future checkout, customer selects saved card
5. Magento sends token to gateway — no card data touches Magento servers

**Exam focus:**
- **Tokenization** = store a gateway-issued token, never the actual card number
- **Vault** = Magento's implementation of tokenization for saved payment methods
- Token has no value outside the gateway — cannot be reversed to get card number
- This is the PCI-compliant way to enable "saved cards" functionality

---

### 5.4 HTTPS Everywhere

**All** pages must use HTTPS in production — not just checkout:

**Path:** `Stores > Configuration > General > Web`

```
Secure > Base URL: https://www.example.com/
Secure > Use Secure URLs on Storefront: Yes
Secure > Use Secure URLs in Admin: Yes
Secure > Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS): Yes
Secure > Upgrade Insecure Requests: Yes
```

**Exam focus:**
- HTTPS must be enabled for **both storefront AND admin**
- HSTS prevents SSL-stripping attacks
- Setting **Upgrade Insecure Requests = Yes** auto-upgrades HTTP to HTTPS

---

### 5.5 TLS 1.2+ Only

Magento 2.4.x requires **TLS 1.2 or higher** for all connections:

- TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are deprecated and insecure
- PCI DSS requires TLS 1.2+ as of June 2018
- This applies to: storefront, admin, API connections, payment gateway connections

**Server configuration (nginx example):**

```bash
# /etc/nginx/nginx.conf or site config
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
ssl_ciphers ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA512:DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA512:...;
ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on;
```

**Exam focus:**
- Magento 2.4.x requires TLS **1.2 minimum**
- TLS 1.3 is supported and preferred
- TLS 1.0/1.1 must be **disabled** on the server

---

### 5.6 PCI DSS Summary Checklist

| Requirement | Magento Implementation |
|-------------|----------------------|
| Never store CVV | Payment modules don't persist CVV |
| Don't store PANs (card numbers) | Use Vault/tokenization |
| Encrypt cardholder data | HTTPS everywhere |
| Use strong cryptography | TLS 1.2+, no weak ciphers |
| Restrict access to cardholder data | Admin RBAC, web server IP restriction |
| Log and monitor access | Admin action logs (EE) |
| Vulnerability management | Regular patches, security updates |

## 6. Common Security Aspects

### 6.1 Custom Admin URL

Moving the admin away from `/admin` reduces automated attack surface:

**Method 1: Installation**
```bash
bin/magento setup:install --backend-frontname="secret_admin_path"
```

**Method 2: env.php**
```php
<?php
// app/etc/env.php
return [
    'backend' => [
        'frontName' => 'your_secret_admin_path'
    ],
    // ...
];
```

**Method 3: Admin UI**
```
Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Admin > Admin Base URL
  Use Custom Admin URL: Yes
  Custom Admin URL: https://www.example.com/your_secret_path/
  Use Custom Admin Path: Yes
  Custom Admin Path: your_secret_path
```

**Exam focus:**
- Custom admin URL is a **security through obscurity** measure — not a replacement for other security
- Stored in `env.php` under `backend > frontName`
- Changing requires cache flush: `bin/magento cache:flush`

---

### 6.2 Strong Password Policy

**Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration > Password Options`

For **Customer passwords**, configurable fields include:
- `minimum_password_length` — Minimum Password Length
- `required_character_classes_number` — Required Character Classes (number of different character types required)
- `lockout_failures` — Maximum Login Failures to Lockout Account
- `lockout_threshold` — Lockout Time (minutes)

For **Admin passwords** (`Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Admin > Security`):

| Setting | Field ID | Notes |
|---------|----------|-------|
| Password Lifetime (days) | `password_lifetime` | Force password change after N days |
| Password Change | `password_is_forced` | When password change is forced |
| Maximum Login Failures | `lockout_failures` | Lockout threshold |
| Lockout Time (minutes) | `lockout_threshold` | Duration of lockout |

> **Note:** Admin password complexity requirements (minimum length, character classes) are enforced in application code, not via separate admin configuration fields. Unlike customer passwords, there are no configurable "Minimum Password Length" or "Required Character Classes" settings for admin users in the admin panel.

---

### 6.3 Login Attempt Limits

**Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Admin > Security`

```
Maximum Login Failures to Lockout Account: 6
Lockout Time (minutes): 30
```

For customer logins:
**Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration > Password Options`

```
Maximum Login Failures to Lockout Account: [configurable]
Lockout Time (minutes): [configurable]
```

**Exam focus:**
- Admin lockout: configurable maximum failures before lockout
- Locked admin accounts can be unlocked via CLI:

```bash
# Unlock a locked admin account
bin/magento admin:user:unlock <username>
```

---

### 6.4 reCAPTCHA

Magento 2.4.x includes built-in Google reCAPTCHA integration:

**Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Security > Google reCAPTCHA Storefront`
**Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Security > Google reCAPTCHA Admin Panel`

**reCAPTCHA versions:**
| Version | Type | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| reCAPTCHA v2 Checkbox | "I'm not a robot" checkbox | User interaction required |
| reCAPTCHA v2 Invisible | Background check | No user interaction |
| reCAPTCHA v3 | Score-based | No user interaction, risk score |
| Invisible reCAPTCHA (v2 badge) | Badge style | No interaction |

**Forms that can be protected:**

*Storefront:*
- Customer Login
- Create Account
- Forgot Password
- Contact Us
- Product Review
- Newsletter Subscription
- **Checkout** (Place Order)
- PayPal PayflowPro (additional checkout protection)

*Admin Panel:*
- Admin Login form
- Forgot Password form

**Exam focus:**
- reCAPTCHA is available on **both storefront AND admin login** in 2.4.x
- Must configure API keys from Google reCAPTCHA console
- Different reCAPTCHA types can be used for different forms
- Important for preventing brute force and spam

---

### 6.5 Security.txt

Magento 2.4.x supports `security.txt` — a standard file that tells security researchers how to report vulnerabilities:

**Path:** `Stores > Configuration > Security > Security.txt`

> **Note:** Security.txt has its own section directly under the Security tab (section ID: `magento_securitytxt_securitytxt`). It is NOT nested under a "Miscellaneous" subsection. The section contains groups for General settings, Contact Information, and Other Information.

## 7. Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)

### 7.1 Overview

**WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) 2.1 Level AA** is the standard Magento themes aim to comply with. This ensures the storefront is usable by people with disabilities.

The four WCAG principles (**POUR**):
- **P**erceivable
- **O**perable
- **U**nderstandable
- **R**obust

---

### 7.2 Key Accessibility Requirements

#### Alt Text on Images

```html
<!-- Correct: descriptive alt text -->
<img src="red-dress.jpg" alt="Women's red floral maxi dress, size S-XL" />

<!-- Correct: decorative image (empty alt) -->
<img src="decorative-divider.jpg" alt="" role="presentation" />

<!-- WRONG: missing alt text -->
<img src="product.jpg" />

<!-- WRONG: non-descriptive alt text -->
<img src="product.jpg" alt="image" />
```

In Magento Admin, alt text for product images:
```
Catalog > Products > [Edit Product] > Images and Videos
  Each image has an "Alt Text" field
```

**Exam focus:**
- Every meaningful image **must** have descriptive alt text
- Decorative images should have `alt=""` (empty, not missing)
- Magento's product image alt text can be set per image in the product editor

---

#### Keyboard Navigation

All interactive elements must be reachable and operable via keyboard:

- `Tab` key to navigate between elements
- `Enter`/`Space` to activate buttons and links
- `Arrow keys` for dropdown menus and sliders
- `Escape` to close modals/popups
- **Focus indicators** must be visible (outline on focused elements)

**Exam focus:**
- No interactive element should be **keyboard-inaccessible**
- Focus order must be **logical** (top-to-bottom, left-to-right typically)
- Custom JS components must maintain keyboard accessibility

---

#### Color Contrast

WCAG 2.1 AA contrast requirements:

| Text Size | Minimum Contrast Ratio |
|-----------|----------------------|
| Normal text (< 18pt / < 14pt bold) | **4.5:1** |
| Large text (>= 18pt / >= 14pt bold) | **3:1** |
| UI components and graphical objects | **3:1** |

```css
/* Example: Ensure sufficient contrast */
/* White (#FFFFFF) on Magento orange (#EB5202) */
/* Contrast ratio: ~3.4:1 - FAILS for normal text! */

/* Better: White on dark orange (#B34000) */
/* Contrast ratio: ~5.8:1 - PASSES */

.btn-primary {
    background-color: #B34000;
    color: #FFFFFF;
}
```

**Exam focus:**
- Normal text requires **4.5:1** contrast ratio minimum (AA)
- Large text requires **3:1** minimum (AA)
- This is a common exam question — know both ratios

---

#### ARIA Labels

**ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications)** attributes provide semantic meaning to screen readers:

```html
<!-- aria-label: provides accessible name -->
<button aria-label="Close dialog">X</button>

<!-- aria-labelledby: references another element's text -->
<div role="dialog" aria-labelledby="dialog-title">
    <h2 id="dialog-title">Confirm Order</h2>
    ...
</div>

<!-- aria-describedby: additional description -->
<input type="password"
       aria-describedby="password-help"
       id="password" />
<span id="password-help">
    Must be at least 8 characters with one number.
</span>

<!-- aria-required: marks required fields -->
<input type="email"
       aria-required="true"
       required
       placeholder="Email address" />

<!-- aria-live: announce dynamic content changes -->
<div aria-live="polite" id="cart-count">
    3 items in cart
</div>

<!-- role: semantic role for custom elements -->
<div role="navigation" aria-label="Main Navigation">
    <!-- nav items -->
</div>
```

**Exam focus:**
- `aria-label` = provides accessible name when visible text is absent/insufficient
- `aria-labelledby` = references visible text by ID as the accessible name
- `aria-live` = announces dynamic content changes to screen readers
- `role` = defines semantic purpose of custom/non-semantic elements

---

### 7.3 Magento's Accessibility Features

Magento's Luma and Blank themes include:

- **Skip to main content** link (keyboard bypass for repetitive navigation)
- Semantic HTML5 elements (`<nav>`, `<main>`, `<header>`, `<footer>`, `<article>`)
- Form labels associated with inputs via `for`/`id`
- ARIA attributes on interactive components (modals, tabs, dropdowns)
- Focus management in modal dialogs

---

### 7.4 WCAG 2.1 AA Quick Reference

| Requirement | Level | Description |
|-------------|-------|-------------|
| Alt text for images | A | All non-decorative images need alt text |
| Keyboard accessible | A | All functionality via keyboard |
| No keyboard trap | A | User can navigate away from any component |
| Captions for video | A | Pre-recorded video needs captions |
| Color not only means | A | Don't use color alone to convey info |
| Focus visible | AA | Keyboard focus indicator must be visible |
| Color contrast 4.5:1 | AA | Normal text contrast requirement |
| Color contrast 3:1 | AA | Large text contrast requirement |
| Resize text 200% | AA | Text resizable to 200% without content loss |
| Language of page | A | `<html lang="en">` attribute required |

## 8. Tricky Exam Concepts

### 8.1 "All" Resource Access = Super Admin

> Setting a role's **Resource Access to "All"** is equivalent to granting **super admin** permissions — the user can do everything any other admin can do, including managing other users and roles.

```
Role Resources Tab:
  Resource Access: [All v]

  Result: User can access EVERY admin feature,
          including User Roles and creating other admins
```

**Exam focus:**
- A user with "All" resources is functionally a **super admin**
- They can create/modify other admin users and roles
- This should be reserved for only the most trusted administrators
- The actual Magento "owner" account (ID=1) always has full access regardless of role

---

### 8.2 Resource Tree Parent-Child Cascading

> In the admin UI, checking or unchecking a parent resource **automatically cascades** to all child resources. This is implemented via JavaScript (`roles-tree.js`) — `_selectChildNodes` selects all children when a parent is checked, and `_deselectChildNodes` deselects all children when a parent is unchecked.

**Example scenario:**

```
Initial Role Setup:
  [x] Catalog
    [x] Products
      [x] Product Attributes
    [x] Categories

Admin unchecks "Catalog":
  [ ] Catalog
    [ ] Products           <-- Auto-unchecked by UI
      [ ] Product Attributes  <-- Auto-unchecked by UI
    [ ] Categories         <-- Auto-unchecked by UI

Result: User loses access to Products and Categories
```

**The correct behavior:**
- Unchecking a parent **automatically unchecks** all child resources in the UI
- Checking a parent **automatically checks** all child resources in the UI
- To grant only specific children, first check the parent (which checks all), then manually uncheck the children you don't want

**Exam focus:**
- The UI **cascades** parent selection/deselection to children
- Individual permissions are stored per resource in the database (`authorization_rule` table)
- The safest practice: switch to "Custom", then carefully select only the specific resources needed

---

### 8.3 GDPR Right to Erasure = Anonymize, NOT Delete Orders

> **Critical:** When a customer exercises their right to erasure, Magento **anonymizes** their personal data in order records. Orders are **NOT deleted**.

**Why orders are kept:**
- Financial/accounting legal requirements
- Tax compliance (must retain records for 7+ years in many jurisdictions)
- Fraud prevention history
- Legal disputes

**What gets anonymized:**
```
Order Record (before erasure):
  Customer Name: Jane Smith
  Email: jane@example.com
  Billing Address: 123 Oak Ave, Chicago, IL 60601

Order Record (after erasure):
  Customer Name: Anonymized1234
  Email: removed1234@example.com  (or hashed)
  Billing Address: [Address Removed]

  ** Order ID, items, totals, dates = PRESERVED **
```

**Exam focus:**
- Right to erasure = **anonymize personal data in orders** (name, email, address)
- Orders themselves (ID, items, amounts, dates) must be **retained**
- The customer account record IS deleted
- This is the most commonly misunderstood GDPR concept in Magento exams

---

### 8.4 Customer Group "NOT LOGGED IN" = Always ID 0

```php
<?php
// Customer group constants
\Magento\Customer\Model\Group::NOT_LOGGED_IN_ID  // = 0
\Magento\Customer\Model\Group::CUST_GROUP_ALL    // = 32000 (wildcard)
```

**Exam focus:**
- Group ID 0 = NOT LOGGED IN (guests)
- Any pricing/tax rule targeting "NOT LOGGED IN" applies to **all guest visitors**
- This group cannot be renamed or deleted

---

### 8.5 Privacy Policy is a CMS Page, Not a Config

The Privacy Policy is an actual **CMS page** in Magento's content management system. It is:
- Created/edited in `Content > Pages`
- Linked from cookie consent notification via its **identifier**
- Default identifier: `privacy-policy-cookie-restriction-mode`
- NOT a configuration value in Stores > Configuration

**Exam focus:**
- Privacy Policy = **CMS page** (editable content, not a system config)
- Default URL key: `privacy-policy-cookie-restriction-mode`

---

### 9.1 Scenario

Create an admin role called **"Catalog Manager"** that can only:
- View and edit Products
- View and edit Categories
- Cannot access: Sales, Customers, Marketing, Reports, System

```
Role Name: Catalog Manager
Current User Identity Verification: [your admin password]
```

```
Resource Access: [Custom v]  <-- Select "Custom"

Expand the resource tree and select ONLY:
[ ] All
  [ ] Dashboard            <-- Leave unchecked
  [x] Catalog
    [x] Products
      [ ] Product Attributes   <-- Optional: restrict further

    [x] Categories

  [ ] Sales                <-- Leave unchecked
  [ ] Customers            <-- Leave unchecked
  [ ] Marketing            <-- Leave unchecked
```

### 9.3 Verify the Role Works

1. Log out of admin

   - Cannot see Customers menu
   - Cannot access System > Permissions

### 9.4 CLI Equivalent Operations

```bash
# Create admin user (role must be assigned in UI or programmatically)
bin/magento admin:user:create \
  --admin-user="catalog_manager" \
```
