- [ ] Resource tree defined in each module's `acl.xml`
- [ ] Root resource: `Magento_Backend::admin` (with `Magento_Backend::all` above it)
- [ ] Resource Access = **"All"** -> super admin (access to everything)
- [ ] Resource Access = **"Custom"** -> manually select specific resources
- [ ] Checking/unchecking a parent resource **cascades** to all child resources in the UI
- [ ] Individual permissions stored per resource in `authorization_rule` table
- [ ] Admin user can only be assigned **one role**
- [ ] `const ADMIN_RESOURCE` in controller = what permission is required to access it
- [ ] Default `ADMIN_RESOURCE` = `Magento_Backend::admin` (all admin users can access)

### Admin Users & Security
- [ ] 2FA is **mandatory in Magento 2.4.x**, cannot be disabled via UI
- [ ] 2FA can only be disabled via CLI (dev only): `bin/magento module:disable Magento_TwoFactorAuth`
- [ ] Reset 2FA for user: `bin/magento security:tfa:reset <username> <provider>`
- [ ] Supported 2FA: Google Authenticator, Duo Security, Authy, U2F (Yubikey and others)
- [ ] Admin panel IP restriction = web server configuration (not a Magento admin setting)
- [ ] Developer IP restriction: Stores > Config > Advanced > Developer > Developer Client Restrictions
- [ ] Admin URL stored in `env.php` under `backend > frontName`
- [ ] Unlock locked account: `bin/magento admin:user:unlock <username>`
- [ ] No `admin:user:list` CLI command exists

### Customer Groups
- [ ] Four defaults: **NOT LOGGED IN (0)**, General (1), Wholesale (2), Retailer (3)
- [ ] NOT LOGGED IN = guest visitors, always Group ID **0**, cannot be deleted
- [ ] General = default group for new registrations
- [ ] Managed at: **Customers > Customer Groups** (NOT Stores > Other Settings)
- [ ] Groups affect: **pricing, tax classes, shipping, promotions** (all four)
- [ ] Changing group immediately affects next session's pricing/tax
- [ ] Customer Segments (EE) do NOT auto-assign to groups — different mechanism

### GDPR
- [ ] Right to erasure = **ANONYMIZE** order data, NOT delete orders
- [ ] Orders must be retained for legal/financial/tax compliance
- [ ] Customer account IS deleted; order personal data is anonymized
- [ ] Data export: customer can request CSV of their personal data
- [ ] Cookie consent: enable "Cookie Restriction Mode = Yes" in config
- [ ] Privacy Policy = **CMS page** (not a system config value)
- [ ] Default CMS page identifier: `privacy-policy-cookie-restriction-mode`
- [ ] GDPR features built into Magento 2.3.1+

### PCI DSS
- [ ] **NEVER store CVV** — immediate PCI violation
- [ ] Use **tokenization** (Vault) instead of storing card numbers
- [ ] Vault stores gateway-issued tokens in `vault_payment_token` table
- [ ] HTTPS required on **all pages** (not just checkout)
- [ ] Enable HSTS for SSL-stripping protection
- [ ] **TLS 1.2 minimum** required (TLS 1.0/1.1 must be disabled)
- [ ] TLS 1.3 is supported and preferred

### Security
- [ ] reCAPTCHA available on storefront forms AND admin login
- [ ] reCAPTCHA forms: login, registration, forgot password, checkout, contact, reviews, PayPal PayflowPro
- [ ] Maximum login failures -> account lockout (configurable)
- [ ] Custom admin URL = security through obscurity measure
- [ ] Admin password complexity enforced in code (not via admin config toggles)
- [ ] Customer password complexity: configurable via Password Options (minimum_password_length, required_character_classes_number)
- [ ] Security.txt: own section under Security tab (not under Miscellaneous)

### Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)
- [ ] All non-decorative images need **descriptive alt text**
- [ ] Decorative images: `alt=""` (empty, not missing)
- [ ] All functionality must be **keyboard accessible**
- [ ] Focus indicator must be **visible** for keyboard users
- [ ] Normal text contrast: **4.5:1 minimum**
- [ ] Large text contrast: **3:1 minimum** (>= 18pt or >= 14pt bold)
- [ ] UI components: **3:1 minimum** contrast
- [ ] `aria-label` = accessible name when visible text insufficient
- [ ] `aria-labelledby` = reference visible text as accessible name
- [ ] `aria-live` = announce dynamic content changes
- [ ] `role` attribute = define semantic purpose of custom elements
- [ ] `<html lang="en">` = language of page declaration required

### Tricky Concepts Summary
- [ ] **Super admin** = Role with Resource Access = "All"
- [ ] **Parent-child cascading** = UI auto-selects/deselects children (cascades)
- [ ] **GDPR erasure ≠ deleting orders** (anonymize, preserve order records)
- [ ] **Privacy Policy = CMS page**, not a configuration setting
- [ ] **NOT LOGGED IN group ID = 0** always
- [ ] **2FA mandatory in 2.4.x** (major version change from 2.3.x)
- [ ] **CVV must never be stored**, anywhere, ever

flashcards.question: What access control system does Magento 2 use to restrict admin users to specific areas and actions?
flashcards.answer: Magento 2 uses Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Each role contains a Resource Tree — a hierarchical list of every admin capability. Access is granted or denied at any node level in the tree, configured under System > Permissions > User Roles.
flashcards.hint: Think of the acronym that describes granting permissions based on job function.

flashcards.question: In which file does each Magento module declare its ACL resources for the admin resource tree?
flashcards.answer: Each module declares its ACL resources in etc/acl.xml. Every ACL resource must be a child of Magento_Backend::admin. The id attribute is the unique identifier used in PHP permission checks.
flashcards.hint: It is an XML file in the module's etc/ directory, named after the access control concept.

flashcards.question: What happens when you set a role's Resource Access to 'All' in the admin UI?
flashcards.answer: Setting Resource Access to 'All' grants the role access to every admin resource, making the user functionally a super admin. They can access all features including managing other admin users and roles.
flashcards.hint: It is the opposite of 'Custom' and grants the maximum possible access.

flashcards.question: How many admin roles can a single admin user be assigned in Magento 2?
flashcards.answer: An admin user can only be assigned one role. The user's assigned role can be changed at any time, and setting the account to Inactive immediately revokes access without deleting the user.
flashcards.hint: Unlike some systems, Magento does not support multiple role assignment per user.

flashcards.question: What is Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) status in Magento 2.4.x, and how can it be disabled?
flashcards.answer: 2FA is mandatory in Magento 2.4.x and cannot be disabled via the admin UI. It can only be disabled via CLI using 'bin/magento module:disable Magento_TwoFactorAuth', which is not recommended for production environments.
flashcards.hint: This was a major security change introduced in the 2.4 major version.

flashcards.question: What are the four default customer groups that ship with Magento 2, and which one cannot be deleted?
flashcards.answer: The four defaults are: NOT LOGGED IN (Group ID 0), General (ID 1), Wholesale (ID 2), and Retailer (ID 3). NOT LOGGED IN (Group ID 0) cannot be deleted and represents guest visitors.
flashcards.hint: Guest visitors always have a specific group ID that starts the numbering.

flashcards.question: What four areas do customer groups affect in Adobe Commerce?
flashcards.answer: Customer groups affect pricing (tier prices, group prices), tax class assignment, shipping method availability, and promotions (catalog and cart price rules). The group is evaluated at cart/checkout time for tax and shipping.
flashcards.hint: Think about what changes when a wholesale buyer vs a retail buyer shops.

flashcards.question: Under GDPR, what happens to order records when a customer exercises their right to erasure in Magento?
flashcards.answer: Order records are NOT deleted. Instead, Magento anonymizes the personal data (name, email, address) in order records while preserving the order itself. Orders must be retained for legal, financial, and tax compliance. The customer account itself IS deleted.
flashcards.hint: The key word is anonymize, not delete — financial records must be preserved.

flashcards.question: What is the Privacy Policy in Adobe Commerce — a configuration setting or a CMS page?
flashcards.answer: The Privacy Policy is a CMS page, not a system configuration value. It is created and edited in Content > Pages with the default identifier 'privacy-policy-cookie-restriction-mode'. It is linked from the cookie consent notification banner and the customer registration form.
flashcards.hint: Think about where merchants would edit the actual content of their privacy policy.

flashcards.question: Why must CVV/CVC codes never be stored in Magento, and what is the consequence of doing so?
flashcards.answer: Storing CVV is an immediate PCI DSS violation under Requirement 3.2. CVV must only be used for authorization and then discarded — not stored in the database, logs, or session. Magento's payment modules are designed to never persist CVV.
flashcards.hint: This is the strictest PCI DSS rule regarding cardholder data.

flashcards.question: What is Magento Vault, and how does it enable saved payment methods without storing card numbers?
flashcards.answer: Magento Vault is the built-in tokenization system. When a customer saves a card, the payment gateway processes it and returns a token. Magento stores only the token in the vault_payment_token table. Future purchases use this token — card data never touches Magento servers.
flashcards.hint: Think of it as a secure substitute that represents the card but has no value outside the gateway.

flashcards.question: What is the minimum TLS version required by Magento 2.4.x, and which versions must be disabled?
flashcards.answer: Magento 2.4.x requires TLS 1.2 as the minimum version. TLS 1.3 is supported and preferred. TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 must be disabled on the server, as required by PCI DSS since June 2018.
flashcards.hint: The required version matches the PCI DSS mandate from 2018.

flashcards.question: Where should admin panel IP restriction be configured in Magento — in the admin UI or at the web server level?
flashcards.answer: Admin panel IP restriction should be configured at the web server level (nginx/Apache), not in the Magento admin. The dev/restrict/allow_ips field in Stores > Configuration restricts access to developer tools only, not the admin panel itself.
flashcards.hint: Many people confuse the developer restriction setting with admin access restriction.

flashcards.question: What are the WCAG 2.1 AA minimum contrast ratios for normal text and large text?
flashcards.answer: Normal text (less than 18pt or less than 14pt bold) requires a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1. Large text (18pt or larger, or 14pt bold or larger) requires a minimum of 3:1. UI components also require 3:1.
flashcards.hint: The smaller the text, the higher the contrast ratio required.

flashcards.question: What does Cookie Restriction Mode do when enabled in Magento, and where is it configured?
flashcards.answer: When Cookie Restriction Mode is enabled (Stores > Configuration > General > Web > Default Cookie Settings), a consent banner appears and non-essential cookies are blocked until the user consents. Only essential cookies like session are allowed before consent.
flashcards.hint: It is the built-in GDPR cookie consent mechanism.

studyNotes.title: Day 23 — Systems Architecture: Websites, Stores & Integrations
studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2 Systems Architecture: Websites, Stores & Integrations
## Comprehensive Study Notes — Week 4

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Website → Store → Store View Hierarchy](#1-website--store--store-view-hierarchy)
2. [Configuration Scope](#2-configuration-scope)
3. [Performance Metrics for Architects](#3-performance-metrics-for-architects)
4. [External Integrations](#4-external-integrations)
5. [Headless vs Traditional Architecture](#5-headless-vs-traditional-architecture)
6. [GraphQL API for Headless Storefronts](#6-graphql-api-for-headless-storefronts)
7. [REST API for Backend Integrations](#7-rest-api-for-backend-integrations)
8. [Multi-Store Configuration in EE Admin](#8-multi-store-configuration-in-ee-admin)
9. [Critical Tricky Concepts](#9-critical-tricky-concepts)
10. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Website → Store → Store View Hierarchy

### 1.1 Overview Diagram

```
Global (Default Config)
  |
  +-- Website A (e.g., US Brand)
  |     |
  |     +-- Store A1 (root category: "US Catalog")
  |     |     |
  |     |     +-- Store View A1-EN  (English, USD)
  |     |     +-- Store View A1-ES  (Spanish, USD)
  |     |
  |     +-- Store A2 (root category: "US B2B Catalog")
  |           |
  |           +-- Store View A2-EN  (English, USD)
  |
  +-- Website B (e.g., EU Brand)
        |
        +-- Store B1 (root category: "EU Catalog")
              |
              +-- Store View B1-EN  (English, EUR)
              +-- Store View B1-DE  (German, EUR)
              +-- Store View B1-FR  (French, EUR)
```

---

### 1.2 Website Level

| Property | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Customer base** | **Completely separate** — each website has its own `customer_entity` rows scoped to that website |
| **Customer login** | Customers cannot log into Website B with Website A credentials |
| **Pricing** | Can have separate price scopes (catalog price scope setting) |
| **Currency** | Base currency can differ per website |
| **Payment methods** | Can be enabled/disabled per website |
| **Shipping methods** | Can be enabled/disabled per website |
| **Product catalog** | **Shared** across websites — same product table, but product visibility can be controlled per website |
| **Use case** | Multi-brand, multi-region, B2B vs B2C separation |

> **Exam focus:** Websites have **separate customer bases**. A customer account created on Website A cannot log in to Website B — the `website_id` column in `customer_entity` enforces this separation.

---

### 1.3 Store (Store Group) Level

| Property | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Root Category** | Each Store has exactly **one** root category — this defines the visible catalog tree |
| **Belongs to** | Exactly one Website |
| **Contains** | One or more Store Views |
| **Default Store View** | Must have at least one; one is designated as default |
| **Products** | Products are **assigned** to stores via root category assignment |
| **Customers** | Shared within the parent Website |

> **Exam focus:** Stores (Store Groups) are the level that determines the **root category**. Two stores under the same website can show entirely different product trees by using different root categories.

---

### 1.4 Store View Level

| Property | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Language/locale variation, translations |
| **Customers** | **Shared** with all other Store Views under the same Website |
| **Products** | Same products as the Store (same root category) |
| **Locale** | Different locale, language, date format |
| **Translations** | Store View is the level where CMS content, attribute labels, and UI strings are translated |
| **Currency display** | Display currency can vary by Store View; base currency set at Website level |
| **Status** | Can be enabled/disabled independently |

> **Exam focus:** Store Views share customers with sibling Store Views under the same Website. Changing locale, translation, or display currency → Store View scope.

---

### 1.5 Scope Inheritance Summary Table

| Capability | Global | Website | Store | Store View |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Separate customer accounts | — | **YES** | No | No |
| Root category | — | — | **YES** | No |
| Locale / Language | default | override | override | **YES** |
| Base currency | default | **YES** | — | — |
| Display currency | default | YES | YES | **YES** |
| Tax settings | default | YES | YES | YES |
| Product price scope | Global or Website | — | — | — |
| CMS page content | — | — | — | **YES** |

---

## 2. Configuration Scope

### 2.1 The Scope Hierarchy

```
Default (Global)
    |
    v
  Website
    |
    v
   Store (Store Group)
    |
    v
 Store View
```

Settings cascade **downward** — a more specific scope **overrides** a less specific scope. This is called **scope inheritance**.

### 2.2 How Scope Works in `core_config_data` Table

```sql
-- Global scope: scope='default', scope_id=0
-- Website scope: scope='websites', scope_id=<website_id>
-- Store View scope: scope='stores', scope_id=<store_view_id>
SELECT path, scope, scope_id, value
FROM core_config_data
WHERE path = 'general/locale/code'
ORDER BY scope_id;
```

**Sample output:**

| path | scope | scope_id | value |
|---|---|---|---|
| general/locale/code | default | 0 | en_US |
| general/locale/code | websites | 2 | de_DE |
| general/locale/code | stores | 5 | fr_FR |

> **Exam focus:** The `core_config_data` table stores only **overrides**. If a value is not present at a specific scope, Magento inherits from the parent scope. This is how the "Use Default" checkbox in Admin works. Note: the scope value `'stores'` represents **Store View** level (not Store Group), matching `ScopeInterface::SCOPE_STORES`.

### 2.3 Key Configuration Scope Decisions

| Setting | Recommended Scope |
|---|---|
| Payment methods | Website |
| Shipping methods | Website |
| Tax configuration | Website or Store View |
| Email sender identity | Store View |
| Store name | Store View |
| Catalog price scope | Global (affects all) or Website |
| Customer account sharing | **Global** (shared) or **Website** (separate) |

> **Exam focus:** **Customer Account Sharing** is configured at `Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration > Account Sharing Options`. Setting it to **"Per Website"** means customers are scoped to a website. This is the foundational setting for multi-brand isolation. Note: this setting is configurable at **Default (Global) scope only** — it cannot be set differently per website.

### 2.4 Catalog Price Scope

```
Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Price > Catalog Price Scope
  - Global: One price for all websites
  - Website: Separate prices per website (requires re-indexing)
```

> **Exam focus:** Changing catalog price scope from Global to Website triggers a **full price reindex** and changes how `catalog_product_index_price` is populated. This setting is also configurable at **Default scope only** (`showInDefault="1"` only).

---

## 3. Performance Metrics for Architects

### 3.1 Core Web Vitals (CWV)

| Metric | Full Name | Measures | Good Threshold | Poor Threshold |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **LCP** | Largest Contentful Paint | Loading performance of largest visible element | <= 2.5s | > 4.0s |
| **FID** | First Input Delay (replaced by INP) | Interactivity responsiveness | <= 100ms | > 300ms |
| **INP** | Interaction to Next Paint | Overall runtime responsiveness | <= 200ms | > 500ms |
| **CLS** | Cumulative Layout Shift | Visual stability, unexpected layout shifts | <= 0.1 | > 0.25 |

> **Exam focus:** Google replaced FID with **INP (Interaction to Next Paint)** as a Core Web Vital in March 2024. Know both. CLS is critical for storefronts with lazy-loading images and dynamic content injection.

### 3.2 Additional Performance Metrics

| Metric | Definition | Architect's Target |
|---|---|---|
| **TTFB** (Time to First Byte) | Time from request to first byte of response received by browser | < 200ms (excellent), < 800ms (acceptable) |
| **FCP** (First Contentful Paint) | Time until first content (text/image) painted | < 1.8s |
| **TTI** (Time to Interactive) | Time until page is fully interactive | < 3.8s |
| **TBT** (Total Blocking Time) | Total time main thread blocked between FCP and TTI | < 200ms |
| **Server Response Time** | Pure backend processing time (PHP, MySQL, Redis) | < 200ms |
| **Cache Hit Ratio** | % of requests served from cache vs. origin | > 90% for production |

### 3.3 Cache Hit Ratio Deep Dive

```
Cache Hit Ratio = (Cache Hits / Total Requests) * 100

Example:
  Total requests: 10,000
  Cache hits (Varnish/CDN served): 9,200
  Cache misses (PHP processed): 800
  Cache Hit Ratio = 92%
```

**Factors reducing cache hit ratio in Magento:**
- Too many unique URL parameters (sort, filter combinations)
- Logged-in customer pages (private content — bypasses full-page cache)
- High number of CMS block cache invalidations
- Missing `X-Magento-Cache-Id` headers
- Broken Varnish VCL configuration

> **Exam focus:** Varnish's cache hit ratio is monitored via `varnishstat` or Magento's built-in cache management. A ratio below 80% indicates a caching architecture problem — investigate hole-punching (ESI) configuration, cookie handling in VCL, and URL parameter normalization.

### 3.4 TTFB Components

```
TTFB = DNS Resolution + TCP Connection + TLS Handshake + Server Processing + First Byte Transfer

Magento Server Processing breakdown:
  - PHP bootstrapping + DI compilation       (~20-50ms cached)
  - Layout XML loading + block generation    (~30-100ms)
  - Database queries (EAV + joins)           (~10-200ms)
  - Redis cache reads                        (~1-5ms per call)
  - Full Page Cache hit (Varnish)            (~1-5ms total TTFB)
```

> **Exam focus:** A high TTFB almost always indicates either a **cache miss** (PHP processing the full page) or **slow database queries**. Varnish in front of Magento should bring TTFB to < 10ms for cached pages.

### 3.5 Metrics Monitoring Tools

| Tool | Use Case |
|---|---|
| **New Relic** | APM, transaction tracing, slow query detection |
| **Blackfire** | PHP profiling, call graph analysis |
| **Google PageSpeed Insights** | Core Web Vitals field + lab data |
| **Lighthouse** | Lab measurement of all CWV metrics |
| **GTmetrix** | Waterfall analysis, TTFB measurement |
| **Varnishstat** | Real-time Varnish cache statistics |
| **Magento Admin** | Cache management, slow query log, cron status |

---

## 4. External Integrations

### 4.1 ERP Integration Patterns

#### 4.1.1 Order Export (Magento → ERP)

```
Magento                       Integration Layer              ERP
  |                                  |                        |
  | -- Order Placed (event) -->      |                        |
  |                                  | -- Transform/Map -->   |
  |                                  |                        | -- Create Order
  |                                  | <-- ACK/Order # ---    |
  | <-- Update order.erp_id ---      |                        |
  |                                  |                        |
  | <-- Shipment/Tracking <--------- | <-- Ship Event ------- |
```

**Common patterns:**

| Pattern | Description | When to Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Queue-based (async)** | Order events published to MQ (RabbitMQ/Kafka); ERP consumer processes | High volume, reliability critical |
| **REST API push** | Magento webhook calls ERP REST endpoint on order creation | Simple, lower volume |
| **File-based (SFTP/EDI)** | Scheduled export of orders as CSV/EDI files | Legacy ERP systems |
| **Middleware (MuleSoft, etc.)** | Dedicated integration platform handles transformation | Complex multi-system environments |

**Order export triggers:**
- `sales_order_place_after` event (dispatched in `Order.php` on order placement)
- Observer on `checkout_onepage_controller_success_action` (dispatched in `Success.php` controller)
- Magento Queue Consumer listening to async order topic

#### 4.1.2 Product Import (ERP/PIM → Magento)

```php
// Product import programmatically using ImportExport module
use Magento\ImportExport\Model\Import;

$import->setData([
    'entity'              => 'catalog_product',
    'behavior'            => Import::BEHAVIOR_APPEND,
    'validation_strategy' => ProcessingErrorAggregatorInterface::VALIDATION_STRATEGY_SKIP_ERRORS,
]);
```

> **Note:** There is no `POST /rest/V1/import/csv` REST endpoint — the ImportExport module does not expose REST API endpoints. Product import is done via: (1) the admin UI (System > Data Transfer > Import), (2) CLI, or (3) programmatic PHP calls to the Import model. For REST-based product creation, use `POST /rest/V1/products` or the async bulk API `POST /rest/async/bulk/V1/products`.

**Product import data flow:**

```
ERP/PIM
  |
  v
Transform to Magento CSV format (SKU, name, price, qty, attributes...)
  |
  v
Validate (check required fields, attribute sets, category paths)
  |
  v
Import via CLI / Magento Admin / ImportExport module (no REST endpoint)
  |
  v
Trigger reindex (catalog_product, catalog_search, inventory)
  |
  v
Flush relevant caches
```

> **Exam focus:** Product import should be followed by **selective reindexing** and **cache flushing**. Avoid full reindexes in production during business hours. Use `bin/magento indexer:reindex` with specific indexer IDs.

### 4.2 Payment Gateway Integration

#### 4.2.1 Integration Approaches

| Approach | Description | Security | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hosted payment page** | Redirect to gateway's page for card entry | PCI SAQ A | PayPal Express, Stripe Checkout |
| **JavaScript SDK (iframe/embedded)** | Card fields rendered by gateway JS in iframes | PCI SAQ A-EP | Braintree, Square |
| **Direct API** | Card data sent to Magento, then forwarded to gateway | **PCI DSS SAQ D** — full compliance required | Authorize.Net Direct Post |
| **Vault/Token** | Store tokenized card references; never store raw PANs | Reduces PCI scope | Braintree Vault |

> **Exam focus:** The **payment gateway integration type determines PCI scope**. Hosted payment pages reduce merchant PCI compliance burden to SAQ A. Direct API integration requires full SAQ D compliance.

#### 4.2.2 Magento Payment Flow

```
Customer submits checkout
    |
    v
Magento calls Payment Gateway API (authorize or authorize+capture)
    |
    +-- Success --> Order placed, payment transaction recorded
    |                   in sales_payment_transaction table
    +-- Failure --> Exception thrown, order not placed, error shown
    |
    v
Webhook/IPN from gateway (async confirmation)
    |
    v
Magento processes webhook: updates transaction status
```

### 4.3 Shipping Carrier API Integration

#### 4.3.1 Real-time Rate Requests

```php
// Shipping carrier rate request flow
Magento\Quote\Model\Cart\ShippingMethodConverter
  -> AbstractCarrier::collectRates($request)
    -> API call to carrier (UPS, FedEx, USPS, DHL)
      -> Parse response -> Return RateResult with Rate objects
```

**Carrier API integration points:**

| Integration Point | API Call | When Called |
|---|---|---|
| **Rate calculation** | `getRates()` | Cart/checkout — can be cached |
| **Label generation** | `requestToShipment()` | On shipment creation in admin |
| **Tracking** | `getTrackingInfo()` | Customer tracking page |
| **Address validation** | Custom call | Checkout address step |

> **Exam focus:** Shipping rate API calls should be **cached at the quote level** to prevent repeated API calls during checkout. Use Magento's built-in carrier rate caching or implement a Redis-backed custom cache.

### 4.4 PIM (Product Information Management) Integration

```
PIM (Akeneo, Salsify, inRiver)
  |
  +-- Master product data: descriptions, attributes, rich content
  |
  v
Integration Middleware
  |
  +-- Transform to Magento attribute format
  +-- Handle attribute set mapping
  +-- Manage media files (images, PDFs)
  |
  v
Magento (via REST API or Import CSV)
  |
  +-- Create/update products
  +-- Assign to categories
  +-- Update images via Media API
```

**PIM integration key considerations:**

| Concern | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Attribute set mapping** | PIM families must map to Magento attribute sets |
| **Media handling** | Images imported via `POST /rest/V1/products/{sku}/media` |
| **Delta sync** | Only send changed products (use PIM change tracking) |
| **Conflict resolution** | What happens if ERP and PIM both update same product? |
| **Category mapping** | PIM category tree ≠ Magento category tree necessarily |

---

## 5. Headless vs Traditional Architecture

### 5.1 Traditional (Monolithic) Architecture

```
Browser
  |
  v
Magento (PHP) <---> MySQL / Redis / Elasticsearch
  |
  +-- Renders HTML server-side (Luma/Blank theme)
  +-- Returns full HTML page response
  +-- Knockout.js for limited client-side components
```

**Characteristics:**
- Server-side rendering (SSR) via Magento's layout/block/template system
- Theme files: `.phtml`, `.xml` layout files, LESS/CSS
- Full page cache (Varnish) for anonymous pages
- Customer session handled by PHP
- Tightly coupled — frontend and backend in same codebase

**Pros:**
- Single deployment unit
- Native Magento features work out of the box
- Simpler DevOps
- Strong Varnish caching for anonymous traffic

**Cons:**
- Slower time-to-interactive (heavy JS bundles with RequireJS)
- Performance ceiling limited by PHP rendering
- Difficult to achieve excellent Core Web Vitals scores
- Frontend updates require Magento deployment

### 5.2 Headless (Decoupled) Architecture

```
Browser
  |
  v
Frontend Application (Next.js / Vue Storefront / custom)
  |         |
  |         +-- Renders React/Vue components
  |         +-- SSR or SSG for performance
  |
  v (GraphQL or REST API calls)
Magento Backend
  |
  +-- Headless API layer only
  +-- No frontend rendering
  +-- Cart, Catalog, Checkout APIs
  |
  +---> MySQL / Redis / Elasticsearch (same backend)
```

### 5.3 Headless Storefront Options

| Technology | Stack | Key Features | Magento API |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PWA Studio** (Venia) | React, GraphQL | Official Magento solution, Peregrine hooks, Buildpack | GraphQL |
| **Hyva** | Alpine.js + Tailwind CSS | *Not truly headless* — replaces Luma with lighter PHP theme | PHP (same Magento) |
| **Vue Storefront** | Vue.js / Nuxt.js | Mature, large ecosystem, works with Magento 2 | GraphQL + REST |
| **Next.js Commerce** | Next.js, React | Vercel-optimized, SSG/ISR, flexible | GraphQL |
| **Gatsby + Magento** | Gatsby (React) | Static site generation, excellent for catalog | GraphQL |

> **Exam focus:** **Hyva is NOT headless** — it is a traditional Magento theme replacement (frontend still rendered by Magento PHP) that replaces Luma's RequireJS/KnockoutJS stack with Alpine.js and Tailwind. This is a common exam trick.

### 5.4 Headless Architecture Decision Matrix

| Factor | Traditional | Headless |
|---|---|---|
| Time to market | Faster | Slower (more infrastructure) |
| Core Web Vitals | Harder to achieve | Easier (SSR + code splitting) |
| Magento feature compatibility | 100% native | Requires custom GraphQL resolver work |
| Team expertise needed | Magento PHP + JS | React/Vue + API integration |
| Infrastructure complexity | Lower | Higher (separate deployment, CDN) |
| Content flexibility | Limited | High (can integrate any CMS) |
| Multi-channel support | Difficult | Natural (API-first) |
| Custom checkout | Complex | Very complex |

> **Exam focus:** Headless architectures use **GraphQL as the primary API** for storefront operations. REST API is used for **backend/admin integrations** (ERP, PIM, order management).

## 6. GraphQL API for Headless Storefronts

### 6.1 GraphQL Fundamentals in Magento 2

- Endpoint: `POST /graphql`
- Schema defined in `<Module>/etc/schema.graphqls`
- Resolvers: PHP classes implementing `ResolverInterface`
- Supports **queries** (read), **mutations** (write), **subscriptions** (not widely used in Magento)

### 6.2 Key Queries

#### 6.2.1 Products Query

```graphql
{
  products(
    search: "jacket",
    filter: {
      category_id: { eq: "12" },
      price: { from: "50", to: "200" }
    },
    pageSize: 20,
    currentPage: 1,
    sort: { price: ASC }
  ) {
    total_count
    page_info {
      total_pages
      current_page
    }
    items {
      id
      sku
      name
      url_key
      price_range {
        minimum_price {
          regular_price { value currency }
          final_price { value currency }
          discount { percent_off amount_off }
        }
      }
      image {
        url
        label
      }
      ... on ConfigurableProduct {
        configurable_options {
          attribute_code
          label
          values { value_index label swatch_data { value } }
        }
        variants {
          attributes { code value_index }
          product { sku price_range { minimum_price { final_price { value } } } }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> **Exam focus:** The `products` query is the most complex GraphQL query in Magento. Know that **inline fragments** (`... on ConfigurableProduct`) are used for product type-specific data. The `search` parameter triggers Elasticsearch/OpenSearch.

#### 6.2.2 Cart Queries and Mutations

```graphql
# Create empty cart (note: deprecated in favor of createGuestCart / customerCart)
mutation {
  createEmptyCart
}

# Add simple product to cart
mutation AddToCart($cartId: String!) {
  addSimpleProductsToCart(
    input: {
      cart_id: $cartId,
      cart_items: [
        {
          data: {
            sku: "MH01-XS-Black",
            quantity: 2
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ) {
    cart {
      id
      items {
        id
        product { name sku }
        quantity
        prices {
          row_total { value currency }
        }
      }
      prices {
        grand_total { value currency }
        subtotal_including_tax { value currency }
      }
    }
  }
}

# Get cart details
query GetCart($cartId: String!) {
  cart(cart_id: $cartId) {
    id
    email
    items {
      id
      product { sku name }
      quantity
    }
    shipping_addresses {
      selected_shipping_method {
        carrier_code method_code amount { value currency }
      }
    }
    available_payment_methods {
      code title
    }
    selected_payment_method { code }
    prices { grand_total { value currency } }
  }
}
```

#### 6.2.3 Checkout Mutations

```graphql
# Set shipping address
mutation SetShippingAddress($cartId: String!) {
  setShippingAddressesOnCart(
    input: {
      cart_id: $cartId,
      shipping_addresses: [{
        address: {
          firstname: "Jane",
          lastname: "Doe",
          street: ["123 Main St"],
          city: "Austin",
          region: "TX",
          postcode: "78701",
          country_code: "US",
          telephone: "555-1234"
        }
      }]
    }
  ) {
    cart { shipping_addresses { city region { code } } }
  }
}

# Set shipping method
mutation SetShippingMethod($cartId: String!) {
  setShippingMethodsOnCart(
    input: {
      cart_id: $cartId,
      shipping_methods: [{
        carrier_code: "flatrate",
        method_code: "flatrate"
      }]
    }
  ) {
    cart { shipping_addresses { selected_shipping_method { carrier_code amount { value } } } }
  }
}

# Set payment method
mutation SetPaymentMethod($cartId: String!) {
  setPaymentMethodOnCart(
    input: {
      cart_id: $cartId,
      payment_method: { code: "checkmo" }
    }
  ) {
    cart { selected_payment_method { code } }
  }
}

# Place order
mutation PlaceOrder($cartId: String!) {
  placeOrder(input: { cart_id: $cartId }) {
    order {
      order_number
    }
  }
}
```

> **Exam focus:** The GraphQL checkout flow follows a **specific sequence**: Create Cart → Add Items → Set Email → Set Shipping Address → Set Shipping Method → Set Payment Method → Place Order. Skipping steps returns validation errors. Know the mutation names for the exam.

#### 6.2.4 Customer Authentication

```graphql
# Generate customer token
mutation GenerateToken {
  generateCustomerToken(email: "customer@example.com", password: "P@ssw0rd!") {
    token
  }
}

# Use token in Authorization header:
# Authorization: Bearer <token>

# Get customer info
query {
  customer {
    firstname
    lastname
    email
    orders {
      items {
        number
        status
        total { grand_total { value currency } }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### 6.3 GraphQL Schema Definition

```graphql
# schema.graphqls example
type Query {
    products(
        search: String,
        filter: ProductAttributeFilterInput,
        pageSize: Int = 20,
        currentPage: Int = 1,
        sort: ProductAttributeSortInput
    ): Products @resolver(class: "Magento\\CatalogGraphQl\\Model\\Resolver\\Products") @cache(cacheIdentity: "Magento\\CatalogGraphQl\\Model\\Resolver\\Product\\Identity")
}
```

> **Exam focus:** The `@resolver` directive links a GraphQL field to a PHP resolver class. The `@cache` directive with `cacheIdentity` enables **GraphQL response caching** in Redis. This is critical for performance in headless storefronts.

### 6.4 GraphQL vs REST Comparison

| Aspect | GraphQL | REST |
|---|---|---|
| Endpoint | Single: `POST /graphql` | Multiple: `/rest/V1/products`, `/rest/V1/orders`, etc. |
| Data fetching | Request exactly what you need | Fixed response shape |
| Over-fetching | Eliminated | Common |
| Under-fetching | Eliminated (single query for nested data) | Multiple requests often needed |
| Versioning | Schema evolution (add fields, deprecate) | API version in URL (`/V1/`, `/V2/`) |
| Use case | Frontend/storefront | Backend/admin integrations |
| Auth | Bearer token / guest cart token | OAuth 1.0a / Bearer token |
| Caching | Per-query cache identity | HTTP cache headers |

> **Note:** GraphQL does **not** support OAuth 1.0a authentication — only Bearer tokens (via `generateCustomerToken`) and guest cart tokens. OAuth 1.0a is available only for REST API integrations (configured via Admin > System > Integrations).

## 7. REST API for Backend Integrations

### 7.1 REST API Overview

- Base URL: `/rest/{store_code}/V1/{resource}`
- Default store: `/rest/default/V1/` or `/rest/all/V1/` (all store views)
- Authentication: OAuth 1.0a (integrations), Bearer token (customer/admin)
- Format: JSON (default), XML supported

### 7.2 Key REST Endpoints for Integrations

#### 7.2.1 Product Management (ERP/PIM → Magento)

```bash
# Create or update product
POST /rest/all/V1/products
PUT  /rest/all/V1/products/{sku}

# Example payload
curl -X POST "https://magento.example.com/rest/all/V1/products" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin_token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "product": {
      "sku": "ERP-SKU-001",
      "name": "Example Product",
      "attribute_set_id": 4,
      "price": 29.99,
      "status": 1,
      "visibility": 4,
      "type_id": "simple",
      "weight": 1.5,
      "custom_attributes": [
        {"attribute_code": "description", "value": "Product description"},
        {"attribute_code": "short_description", "value": "Short desc"}
      ]
    }
  }'

# Get product by SKU
GET /rest/V1/products/{sku}

# Bulk product update (async)
POST /rest/async/bulk/V1/products
```

#### 7.2.2 Inventory Management

```bash
# Update stock item
PUT /rest/V1/products/{sku}/stockItems/{itemId}

# MSI source items
POST /rest/V1/inventory/source-items

# Check salability
GET /rest/V1/inventory/is-product-salable/{sku}/{stockId}
```

#### 7.2.3 Order Management (Magento → ERP)

```bash
# Get orders (for ERP polling)
GET /rest/V1/orders?searchCriteria[filter_groups][0][filters][0][field]=status
  &searchCriteria[filter_groups][0][filters][0][value]=pending
  &searchCriteria[filter_groups][0][filters][0][condition_type]=eq

# Update order status
POST /rest/V1/orders/{orderId}/comments

# Create shipment
POST /rest/V1/order/{orderId}/ship
# Payload includes tracking number, carrier code

# Create invoice
POST /rest/V1/invoices
# Or
POST /rest/V1/order/{orderId}/invoice
```

#### 7.2.4 Customer Management

```bash
# Create customer (website-scoped!)
POST /rest/V1/customers
# payload must include website_id for proper scoping

# Get customer by email
GET /rest/V1/customers/search?searchCriteria[filter_groups][0][filters][0][field]=email
  &searchCriteria[filter_groups][0][filters][0][value]=customer@example.com
```

### 7.3 REST API Authentication Types

| Auth Type | Used By | How It Works |
|---|---|---|
| **Admin Bearer Token** | Admin scripts, ERP integrations | `POST /rest/V1/integration/admin/token` |
| **Customer Bearer Token** | Mobile apps, custom frontends | `POST /rest/V1/integration/customer/token` |
| **OAuth 1.0a** | Third-party integrations (preferred for production) | 4-leg OAuth flow via Admin > System > Integrations |
| **Guest** | No auth | Guest cart operations only |

```bash
# Get admin token
curl -X POST "https://magento.example.com/rest/V1/integration/admin/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"admin","password":"Admin123!"}'
# Returns: "abc123tokenstring..."

# Use token
curl -X GET "https://magento.example.com/rest/V1/orders" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer abc123tokenstring..."
```

> **Exam focus:** For production ERP integrations, use **OAuth 1.0a** (configured in Admin > System > Integrations) rather than admin bearer tokens, which expire and expose admin credentials. OAuth integrations have configurable resource access scopes.

### 7.4 Async and Bulk REST APIs

```bash
# Async single operation (returns bulk UUID, processed via queue)
POST /rest/async/V1/products

# Bulk operation (multiple items, single request)
POST /rest/async/bulk/V1/products

# Check bulk operation status
GET /rest/V1/bulk/{bulkUuid}/status
```

> **Exam focus:** The **Async/Bulk REST API** requires **RabbitMQ** (or MySQL queue in development). Operations are processed asynchronously by queue consumers. Use for large product imports to avoid HTTP timeout issues.

## 8. Multi-Store Configuration in EE Admin

### 8.1 Creating the Hierarchy

```
Step 1: Create Website
  Stores > Settings > All Stores > Create Website
  - Name: "US Brand"
  - Code: us_brand (unique, lowercase, no spaces)
  - Default Store: (assign after store creation)

Step 2: Create Store (Store Group)
  Stores > Settings > All Stores > Create Store
  - Website: US Brand
  - Name: "US Main Store"
  - Root Category: (select existing or create new)
  - Default Store View: (assign after store view creation)

Step 3: Create Store View
  Stores > Settings > All Stores > Create Store View
  - Store: US Main Store
  - Name: "English"
  - Code: us_brand_en
  - Status: Enabled
  - Sort Order: 0

Step 4: Run setup upgrade (if needed)
  bin/magento setup:upgrade
  bin/magento indexer:reindex
  bin/magento cache:flush
```

### 8.2 nginx Configuration for Multiple Websites

```nginx
# nginx.conf — Multi-website setup using server blocks
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name us.example.com;

    set $MAGE_RUN_CODE "us_brand";
    set $MAGE_RUN_TYPE "website";  # or "store" for store-level

    include /var/www/html/nginx.conf.sample;
}

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name eu.example.com;

    set $MAGE_RUN_CODE "eu_brand";
    set $MAGE_RUN_TYPE "website";

    include /var/www/html/nginx.conf.sample;
}
```

### 8.3 Magento Entry Point Configuration

```php
// pub/index.php (or via env.php for Cloud)
// Set store/website programmatically via bootstrap params

// In nginx or Apache, set environment variable:
// MAGE_RUN_CODE = website_code
// MAGE_RUN_TYPE = website|store
```

### 8.4 Cloud (`app/etc/env.php`) Multi-Store

```php
// app/etc/env.php
return [
    'system' => [
        'default' => [

                'secure'   => ['base_url' => 'https://default.example.com/']
            ]

        'websites' => [

                ]

];
```

### 8.5 EE-Specific Multi-Store Features

| Feature | Description | Location in Admin |
|---|---|---|
| **Shared Catalog** | B2B: assign different product catalogs per customer group/website | Catalog > Shared Catalogs |
| **Company Accounts** | B2B: company hierarchy, multiple buyers per company | Customers > Companies |
| **Content Staging** | Schedule content updates per store view | Content > Content Staging > Dashboard |
| **Customer Segments** | Target content/promotions by segment, scoped to website | Customers > Segments |
| **Store Credit** | Per-website credit balance | Stores > Configuration > Customers |

> **Note:** **Page Builder** is available in both Adobe Commerce (EE) and Magento Open Source (CE) — it is NOT an EE-exclusive feature. It has no dependency on `magento2-ee-base`.

> **Exam focus:** In **Magento Commerce (EE)**, the **Shared Catalog** feature is critical for B2B multi-store setups. It allows different product visibility and pricing per customer group, scoped at the website level.

## 9. Critical Tricky Concepts

### 9.1 THE Most Important Exam Trap: Customer Scoping

```
+----------------------------------+----------------------------------+
|         WEBSITE LEVEL            |        STORE VIEW LEVEL          |
|----------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Separate customer accounts       | SHARED customer accounts         |
| Different login credentials      | Same login works across          |
| customer_entity.website_id       | all store views of same website  |
| enforces separation              |                                  |
|                                  |                                  |
| Use case: Multi-brand where      | Use case: Same brand, different  |
| customers must be brand-specific | languages (EN/FR/DE)             |
+----------------------------------+----------------------------------+
```

**Concrete example:**
- Website A: `north-america.brand.com`
- Website B: `europe.brand.com`
- Customer registers on Website A → `customer_entity.website_id = 1`
- Customer tries to log in on Website B → **FAILS** — different website
- Website A has Store Views: `en_US` and `es_MX` — customer can log in to **both** with same credentials

### 9.2 Product Scope Subtleties

```
Products are global entities but their ATTRIBUTES can be scoped:

product.name       -> Store View scope (translated per locale)
product.price      -> Global OR Website scope (catalog price scope setting)
product.status     -> Website scope (can disable on one website, enable on another)
product.visibility -> Store View scope
product.url_key    -> Store View scope (can have different URL per language)
product.stock      -> Global (simple) or Source (MSI)
```

> **Exam focus:** Product **status** is configurable at the Website scope. A product can be `Enabled` on Website A and `Disabled` on Website B. Product **name** and **description** are scoped to Store View for translation purposes.

### 9.3 Root Category Scoping Trap

```
Scenario: 
  Website A
    +-- Store 1 (Root Category: "Main Website Store")
    |     +-- Store View EN
    |     +-- Store View FR
    +-- Store 2 (Root Category: "B2B Products")
          +-- Store View B2B-EN

Q: Can Store View FR see products in "B2B Products" root category?
A: NO — Store View FR belongs to Store 1, which uses "Main Website Store"
   as root category. Categories in "B2B Products" tree are not accessible
   from Store 1's store views.
```

### 9.4 Configuration "Use Default" / "Use Website" Checkbox

```
Admin > Stores > Configuration > [Select Store View Scope]

When a checkbox shows "Use Default" or "Use Website":
- Checked = inherit from parent scope (no row in core_config_data)
- Unchecked = override at this scope (row exists in core_config_data)

To reset to inherited: check the "Use Default" box and Save.
This DELETES the row from core_config_data for that path/scope combination.
```

### 9.5 Hyva vs Headless — The Architecture Distinction

```
TRADITIONAL (Luma)          HYVA                    HEADLESS (PWA/Next.js)
+------------------+    +------------------+    +------------------+
| Browser          |    | Browser          |    | Browser          |
|    <HTML>        |    |    <HTML>        |    |   React/Vue App  |
+------------------+    +------------------+    +------------------+
        |                       |                       |
        v                       v                       | (GraphQL/REST)
+------------------+    +------------------+            v
| Magento PHP      |    | Magento PHP      |    +------------------+
| (renders HTML)   |    | (renders HTML)   |    | Magento PHP      |
| RequireJS +      |    | Alpine.js +      |    | (API only,       |
| KnockoutJS       |    | Tailwind CSS     |    | no HTML render)  |
+------------------+    +------------------+    +------------------+

Both Traditional and Hyva = Monolithic (PHP renders the page)
Only PWA/Next.js = True Headless (PHP is pure API)
```

### 9.6 GraphQL vs REST — When to Use Which

| Situation | Use |
|---|---|
| Building a React/Vue storefront | **GraphQL** |
| ERP sending orders to Magento | **REST** |
| PIM pushing products to Magento | **REST** (Bulk Async REST) |
| Mobile app needing cart/checkout | **GraphQL** |
| Reporting/BI pulling order data | **REST** or direct DB read |
| Shipping carrier label generation | **REST** |
| Customer data for CRM | **REST** |

## 10. Quick-Reference Checklist

### Website → Store → Store View Hierarchy

- [ ] **Website** = separate customer base (separate login credentials, `customer_entity.website_id`)
- [ ] **Store (Group)** = defines the root category; one root category per store
- [ ] **Store View** = locale/language/translation; customers are **shared** within the website
- [ ] Products are global but attributes can be scoped to Store View (name, description) or Website (status, price)
- [ ] A Store View cannot exist without a Store; a Store cannot exist without a Website
- [ ] Customer account sharing is set at `Stores > Config > Customers > Customer Configuration > Account Sharing Options` (Default scope only)

### Configuration Scope

- [ ] Scope hierarchy: Global → Website → Store → Store View (most specific wins)
- [ ] `core_config_data` table stores only **overrides** — blank = inherit from parent
- [ ] Scope values: `'default'` (global), `'websites'` (website), `'stores'` (store view — NOT 'store_views')
- [ ] "Use Default" checkbox = delete override row = inherit from parent scope
- [ ] Catalog Price Scope (Global vs Website) requires full price reindex when changed
- [ ] Base currency is set at Website scope; display currency at Store View scope

### Performance Metrics

- [ ] **TTFB** < 200ms target; high TTFB = cache miss or slow DB
- [ ] **FCP** < 1.8s; **LCP** <= 2.5s; **CLS** <= 0.1; **INP** <= 200ms
- [ ] FID is **deprecated** — replaced by **INP** (Interaction to Next Paint) in 2024
- [ ] Cache hit ratio > 90% is production target; measure with `varnishstat`
- [ ] Varnish in front of Magento → TTFB drops to < 10ms for cached pages
- [ ] New Relic for APM; Blackfire for PHP profiling; Lighthouse for CWV

### External Integrations

- [ ] **ERP order export**: Queue-based (async RabbitMQ) is most reliable pattern
- [ ] **Product import**: Follow with `indexer:reindex` and `cache:flush`; no REST import endpoint exists
- [ ] **Payment gateway**: Hosted page = SAQ A (lowest PCI scope); Direct API = SAQ D (full PCI)
- [ ] **Shipping API**: Rate calls should be cached at quote level
- [ ] **PIM**: Maps families → attribute sets; use delta sync (changed products only)
- [ ] Async/Bulk REST API requires RabbitMQ for queue processing

### Headless vs Traditional

- [ ] **Hyva is NOT headless** — it's a lightweight PHP-rendered theme (Alpine.js + Tailwind)
- [ ] True headless = separate frontend application consuming Magento GraphQL/REST APIs
- [ ] Headless options: PWA Studio (React), Vue Storefront (Vue), Next.js Commerce
- [ ] Headless → better CWV potential; higher infrastructure complexity
- [ ] Traditional → simpler DevOps; harder to achieve excellent CWV
- [ ] Page Builder is available in BOTH CE and EE (not EE-only)

### GraphQL

- [ ] Single endpoint: `POST /graphql`
- [ ] Key queries: `products`, `cart`, `customer`
- [ ] Key mutations: `createEmptyCart` (deprecated → use `createGuestCart`/`customerCart`), `addSimpleProductsToCart`, `setShippingAddressesOnCart`, `setShippingMethodsOnCart`, `setPaymentMethodOnCart`, `placeOrder`, `generateCustomerToken`
- [ ] Checkout sequence: Cart → Items → Email → Shipping Address → Shipping Method → Payment Method → Place Order
- [ ] Inline fragments (`... on ConfigurableProduct`) for product-type-specific data
- [ ] Schema defined in `schema.graphqls`; `@resolver` links field to PHP class; `@cache` enables caching
- [ ] GraphQL response caching uses `cacheIdentity` class for cache key generation
- [ ] GraphQL does NOT support OAuth 1.0a — only Bearer tokens and guest tokens

### REST API

- [ ] Base URL pattern: `/rest/{store_code}/V1/{resource}`
- [ ] Auth: OAuth 1.0a (production integrations), Bearer token (scripts/dev)
- [ ] Create customer via REST → include `website_id` for correct scoping
- [ ] Async Bulk API: `POST /rest/async/bulk/V1/products` — requires RabbitMQ
- [ ] Order export: `GET /rest/V1/orders` with `searchCriteria` filter parameters
- [ ] Shipment creation: `POST /rest/V1/order/{orderId}/ship` includes tracking
- [ ] Admin token: `POST /rest/V1/integration/admin/token`
- [ ] Customer token: `POST /rest/V1/integration/customer/token`

### Multi-Store EE Specifics

- [ ] Set website via nginx: `$MAGE_RUN_CODE` and `$MAGE_RUN_TYPE` variables
- [ ] Store management: Stores > Settings > All Stores
- [ ] EE-only: Shared Catalog (B2B per-customer-group product/price visibility)
- [ ] EE-only: Content Staging (Content > Content Staging > Dashboard)
- [ ] EE-only: Customer Segments (scoped to website)
- [ ] After creating stores/websites: run `bin/magento setup:upgrade`, reindex, flush cache

### Critical Traps to Remember

- [ ] **TRAP**: "Store Views have separate customer bases" — **FALSE**. Websites have separate customer bases; Store Views share customers.
- [ ] **TRAP**: "Hyva is headless" — **FALSE**. Hyva is a PHP-rendered Magento theme.
- [ ] **TRAP**: "GraphQL is used for ERP integration" — **MOSTLY FALSE**. REST API is the standard for backend/ERP integrations.
- [ ] **TRAP**: "All product data is global" — **FALSE**. Product name/description = Store View scope; price = Global or Website scope; status = Website scope.
- [ ] **TRAP**: "Changing catalog price scope takes effect immediately" — **FALSE**. Requires full price reindex.
- [ ] **TRAP**: "Import products via REST API" — **MISLEADING**. Use `POST /rest/V1/products` for individual products or async bulk API for batches. There is no `POST /rest/V1/import/csv` endpoint.

flashcards.answer: Customer accounts are scoped at the Website level. A customer account created on Website A cannot log in to Website B — the website_id column in customer_entity enforces this separation. Store Views within the same Website share customer accounts.
flashcards.hint: Think about the column in the customer database table that enforces separation.

flashcards.question: What does the Store (Store Group) level determine in the Magento hierarchy?
flashcards.answer: The Store (Store Group) level determines the root category, which defines the visible catalog tree. Each Store has exactly one root category. Two stores under the same website can show entirely different product trees by using different root categories.
flashcards.hint: This is the level between Website and Store View, and it controls what products are browsable.

flashcards.question: How does the core_config_data table handle configuration scope and inheritance?
flashcards.answer: The core_config_data table stores only overrides. If a value is not present at a specific scope, Magento inherits from the parent scope. The scope column uses 'default' for global (scope_id 0), 'websites' for website level, and 'stores' for store view level (not store group).
flashcards.hint: Think of what happens when you check the 'Use Default' checkbox in admin — the row is deleted.

flashcards.question: What replaced FID as a Core Web Vital in March 2024, and what does it measure?
flashcards.answer: INP (Interaction to Next Paint) replaced FID (First Input Delay) as a Core Web Vital. INP measures overall runtime responsiveness with a good threshold of 200ms or less, compared to FID which only measured the delay of the first input.
flashcards.hint: The new metric covers ALL interactions, not just the first one.

flashcards.question: Why is Hyva NOT considered a headless commerce solution?
flashcards.answer: Hyva is NOT headless because it is a traditional Magento theme replacement where the frontend is still rendered by Magento PHP on the server. It replaces Luma's RequireJS/KnockoutJS stack with Alpine.js and Tailwind CSS, but the page rendering architecture remains monolithic.
flashcards.hint: Consider whether the frontend is a separate application or still rendered by the same PHP process.

flashcards.question: What is the correct GraphQL checkout flow sequence in Adobe Commerce?
flashcards.answer: The sequence is: Create Cart, Add Items, Set Email, Set Shipping Address, Set Shipping Method, Set Payment Method, Place Order. Skipping steps returns validation errors. Key mutations include createEmptyCart, addSimpleProductsToCart, setShippingAddressesOnCart, setPaymentMethodOnCart, and placeOrder.
flashcards.hint: Think of it as following the same logical order as the storefront checkout steps.

flashcards.question: When should you use GraphQL vs REST API in Adobe Commerce integrations?
flashcards.answer: GraphQL is used for storefront/frontend applications (React, Vue, mobile apps) where you need to request exactly the data you need. REST API is used for backend integrations like ERP order management, PIM product imports, and CRM data sync.
flashcards.hint: Frontend-facing = GraphQL; backend system-to-system = REST.

flashcards.question: What authentication method does GraphQL support in Adobe Commerce, and what does it NOT support?
flashcards.answer: GraphQL supports Bearer tokens (via generateCustomerToken mutation) and guest cart tokens. It does NOT support OAuth 1.0a authentication. OAuth 1.0a is available only for REST API integrations configured via Admin > System > Integrations.
flashcards.hint: The newer API technology uses the simpler token-based auth, not the older OAuth flow.

flashcards.question: What does the Async/Bulk REST API require for processing, and when should it be used?
flashcards.answer: The Async/Bulk REST API requires RabbitMQ (or MySQL queue in development) for processing. Operations are processed asynchronously by queue consumers. It should be used for large product imports to avoid HTTP timeout issues, via POST /rest/async/bulk/V1/products.
flashcards.hint: Think about what message broker handles the queue for asynchronous operations.

flashcards.question: How do you configure multiple websites in nginx for Magento?
flashcards.answer: Each website gets its own server block in nginx with MAGE_RUN_CODE set to the website code and MAGE_RUN_TYPE set to 'website'. Each server block includes Magento's nginx.conf.sample. The website codes must match those configured in Stores > Settings > All Stores.
flashcards.hint: Two environment variables in the nginx config tell Magento which website to load.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between product status scope and product name scope in Adobe Commerce?
flashcards.answer: Product status is scoped at the Website level, meaning a product can be Enabled on Website A and Disabled on Website B. Product name and description are scoped at the Store View level, allowing different translations per language/locale.
flashcards.hint: Turning a product on/off is a website decision; naming it is a language decision.

flashcards.question: What is Catalog Price Scope, and what happens when you change it from Global to Website?
flashcards.answer: Catalog Price Scope (Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Price) determines whether products have one price for all websites (Global) or separate prices per website (Website). Changing from Global to Website triggers a full price reindex and is configurable at Default scope only.
flashcards.hint: This is a configuration that requires background processing to take effect after change.
