# AD0-E708 Full Exam Simulation #4 — Complete Study Notes
### Adobe Commerce Business Practitioner Expert Certification

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Exam Overview & Simulation Strategy](#1-exam-overview--simulation-strategy)
2. [Section 1 — Core Features (46%)](#2-section-1--core-features-46)
3. [Section 2 — Merchandising (10%)](#3-section-2--merchandising-10)
4. [Section 3 — Digital Marketing (4%)](#4-section-3--digital-marketing-4)
5. [Section 4 — Add-on Modules (18%)](#5-section-4--add-on-modules-18)
6. [Section 5 — Systems Architecture (10%)](#6-section-5--systems-architecture-10)
7. [Section 6 — Compliance (12%)](#7-section-6--compliance-12)
8. [Error Pattern Analysis Framework](#8-error-pattern-analysis-framework)
9. [Section Ranking & Final 4-Day Prep Plan](#9-section-ranking--final-4-day-prep-plan)
10. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#10-quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Exam Overview & Simulation Strategy

### 1.1 Exam Vitals

| Parameter | Detail |
|---|---|
| Exam Code | AD0-E708 |
| Total Questions | ~60 |
| Time Allowed | 105 minutes |
| Passing Score | ~64–68% (varies by form) |
| Format | Multiple choice, multi-select |
| Delivery | Adobe Credential Manager / PSI |

### 1.2 Section Weights at a Glance

```
+----------------------------------+-------+-------------------+
| Section                          | Weight| ~Questions (of 60)|
+----------------------------------+-------+-------------------+
| 1. Core Features                 |  46%  |  ~28              |
| 2. Merchandising                 |  10%  |   ~6              |
| 3. Digital Marketing             |   4%  |   ~2              |
| 4. Add-on Modules                |  18%  |  ~11              |
| 5. Systems Architecture          |  10%  |   ~6              |
| 6. Compliance                    |  12%  |   ~7              |
+----------------------------------+-------+-------------------+
| TOTAL                            | 100%  |  ~60              |
+----------------------------------+-------+-------------------+
```

> **Exam focus:** Section 1 (Core Features) at 46% means every question you save here is worth 2.5× a Compliance question. A perfect Section 1 score nearly guarantees a pass even with moderate performance elsewhere.

### 1.3 Simulation Protocol

**Before you start:**
- Set a physical timer for 105 minutes
- Close all browser tabs, notes, and IDE
- Print or copy the question set — no scrolling back
- Use scratch paper for working (allowed in real exam)

**Time budgeting strategy:**

```
+-------------------+----------+---------------------+
| Phase             | Time     | Notes               |
+-------------------+----------+---------------------+
| First pass        | 70 min   | Answer all, flag    |
|                   |          | uncertain ones      |
| Review flagged    | 25 min   | Change only if sure |
| Final scan        | 10 min   | Gut-check blanks    |
+-------------------+----------+---------------------+
```

**Per-question budget:** 105 min ÷ 60 questions = **1 min 45 sec per question**

### 1.4 Post-Simulation Scoring Worksheet

```
Section 1 — Core Features     ( /28)  _____ %
Section 2 — Merchandising     ( /6 )  _____ %
Section 3 — Digital Marketing ( /2 )  _____ %
Section 4 — Add-on Modules    ( /11)  _____ %
Section 5 — Systems Arch.     ( /6 )  _____ %
Section 6 — Compliance        ( /7 )  _____ %

Weighted Score = Sum of (section% × weight)
```

**Weighted score formula:**
```
Weighted = (S1/28 × 0.46) + (S2/6 × 0.10) + (S3/2 × 0.04)
         + (S4/11 × 0.18) + (S5/6 × 0.10) + (S6/7 × 0.12)
```

---

## 2. Section 1 — Core Features (46%)

> This is the highest-value section. It covers the foundational mechanics of Adobe Commerce: catalog, pricing, checkout, orders, customers, admin, and site configuration.

### 2.1 Catalog & Product Types

#### Product Type Matrix

| Type | SKU Model | Configurable Child? | Stock Tracked At | Key Use Case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Simple | Single SKU | No | Product level | One-size t-shirt |
| Configurable | Parent + children | Yes (simple products) | Child level | Shirt with color/size |
| Grouped | Set of simples | No | Each simple | Product bundles display |
| Bundle | Dynamic assembly | No | Option level | Build-your-own PC |
| Virtual | No shipping | No | Product level | Service/subscription |
| Downloadable | No shipping | No | Product level | Software, PDFs |
| Gift Card | Varies by type | No | Virtual/physical | Store credits |

> **Exam focus:** Gift Cards come in three types: Virtual (no shipping), Physical (requires shipping), and Combined (customer chooses). Do not assume all gift cards are virtual — the type determines shipping behavior.

> **Exam focus:** Configurable products track inventory at the **child (simple) level**, not the parent. The parent's "in stock" status is derived.

> **Exam focus:** Bundle products can have **fixed or dynamic pricing**. Dynamic price = sum of selected options. Fixed price = set regardless of options.

#### Attribute Sets & EAV

```
Global Scope
    |
    +-- Website Scope
          |
          +-- Store Scope
                |
                +-- Store View Scope  <-- Attribute values can be set here
```

- **EAV (Entity-Attribute-Value)** model used for product, customer, category attributes
- **Flat tables** are generated from EAV for frontend performance (`catalog_product_flat`)
- Flat catalog must be **reindexed** after changes

> **Exam focus:** Attribute scope determines where a value can differ. *Store View* scope allows different product names per language. *Website* scope allows different prices per website.

#### Category Configuration

| Setting | Location | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Is Anchor | Category > Display Settings | Allows layered nav from subcategory products |
| URL Key | Category > Search Engine Optimization | Used in canonical URLs |
| Display Mode | Category | Products only / Static block only / Both |
| Root Category | Store > Configuration | Each store must be assigned one root category |

> **Exam focus:** Setting **Is Anchor = Yes** on a parent category makes it aggregate products from all child categories in layered navigation.

### 2.2 Pricing Architecture

#### Price Hierarchy (lowest wins for customer)

```
Base Price (MSRP / Regular Price)
    |
    v
Special Price (date-ranged override)
    |
    v
Tier Price (qty-based reduction)
    |
    v
Group Price (customer group specific)
    |
    v
Catalog Price Rule (condition-based, no coupon)
    |
    v
Cart Price Rule (cart-level, optional coupon)
```

> **Exam focus:** **Catalog Price Rules** apply before the cart. **Cart Price Rules** apply during checkout. A catalog rule can stack with a cart rule unless "Discard subsequent rules" is checked (the actual admin UI label for the stop-processing toggle).

#### Tier Pricing

```php
// Tier price table: catalog_product_entity_tier_price
// Fields: website_id, all_groups, customer_group_id, qty, value, percentage_value
```

- Tier prices can be **fixed amounts** or **percentage discounts**
- Lowest price wins when multiple tiers qualify

#### MAP (Minimum Advertised Price)

- Configured per product
- Can show "Add to Cart" without revealing actual price on category page
- Requires **Apply MAP** = Yes in configuration

> **Exam focus:** MAP is a **display** feature, not an enforcement mechanism. It shows the "Click for price" popup but does NOT prevent selling below MAP.

### 2.3 Checkout & Payment Architecture

#### Checkout Flow (Luma/Default)

```
Cart --> Shipping Address --> Shipping Method --> Payment --> Order Review --> Place Order
                                                                                |
                                                                                v
                                                                         Order Created
                                                                         (status: Pending)
```

#### Payment Method Types

| Method | Capture Timing | Suitable For |
|---|---|---|
| Authorize only | Manual capture later | Physical goods |
| Authorize & Capture | Immediate | Digital goods |
| Offline (Check/MO) | Manual | Low-volume B2B |
| PayPal Express | Auth or sale | Quick checkout |
| Vault | Tokenized reuse | Returning customers |

> **Exam focus:** **Authorize only** creates a payment authorization but does NOT charge the card. Charge happens when **invoice is created**. This is the default for physical goods best practice.

#### Guest Checkout

- Enabled/disabled: **Stores > Configuration > Sales > Checkout > Allow Guest Checkout**
- Guest orders are linked to email; account merge available post-registration
- Guest checkout disabling is a common B2B/compliance requirement

### 2.4 Order Lifecycle

#### Order Status vs. State

```
State (internal system state)       Status (merchant-visible label)
new                            -->  Pending
pending_payment                -->  Pending Payment
processing                     -->  Processing
complete                       -->  Complete
closed                         -->  Closed
canceled                       -->  Canceled
holded                         -->  On Hold
payment_review                 -->  Payment Review
```

> **Exam focus:** **State** is fixed by the system; **Status** is configurable and can be customized. Multiple statuses can map to one state. You can create custom statuses under **Stores > Settings > Order Status**. Note: the "fraud" status maps to both processing and payment_review states.

#### Order Operations & Documents

| Operation | Document Created | Stock Impact |
|---|---|---|
| Place Order | Order | Reservation created |
| Create Invoice | Invoice | Sale confirmed |
| Create Shipment | Shipment + Tracking | Stock decremented |
| Create Credit Memo | Credit Memo | Optional restock |
| Cancel Order | — | Reservation released |

> **Exam focus:** Stock is **decremented** when a **shipment** is created, not when the order is placed (with MSI). Without MSI, stock decrements on invoice or order depending on configuration.

### 2.5 Customer Management

#### Customer Groups

- Default groups: **General, Not Logged In, Wholesale, Retailer**
- Used for: tier pricing, cart rules, catalog visibility, tax classes
- B2B companies can be assigned a default customer group

#### Customer Segments (Commerce only)

- Dynamic, rule-based grouping
- Used with: banners, cart rules, catalog rules
- Recalculated on schedule or customer action
- Rules can match: order history, cart contents, address attributes

> **Exam focus:** **Customer Segments** are a **Commerce (paid)** feature. Open Source only has static customer groups. This is a common exam trap.

#### Customer Account Features

| Feature | Open Source | Commerce |
|---|---|---|
| Basic account management | Yes | Yes |
| Wish Lists | Yes (1) | Yes (multiple) |
| Order History | Yes | Yes |
| Store Credit | No | Yes |
| Reward Points | No | Yes |
| Gift Registry | No | Yes |

### 2.6 Admin Configuration Architecture

#### Config Scope Hierarchy

```
Default (Global)
    |
    +-- Website
          |
          +-- Store
                |
                +-- Store View
```

- Settings cascade downward; child scopes can **override** parent
- "Use Default" checkbox restores inheritance
- Some settings are **global only** (cannot be overridden per website)

> **Exam focus:** Payment methods and shipping methods are configured at the **Website** scope, allowing different methods per website. Tax configuration is also **Website** scope.

#### Indexers

| Indexer | Triggers Reindex |
|---|---|
| Catalog Product Rule | Price rule save |
| Catalog Search | Product save, search config change |
| Category Products | Product/category assignment change |
| Product Price | Price, tier price, rule change |
| Stock | Inventory change |
| Customer Grid | Customer save |

```bash
# Reindex all
bin/magento indexer:reindex

# Reindex specific
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalog_product_price

# Check indexer status
bin/magento indexer:status

# Set to schedule mode (recommended for production)
bin/magento indexer:set-mode schedule catalog_product_price
```

> **Exam focus:** Indexers in **schedule** mode update via cron. Indexers in **real-time** mode update immediately on save, which can slow admin saves on large catalogs.

### 2.7 Caching Architecture

#### Cache Types

| Cache ID | What It Stores |
|---|---|
| `config` | XML configuration merges |
| `layout` | Layout XML compilation results |
| `block_html` | HTML block output |
| `collections` | DB collection results |
| `reflection` | API/method reflection data |
| `db_ddl` | DB schema cache |
| `compiled_config` | DI compiled configuration |
| `full_page` | FPC (Full Page Cache) |
| `translate` | Translation strings |

```bash
# Flush all cache
bin/magento cache:flush

# Clean specific cache type
bin/magento cache:clean full_page

# Enable/disable FPC
bin/magento cache:enable full_page
bin/magento cache:disable full_page
```

> **Exam focus:** `cache:clean` removes **invalid** cache entries. `cache:flush` removes **all** entries from the cache storage, including entries from other applications sharing the same Redis/Memcached instance.

### 2.8 Search Architecture

#### Elasticsearch / OpenSearch Configuration

```
Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog Search
    - Search Engine: Elasticsearch 7 / OpenSearch
    - Hostname, Port, Index Prefix
    - Minimum Query Length
    - Maximum Query Length
    - Allowed HTML Tags in Search Results
```

- **Elasticsearch/OpenSearch** is the only search engine available in Commerce 2.4.x (MySQL search was removed, not just deprecated)
- Index prefix allows multiple Magento instances to share one ES cluster

#### Search Weighting

| Attribute Setting | Effect |
|---|---|
| Use in Search = Yes | Attribute included in search index |
| Search Weight (1-10) | Higher = more relevant in results |
| Visible in Advanced Search | Shows field in advanced search form |

> **Exam focus:** The **Search Weight** attribute property controls relevance ranking in Elasticsearch. The default search weight for all attributes is **1**; administrators can customize weights per attribute to tune relevance.

---

## 3. Section 2 — Merchandising (10%)

### 3.1 Visual Merchandiser (Commerce)

- **Category > Products tab > Visual Merchandiser** (drag-and-drop grid)
- Automated sort rules:
  - New Products First
  - Low Stock First
  - Special Price First
  - Alphabetical by Name/SKU/Price
- **Pin** products to keep them in a fixed position regardless of automatic sort
- **Match by Rule** auto-adds products matching attribute conditions

> **Exam focus:** Visual Merchandiser is a **Commerce-only** feature. Products can be **pinned** to prevent them from being displaced by sort rules.

### 3.2 Related Products, Up-sells, Cross-sells

| Type | Where Displayed | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Related Products | Product page (below desc.) | Similar alternatives |
| Up-sells | Product page (widget area) | Higher-value alternatives |
| Cross-sells | Cart page | Complementary add-ons |

- Can be set **manually** (per product) or via **rules** (Commerce Product Relations)
- Rule-based relations: condition-based, apply globally, Commerce feature

> **Exam focus:** **Cross-sells** appear on the **cart page**, not the product page. This is a common exam trap between cross-sell and upsell placement.

### 3.3 Catalog Price Rules (Merchandising Context)

- Applied to catalog before cart
- Conditions: attribute set, category, product attributes, customer segment
- Actions: "Apply as percentage of original", "Apply as fixed amount", "Adjust final price to this percentage", "Adjust final price to discount value"
- Priority: lower number = higher priority
- **Discard subsequent rules**: prevents subsequent rules from applying (this is the actual admin UI label; sometimes referred to as "Stop Further Rules Processing" in documentation)

### 3.4 Layered Navigation

- Requires **Is Anchor = Yes** on categories (or Search results page)
- Filterable attributes: **Use in Layered Navigation** must be set
- Options:
  - Filterable (with results) — only shows options that return products
  - Filterable (no results) — shows all options even if zero results
  - No — not shown in layered nav

> **Exam focus:** An attribute must have **Use in Layered Navigation** set to "Filterable (with results)" or "Filterable (no results)" AND must be assigned to the product's attribute set to appear in faceted navigation.

### 3.5 Search Merchandising (Live Search — Commerce SaaS)

- **Live Search** replaces Elasticsearch for SaaS Commerce
- Features: Facets, Synonyms, Search Rules, Query Pinning, Rankings
- **Search Rules**: condition-based boost/bury/pin for specific search queries
- **Synonyms**: one-way (keyword maps to broader terms) or two-way (bidirectional)
- Powered by **Adobe Sensei** for relevance

> **Exam focus:** Live Search is **SaaS-only** (Commerce Cloud or SaaS Add-on). It uses its own indexing pipeline separate from the on-premise Elasticsearch integration.

---

## 4. Section 3 — Digital Marketing (4%)

> This is the smallest section (~2 questions). Focus on high-confidence topics only.

### 4.1 SEO Features

| Feature | Configuration Path |
|---|---|
| URL Rewrites | Marketing > SEO & Search > URL Rewrites |
| Meta Title/Desc | Product/Category > Search Engine Optimization |
| Canonical Tags | Stores > Config > Catalog > Search Engine Optimization |
| Sitemap | Marketing > SEO & Search > Site Map |
| robots.txt | Content > Design > Configuration > Search Engine Robots |
| Hreflang | Configured via store views/store codes |

> **Exam focus:** **Canonical URL for Products** should be enabled to prevent duplicate content from layered navigation filtering generating multiple URLs for the same product.

### 4.2 Google Integrations

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Google API
    - Google Analytics: UA / GA4
    - Google AdWords: Conversion ID, Color, Label, Value
    - Google Tag Manager: Container ID (Commerce only — module-google-tag-manager is EE)
```

- **GTM** (Google Tag Manager) replaces direct Analytics integration in modern setups
- Adobe Commerce supports **Google Analytics 4** via GTM or native integration

### 4.3 Email Marketing

- **Dotdigital** (formerly Dotmailer) is a commonly used email marketing integration for Adobe Commerce, but is NOT a native module — it is a third-party extension available via Marketplace
- Adobe Commerce natively supports **Magento Order Confirmation, Shipment, Invoice** transactional emails
- Email templates: **Marketing > Communications > Email Templates**
- Custom transactional email variables use `{{var order.increment_id}}` syntax

### 4.4 Customer Segmentation for Marketing

- Segments power: **banners**, **cart rules**, **catalog rules** targeting
- **Related Product Rules** (Commerce): condition-based, replace manual product linking
- **Private Sales / Invitations** (Commerce): invite-only events with restricted access

> **Exam focus:** For the Digital Marketing section, focus on the **distinction between native SEO tools** (sitemap, canonical, meta) and **third-party integrations** (GTM, GA4). The exam tests knowing which tool lives where.

---

## 5. Section 4 — Add-on Modules (18%)

> This section covers B2B, MSI, Page Builder, PWA Studio, and Adobe Commerce Services. Worth ~11 questions — strong here gives a major score boost.

### 5.1 B2B Module Suite

#### B2B Feature Matrix

| Feature | Description | Required Config |
|---|---|---|
| Company Accounts | Multi-user hierarchical accounts | Enable B2B Features |
| Shared Catalogs | Assign custom prices/products to company | Enable Shared Catalog |
| Negotiated Quotes | Quote workflow between buyer/seller | Enable Quotes |
| Purchase Orders | PO approval workflow | Enable Purchase Orders |
| Requisition Lists | Saved shopping lists (B2B wishlists) | Enable Requisition Lists |
| Quick Order | Order by SKU upload | Enable Quick Order (disabled by default) |
| Payment on Account | Credit limit-based payment | Enable Payment on Account |

> **Exam focus:** Enabling **Shared Catalog** automatically enables the **B2B Module** and creates a "Public Shared Catalog" that mirrors the default catalog. Disabling Shared Catalog reverts all customers to the default catalog visibility.

#### Company Hierarchy

```
Company Admin (top-level buyer account)
    |
    +-- Division / Team
          |
          +-- Buyer User 1
          +-- Buyer User 2
          |
          +-- Sub-Team
                |
                +-- Buyer User 3
```

- Company Admin manages users, roles, and permissions
- **Roles & Permissions** within a company are separate from Magento admin ACL
- Company can have a **credit limit** for Payment on Account

#### Negotiated Quotes Workflow

```
Buyer requests quote from cart
        |
        v
Quote status: New / Submitted to Seller
        |
        v
Seller reviews and adjusts (Admin > Sales > Quotes)
        |
        v
Quote status: Updated by Seller
        |
        v
Buyer reviews, accepts or counters
        |
        v
Quote status: Ordered (converted to order)
```

> **Exam focus:** Negotiated Quotes work **per website**. A quote cannot span multiple websites. Quotes expire based on the **Quote Lifetime** setting in B2B configuration.

#### Purchase Order Approval Workflow

- PO rules set by Company Admin: conditions (order amount, SKU, shipping cost) + approvers
- Approval chain can require **single or sequential approvers**
- Orders placed via PO go to **Pending Approval** status until approved
- Approved POs convert to standard orders

### 5.2 Multi-Source Inventory (MSI)

#### Core Concepts

```
Stock
  |
  +-- Source Assignment (many-to-many)
        |
        +-- Source 1 (Warehouse East)   qty: 50
        +-- Source 2 (Warehouse West)   qty: 30
        +-- Source 3 (Retail Store)     qty: 10
                                              |
                                              v
                                     Salable Qty = 90
                                     (minus reservations)
```

> **Exam focus:** **Salable Quantity** = Sum of assigned source quantities minus open order reservations. This is what customers see as "In Stock." It is NOT the physical quantity at any individual source.

#### MSI Algorithms

| Algorithm | Description | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| Source Priority | Deduct from sources in configured priority order | Simple single-zone fulfillment |
| Distance Priority | Deduct from nearest source to shipping address | Multi-warehouse geo-distributed |
| SSA (Source Selection Algorithm) | Interface — custom algorithms can implement this | Custom fulfillment logic |

```php
// Custom SSA implementation
interface SourceSelectionServiceInterface
{
    public function execute(
        InventoryRequestInterface $inventoryRequest,
        AlgorithmInterface $algorithm
    ): SourceSelectionResultInterface;
}
```

#### MSI Key Tables

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `inventory_source` | Source definitions |
| `inventory_stock` | Stock definitions |
| `inventory_source_item` | Source-level quantities |
| `inventory_reservation` | In-flight reservations |
| `inventory_stock_sales_channel` | Stock-to-website assignments |

> **Exam focus:** MSI reservations are created when an **order is placed** and compensated (removed) when a **shipment is created** or the order is **cancelled**.

### 5.3 Page Builder

#### Content Types

| Category | Content Types |
|---|---|
| Layout | Row, Column, Tab |
| Elements | Text, Heading, Buttons, Divider, HTML Code |
| Media | Image, Video, Banner, Slider, Map |
| Add Content | Block, Dynamic Block, Products |

> **Exam focus:** **Dynamic Blocks** (formerly Banners) in Page Builder are linked to **customer segments** and/or **cart/catalog price rules**. They display contextually based on customer data. Static blocks always display.

#### Page Builder Storage

- Content stored as **HTML with embedded JSON** data attributes in CMS page/block `content` field
- Editing via Page Builder serializes back to this format
- Not a separate storage engine — content lives in `cms_page.content` and `cms_block.content`

### 5.4 PWA Studio / Headless Commerce

#### Architecture

```
PWA Studio (React/GraphQL)
    |
    +-- Venia Storefront (reference implementation)
    +-- Peregrine (React hooks library)
    +-- Buildpack (Webpack build tools)
    +-- UPWARD (Unified Proxy/Router)
          |
          v
Adobe Commerce GraphQL API
          |
          v
Commerce Backend (catalog, cart, checkout, customer)
```

> **Exam focus:** PWA Studio uses **GraphQL exclusively** for data fetching — no REST API calls in the standard implementation. Adding B2B features to PWA requires **additional GraphQL resolvers**.

#### GraphQL Key Operations

```graphql
# Product query
query GetProduct($sku: String!) {
  products(filter: { sku: { eq: $sku } }) {
    items {
      name
      sku
      price_range {
        minimum_price {
          final_price {
            value
            currency
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

# Cart mutation
mutation AddToCart($cartId: String!, $sku: String!, $qty: Float!) {
  addSimpleProductsToCart(
    input: {
      cart_id: $cartId
      cart_items: [{ data: { quantity: $qty, sku: $sku } }]
    }
  ) {
    cart {
      items {
        product { name }
        quantity
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> **Exam focus:** Adobe Commerce SaaS services require a **SaaS Data Space** (configured in Commerce Admin via API keys). Each environment (production/sandbox) requires its own data space. Services sync data to **Adobe's cloud infrastructure** — not your server.

## 6. Section 5 — Systems Architecture (10%)

### 6.1 Adobe Commerce Architecture Stack

```
+------------------------------------------------+
|         Storefront (Luma / PWA / Headless)     |
+------------------------------------------------+
|         GraphQL API  |  REST API  |  SOAP API  |
+------------------------------------------------+
|                Application Layer               |
|  Modules | Plugins | Observers | Service Layer |
+------------------------------------------------+
|              Framework Layer                   |
|   DI | ORM | Cache | Queue | Session | Events  |
+------------------------------------------------+
|              Data Layer                        |
|   MySQL / MariaDB  |  Elasticsearch/OpenSearch  |
+------------------------------------------------+
|              Infrastructure                    |
|  PHP-FPM | Nginx/Apache | Varnish | Redis       |
+------------------------------------------------+
```

### 6.2 Deployment Architecture

#### Adobe Commerce Cloud Topology

```
                     Fastly CDN (Varnish)
                           |
                     Load Balancer
                    /              \
              Web Node 1        Web Node 2
              (PHP-FPM)         (PHP-FPM)
                    \              /
                     Shared NFS
                    /              \
              Redis (Session)   Redis (Cache/FPC)
                    \              /
                 MySQL (Master)
                       |
                 MySQL (Slave)
                       |
              Elasticsearch Cluster
```

> **Exam focus:** On Commerce Cloud **Pro** plan, the Staging environment has the **same topology** as Production. The Starter plan uses a simplified 4-branch model (master, staging, 2 dev branches).

#### Environment Types (Cloud)

| Environment | Pro Plan | Starter Plan |
|---|---|---|
| Production | 3-node cluster | Master branch |
| Staging | 3-node cluster | Staging branch |
| Development | Up to 50 envs | 2 dev branches |
| Integration | Separate tier | Same as dev |

### 6.3 Deployment Process

```bash
# Build phase (no DB access, no services)
composer install
bin/magento setup:di:compile
bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy
bin/magento module:enable --all

# Deploy phase (maintenance mode on)
bin/magento setup:upgrade
bin/magento setup:db:status

# Post-deploy phase (maintenance mode off)
bin/magento cache:flush
bin/magento indexer:reindex
```

> **Exam focus:** The **build phase** has **no access** to the database or services (Redis, Elasticsearch). `setup:di:compile` and `setup:static-content:deploy` run without a live DB connection. This is why static deploy configs must be committed.

#### Zero-Downtime Deployment (Blue/Green)

- Commerce Cloud Pro supports **warm-up** after deploy via post_deploy hooks
- Varnish/Fastly cache is flushed post-deploy, **not** during deployment
- Sessions are maintained via **Redis** shared between nodes

### 6.4 Performance Architecture

#### Full Page Cache (FPC)

```
Request arrives
    |
    v
Varnish/Fastly checks cache
    |-- HIT  --> Return cached response (no PHP execution)
    |
    +-- MISS --> PHP processes request
                    |
                    v
                 Response tagged with cache tags
                    |
                    v
                 Varnish stores response
```

#### Cache Tags & Invalidation

- Every cacheable page is tagged: `cat_c_1`, `cat_p_42`, `cms_p_3`
- When an entity is updated, Commerce sends **ban/purge requests** for relevant tags
- Varnish: uses `BAN` requests; Fastly: uses `Surrogate-Key` purge API

> **Exam focus:** Commerce uses **cache tags** (not URL-based cache keys) for intelligent invalidation. Updating product 42 invalidates only pages tagged `cat_p_42`, not all cached pages.

#### Redis Architecture

```
Redis Instance 1 (Sessions)
    - session.save_path = "tcp://redis:6379?database=0"

Redis Instance 2 (Default Cache)
    - backend = Cm_Cache_Backend_Redis
    - database = 1

Redis Instance 3 (FPC)
    - backend = Cm_Cache_Backend_Redis  
    - database = 2
    (or use Fastly for FPC on Cloud)
```

> **Exam focus:** Best practice is **separate Redis instances** (or databases) for sessions, cache, and FPC. Sharing can cause session eviction if cache fills Redis memory.

### 6.5 Message Queue Architecture

```
Producer (e.g., API request)
    |
    v
Message Publisher
    |
    v
RabbitMQ Exchange
    |
    v
Queue (inventory.reservations.update)
    |
    v
Consumer (bin/magento queue:consumers:start <consumer_name>)
    |
    v
Action executed asynchronously
```

#### Key Queues in Commerce

| Queue | Consumer | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `inventory.reservations.update` | `inventory.reservations.update` | MSI reservation updates |
| `async.operations.all` | `async.operations.all` | Bulk API operations |
| `product_action_attribute.update` | `product_action_attribute.update` | Mass product attribute updates |

```bash
# Start specific consumer (consumer name is a required argument)
bin/magento queue:consumers:start inventory.reservations.update

# List consumers
bin/magento queue:consumers:list
```

> **Exam focus:** RabbitMQ is **required for production MSI** environments. Without RabbitMQ, inventory reservation updates are processed synchronously, which causes performance issues at scale. Note: the `queue:consumers:start` command requires a specific consumer name — there is no `--all` flag.

### 6.6 Dependency Injection & Module Architecture

```xml
<!-- di.xml - Dependency injection configuration -->
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:ObjectManager/etc/config.xsd">

    <!-- Virtual type -->
    <virtualType name="Magento\Catalog\Model\ResourceModel\Product\Collection\Grid"
                 type="Magento\Catalog\Model\ResourceModel\Product\Collection">
        <arguments>
            <argument name="fetchStrategy"
                      xsi:type="object">Magento\Framework\Data\Collection\Db\FetchStrategy\Query
            </argument>
        </arguments>
    </virtualType>

    <!-- Plugin (interceptor) -->
    <type name="Magento\Catalog\Model\Product">
        <plugin name="my_product_plugin"
                type="MyVendor\MyModule\Plugin\ProductPlugin"
                sortOrder="10"
                disabled="false"/>
    </type>

    <!-- Preference (interface substitution) -->
    <preference for="Magento\Catalog\Api\ProductRepositoryInterface"
                type="MyVendor\MyModule\Model\ProductRepository"/>
</config>
```

> **Exam focus:** **Plugins (interceptors)** are the preferred extension point in Commerce architecture over **rewrites/preferences**. Plugins with `around` methods must call `$proceed()` to continue the chain. Multiple plugins can intercept the same method; `sortOrder` controls execution order.

## 7. Section 6 — Compliance (12%)

> Compliance covers GDPR, PCI DSS, accessibility, cookie consent, and data management. Worth ~7 questions — stronger than most candidates expect.

### 7.1 GDPR Compliance

#### Key GDPR Rights Implemented in Commerce

| Right | Commerce Feature | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Right to Access | Customer Data Download | Admin > Customer > Edit > Personal Information |
| Right to Erasure | Delete Customer Account | Admin or customer self-service |
| Right to Rectification | Customer account edit | Standard account functionality |
| Data Portability | Export customer data | Admin export |
| Consent Management | Cookie consent, email opt-in | Configured per store |

> **Exam focus:** Adobe Commerce provides **GDPR tools** for **data export and deletion** but does NOT automatically ensure compliance — merchants must configure and operationalize them. The platform provides *capability*, not *compliance*.

#### Privacy & Cookie Compliance

```
Stores > Configuration > General > Web > Default Cookie Settings
    - Cookie Lifetime (default: 3600 seconds)
    - Cookie Path (default: /)
    - Cookie Domain (optional)
    - Use HTTP Only (recommended: Yes)
    - Cookie Restriction Mode (GDPR cookie consent gate)
```

- **Cookie Restriction Mode**: When enabled, a consent notice is shown; cookies not set until accepted
- Analytics/tracking cookies not set until consent (when using restriction mode)

> **Exam focus:** **Cookie Restriction Mode** in Commerce blocks cookies from being set until the customer clicks "Allow Cookies." This is the built-in GDPR cookie consent mechanism. Disabling it removes the consent gate.

#### Data Retention & Cleanup

```bash
# Upgrade customer password hashes to latest algorithm
bin/magento customer:hash:upgrade
# Note: This command upgrades password hash algorithms — it does NOT anonymize or delete customer data for GDPR purposes.

# Sales data cleanup (via cron configuration)
# Stores > Configuration > Sales > Sales > Orders > Pending Payment Order Lifetime (minutes)
```

### 7.2 PCI DSS Compliance

#### PCI DSS Scope in Commerce

| Scope Item | Commerce Approach |
|---|---|
| Card Data | Never stored (tokenization via payment gateway) |
| HTTPS/TLS | Required for all checkout pages |
| Admin URL | Should be non-default URL |
| 2FA Admin | Required in Commerce 2.4+ |
| Admin Logging | Action log (Commerce feature) |
| File Permissions | 664/644 for files, 755 for directories |

> **Exam focus:** Adobe Commerce **does NOT store raw card data** by design. Payment tokens (vault) store gateway tokens, not card numbers. This is the key PCI scope reduction architecture.

#### Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)

- **Mandatory in Commerce 2.4+** for Admin access
- Supported providers: Google Authenticator, Authy, U2F (YubiKey), Duo Security
- Can be configured per admin user
- Bypass for API tokens (machine-to-machine): configured separately

```bash
# Disable 2FA for development (NOT for production)
bin/magento module:disable Magento_TwoFactorAuth

# Reset 2FA for a specific admin user
bin/magento security:tfa:reset admin@example.com google
```

> **Exam focus:** 2FA cannot be disabled in production without explicitly overriding security configurations. Adobe recommends using **IP allowlisting** at the server level instead of disabling 2FA.

#### Admin Security Settings

```
Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Admin > Security
    - Use Custom Admin URL: Yes (recommended)
    - Admin Base URL: https://example.com/secure_admin/
    - Add Secret Key to URLs: Yes
    - Login Captcha: Yes
    - Session Lifetime: 900 seconds (recommended)
    - Maximum Login Failures: 6
    - Lockout Time: 30 minutes
```

### 7.3 Accessibility Compliance (WCAG)

| Standard | Level | Commerce Support |
|---|---|---|
| WCAG 2.1 AA | Target | Luma theme designed for this |
| ARIA roles | Required | Commerce uses ARIA landmarks |
| Keyboard navigation | Required | Tab order maintained in Luma |
| Color contrast | 4.5:1 minimum | Default Luma compliant |

> **Exam focus:** Adobe Commerce's **Luma theme** is designed to meet **WCAG 2.1 AA** standards. Custom themes may need accessibility audits. The admin panel has separate (lower) accessibility coverage.

### 7.4 Data Privacy & Consumer Rights (CCPA)

| CCPA Right | Commerce Tool |
|---|---|
| Know what data is collected | Privacy policy page + data export |
| Delete personal data | Customer deletion + anonymization |
| Opt-out of data sale | Manual business process (not automated) |
| Non-discrimination | Platform does not facilitate |

> **Exam focus:** Commerce provides **similar tools for GDPR and CCPA** since both require data export and deletion capabilities. The **Privacy Policy** is a CMS page (identifier: `privacy-policy-cookie-restriction-mode`) managed under Content > Elements > Pages — it is not a system configuration field.

### 7.5 Security Patching & Compliance

```
Security Patch Release Cadence:
    - Full release: ~Feb, ~May, ~Aug, ~Oct (quarterly)
    - Security-only patches: As needed
    - Bug fix patches: Monthly

Patch Naming:
    - 2.4.6-p1 = Security patch on top of 2.4.6
    - 2.4.7   = Full release
```

#### Security Scan Tool

- **Adobe Commerce Security Scan**: Free tool at account.magento.com
- Scans for: known vulnerabilities, malware, patching status
- **Weekly scans recommended**; can be scheduled
- Results reported to admin email

> **Exam focus:** The **Security Scan Tool** is free, SaaS-based, and scans **public-facing URLs** — it does not require server access. It detects missing patches by checking for known vulnerability indicators in page responses.

### 7.6 Content Security Policy (CSP)

```xml
<!-- etc/csp_whitelist.xml - Add trusted domains -->
<csp_whitelist xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
               xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:module:Magento_Csp/etc/csp_whitelist.xsd">
    <policies>
        <policy id="script-src">
            <values>
                <value id="my-cdn" type="host">https://cdn.example.com</value>
            </values>
        </policy>
    </policies>
</csp_whitelist>
```

- Commerce 2.4.0+ ships with CSP in **report-only mode** by default
- Commerce 2.4.7+ has stricter CSP defaults
- Custom JS/inline scripts may break with CSP enabled — require nonce or whitelist

> **Exam focus:** CSP violations in Commerce can break payment iframes and third-party scripts. The fix is to add the domain to `csp_whitelist.xml`, NOT to disable CSP entirely.

### 7.7 Admin Action Log (Commerce)

- **System > Action Logs > Report** (Commerce feature, not Open Source)
- Logs: admin user, action, date/time, IP address
- Configurable which actions to log: **Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Admin > Admin Actions Logging**

## 10. Quick-Reference Checklist

### Core Features (46%)

- [ ] **Product Types:** Simple, Configurable (child inventory), Grouped, Bundle (fixed/dynamic price), Virtual, Downloadable, Gift Card (Virtual/Physical/Combined)
- [ ] **Configurable products:** inventory tracked at child (simple) level, not parent
- [ ] **Attribute scope:** Default > Website > Store > Store View; some settings are global-only
- [ ] **Price hierarchy:** Base > Special > Tier > Group > Catalog Rule > Cart Rule
- [ ] **Catalog Price Rules:** applied pre-cart, no coupon code, conditions-based
- [ ] **Cart Price Rules:** applied at checkout, can require coupon code
- [ ] **Discard subsequent rules:** prevents lower-priority rules from applying
- [ ] **MAP:** display feature only — does NOT enforce minimum selling price
- [ ] **Authorize only:** no charge until invoice created; standard for physical goods
- [ ] **Order State vs Status:** State = system-internal (fixed); Status = merchant-label (customizable)
- [ ] **Stock decrement:** occurs at shipment creation with MSI
- [ ] **Credit memo:** creates refund document; optionally restocks inventory
- [ ] **Customer Segments:** Commerce-only, dynamic rules, powers banners/cart/catalog rules
- [ ] **Customer Groups:** available in both Open Source and Commerce
- [ ] **Is Anchor = Yes:** category aggregates products from subcategories in layered nav
- [ ] **Filterable attribute:** must have "Use in Layered Navigation" set + assigned to attribute set
- [ ] **Indexer modes:** real-time (on save) vs. schedule (via cron)
- [ ] **cache:clean vs cache:flush:** clean = invalid entries only; flush = all entries in backend
- [ ] **Elasticsearch/OpenSearch:** required for Commerce 2.4.x (MySQL search removed)
- [ ] **Search Weight:** controls attribute relevance in ES results (1–10 scale, default 1 for all attributes)

### Merchandising (10%)

- [ ] **Visual Merchandiser:** Commerce-only; drag-and-drop category product sorting
- [ ] **Pin product:** locks position in Visual Merchandiser regardless of sort rules
- [ ] **Cross-sells:** appear on **cart page** (not product page)
- [ ] **Related Products:** appear on product page (below description)
- [ ] **Up-sells:** appear on product page (sidebar/widget)
- [ ] **Live Search:** SaaS-only, Commerce feature, AI-powered, replaces Elasticsearch frontend
- [ ] **Synonyms:** one-way or two-way; managed in Live Search admin panel
- [ ] **Layered nav requires:** Is Anchor = Yes + filterable attribute + product assigned to category

### Digital Marketing (4%)

- [ ] **Canonical URLs:** prevent duplicate content from layered nav filter URLs
- [ ] **URL Rewrites:** manual or auto-generated; Marketing > SEO & Search
- [ ] **Cookie Restriction Mode:** GDPR gate — blocks all cookies until user accepts
- [ ] **GTM:** replaces direct GA integration; Container ID in Sales > Google API
- [ ] **Dotdigital:** third-party email marketing integration (not a native module)
- [ ] **Transactional email variables:** `{{var order.increment_id}}` syntax in templates

### Add-on Modules (18%)

- [ ] **B2B requires enabling:** Company, Shared Catalog, Quotes, POs, Quick Order are all toggle-enabled
- [ ] **Shared Catalog enabled:** creates Public Shared Catalog mirroring default catalog
- [ ] **Shared Catalog disabled:** all customers revert to default catalog
- [ ] **Negotiated Quotes:** per-website, buyer-initiated from cart, quote lifetime configurable
- [ ] **PO approval workflow:** rules set by Company Admin; pending approval before order conversion
- [ ] **Requisition Lists:** saved shopping lists (B2B), different from Wish Lists
- [ ] **Payment on Account:** credit-limit based, B2B-only payment method
- [ ] **MSI Salable Qty:** sum of source quantities minus open reservations
- [ ] **MSI reservation:** created on order place, compensated on shipment or cancel
- [ ] **Distance Priority algorithm:** routes orders to nearest source geographically
- [ ] **RabbitMQ:** required for production MSI environments (async reservation processing)
- [ ] **Page Builder — Dynamic Blocks:** linked to customer segments and/or price rules
- [ ] **Page Builder content:** stored as HTML+JSON in cms_page.content field
- [ ] **PWA Studio:** React + GraphQL only (no REST in standard implementation)
- [ ] **SaaS Data Space:** required for all Adobe Commerce SaaS services; separate per environment
- [ ] **Product Recommendations:** requires behavioral event tracking; 9 recommendation types
- [ ] **Cold-start recs:** fall back to "Most Viewed" before enough behavioral data

### Systems Architecture (10%)

- [ ] **Build phase:** NO database access; runs composer, di:compile, static:deploy
- [ ] **Deploy phase:** runs setup:upgrade; maintenance mode on
- [ ] **Post-deploy phase:** cache flush, indexer reindex; maintenance off
- [ ] **Commerce Cloud Pro:** Staging mirrors Production topology (3-node cluster)
- [ ] **Cache tags:** enable surgical invalidation (e.g., update product 42 → only purge `cat_p_42`)
- [ ] **Varnish uses BAN:** Fastly uses Surrogate-Key purge API — same concept, different impl.
- [ ] **Redis best practice:** separate instances/databases for Sessions, Cache, FPC
- [ ] **Plugin (interceptor):** preferred extension point over preference/rewrite
- [ ] **Plugin `around`:** must call `$proceed()` to continue the interception chain
- [ ] **Preference:** replaces entire class; use only when plugin insufficient
- [ ] **`sortOrder` in plugins:** lower number executes first (before/around/after)

### Compliance (12%)

- [ ] **GDPR tools:** data export (download), customer deletion, anonymization
- [ ] **Commerce provides capability, NOT compliance** — merchants must operationalize
- [ ] **Cookie Restriction Mode:** gate that blocks ALL cookies until user consents
- [ ] **PCI: no raw card data stored** — payment tokens only (vault = gateway token)
- [ ] **2FA mandatory:** Commerce 2.4+ requires 2FA for admin; 4 supported providers
- [ ] **Admin security best practices:** custom URL, secret key, session timeout, login lockout
- [ ] **CSP:** add domains to `csp_whitelist.xml`; do NOT disable CSP in production
- [ ] **CSP in Commerce 2.4.0:** report-only by default; stricter in 2.4.7+
- [ ] **Security Scan Tool:** free, SaaS, scans public-facing URLs, no server access required
- [ ] **Patching cadence:** quarterly full releases; `-pN` suffix = security patch
- [ ] **CCPA:** same Commerce tools as GDPR (export/delete); opt-out of data sale is manual
- [ ] **WCAG 2.1 AA:** Luma theme target standard; admin panel has lower coverage
- [ ] **Admin Action Log:** Commerce-only feature; logs admin actions with user + IP + timestamp

### Open Source vs. Commerce (Cross-Section — HIGH EXAM VALUE)

- [ ] **Commerce ONLY:** Customer Segments, Visual Merchandiser, B2B Suite, Store Credit, Reward Points, Content Staging, Admin Action Log, Product Recommendations, Live Search, Multiple Wish Lists, RMA, Gift Cards, Gift Registry, Private Sales
- [ ] **Both (Open Source + Commerce):** Customer Groups, Basic Wish List (single), Order History, Checkout, Catalog Price Rules, Cart Price Rules, Elasticsearch, REST/GraphQL APIs, Layered Navigation, Page Builder

flashcards.question: What are the six exam sections for AD0-E708 and their approximate weights?
flashcards.answer: Core Features: 46% (~28 questions), Merchandising: 10% (~6 questions), Digital Marketing: 4% (~2 questions), Add-on Modules: 18% (~11 questions), Systems Architecture: 10% (~6 questions), Compliance: 12% (~7 questions). Core Features alone accounts for nearly half the exam.
flashcards.hint: One section dominates with almost half the exam weight.

flashcards.question: What are the three types of Gift Cards in Adobe Commerce, and which edition supports them?
flashcards.answer: Gift Cards come in three types: Virtual (no shipping required), Physical (requires shipping), and Combined (customer chooses). Gift Cards are an EE-only feature — they are not available in Magento Open Source.
flashcards.hint: Not all gift cards are digital — one type requires a shipping address.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between order State and order Status in Adobe Commerce?
flashcards.answer: State is a fixed, system-level code (e.g., new, processing, complete) that cannot be customized. Status is a configurable, merchant-visible label (e.g., Pending, Processing) that can be customized and mapped to states. Multiple statuses can map to one state.
flashcards.hint: One is hardcoded in the system; the other is a customizable label.

flashcards.question: At what point is stock decremented in Adobe Commerce when MSI is enabled?
flashcards.answer: With MSI enabled, stock is decremented when a shipment is created, not when the order is placed. At order placement, a reservation is created that reduces salable quantity, but the physical source quantity is only deducted upon shipment creation.
flashcards.hint: Think about when physical inventory actually leaves the warehouse.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between cache:clean and cache:flush in Magento?
flashcards.answer: cache:clean removes only invalid (Magento-tagged) cache entries. cache:flush removes all entries from the cache storage backend, including entries from other applications sharing the same Redis/Memcached instance. Flush is the more aggressive option.
flashcards.hint: One is surgical and tag-based; the other empties the entire storage.

flashcards.question: What search engine is required in Adobe Commerce 2.4.x, and what happened to MySQL search?
flashcards.answer: Elasticsearch or OpenSearch is the only search engine available in Commerce 2.4.x. MySQL search was fully removed (not just deprecated). The Search Weight attribute property (1-10 scale) controls relevance ranking in search results.
flashcards.hint: A dedicated search service is now mandatory, not optional.

flashcards.question: Where do cross-sell products appear in Adobe Commerce, and how does this differ from related products?
flashcards.answer: Cross-sells appear on the cart page as complementary add-on suggestions. Related products appear on the product page below the description as similar alternatives. Up-sells also appear on the product page as higher-value alternatives.
flashcards.hint: Think about where in the shopping journey each type makes sense — browsing vs ready to buy.

flashcards.question: What is MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) in Adobe Commerce — a price enforcement or a display feature?
flashcards.answer: MAP is a display feature only, not an enforcement mechanism. It shows a 'Click for price' popup on the category page but does NOT prevent selling below the minimum advertised price. The actual selling price can still be lower than MAP.
flashcards.hint: The word 'advertised' is key — it controls what price is shown, not what price is charged.

flashcards.question: What does enabling Shared Catalog automatically do in Adobe Commerce B2B?
flashcards.answer: Enabling Shared Catalog automatically enables the B2B Module and creates a 'Public Shared Catalog' that mirrors the default catalog. Disabling Shared Catalog reverts all customers to the default catalog visibility. Only one shared catalog can be assigned per company.
flashcards.hint: Turning on this feature changes the default catalog experience for everyone, including B2C customers.

flashcards.question: What does Salable Quantity mean in MSI, and how is it calculated?
flashcards.answer: Salable Quantity is the aggregated available quantity across all Sources assigned to a Stock, minus open order reservations. It is what customers see as 'In Stock.' It is NOT the physical quantity at any individual source. Formula: Salable Qty = Sum of source quantities - reservations.
flashcards.hint: It accounts for orders that have been placed but not yet shipped.

flashcards.question: Which features are exclusive to Adobe Commerce (EE) and NOT available in Magento Open Source?
flashcards.answer: EE-only features include: Customer Segments, Visual Merchandiser, B2B Suite, Store Credit, Reward Points, Content Staging, Admin Action Log, Product Recommendations, Live Search, Multiple Wish Lists, RMA, Gift Cards, Gift Registry, and Private Sales.
flashcards.hint: If a feature sounds 'premium' or enterprise-oriented, it is probably EE-only.

flashcards.question: What is the recommended payment gateway integration approach for minimizing PCI compliance scope?
flashcards.answer: Hosted payment pages (like PayPal Express, Stripe Checkout) or JavaScript SDK with iframes (like Braintree hosted fields) minimize PCI scope to SAQ A or SAQ A-EP. Direct API integration where card data is sent to Magento requires full SAQ D compliance, which is the most burdensome.
flashcards.hint: The less card data that touches your server, the simpler your PCI compliance.

flashcards.question: What happens during the build phase of an Adobe Commerce Cloud deployment?
flashcards.answer: During the build phase, there is NO access to the database or services (Redis, Elasticsearch). The phase runs composer install, setup:di:compile, and setup:static-content:deploy. This is why static deploy configurations must be committed to the codebase.
flashcards.hint: Think about what can run without any live service connections.

flashcards.question: How does Adobe Commerce use cache tags for invalidation, and why is this better than URL-based invalidation?
flashcards.answer: Commerce tags every cacheable page with entity-specific tags like cat_p_42 for product 42. When that product is updated, Commerce sends purge requests for only that tag. This enables surgical invalidation — updating product 42 invalidates only pages displaying that product, not all cached pages.
flashcards.hint: Tags allow precise targeting rather than clearing entire URL patterns.

studyNotes.content:
# Adobe Commerce (Magento) — Weak Area Deep Dive Study Notes
### Adobe Commerce Business Practitioner Expert (AD0-E708) | Week 4

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Core Features: Product Types & Order Lifecycle](#1-core-features-product-types--order-lifecycle)
2. [Core Features: Payment Methods](#2-core-features-payment-methods)
3. [Core Features: Shipping Configuration](#3-core-features-shipping-configuration)
4. [Merchandising: Catalog Price Rules](#4-merchandising-catalog-price-rules)
5. [Merchandising: Cart Price Rules](#5-merchandising-cart-price-rules)
6. [Merchandising: Pricing Hierarchy](#6-merchandising-pricing-hierarchy)
7. [Add-on Modules: B2B Flow](#7-add-on-modules-b2b-flow)
8. [Add-on Modules: MSI Reservations](#8-add-on-modules-msi-reservations)
9. [Add-on Modules: Live Search vs Native Search](#9-add-on-modules-live-search-vs-native-search)
10. [Systems Architecture: Scope Hierarchy](#10-systems-architecture-scope-hierarchy)
11. [Systems Architecture: Headless Concepts](#11-systems-architecture-headless-concepts)
12. [Compliance: GDPR](#12-compliance-gdpr)
13. [Compliance: PCI DSS](#13-compliance-pci-dss)
14. [Compliance: Admin Permissions & ACL](#14-compliance-admin-permissions--acl)
15. [Hands-On Sandbox Verification Checklist](#15-hands-on-sandbox-verification-checklist)
16. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Core Features: Product Types & Order Lifecycle

### 1.1 Product Types

Adobe Commerce supports **seven product types** (six in Open Source, plus Gift Card in Commerce).

| Product Type | Key Characteristics | Inventory Tracked? | Child Products? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Simple** | Single SKU, no variants | Yes | No |
| **Configurable** | Parent + child simples (attributes) | On children only | Yes (Simple) |
| **Grouped** | Collection of simples shown together | On each simple | Yes (Simple) |
| **Bundle** | Customer builds their own product | On components | Yes (Simple/Virtual) |
| **Virtual** | No shipping required (services, warranties) | Yes | No |
| **Downloadable** | Digital files/links, no shipping | Yes | No |
| **Gift Card** | Virtual, Physical, or Combined (EE only) | Varies by type | No |

> **Exam focus:**
> - Configurable products track inventory **on child simples, not the parent**
> - Grouped products do NOT have a single combined price — each item adds to cart independently
> - Bundle products can have **fixed or dynamic** pricing
> - Virtual products do not trigger shipping address collection (by default)
> - Downloadable products have **Links** (the actual file) and **Samples** (previews)
> - Gift Cards can be Virtual (no shipping), Physical (with shipping), or Combined

#### Configurable Product Attribute Requirements

```php
// Attributes used for configurable variations must be:
// 1. scope = global
// 2. type = dropdown (or visual swatch / text swatch)
// 3. user-defined (not system attributes)
//
// Eligibility is AUTOMATIC based on these criteria — there is NO
// "Use to Create Configurable Product" toggle in the admin UI.
// ConfigurableAttributeHandler checks: frontend_input=select, is_user_defined=1, is_global=SCOPE_GLOBAL

// Check attribute properties via: Stores > Attributes > Product > [attribute] > Properties
```

#### Bundle Pricing Modes

```
Fixed Price Bundle:
  Parent has fixed price regardless of options chosen

Dynamic Price Bundle:
  Price = sum of selected option prices
  Can have Special Price applied as % discount to total
```

> **Exam focus:** Dynamic-price bundles **cannot** use catalog price rules — only special prices and customer group pricing apply.

---

### 1.2 Order Lifecycle (State vs. Status)

Understanding the difference between **State** (system-level, immutable set) and **Status** (merchant-configurable label) is critical.

```
Order Created
     |
     v
[new]               <- State: new | "Pending" status | customer placed order
     |
     v
[pending_payment]   <- State: pending_payment | awaiting payment gateway response
     |
     v
[processing]        <- State: processing | payment captured / invoiced
     |
     v
[complete]          <- State: complete | shipped + invoice exists
     |
     v
[closed]            <- State: closed | refunded (credit memo issued)
     |
     v
[canceled]          <- State: canceled | order canceled before fulfillment
     |
     v
[holded]            <- State: holded | merchant placed on hold
```

> Note: The first order state is `new` (not `pending`). "Pending" is a **status** that maps to the `new` state. There are 8 states total: new, pending_payment, processing, complete, closed, canceled, holded, payment_review.

#### Order Documents

| Document | Triggers | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Invoice** | Captures payment | Moves order to `processing` |
| **Shipment** | Records shipping | Triggers tracking, moves toward `complete` |
| **Credit Memo** | Issues refund | Moves order to `closed`; can be online or offline |

> **Exam focus:**
> - An order reaches `complete` state only when **both** an invoice AND a shipment exist
> - `closed` state = a credit memo was issued (full refund)
> - `canceled` state: inventory is **returned to stock** automatically if configured
> - You cannot create a Credit Memo without first creating an Invoice

#### Order Cancellation & Inventory

```
Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Inventory
  > Automatically Return Credit Memo Item to Stock

  This controls whether credit memo items are restocked automatically.
  Field ID: auto_return, showInDefault=1 only (global scope).

  Note: Order cancellation inventory return is handled separately
  by MSI's CancelOrderItemObserver, which automatically releases
  reservations when an order is canceled.
```

---

## 2. Core Features: Payment Methods

### 2.1 Payment Method Architecture

All payment methods implement `Magento\Payment\Model\Method\AbstractMethod` (legacy) or the newer **Payment Provider Gateway** framework.

```
Payment Gateway Framework (recommended):
  - Command Pool  -> maps actions (authorize, capture, void, refund)
  - Validators    -> validates request/response
  - Builders      -> builds request data
  - Transferfactory -> sends request to gateway
  - Handler       -> processes response
```

### 2.2 Common Payment Methods

| Method | Auth Only | Auth+Capture | Offline? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Check / Money Order** | - | - | Yes |
| **Bank Transfer** | - | - | Yes |
| **Zero Subtotal Checkout** | - | - | Yes (auto) |
| **Braintree** | Yes | Yes | No |
| **PayPal Express** | Yes | Yes | No |
| **PayPal Payments Pro** | Yes | Yes | No |

> **Exam focus:**
> - **Authorize only** = payment is reserved but not captured until invoice is created
> - **Authorize and Capture** = payment captured immediately at order placement
> - **Offline payments** (Check/MO, Bank Transfer) create an invoice with status `pending` — payment must be manually marked
> - **Zero Subtotal Checkout** activates automatically when order total = $0 (e.g., 100% coupon)

### 2.3 Payment Action Settings

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > [Method]
  > Payment Action:
    - "Authorize Only"      : creates authorization transaction
    - "Authorize and Capture": creates auth + capture transaction
```

### 2.4 Payment Method Scope

```
Payment methods can be configured at:
  - Default (global)
  - Website level

They CANNOT be configured at Store or Store View level
```

> **Exam focus:** Payment method availability is **website-scoped**, not store view scoped.

---

## 3. Core Features: Shipping Configuration

### 3.1 Carriers Overview

| Carrier | Type | Requires Account? |
|---|---|---|
| **Flat Rate** | Built-in | No |
| **Free Shipping** | Built-in | No |
| **Table Rates** | Built-in (CSV import) | No |
| **UPS** | Real-time | Yes (API key) |
| **USPS** | Real-time | Yes (user ID) |
| **FedEx** | Real-time | Yes (API key) |
| **DHL** | Real-time | Yes |

### 3.2 Table Rates

Table rates use **conditions** to determine shipping cost. Three condition types:

```
Weight vs. Destination
Price vs. Destination
# of Items vs. Destination
```

Table Rate CSV columns (no City column — only 5 columns):

```csv
Country,Region/State,Zip/Postal Code,Weight (and above),Shipping Price
US,*,*,0,5.00
US,CA,*,0,7.50
```

> **Exam focus:**
> - Table rates are imported as **CSV per website** (the import/export buttons only appear at website scope)
> - Wildcard `*` matches any value in that column
> - You can only use **one condition type** at a time per store
> - There is NO City column — only Country, Region/State, Zip/Postal Code, the dynamic condition column, and Shipping Price

### 3.3 Shipping Scope

```
Stores > Configuration > Sales > Shipping Settings
  - Scope: Website level

Origin address: set at website scope
```

### 3.4 Free Shipping

Two ways to trigger free shipping:
1. **Carrier: Free Shipping** — minimum order amount threshold
2. **Cart Price Rule** — apply free shipping as a rule action

> **Exam focus:** When a Cart Price Rule grants free shipping, it overrides carrier calculations entirely for that cart. Note: the Free Shipping carrier does NOT need to be enabled for cart price rule free shipping to work.

### 3.5 Shipping Method at Checkout

```
Checkout flow:
  1. Customer enters shipping address
  2. Magento calls all enabled carriers with address + cart weight/price
  3. Carriers return available methods + rates
  4. Customer selects method
  5. Rate saved to quote, then to order as shipping_method field
```

---

## 4. Merchandising: Catalog Price Rules

### 4.1 How Catalog Price Rules Work

Catalog price rules apply **before** the product is added to cart. They modify the displayed price on the catalog/product page.

```
Flow:
  Product Price
       |
       v
  [Catalog Price Rule Applied]  <- changes "final price" in index
       |
       v
  Customer sees discounted price on PDP/PLP
```

> **Exam focus:** Catalog price rules run via **indexer** (`catalogrule_product` and `catalogrule_product_price` tables). Changes require re-indexing to take effect.

### 4.2 Rule Conditions

```
Marketing > Promotions > Catalog Price Rule  (note: singular in admin menu)

Conditions (IF):
  - Attribute Set
  - Category
  - Product Attribute (SKU, price, weight, etc.)
  - Combinations with AND / OR logic

Actions (THEN):
  - Apply as percentage of original
  - Apply as fixed amount discount
  - Adjust final price to this percentage
  - Adjust final price to discount value
```

| Action Type | Example | Result on $100 product |
|---|---|---|
| By percentage of orig price | 10% | $90 |
| By fixed amount | $10 off | $90 |
| To percentage of orig price | 90% | $90 |
| To fixed amount | $90 | $90 |

> **Exam focus:**
> - Catalog rules apply to **Customer Groups** — you can target specific groups
> - Rules have **From Date / To Date** — scheduling is built in
> - Multiple catalog rules: **lowest price wins** (not stackable by default)
> - Catalog rules do NOT apply to Bundle (dynamic price) or Grouped product totals directly

### 4.3 Priority & Discard Subsequent Rules

```
Lower priority number = applied FIRST
"Discard Subsequent Rules" = stop processing further rules once this one matches
(This is the actual admin UI label — sometimes referred to as "Stop Further Rules Processing" in documentation)
```

---

## 5. Merchandising: Cart Price Rules

### 5.1 Cart Price Rules vs. Catalog Price Rules

| Feature | Catalog Price Rule | Cart Price Rule |
|---|---|---|
| When applied | Before cart (index) | During checkout (cart) |
| Coupon code | No | Optional |
| Targets | Products | Cart/line items |
| Free shipping | No | Yes |
| Buy X Get Y | No | Yes |

### 5.2 Cart Price Rule Conditions

```
Marketing > Promotions > Cart Price Rules

Conditions tab (IF):
  - Cart attributes (subtotal, qty, weight, payment method, shipping method)
  - Product attributes (SKU, category, attribute)
  - Customer segment (EE only)

Actions tab (THEN):
  - Percent of product price discount
  - Fixed amount discount
  - Fixed amount discount for whole cart
  - Buy X get Y free
  - Free shipping (options: for matching items, for shipment with matching items)
```

### 5.3 Coupon Codes

```
Coupon Types:
  - No Coupon       : rule applies automatically when conditions met
  - Specific Coupon : requires customer to enter code
  - Auto Generated  : system generates unique codes (available in BOTH CE and EE)

Auto-generation settings:
  - Code Length
  - Code Format (alphanumeric, alpha, numeric)
  - Code Prefix / Suffix
  - Dash Every X Characters
```

> **Exam focus:**
> - **Auto-generated coupons** are available in both Open Source and Commerce — the Generate controller exists in base module-sales-rule
> - A single cart price rule can generate **multiple unique coupon codes** (for campaigns)
> - `Uses Per Coupon` limits how many times a single code can be used globally
> - `Uses Per Customer` limits how many times per customer account

### 5.4 Cart Rule Priority & Combinations

```
Rules processed in priority order (lower number = higher priority)
"Discard subsequent rules" = prevents lower-priority rules from applying
(Same label as catalog price rules)

Discount stacking behavior:
  - By default, cart rules CAN stack
  - "Discard subsequent rules" prevents stacking
```

> **Exam focus:** Unlike catalog rules, cart price rules **can stack** unless explicitly stopped.

---

## 6. Merchandising: Pricing Hierarchy

### 6.1 Complete Price Waterfall

Adobe Commerce evaluates prices in a defined order. The **lowest applicable price** is generally shown.

```
Price Evaluation Order (highest priority first):

1. Special Price          (date-ranged, beats everything except...)
2. Tier Price / Group Price (customer group specific)
3. Catalog Rule Price     (from catalog price rule index)
4. Regular Price          (base product price)

Final displayed price = lowest of all applicable prices
```

> **Exam focus:** Special Price does NOT always win — if a Tier Price is lower than the Special Price, the **tier price wins**.

### 6.2 Price Types Defined

| Price Type | Location in Admin | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Base Price** | Product > Price field | Default price |
| **Special Price** | Product > Special Price | Needs From/To dates (optional) |
| **Tier Price** | Product > Advanced Pricing | Qty breaks + customer groups |
| **Group Price** | Part of Tier Price (qty=1) | Per customer group, no qty break |
| **MSRP** | Product > Advanced Pricing | Display only, no enforcement |

### 6.3 Tier Pricing

```
Advanced Pricing > Tier Price:
  - All Groups / Specific Group
  - Minimum Qty
  - Price (fixed amount or percentage discount)

Example:
  Qty 1-4  : $100 (base)
  Qty 5-9  : $90  (tier)
  Qty 10+  : $80  (tier)
```

### 6.4 Customer Group Pricing

```
Customer Groups:
  - NOT LOGGED IN (Guest)
  - General
  - Wholesale
  - Retailer
  (Custom groups can be created)

Pricing can vary by group via:
  1. Tier price with qty = 1
  2. Catalog price rules scoped to a customer group
```

> **Exam focus:**
> - Customer group pricing is set via **Tier Price with qty = 1** in the product's Advanced Pricing tab
> - B2B **Shared Catalog** overrides all of the above with its own pricing layer

---

## 7. Add-on Modules: B2B Flow

### 7.1 B2B Module Overview

Adobe Commerce B2B (`magento/module-b2b`) includes several sub-features that can be enabled independently.

```
B2B Feature Set:
  +---------------------------+
  | Company Accounts          |
  | Shared Catalog            |
  | Negotiable Quotes         |
  | Quick Order               |
  | Requisition Lists         |
  | Purchase Orders           |
  +---------------------------+
```

### 7.2 Company Account Structure

```
Company Account Hierarchy:

  Company Admin
       |
       +-- Sales Manager (role)
       |        |
       |        +-- Sales Rep 1
       |        +-- Sales Rep 2
       |
       +-- Buyer (role)
            |
            +-- Buyer 1
            +-- Buyer 2

Each user = a standard Magento customer account
Roles & permissions defined by Company Admin
```

> **Exam focus:**
> - Company Admin is a **regular customer** with elevated permissions
> - A customer can only belong to **one company**
> - Company accounts must be **approved** by the merchant admin before activation

### 7.3 Shared Catalog

```
Two types:
  1. Public Shared Catalog   : replaces the default catalog for guests/non-company customers
  2. Custom Shared Catalog   : assigned to specific companies

Shared Catalog controls:
  - Which products are visible
  - Custom pricing per product (overrides all other price rules for that company)
  - Category visibility
```

> **Exam focus:**
> - Shared Catalog pricing **overrides** tier prices, special prices, and catalog rules for assigned companies
> - You cannot have different Shared Catalog prices per store view — it's scoped to **website**
> - Disabling B2B Shared Catalog reverts to standard pricing

### 7.4 Negotiable Quotes

```
Flow:
  Buyer adds items to cart
       |
       v
  Buyer requests a quote (submits cart as quote)
       |
       v
  Quote enters "Submitted" state
       |
       v
  Sales Rep reviews, can:
    - Adjust line item prices
    - Add discounts (% or fixed)
    - Add expiration date
    - Decline or send back
       |
       v
  Quote in "Pending" -> "Updated" -> "Ordered"
       |
       v
  Buyer accepts, converts to order
```

Quote States:

| State | Who can act |
|---|---|
| New / Submitted | Seller reviews |
| Pending | Awaiting seller response |
| Updated | Seller sent back to buyer |
| Open | Buyer has draft |
| Ordered | Converted to order |
| Closed | Expired or declined |

> **Exam focus:** Negotiable Quotes require **Company Accounts** to be enabled (depends on company_active, NOT on Shared Catalog). Shared Catalog is a separate feature that can be enabled independently.

### 7.5 Purchase Orders

```
Enables approval workflow for B2B purchases:

  Buyer places order as Purchase Order
       |
       v
  PO enters approval queue based on rules:
    - Order amount > $X -> requires approval
    - Shipping cost > $X -> requires approval
    - Number of SKUs > N -> requires approval
       |
       v
  Approver: Approve / Reject / Comment
       |
       v
  Approved PO converts to real order
```

> **Exam focus:** Purchase Order approval rules are configured by the **Company Admin**, not the merchant admin. Only three condition types exist: Order Total, Shipping Cost, and Number of SKUs — there is no category-based condition.

### 7.6 Requisition Lists

- Saved lists of products (like wishlists but for repeat B2B purchasing)
- A customer can have **multiple** requisition lists
- Items added directly to cart from requisition list
- **Not order-based** — just a saved product list

### 7.7 Quick Order

- Allows B2B buyers to order by **SKU** (upload CSV or type SKUs)
- Bypasses normal product browsing
- Requires customer to be logged in
- Must be enabled via Stores > Config > General > B2B Features > Enable Quick Order (disabled by default)

---

## 8. Add-on Modules: MSI Reservations

### 8.1 MSI Architecture Overview

Multi-Source Inventory (MSI) decouples physical stock locations from sales channels.

```
Key Concepts:

  Source     = Physical location (warehouse, store, supplier)
  Stock      = Virtual pool of sources assigned to a sales channel
  Sales Channel = Website (or custom channel)

Relationship:
  Sources --> (assigned to) --> Stock --> (assigned to) --> Sales Channel (Website)
```

### 8.2 Sources

```
Stores > Inventory > Sources

Each source has:
  - Name, Code (immutable after creation)
  - Address (for distance priority algorithm)
  - Enabled / Disabled
  - Carrier-specific settings
  - Source items: [SKU] -> [qty at this source]

Default Source: cannot be deleted, used for non-MSI-aware 3rd party integrations
```

### 8.3 Stocks

```
Stores > Inventory > Stocks

Stock = aggregation of source quantities for a sales channel
  Salable Qty = sum of source quantities - existing reservations

Example:
  Source A: 10 units
  Source B: 5 units
  Reservations: -3
  Salable Qty shown to customer: 12
```

> **Exam focus:** **Salable Qty** != Physical Qty. Salable Qty accounts for **reservations** (pending orders).

### 8.4 Reservation System

The reservation system is the core innovation of MSI.

```
Reservation Flow:

  Customer places order
       |
       v
  Reservation created: -qty against Stock (salable qty decremented)
  (Physical source qty NOT yet changed)
       |
       v
  Shipment created (source selected)
       |
       v
  Source deduction runs: physical qty at source decremented
  Reservation compensated: +qty reservation added (net zero)

Result: source qty reflects actual physical inventory
```

> **Exam focus:**
> - Reservations are **append-only** — they are never deleted, only compensated
> - Reservations are stored in `inventory_reservation` table
> - The `inventory_reservation` table uses negative values for reservations and positive for compensation
> - **Source deduction** (physical qty change) happens at **shipment creation**, not order placement

### 8.5 Source Selection Algorithms (SSA)

When creating a shipment, MSI selects which source(s) to fulfill from:

| Algorithm | Logic |
|---|---|
| **Source Priority** | Use sources in admin-defined priority order |
| **Distance Priority** | Use source geographically closest to shipping address |

```
Distance Priority requires:
  - Google Maps API key OR offline calculation (GeoNames + Haversine)
  - Source addresses configured
  - Address geolocation data
```

> **Exam focus:** You can create **custom SSA** by implementing `Magento\InventorySourceSelectionApi\Model\SourceSelectionInterface` (not SourceSelectionServiceInterface — that is the dispatching service, not the algorithm interface).

### 8.6 MSI & Non-MSI Products

```
If MSI is installed but a product has:
  manage_stock = false -> MSI is bypassed

Default Source is used for backward compatibility with legacy code
that directly reads cataloginventory_stock_item table
```

---

## 9. Add-on Modules: Live Search vs Native Search

### 9.1 Native Search (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch)

```
Tech Stack:
  - OpenSearch or Elasticsearch 8 (Deprecated) — required for Commerce 2.4.x
  - MySQL search was fully removed in 2.4.x
  - Indexer: catalogsearch_fulltext
  - Real-time updates via indexer

Native Search Features:
  - Full-text search across configured attributes
  - Faceted filtering (layered navigation)
  - Synonyms (Admin > Marketing > Search Synonyms)
  - Search terms redirect (Admin > Marketing > Search Terms)
  - Stopwords
  - Relevance boosting via attribute "Search Weight"
```

### 9.2 Live Search (SaaS)

Live Search is an **Adobe-hosted SaaS service** — NOT running on the merchant's server.

```
Architecture:

  Merchant Store
       |
       v
  [Data Export] -> Adobe Commerce Services (SaaS) <- Customer Search Query
                          |
                          v
                   [Results returned via GraphQL]
                          |
                          v
                   Storefront (headless or Luma widget)
```

> **Exam focus:**
> - Live Search requires **Adobe Commerce (EE)** and an **API key** from Adobe Commerce Services
> - Live Search is **not available for Magento Open Source**
> - Data is synced to Adobe's SaaS via the **Data Export module**

### 9.3 Feature Comparison

| Feature | Native Search | Live Search |
|---|---|---|
| Hosting | Merchant server (ES/OS) | Adobe SaaS |
| Setup complexity | Medium (ES install) | Low (API key) |
| Merchandising rules | Limited | Advanced (pin, boost, bury, hide) |
| Synonyms | Admin UI | Admin UI (Live Search workspace) |
| Facets | Layered nav (config heavy) | Dynamic facets (auto) |
| Personalization | No | Yes (behavioral data) |
| GraphQL | Partial | Full (required for headless) |
| Price | Included | Additional cost (included in EE subscription tiers) |
| B2B Shared Catalog | Yes | Yes (as of recent versions) |

> **Exam focus:**
> - Live Search uses **GraphQL exclusively** for query results on the frontend
> - Live Search replaces the **storefront search** experience, but Elasticsearch/OpenSearch remains active for **catalog indexing** (category pages, layered navigation). They coexist — ES/OS is not fully replaced.
> - Live Search has **Intelligent Ranking** (conversion-optimized) vs. native's text-relevance ranking

### 9.4 Live Search Merchandising Rules

```
Live Search > Rules:

  Conditions: search query matches keyword/phrase

  Actions (per product position):
    - Pin product   : force a product to a specific position
    - Boost product : move product higher in results
    - Bury product  : move product lower in results
    - Hide product  : remove from results entirely

Rules can be:
  - Intelligent (auto-optimized)
  - Manual overrides
```

### 9.5 Search Configuration Paths

```bash
# Native search config location
Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Catalog Search
  - Search Engine: OpenSearch / Elasticsearch 8 (Deprecated)
  - Server hostname, port, index prefix

# Live Search is a separate SaaS package (not in base EE)
# Once installed, configured via Commerce Services Connector API keys
```
