## 10. Systems Architecture: Scope Hierarchy

### 10.1 The Three-Level Scope

```
Adobe Commerce Scope Hierarchy:

  +--------------------------------------------------+
  |  GLOBAL (Default)                                |
  |  - Default config values                         |
  |  - Applies everywhere unless overridden           |
  |                                                  |
  |  +--------------------------------------------+ |
  |  |  WEBSITE                                   | |
  |  |  - Separate domain, customer base          | |
  |  |  - Has own payment methods, currency       | |
  |  |  - Customers are website-scoped            | |
  |  |                                            | |
  |  |  +--------------------------------------+  | |
  |  |  |  STORE (Store Group)                 |  | |
  |  |  |  - Root category assignment          |  | |
  |  |  |  - Groups store views                |  | |
  |  |  |                                      |  | |
  |  |  |  +--------------------------------+  |  | |
  |  |  |  |  STORE VIEW                    |  |  | |
  |  |  |  |  - Language / locale           |  |  | |
  |  |  |  |  - Translations                |  |  | |
  |  |  |  |  - Theme                       |  |  | |
  |  |  |  +--------------------------------+  |  | |
  |  |  +--------------------------------------+  | |
  |  +--------------------------------------------+ |
  +--------------------------------------------------+
```

### 10.2 What Lives at Each Scope

| Item | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Customers | Website | Cannot share customers across websites without custom code |
| Orders | Website | Tied to website |
| Products | Global | Product catalog is global; visibility per store view |
| Categories | Global | But can be assigned to root category per store |
| Payment methods | Website | |
| Tax rules | Website | |
| Currency | Website | |
| Pricing | Website | Can be different per website |
| CMS Pages | Store View | |
| URL rewrites | Store View | |
| Themes | Store View | |
| Translations | Store View | |
| Email templates | Store View | |
| Root category | Store | Each store group has one root category |

> **Exam focus:**
> - **Customers are website-scoped** — logging in on Website A does not log you into Website B
> - **Prices are website-scoped** — different prices per website is supported out of the box
> - **Products and attributes are global** — but visibility (Catalog, Search, etc.) is store view scoped

### 10.3 Configuration Scope in Admin

```
When editing configuration:
  Admin top-left scope selector:
    Default Config -> Website -> Store View

Config values cascade DOWN:
  Global default -> overridden by Website -> overridden by Store View

"Use Default" checkbox: inherits from parent scope
"Use Website" checkbox: inherits from website scope (shown at store view level)
```

### 10.4 System Configuration Storage

```sql
-- config values stored in core_config_data
SELECT scope, scope_id, path, value
FROM core_config_data
WHERE path LIKE 'general/country%';

-- scope values:
--   'default' (scope_id = 0) = global
--   'websites' (scope_id = website_id) = website
--   'stores'   (scope_id = store_id) = store view
```

> **Exam focus:** `scope_id` for **default** scope is always **0**.

### 10.5 Multi-Website Architecture

```
Common Setup:
  Website 1: US Store (USD, English)
    Store 1: Main Store
      Store View: English
      Store View: Spanish

  Website 2: EU Store (EUR)
    Store 2: EU Store
      Store View: German
      Store View: French

Different Magento instances vs. Multi-website:
  - Single Magento install, multiple websites = shared codebase, separate config
  - Different base_url per website in core_config_data
```

### 10.6 Website vs. Store vs. Store View — Exam Traps

> **Exam focus:**
> - "Store" in Magento terminology = **Store Group** (not what customers call a store)
> - A Store View is what customers actually **see and navigate**
> - A Store Group can have **multiple Store Views** but only **one Root Category**
> - Each Website must have **one Default Store Group** and **one Default Store View**

## 11. Systems Architecture: Headless Concepts

### 11.1 What is Headless Commerce?

```
Traditional (Coupled):
  [Magento Backend] <-> [Luma/Hyva Frontend] = same server, PHP templates

Headless (Decoupled):
  [Magento Backend (API)] <-> [Frontend Framework (React, Vue, Next.js, PWA)]
  Communication via: GraphQL or REST API
```

### 11.2 Adobe Commerce GraphQL

Adobe Commerce provides a comprehensive GraphQL API:

```graphql
# Example: Product Query
query {
  products(search: "hoodie") {
    items {
      sku
      name
      price_range {
        minimum_price {
          regular_price {
            value
            currency
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Key GraphQL schemas:

```
Catalog:     products, categories, categoryList
Cart:        cart, addProductsToCart, updateCartItems
Customer:    customer, createCustomer, generateCustomerToken
Checkout:    setShippingAddressOnCart, setPaymentMethodOnCart, placeOrder
CMS:         cmsPage, cmsBlocks
B2B:         company, negotiableQuote, requisitionList
```

> **Exam focus:**
> - GraphQL endpoint: `/graphql`
> - REST API endpoint: `/rest/[store_code]/V1/`
> - GraphQL **mutations** change data; **queries** read data
> - Customer-specific GraphQL operations require **Bearer token** (from `generateCustomerToken`)

### 11.3 PWA Studio

Adobe's official headless frontend toolkit:

```
Components:
  - Venia: reference storefront (React)
  - Peregrine: hooks library (React)
  - Buildpack: webpack configuration
  - UPWARD: server definition for SSR/routing (YAML/JSON spec)

UPWARD (Unified Progressive Web App Response Definition):
  - Defines server behavior declaratively
  - Can run on Node.js or PHP
  - Handles routing, context resolution
```

### 11.4 API Mesh (Adobe Developer App Builder)

```
API Mesh allows:
  - Combining multiple APIs (Magento GraphQL + 3rd party APIs) into single endpoint
  - Schema stitching
  - Run on Adobe's edge network

Use case:
  Merge Magento GraphQL with ERP GraphQL into one endpoint
  Frontend queries one unified API
```

### 11.5 Headless Authentication

```
Guest operations: no auth required (public mutations/queries)

Customer auth:
  POST /graphql
  mutation: generateCustomerToken(email, password) -> token

  Use token in header:
  Authorization: Bearer [token]

Admin operations:
  POST /rest/V1/integration/admin/token
  -> returns admin token
  Use in: Authorization: Bearer [admin_token]
```

### 11.6 Store Code in Headless

```
For multi-store headless setup, pass store code in:

HTTP Header: Store: [store_code]
  OR
URL prefix: /rest/us_english/V1/ (store code in URL)

GraphQL: Store header
  Store: us_english
```

> **Exam focus:**
> - GraphQL does not support **file uploads** natively in Magento's implementation
> - REST API supports **file uploads** via multipart form data
> - **Both** REST and GraphQL support customer/guest/admin authentication

## 12. Compliance: GDPR

### 12.1 GDPR Overview for Adobe Commerce

General Data Protection Regulation — applies to merchants with EU customers.

```
Adobe Commerce provides:
  - Privacy request management (access, delete)
  - Cookie consent tools
  - Data anonymization
  - Customer data export
```

### 12.2 Privacy Requests

```
Two types of GDPR privacy requests in Magento:

1. ACCESS request  : export customer's personal data as downloadable file
2. DELETE request  : anonymize/delete customer personal data

Note: There is no dedicated "Magento\Privacy" module or "Marketing > Privacy > Privacy Requests"
menu in the base EE 2.4.8-p3 codebase. GDPR functionality is handled through
customer account deletion (Admin > Customers > Edit > Delete) and data export features.
Third-party GDPR extensions may add dedicated privacy request management interfaces.
```

> **Exam focus:**
> - DELETE request **anonymizes** data rather than hard-deleting records (to preserve order integrity)
> - Customer must have an **account** for the request to work through the standard flow
> - The base platform provides GDPR capability (delete/anonymize/export), but does NOT include a dedicated Privacy module with admin UI for managing requests

### 12.3 What Data is Anonymized on Delete

```
Fields anonymized during GDPR delete:
  - customer_entity: email -> anonymous@[id].anon, name -> "Anonymous"
  - customer_address_entity: name, address fields
  - sales_order: customer email, billing/shipping name/address
  - quote: customer data

Note: Order RECORDS are preserved for accounting/legal purposes
      Only PII (personally identifiable information) is anonymized
```

### 12.4 Cookie Compliance

```
Stores > Configuration > General > Web > Default Cookie Settings:
  - Cookie Lifetime (default: 3600 seconds)
  - Cookie Path
  - Cookie Domain
  - Use HTTP Only
  - Cookie Restriction Mode (GDPR consent banner)

Cookie Restriction Mode:
  - When enabled: displays consent notice
  - Cookies not set until customer consents
  - Except: essential cookies (session, cart)
```

> **Exam focus:**
> - **Cookie Restriction Mode** is Adobe Commerce's built-in GDPR consent mechanism
> - It is NOT a full GDPR compliance solution — additional consent management may be needed
> - Setting location: `Stores > Config > General > Web > Default Cookie Settings`

## 13. Compliance: PCI DSS

### 13.1 PCI DSS and Adobe Commerce

Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard — for any merchant storing, processing, or transmitting cardholder data.

```
Adobe Commerce's approach:
  - Does NOT store raw card numbers by default
  - Payment vaulting stores tokens (not actual card data)
  - PCI compliance is shared responsibility:
    Merchant + Payment Gateway + Adobe Commerce Cloud (infrastructure)
```

### 13.2 PCI Scope Reduction Strategies

```
1. Use hosted payment pages (PayPal, Stripe hosted fields)
   -> Card data never touches Magento server
   -> Reduces PCI scope to SAQ A

2. iFrame-based payment fields (Braintree hosted fields)
   -> Card data entered in gateway's iFrame
   -> Reduces scope

3. JavaScript tokenization
   -> Card tokenized client-side before touching server
   -> Magento server only receives token

Avoid:
  - Direct POST of card data to Magento server (full PCI scope)
```

> **Exam focus:**
> - **SAQ A** = lowest PCI compliance level — only possible with fully redirected/hosted payments
> - Adobe Commerce on Cloud is **PCI compliant at the infrastructure level** (PCI DSS Level 1 service provider)
> - The **merchant** is still responsible for their own SAQ level

### 13.3 Payment Vault (Token Storage)

```
Magento\Vault module:

  Customer saves payment method ->
  Gateway returns payment token ->
  Token stored in vault_payment_token table ->
  Future purchases use token (not card data)

Token Types:
  - Card (credit/debit)
  - Bank account (ACH)
```

### 13.4 HTTPS Requirements

```
Required for PCI compliance:
  - All checkout pages served over HTTPS
  - Admin panel over HTTPS

Config:
  Stores > Configuration > General > Web
    > Base URLs (Secure): https://...
    > Use Secure URLs on Storefront: Yes
    > Use Secure URLs in Admin: Yes
```

### 13.5 Admin Security for PCI

```
Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Admin > Security:
  - Admin Session Lifetime
  - Maximum Login Failures to Lockout Account
  - Lockout Time (minutes)
  - Add Secret Key to URLs: Yes (CSRF protection)

Two-Factor Authentication (2FA):
  - Required by default in Adobe Commerce 2.4+
  - Supported providers: Google Authenticator, Duo, Authy, U2F
  - Cannot be disabled without code change
```

> **Exam focus:** **2FA is mandatory in Adobe Commerce 2.4+** and cannot be disabled via Admin UI — only via CLI or module disabling (strongly discouraged for production).

## 14. Compliance: Admin Permissions & ACL

### 14.1 Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

```
System > Permissions > User Roles

Structure:
  Role -> Resources (ACL tree) -> Users

Each role defines:
  - Which admin resources are accessible
  - "Role Scopes" (in EE): limit to specific websites/stores
```

### 14.2 ACL (Access Control List) Architecture

```
ACL Resources defined in:
  [Vendor]/[Module]/etc/acl.xml

Example acl.xml:
```

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Acl/etc/acl.xsd">
    <acl>
        <resources>
            <resource id="Magento_Backend::admin">
                <resource id="Vendor_Module::manage" title="Manage Custom Items" sortOrder="10">
                    <resource id="Vendor_Module::save" title="Save Custom Items" sortOrder="10"/>
                    <resource id="Vendor_Module::delete" title="Delete Custom Items" sortOrder="20"/>
                </resource>
            </resource>
        </resources>
    </acl>
</config>
```

### 14.3 Checking ACL in Code

```php
// In a controller:
protected function _isAllowed()
{
    return $this->_authorization->isAllowed('Vendor_Module::manage');
}

// In a UI component (menu/button visibility):
// adminhtml/menu.xml
// <add id="Vendor_Module::menu_item" resource="Vendor_Module::manage" ... />
```

### 14.4 Admin User Configuration

```
System > Permissions > All Users

Per user:
  - Username, password, email
  - Account status (Active/Inactive)
  - Role assignment

User creation best practices (PCI):
  - Unique accounts per person (no shared logins)
  - Minimum necessary permissions (least privilege)
  - Regular password rotation
  - Deactivate immediately on employee departure
```

> **Exam focus:**
> - ACL resources use **double-colon IDs**: `Vendor_Module::resource_name`
> - The ACL tree has `Magento_Backend::all` ("Allow everything") at the very top, with `Magento_Backend::admin` ("Magento Admin") as the practical root beneath it
> - All ACL checks go through `Magento\Framework\AuthorizationInterface`

### 14.5 Role Scopes (EE Only)

```
Enterprise Edition allows limiting admin user access to:
  - Specific Websites
  - Specific Store Groups
  - Specific Store Views

This is the "Scoped Roles" feature.
A scoped admin user can only see/edit data for their assigned scope.
```

### 14.6 Admin Activity Log (EE)

```
Enterprise Edition: Action Log

Records:
  - All admin user actions
  - Login/logout events
  - Data changes (what was changed, from/to values)
  - IP address, timestamp

Location: System > Action Logs > Report
Config: Stores > Configuration > Advanced > Admin > Admin Actions Logging
Retention: configurable
```

> **Exam focus:** Admin Action Log is an **EE-only** feature for audit trail compliance.

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Product Types
- [ ] 7 product types: Simple, Configurable, Grouped, Bundle, Virtual, Downloadable, Gift Card (EE)
- [ ] Configurable inventory tracked on **child simples only**
- [ ] Bundle: fixed vs. dynamic pricing — dynamic bundles cannot use catalog price rules
- [ ] Grouped products: no single price; each item adds independently
- [ ] Virtual products: no shipping required, no shipping address shown
- [ ] Downloadable: has Links (files) and Samples (previews)
- [ ] Gift Card: Virtual, Physical, or Combined types (EE only)

### Order Lifecycle
- [ ] States: new -> pending_payment -> processing -> complete -> closed / canceled / holded / payment_review
- [ ] `complete` requires both **Invoice + Shipment**
- [ ] `closed` = credit memo issued (refund)
- [ ] Inventory returns to stock on cancellation (MSI reservation compensated automatically)
- [ ] Cannot create Credit Memo without first creating Invoice
- [ ] Check/Money Order = offline payment; invoice created as `pending`

### Payment Methods
- [ ] Authorize Only vs. Authorize and Capture
- [ ] Payment method scope = **Website** level
- [ ] Zero Subtotal Checkout = auto-triggered when cart total = $0
- [ ] Offline methods: Check/MO, Bank Transfer, Zero Subtotal

### Shipping
- [ ] Table rates: Weight/Price/Item count vs. Destination — one condition type at a time
- [ ] Table rates imported as **CSV per website** (no City column)
- [ ] Shipping origin scoped to **website**
- [ ] Cart price rule free shipping overrides carrier rates (Free Shipping carrier does NOT need to be enabled)

### Pricing Hierarchy
- [ ] Order: Special Price vs. Tier Price — **lowest wins**
- [ ] Tier Price at qty=1 = Customer Group Price
- [ ] Special Price does not always beat tier price
- [ ] Catalog rules require re-indexing; processed after special/tier comparison
- [ ] B2B Shared Catalog pricing overrides ALL other pricing

### Catalog Price Rules
- [ ] Applied before cart via indexer
- [ ] Conditions: attributes, categories, attribute sets
- [ ] 4 action types: % of orig, fixed amount, to %, to fixed
- [ ] Scoped to customer groups
- [ ] Lower priority number = applied first
- [ ] "Discard subsequent rules" = stop after this rule

### Cart Price Rules
- [ ] Applied during checkout/cart session
- [ ] Support coupon codes; auto-generated coupons available in **both CE and EE**
- [ ] `Uses Per Coupon` = global limit; `Uses Per Customer` = per account
- [ ] Rules can stack unless "Discard subsequent rules" is set
- [ ] Supports: Buy X Get Y, free shipping action

### B2B
- [ ] Features: Company, Shared Catalog, Negotiable Quotes, Quick Order, Requisition Lists, Purchase Orders
- [ ] Customer can belong to **one company** only
- [ ] Company must be **approved** by merchant
- [ ] Negotiable Quotes require **Company** enabled (not Shared Catalog)
- [ ] PO approval rules set by **Company Admin**, not merchant; conditions: Order Total, Shipping Cost, Number of SKUs
- [ ] Shared Catalog pricing overrides all other pricing for assigned companies

### MSI
- [ ] Source = physical location; Stock = virtual pool; Sales Channel = website
- [ ] Salable Qty = source total - reservations
- [ ] Reservations created at **order placement**; source deducted at **shipment**
- [ ] Reservations are append-only (never deleted, only compensated)
- [ ] `inventory_reservation` table: negative = reservation, positive = compensation
- [ ] SSA algorithms: Source Priority, Distance Priority
- [ ] Default Source cannot be deleted

### Live Search vs Native
- [ ] Live Search = Adobe SaaS; requires EE + API key; not available on Open Source
- [ ] Live Search replaces **storefront search** but Elasticsearch/OpenSearch remains for catalog indexing
- [ ] Live Search uses **GraphQL only** for queries
- [ ] Live Search supports: pin, boost, bury, hide merchandising rules
- [ ] Native search uses Elasticsearch 8 (Deprecated) or OpenSearch on merchant server
- [ ] Both support synonyms; Live Search has more advanced merchandising

### Scope Hierarchy
- [ ] 4 levels: Global (Default) -> Website -> Store (Group) -> Store View
- [ ] Customers are **website-scoped**
- [ ] Products/attributes are **global-scoped**
- [ ] Store View: language, theme, translations, CMS pages
- [ ] Website: customers, orders, payment methods, currency, pricing
- [ ] Store (Group): one Root Category per store group
- [ ] `core_config_data`: scope_id = 0 for default/global

### Headless / GraphQL
- [ ] GraphQL endpoint: `/graphql`; REST: `/rest/[store_code]/V1/`
- [ ] Customer auth: `generateCustomerToken` mutation -> Bearer token
- [ ] Mutations = write; Queries = read
- [ ] Pass store code in `Store` HTTP header for multi-store
- [ ] PWA Studio: Venia (storefront), Peregrine (hooks), UPWARD (server spec)
- [ ] API Mesh: combines multiple APIs into one GraphQL endpoint

### GDPR
- [ ] Two request types: **Access** (export data) and **Delete** (anonymize PII)
- [ ] Delete anonymizes data — does NOT delete order records
- [ ] Cookie Restriction Mode = built-in consent banner
- [ ] No dedicated Privacy module or admin menu in base EE 2.4.8-p3
- [ ] Location: Cookie settings at Stores > Config > General > Web > Default Cookie Settings

### PCI DSS
- [ ] Adobe Commerce doesn't store raw card numbers — uses tokens
- [ ] Hosted payment fields / iFrames reduce PCI scope to SAQ A
- [ ] 2FA mandatory in Commerce 2.4+ — cannot be disabled via Admin UI
- [ ] `vault_payment_token` table stores payment tokens
- [ ] Commerce Cloud is PCI Level 1 service provider (infrastructure)

### Admin Permissions / ACL
- [ ] ACL defined in `[Module]/etc/acl.xml`
- [ ] Top-level resource: `Magento_Backend::all` ("Allow everything"); admin root: `Magento_Backend::admin`
- [ ] Resource IDs format: `Vendor_Module::resource_name`
- [ ] Check permission: `$this->_authorization->isAllowed('Vendor_Module::resource')`
- [ ] All controllers must implement `_isAllowed()` for protected resources
- [ ] Scoped Roles (limit by website/store) = **EE only**
- [ ] Admin Action Log (audit trail) = **EE only** (System > Action Logs > Report)
- [ ] PCI best practice: unique accounts, least privilege, deactivate departing users immediately

flashcards.question: What is the correct sequence of the pricing hierarchy in Adobe Commerce, and which price wins?
flashcards.answer: The hierarchy from highest to lowest priority is: Special Price (date-ranged), Tier Price (qty-based), Group Price (customer group specific), Catalog Price Rule (condition-based), Cart Price Rule (at checkout). The lowest applicable price wins at each level.
flashcards.hint: Multiple price types can compete — the customer always gets the lowest one.

flashcards.question: When does a Tier Price beat a Special Price in Adobe Commerce?
flashcards.answer: A Tier Price beats a Special Price when the tier price is lower. For example, if the special price is $85 and the tier price at qty 10+ is $80, the customer pays $80. The system always applies the lowest applicable price, so tier and special prices compete directly.
flashcards.hint: The rule is simple: lowest always wins, regardless of which price type it is.

flashcards.question: How do you set a customer group-specific base price using Tier Pricing?
flashcards.answer: Set a Tier Price with qty = 1 for a specific customer group. For example, setting Tier Price for Wholesale group at qty 1 with price $45 effectively creates a group-specific base price (instead of the regular $65 price). This is the standard way to implement group pricing.
flashcards.hint: The trick is using a quantity threshold of just one unit for a specific group.

flashcards.question: What are the four action types available in Catalog Price Rules?
flashcards.answer: The four action types are: 1) Apply as percentage of original (e.g., 10% off), 2) Apply as fixed amount discount (e.g., $10 off), 3) Adjust final price to this percentage (e.g., set to 90% of original), 4) Adjust final price to discount value (e.g., set to $90). All four can produce the same result with different inputs.
flashcards.hint: Two reduce BY an amount; two set TO a target.

flashcards.question: What is the key difference between how Catalog Price Rules and Cart Price Rules are applied?
flashcards.answer: Catalog Price Rules apply before the cart via the indexer — they modify the displayed price on catalog and product pages. Cart Price Rules apply during checkout in the cart session — they show as discount lines in the cart totals. Only cart rules support coupon codes, free shipping, and Buy X Get Y.
flashcards.hint: One changes what the customer sees while browsing; the other applies at the register.

flashcards.question: What must be true about product attributes used for configurable product variations?
flashcards.answer: Attributes used for configurable variations must be: 1) Global scope, 2) Dropdown type (or visual/text swatch), and 3) User-defined (not system attributes). Eligibility is checked automatically — there is no 'Use to Create Configurable Product' toggle in the admin UI.
flashcards.hint: Three criteria must all be met, and they are checked automatically by the system.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Bundle product Fixed pricing and Dynamic pricing?
flashcards.answer: Fixed Price bundles have a set parent price regardless of which options the customer selects. Dynamic Price bundles calculate the total as the sum of selected option prices. Dynamic-price bundles cannot use catalog price rules — only special prices and customer group pricing apply.
flashcards.hint: One price is predetermined; the other is calculated based on customer selections.

flashcards.question: What are the conditions required for an order to reach the 'complete' state?
flashcards.answer: An order reaches the 'complete' state only when BOTH an invoice AND a shipment exist. Without either one, the order remains in 'processing'. The 'closed' state is different — it means a credit memo was issued (refund). You cannot create a Credit Memo without first creating an Invoice.
flashcards.hint: Two documents must both exist for the order to be considered fully done.

flashcards.question: What are Table Rate shipping conditions, and how many condition types can be used at once?
flashcards.answer: Table Rates support three condition types: Weight vs. Destination, Price vs. Destination, and Number of Items vs. Destination. Only one condition type can be used at a time per store. Table rates are imported as CSV per website with 5 columns (Country, Region/State, Zip, the condition column, and Shipping Price) — there is no City column.
flashcards.hint: You pick one condition to calculate against, and import rates as a spreadsheet file.

flashcards.question: What happens when a Cart Price Rule grants free shipping — does the Free Shipping carrier need to be enabled?
flashcards.answer: When a Cart Price Rule grants free shipping, it overrides carrier calculations entirely for that cart. The Free Shipping carrier does NOT need to be enabled for cart price rule free shipping to work. These are two independent mechanisms for offering free shipping.
flashcards.hint: The rule-based free shipping is independent of the carrier configuration.

flashcards.question: At what scope are payment methods configured in Adobe Commerce?
flashcards.answer: Payment methods can be configured at Default (global) and Website level. They CANNOT be configured at Store or Store View level. This means different websites can have different payment methods, but all store views within a website share the same payment configuration.
flashcards.hint: The scope matches the level at which separate customer bases exist.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Authorize Only and Authorize & Capture payment actions?
flashcards.answer: Authorize Only reserves/holds funds on the card but does NOT capture them. Money only moves when an admin manually creates an invoice. Authorize & Capture captures funds immediately at order placement, and an invoice is auto-created. Authorize Only is the standard for physical goods.
flashcards.hint: One requires a manual step after order placement; the other is fully automatic.

flashcards.question: Are auto-generated coupon codes a CE or EE feature in Adobe Commerce?
flashcards.answer: Auto-generated coupon codes are available in BOTH Open Source (CE) and Commerce (EE). A single cart price rule can generate multiple unique coupon codes for campaigns. 'Uses Per Coupon' limits how many times a single code can be used globally, while 'Uses Per Customer' limits per customer account.
flashcards.hint: This is a common exam trap — many assume it is EE-only, but it is not.

flashcards.question: What is Live Search in Adobe Commerce, and how does it coexist with Elasticsearch?
flashcards.answer: Live Search is an Adobe-hosted SaaS service that replaces the storefront search experience with AI-powered search using Adobe Sensei. However, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch remains active for catalog indexing (category pages, layered navigation). They coexist — ES/OS is not fully replaced. Live Search requires EE and is not available for Open Source.
flashcards.hint: The SaaS service handles what customers type in the search bar, but the on-premise engine still handles other catalog functions.
