studyNotes.content:
# Adobe Commerce Business Practitioner Expert (AD0-E708) — Weak Area Deep Dive #2 & Scenario Drill

## Table of Contents
1. [Overview & Exam Context](#1-overview--exam-context)
2. [Scenario Pattern 1: B2B Pricing for Different Customer Groups](#2-scenario-pattern-1-b2b-pricing-for-different-customer-groups)
3. [Scenario Pattern 2: Content Visibility for Logged-In Users](#3-scenario-pattern-2-content-visibility-for-logged-in-users)
4. [Scenario Pattern 3: Shipping from Multiple Warehouses](#4-scenario-pattern-3-shipping-from-multiple-warehouses)
5. [Scenario Pattern 4: Orders Stuck in Processing](#5-scenario-pattern-4-orders-stuck-in-processing)
6. [Scenario Pattern 5: Testing a New Homepage Before Publishing](#6-scenario-pattern-5-testing-a-new-homepage-before-publishing)
7. [Supporting Concepts: Customer Groups & Segments](#7-supporting-concepts-customer-groups--segments)
8. [Supporting Concepts: B2B Module Ecosystem](#8-supporting-concepts-b2b-module-ecosystem)
9. [Supporting Concepts: Payment Capture Modes Deep Dive](#9-supporting-concepts-payment-capture-modes-deep-dive)
10. [Supporting Concepts: MSI Architecture](#10-supporting-concepts-msi-architecture)
11. [Supporting Concepts: Content Staging & Preview](#11-supporting-concepts-content-staging--preview)
12. [Architect-Style Decision Framework](#12-architect-style-decision-framework)
13. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Overview & Exam Context

This deep-dive targets the **architect/scenario reasoning** style of exam questions — the kind where you are given a business requirement and must identify the *correct Adobe Commerce feature or configuration* that solves it. These questions are **not** about memorizing menus; they test whether you can map a business problem to the right tool.

### How the Exam Presents These

| Question Format | Example Stem |
|---|---|
| "A merchant wants to…" | Feature recommendation |
| "A client reports that…" | Troubleshooting / root cause |
| "Which feature should…" | Architecture selection |
| "What is the BEST approach…" | Comparing two valid options |

**Exam focus:**
- The exam heavily favors questions where **two answers seem correct** — the differentiator is always *which edition* (CE vs. EE) or *which is the most direct native solution* vs. a workaround.
- Always ask: *Is this a CE feature or an EE/B2B feature?*

---

## 2. Scenario Pattern 1: B2B Pricing for Different Customer Groups

### The Business Problem

> *"A client sells to both retail consumers and wholesale business accounts. They want wholesale customers to see different — typically lower — prices than retail customers, and they may want entire product catalogs hidden from the general public."*

### Decision Tree

```
Client wants different pricing?
        |
        v
Is it per-customer negotiation  ----YES---> Negotiable Quotes (B2B EE)
or group-based pricing?
        |
       NO (group-based)
        v
Is it just a price rule/discount? --YES---> Customer Group + Tier Pricing
                                            OR Cart Price Rules scoped to group
        |
       NO (separate catalog / hide products)
        v
        Use Shared Catalog (B2B EE)
```

---

### Solution A: Customer Groups (CE + EE)

Customer Groups are the **foundation** of all tiered pricing in Adobe Commerce. Every customer — including guests — belongs to a group.

```
Default Groups (out of the box):
+------------------+-------------------+
| Group Name       | Tax Class         |
+------------------+-------------------+
| NOT LOGGED IN    | Taxable Goods     |
| General          | Taxable Goods     |
| Wholesale        | Taxable Goods     |
| Retailer         | Taxable Goods     |
+------------------+-------------------+
```

**What Customer Groups control:**
- **Tier Prices** — set per-product, per-group, per-quantity
- **Cart Price Rules** — condition "Customer Group is Wholesale"
- **Catalog Price Rules** — apply discounts to a group
- **Tax classes** — different VAT treatment per group
- **Free shipping thresholds** — scoped per group via rules

#### Tier Pricing Configuration Path
```
Admin > Catalog > Products > [Product] > Advanced Pricing
  - Price: base price
  - Special Price: time-limited discount
  - Tier Price: qty-based + group-based
    - Customer Group: [Wholesale]
    - Qty: 1
    - Price: $45.00  (vs. $65.00 retail)
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Customer Groups exist in CE** — they are NOT an EE-only feature.
- Tier prices set with `Qty = 1` for a specific group effectively create a **group-specific base price**.
- A customer can only belong to **one Customer Group** at a time.

---

### Solution B: Shared Catalog (B2B EE Only)

Shared Catalog extends beyond pricing — it controls **which products are visible** to which company accounts.

```
Shared Catalog Structure:
+-------------------------------+
|       Shared Catalog          |
|  (Public or Custom)           |
+-------------------------------+
         |           |
         v           v
   Products      Custom Prices
   (subset)      (per product,
                  per catalog)
         |
         v
   Assigned to
   Company Account(s)
         |
         v
   All users of that
   Company see only
   those products + prices
```

**Key distinctions:**

| Feature | Customer Group Pricing | Shared Catalog |
|---|---|---|
| Edition | CE & EE | B2B EE only |
| Hides products from group | No | Yes |
| Per-product custom price | Via tier price | Yes, directly |
| Attached to | Customer Group | Company Account |
| Multiple price levels | Via qty tiers | One price per product per catalog |
| Category-level visibility | No (use Permissions) | Yes |

#### Shared Catalog Types
- **Public Catalog** — replaces the default storefront catalog; all guests and non-company customers see this
- **Custom Catalog** — assigned to specific B2B Company accounts; completely independent product/price set

**Exam focus:**
- **Shared Catalog requires the B2B module AND EE** — never recommend it for CE clients.
- When a Shared Catalog is assigned to a company, it **overrides** the customer group pricing for that company's users. (Shared Catalog pricing is stored as tier prices in the same `catalog_product_entity_tier_price` table, using the shared catalog's auto-created customer group.)
- The public Shared Catalog, when enabled, becomes the **new default catalog** — the standard catalog is replaced.

---

### Solution C: Catalog Price Rules (CE + EE)

Use when you want **automatic percentage or fixed discounts** for a group without per-product configuration.

```php
// Catalog Price Rule Logic (conceptual)
Rule: "Wholesale 20% Off"
  Conditions:
    - Customer Group: Wholesale
    - Category: [All Categories] OR specific
  Action:
    - Apply: Apply as percentage of original
    - Discount Amount: 20
    - Discard subsequent rules: Yes/No
```

**Exam focus:**
- Catalog Price Rules run on a **cron schedule** — they are not real-time until reindex runs.
- They apply **before** the customer adds to cart (reflected in catalog price display).

---

### Exam Scenario Walkthrough

**Scenario:** *"A B2B merchant using Adobe Commerce (cloud, EE) wants corporate accounts to see only the products relevant to their contract, with custom negotiated prices per product. Retail visitors should not see these products at all."*

**Answer:** **Shared Catalog** — because:
1. Product visibility restriction ✓ (Customer Groups cannot hide products)
2. Per-product custom pricing ✓
3. Tied to Company accounts ✓
4. EE edition confirmed ✓

---

## 3. Scenario Pattern 2: Content Visibility for Logged-In Users

### The Business Problem

> *"A client wants certain categories, products, or CMS pages to be visible only to logged-in customers — or only to specific customer segments (e.g., VIP members, loyalty tier)."*

### Decision Tree

```
Restrict content visibility?
        |
        v
CE or EE?
  |         |
  CE        EE
  |         |
  v         v
Limited   Catalog Permissions
options:  + Customer Segments
Login     (full solution)
redirect
```

---

### Solution A: Catalog Permissions (EE Only)

Catalog Permissions allow you to **restrict category and product browsing** based on Customer Group.

**What it controls:**
- Whether a category is **browsable** by a group
- Whether products in a category **display pricing** to a group
- Whether products can be **added to cart** by a group

```
Admin > Catalog > Categories > [Category] > Category Permissions
  + Add Permission
    - Customer Group: NOT LOGGED IN
    - Browsing Category: Deny
    - Display Product Prices: Deny
    - Add to Cart: Deny
```

**Behavior when denied:**
- Category disappears from navigation for that group
- Direct URL access shows "Access Denied" or redirects (configurable)
- Products within still appear in search unless **Search Engine Optimization** is also restricted

**Exam focus:**
- **Catalog Permissions is EE only** — CE has no native equivalent for hiding categories by group.
- Must be **enabled globally first**: `Admin > Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Category Permissions > Enable` (Note: the admin config label is "Category Permissions", not "Catalog Permissions".)
- Permissions apply at the **category level** — they cascade to products within.
- "NOT LOGGED IN" group = guest customers — denying this group forces login.

---

### Solution B: Customer Segments (EE Only)

Customer Segments are **dynamic groupings** based on real-time customer data — more powerful than static Customer Groups.

```
Customer Segment Conditions (examples):
+------------------------------------------+
| Condition Type    | Example               |
+------------------------------------------+
| Shopping Cart    | Amount > $500          |
| Sales / Orders   | Sales Amount, Number   |
|                  | of Orders, Purchased   |
|                  | Quantity               |
| Customer Profile | Customer Attributes    |
| Products         | Product List, Product  |
|                  | History (viewed/ordered)|
| Customer Address | Address Attributes     |
+------------------------------------------+
```

**Customer Segments vs. Customer Groups:**

| Aspect | Customer Groups | Customer Segments |
|---|---|---|
| Edition | CE & EE | EE only |
| Assignment | Manual or rule-based | Automatic / real-time |
| Used for pricing | Yes (tier prices, rules) | Via price rules |
| Used for content | Limited | Yes (banners, blocks) |
| Dynamic conditions | No | Yes |
| Cart-based | No | Yes |

**What Customer Segments power:**
- **Banner targeting** — show banners only to a segment
- **Cart/Catalog Price Rules** — apply discounts to segment
- **Related product rules** — personalized recommendations
- **Private Sales / Events** — gate access by segment

**Exam focus:**
- Customer Segments **do NOT directly restrict catalog visibility** the way Catalog Permissions do — they work with banners, price rules, and related products.
- For pure "hide this category from guests" → **Catalog Permissions**.
- For "show this promotional banner only to VIP members" → **Customer Segments + Banners**.

---

### Solution C: CMS Page / Block Restrictions (CE workaround)

For CE merchants needing basic gating:
- Use **customer login redirect** — force login before browsing
- Use **Widget conditions** — show CMS blocks only when `Customer is logged in` (limited)
- Third-party extensions or custom development required for fine-grained control

**Exam focus:**
- The exam will never recommend a custom extension as the *correct* answer — always look for the native feature.
- If the question mentions CE + "content only for logged-in users," the answer will involve acknowledging the limitation, not a workaround.

---

### Exam Scenario Walkthrough

**Scenario:** *"A merchant on Adobe Commerce EE wants the 'Members Only' category to be invisible to guests and visible only to customers tagged as Gold loyalty members. Gold members are determined by lifetime spend over $1,000."*

**Answer:** 
1. **Customer Segment** — create segment with condition "Sales Amount > $1,000", which auto-identifies customers.
2. Create a **Customer Group** for Gold members. (Note: Customer Segments do NOT auto-assign customers to groups — you would use the segment in price rules for Gold benefits, and manually or programmatically assign qualifying customers to the Gold group for catalog permissions.)
3. **Catalog Permissions** — deny "NOT LOGGED IN" and all non-Gold groups from browsing the "Members Only" category.

---

## 4. Scenario Pattern 3: Shipping from Multiple Warehouses

### The Business Problem

> *"A client has inventory stored in three warehouses across the country. They want orders to be fulfilled from the nearest warehouse to the customer, or from the warehouse with available stock."*

### Solution: Multi-Source Inventory (MSI)

MSI was introduced in Magento 2.3 and is available in **both CE and EE**. It decouples physical inventory locations from the salable quantity shown to customers.

### MSI Core Architecture

```
MSI Hierarchy:
+------------------+
|     STOCK        |  <-- Salable qty pool presented to storefront
+------------------+
         |
         | (linked via Stock-Source assignment)
         |
+--------+--------+--------+
|        |        |        |
v        v        v        v
SOURCE  SOURCE  SOURCE  SOURCE
(WH 1)  (WH 2)  (WH 3)  (WH 4)
         Physical inventory locations
```

**Key Definitions:**

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Source** | A physical location with inventory (warehouse, store, dropshipper) |
| **Stock** | A virtual inventory pool assigned to a sales channel (website) |
| **Source Item** | The quantity of a specific SKU at a specific Source |
| **Salable Quantity** | Aggregated available qty across all Sources assigned to a Stock |
| **Source Selection Algorithm (SSA)** | The rule that determines which Source(s) fulfill an order |

---

### Source Selection Algorithms (SSA)

```
Available SSAs:
+----------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
| SSA Name                   | Logic                                     |
+----------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
| Distance Priority          | Fulfill from Source nearest to shipping   |
|                            | address (requires Google Maps API)        |
+----------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
| Source Priority            | Fulfill from Sources in admin-defined     |
|                            | priority order (top = first used)         |
+----------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
| Custom (via plugin)        | Developer-defined logic                   |
+----------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
```

**Distance Priority SSA requirements:**
- Google Maps API key configured
- Source addresses must be complete (lat/long or full address)
- Customer's shipping address must be resolvable

---

### MSI Configuration Workflow

```
Step 1: Create Sources
  Admin > Stores > Inventory > Sources > Add New Source
    - Name: "East Coast Warehouse"
    - Code: east_coast_wh
    - Address, lat/long
    - Carrier-specific settings (optional)

Step 2: Create Stock
  Admin > Stores > Inventory > Stocks > Add New Stock
    - Name: "Main Website Stock"
    - Assign Sources: [east_coast_wh, west_coast_wh, central_wh]
    - Assign Sales Channels: [Main Website]

Step 3: Assign Source Quantities per Product
  Admin > Catalog > Products > [Product] > Sources (tab)
    - East Coast Warehouse: Qty 150, In Stock
    - West Coast Warehouse: Qty 75, In Stock
    - Central Warehouse: Qty 200, In Stock
```

Note: **SSA is NOT configured per-stock.** There is no Algorithm tab on the Stock edit form. Instead, the SSA is selected at **shipment creation time** — when processing an order, the admin chooses which algorithm to use for source selection. The default SSA is "Source Priority" (priority-based). Source priority order is set via the priority field on each source-stock link.

---

### Default Source & Default Stock

- **Default Source** — a system source that cannot be deleted; maps to legacy single-source behavior
- **Default Stock** — the system stock; always linked to Default Source
- When upgrading from pre-MSI, all inventory moves to Default Source/Stock automatically

**Exam focus:**
- MSI is available in **CE and EE** — it is NOT an EE-only feature.
- The **Distance Priority SSA** requires Google Maps API — exam may test this prerequisite.
- A **Stock** is assigned to a **Sales Channel** (website) — one website can use one Stock, but one Stock can aggregate many Sources.
- **Salable Quantity** ≠ physical qty at any one source — it is the *aggregate* minus reservations.
- The Default Source/Stock **cannot be deleted**.

---

### Ship from Store Use Case

MSI also enables **ship-from-store** scenarios:

```
Sources can be:
- Traditional warehouses
- Retail store locations (enable "Use as Pickup Location" for BOPIS)
- Third-party dropship vendors
- Virtual sources (digital goods)
```

**Exam focus:**
- BOPIS (Buy Online, Pick Up In Store) uses MSI Sources with **In-Store Pickup** enabled. The In-Store Pickup module (`Magento_InventoryInStorePickup`) is available in **both CE and EE** (OSL-3.0 license). There is no separate "Store Fulfillment extension" — this functionality is built into the core MSI In-Store Pickup modules.

---

## 5. Scenario Pattern 4: Orders Stuck in Processing

### The Business Problem

> *"A client reports that all orders are stuck in 'Processing' status and are not moving to 'Complete'. Customers are being charged, but fulfillment teams say they cannot ship."*

### Root Cause Analysis Framework

```
Orders stuck in "Processing"?
          |
          v
Are invoices being created? ---NO---> Payment capture issue
          |                           (most likely cause)
         YES
          v
Are shipments being created? --NO---> Fulfillment workflow issue
          |                           (3PL, ERP integration)
         YES
          v
Did order status not update? -------> Custom status mapping issue
```

---

### Primary Root Cause: Payment Capture Mode

This is the **most tested scenario**. Understanding the Authorize vs. Capture distinction is critical.

```
Payment Flow Options:
+---------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Mode                      | Behavior                                 |
+---------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Authorize Only            | Funds HELD on card, NOT captured.        |
|                           | Invoice must be created MANUALLY to      |
|                           | capture funds. Order stays "Processing". |
+---------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Authorize & Capture       | Funds captured immediately at order      |
| (Sale)                    | placement. Invoice auto-created.         |
+---------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Authorize & Capture       | For offline methods (check/MO):          |
| (Offline)                 | Invoice created manually, no gateway     |
|                           | call needed.                             |
+---------------------------+------------------------------------------+
```

### The "Processing" Order Lifecycle

```
Authorize Only Mode:
  Customer Places Order
        |
        v
  Order Status: PENDING
        |
        v  (payment authorization occurs)
  Order Status: PROCESSING  <--- STUCK HERE if no invoice created
        |
        v  (admin manually creates invoice -> triggers capture)
  Order Status: PROCESSING (with invoice)
        |
        v  (admin creates shipment)
  Order Status: COMPLETE
```

```
Authorize & Capture Mode:
  Customer Places Order
        |
        v  (authorization + capture happen simultaneously)
  Order Status: PROCESSING (invoice auto-created)
        |
        v  (admin creates shipment)
  Order Status: COMPLETE
```

---

### How to Create an Invoice (Manual Capture)

```
Admin > Sales > Orders > [Order] > Invoice (button, top right)
  - Items to Invoice: [all or partial]
  - Invoice Total: $XXX.XX
  - Invoice Comments (optional)
  - [Submit Invoice] button
    -> This triggers the CAPTURE request to the payment gateway
    -> Funds move from "authorized" to "captured"
    -> Order status updates
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Authorize Only mode** is the #1 cause of orders stuck in Processing on the exam.
- The fix is: **create an invoice** — this triggers the actual payment capture.
- `Payment Action = Authorize` in payment gateway config = Authorize Only mode.
- `Payment Action = Authorize and Capture` (or "Sale") = auto-capture.
- An order in "Processing" with NO invoice = waiting for capture.
- An order in "Processing" WITH an invoice = waiting for shipment.

---

### Other Causes of Orders Stuck in Processing

| Cause | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Authorize Only mode | No invoice created | Create invoice manually |
| 3PL/ERP integration failure | Invoice exists, no shipment | Check integration logs |
| Custom order status misconfigured | Status label ≠ state | Review order status mapping |
| Cron not running | Scheduled operations queued | Fix cron configuration |
| Stock not deducted | Order confirmed but inventory issue | Reindex inventory |

**Exam focus:**
- The exam scenario will usually say *"all orders"* are stuck — pointing to a **configuration issue** (Authorize Only), not a one-off order problem.
- If it says *"one order"* is stuck, suspect integration or payment gateway failure.

---

### Order States vs. Order Statuses

A frequently tested distinction:

```
Order STATE (system, fixed):       Order STATUS (configurable label):
+------------------+               +---------------------------+
| new              |  <--------->  | Pending                   |
| pending_payment  |               | Pending Payment           |
| processing       |               | Processing                |
| complete         |               | Complete                  |
| closed           |               | Closed                    |
| canceled         |               | Canceled                  |
| holded           |               | On Hold                   |
| payment_review   |               | Payment Review            |
+------------------+               +---------------------------+

States are hardcoded in the codebase.
Statuses are configurable (you can add custom statuses and map them to states).
```

**Exam focus:**
- You **cannot create custom States** — only custom **Statuses** that map to existing States.
- `Admin > Stores > Settings > Order Status` — manage and assign custom statuses here.

---

## 6. Scenario Pattern 5: Testing a New Homepage Before Publishing

### The Business Problem

> *"A client wants to redesign their homepage for an upcoming sale campaign. They want to build it now, have stakeholders review it, and have it go live automatically at midnight on launch day — without manually switching it."*

### Solution: Content Staging (EE Only)

Content Staging is one of the most powerful — and most tested — EE-exclusive features.

### What Content Staging Can Schedule

```
Stageable Content Types:
+----------------------------------+
| CMS Pages                        |
| CMS Blocks                       |
| Category attributes/images       |
| Product attributes/prices        |
| Catalog Price Rules              |
| Cart Price Rules                 |
| Banners (EE)                     |
+----------------------------------+
```

---

### How Staging Updates Work

```
Content Staging Workflow:
                                        TIMELINE
  NOW                                                         FUTURE
  |                                                              |
  v                                                              v
[Current Live Content]---+                             +---[Scheduled Update Goes Live]
                         |                             |
                         |   STAGING DASHBOARD         |
                         +-->[Update: "Summer Sale     |
                                 Homepage Redesign"]---+
                                 Start: July 1, 00:00
                                 End: July 8, 23:59 (optional)
```

**Creating a Scheduled Update:**

```
Admin > Content > Pages > [Homepage] > Schedule New Update
  - Update Name: "Summer Sale Homepage"
  - Description: "New hero banner and featured products"
  - Start Date: YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00
  - End Date: YYYY-MM-DD 23:59:59 (optional — reverts after)

  -> Make edits to the page within this update context
  -> Save

  Cron runs at scheduled time and publishes automatically.
```

---

### Preview Functionality

This directly addresses the "test before publishing" requirement:

```
Admin > Content > Content Staging > Dashboard
  -> Find the scheduled update
  -> Click "Preview"
     -> Opens a storefront preview URL with a timestamp parameter
     -> Stakeholders can review without affecting live site
     -> Preview link is shareable (with admin session or token)
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Preview** shows exactly how the site will look at the scheduled time.
- Preview does **not** affect the live storefront.
- Content Staging is **EE only** — CE has no native scheduling or preview.
- Updates can be **assigned to a campaign** — multiple content changes bundled together.
- If an update has **no end date**, it persists indefinitely (becomes the new default).
- If an update has an **end date**, content reverts to the previous version after that date.

---

### Staging Dashboard

```
Admin > Content > Content Staging > Dashboard

Timeline View:
  |---[Campaign A: Spring Sale]---|
                |---[Campaign B: Product Launch]---|
                                     |---[Campaign C: Holiday]---|

  Each bar shows start/end dates
  Overlapping campaigns are managed by priority
```

**Exam focus:**
- The Staging Dashboard provides a **timeline view** of all scheduled updates.
- You can **edit a scheduled update** before it goes live without creating a new one.
- Staging updates use a **versioning system** — each update is a version snapshot.

---

### Content Staging vs. Manual Publishing (CE Approach)

| Aspect | Content Staging (EE) | Manual Approach (CE) |
|---|---|---|
| Scheduling | Automatic via cron | Manual admin action required |
| Preview | Yes, shareable URL | No native preview |
| Rollback | Automatic (end date) | Manual revert |
| Campaign grouping | Yes | No |
| Multiple content types | Yes, in one campaign | Each item separately |

---

## 7. Supporting Concepts: Customer Groups & Segments

### Customer Groups Deep Dive

Every store interaction — pricing, tax, promotions — flows through Customer Groups. This is foundational knowledge.

```
Customer Group Assignment Sources:
+------------------------------------------+
| Source                 | Method           |
+------------------------------------------+
| Registration default   | Store config     |
| Admin manual assign    | Customer record  |
| VAT validation (EU)    | Automatic        |
| B2B Company assignment | Automatic        |
+------------------------------------------+
```

**VAT Group Auto-Assignment (important edge case):**
```
Admin > Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration
  > Create New Account Options
    - Enable Automatic Assignment to Customer Group: Yes
    - Default Group: General
    - Group for Valid VAT ID - Domestic: Wholesale
    - Group for Valid VAT ID - Intra-Union: [EU Wholesale]
    - Group for Invalid VAT ID: General
```

**Exam focus:**
- VAT-based auto-assignment is a **CE feature** — useful for EU merchants.
- A customer can only be in **one group at a time**.
- Changing a customer's group immediately affects their prices on next page load.

---

### Customer Segments vs. Groups — Exam Trap

The exam loves to test this distinction. Here is the precise decision rule:

```
Need to TARGET customers based on...

Real-time behavior (cart contents, browsing)?  --> Customer Segment (EE)
Historical behavior (past orders)?             --> Customer Segment (EE)
Static manual grouping?                        --> Customer Group (CE/EE)
Pricing differentiation?                       --> Customer Group (CE/EE)
                                                   (Segments feed into rules)
Personalized banner/content?                   --> Customer Segment (EE)
Category access restriction?                   --> Customer Group + 
                                                   Catalog Permissions (EE)
```

**Exam focus:**
- Customer Segments **cannot directly set prices** — they work through **Price Rules** that use segment as a condition.
- Customer Groups **can directly be used in Tier Prices** — more direct for pricing.

---

## 8. Supporting Concepts: B2B Module Ecosystem

### B2B Features Map (EE only)

```
Adobe Commerce B2B Module
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                           |
|  Company Accounts          Shared Catalogs                |
|  - Company hierarchy       - Custom product sets          |
|  - Company admin           - Custom pricing               |
|  - Sub-accounts/users      - Linked to companies          |
|                                                           |
|  Quotes (Negotiable)       Purchase Orders                |
|  - Request quote           - PO workflow                  |
|  - Admin negotiation       - Approval rules               |
|  - Accept/reject           - Payment on PO                |
|                                                           |
|  Requisition Lists         Quick Order                    |
|  - Saved shopping lists    - Order by SKU                 |
|  - Reorder quickly         - CSV upload                   |
|                                                           |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

### B2B Feature Dependency Chain

```
Prerequisite dependencies:
  Shared Catalog REQUIRES Company Accounts to be enabled
  Negotiable Quotes REQUIRES Company Accounts to be enabled
  Purchase Orders REQUIRES Company Accounts to be enabled
  Requisition Lists: independent (can work without Company)
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Company Accounts** is the master switch for B2B — most B2B features require it.
- `Admin > Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features` — enable/disable each B2B module here.
- **Requisition Lists** are the B2B equivalent of Wish Lists, but designed for repurchase.
- **Quick Order** allows ordering by SKU — critical for buyers who know exactly what they want. Note: Quick Order defaults to **disabled** — it must be explicitly enabled via B2B Features config.

---

### Negotiable Quotes Flow

```
B2B Quote Lifecycle:
  Buyer: Adds items to cart
      |
      v
  Buyer: Requests Quote (from cart or quotes page)
      |
      v
  Sales Rep: Reviews quote in Admin
      |
      +---> Adjusts prices, adds comments, sets expiry
      |
      v
  Sales Rep: Sends quote back to Buyer
      |
      v
  Buyer: Reviews, may counter-propose
      |
      v
  [Negotiation loop until agreed]
      |
      v
  Buyer: Accepts quote
      |
      v
  Quote converts to Order (locked prices honored)
```

**Exam focus:**
- A negotiable quote **locks the price** agreed during negotiation — catalog price changes don't affect it.
- Quotes expire based on an **expiry date** set during negotiation.
- Quotes exist in frontend statuses: Draft, Submitted, Open, Pending, Updated, Ordered, Expired, Declined, Closed (9 statuses). The "Draft" status is often overlooked but exists for quotes saved but not yet submitted.

---

## 9. Supporting Concepts: Payment Capture Modes Deep Dive

### Configuration Location

```
Admin > Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods
  > [Payment Provider e.g., Braintree, Authorize.net]
    - Payment Action: [Authorize / Authorize and Capture]
```

### Impact on Order Workflow

```
Authorize Only Configuration:
+----------+    +------------+    +----------+    +----------+
|  Order   | -> | Processing | -> | Invoice  | -> | Shipment |
| Placed   |    | (no inv.)  |    | Created  |    | Created  |
+----------+    +------------+    +----------+    +----------+
                     ^                 ^
                  STUCK HERE    Manual step required
                  (exam Q)      (triggers capture)

Authorize + Capture Configuration:
+----------+    +-------------------+    +----------+
|  Order   | -> | Processing        | -> | Shipment |
| Placed   |    | (auto-invoice)    |    | Created  |
+----------+    +-------------------+    +----------+
                         ^
                 Invoice auto-created,
                 no manual step needed
```

### Partial Invoicing & Partial Capture

```
Partial Invoice Scenario:
  Order: 3 items
  Invoice 1: items 1 & 2 -> captures partial amount
  Invoice 2: item 3 -> captures remaining amount

  Use case: backorders, partial fulfillment
  Result: Multiple invoices per order, multiple capture transactions
```

**Exam focus:**
- **One order can have multiple invoices** (partial invoicing).
- **One order can have multiple shipments** (partial shipping).
- **One order can have multiple credit memos** (partial refunds).
- The `can_invoice` flag is controlled by payment method and order state.

---

### Online vs. Offline Payment Actions

```
Online Payment Methods (gateway integration):
  - Authorize.net, Braintree, PayPal
  - Capture/refund triggers API call to gateway
  - Funds move in real-time

Offline Payment Methods:
  - Check/Money Order, Bank Transfer, Cash on Delivery
  - Invoice creation is administrative confirmation only
  - No API call — no actual fund movement
  - Admin must confirm receipt separately
```

**Exam focus:**
- For **offline payment methods**, creating an invoice does NOT move money — it is purely a record-keeping action.
- **Credit Memos** for online methods trigger a **refund API call** to the gateway. For offline methods, you must return funds manually.

---

## 10. Supporting Concepts: MSI Architecture

### Reservation System

MSI uses a **reservation system** to prevent overselling without permanently modifying Source quantities.

```
Reservation Flow:
  Customer adds to cart:
    -> NO reservation created — only availability checking occurs

  Customer places order:
    -> Reservation created: -qty (reduces Salable Quantity)
    -> Source Quantity unchanged at this point

  Admin ships order (creates shipment):
    -> Source deduction occurs (Source Item qty decremented)
    -> Compensating reservation created (+qty to offset the order reservation)
    -> Net reservation effect returns to zero

  Salable Qty = Sum(Source Qtys in Stock) + Sum(Reservations for that Stock)
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Salable Quantity** is what customers see — it factors in reservations.
- **Source Quantity** is the physical count — only deducted when a shipment is created.
- Salable Quantity drops when an **order is placed** (not when items are added to cart). The reservation is created by `AppendReservationsAfterOrderPlacementPlugin` at order placement time.

---

### Source Priority SSA Example

```
Stock: "US Store Stock"
  Sources (in priority order):
    1. East Coast WH (priority 1 - highest)
    2. Central WH    (priority 2)
    3. West Coast WH (priority 3)

Order for 150 units:
  - East Coast WH has 100 -> use 100, need 50 more
  - Central WH has 75    -> use 50 (need satisfied)

Result: Split shipment from 2 sources
```

---

### MSI and Multi-Source Product Configuration

```
Product Types and MSI:
+----------------------+------------------+
| Product Type         | MSI Support      |
+----------------------+------------------+
| Simple               | Yes - full       |
| Configurable         | Manage at child  |
| Bundle               | Manage at child  |
| Grouped              | Manage at child  |
| Virtual              | Yes (no ship)    |
| Downloadable         | Yes (no ship)    |
+----------------------+------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- For **Configurable products**, inventory is managed at the **simple product (child)** level, not the configurable parent.
- You cannot assign quantities directly to a configurable product parent.

---

## 11. Supporting Concepts: Content Staging & Preview

### Staging Update Types

```
Update Types:
  Permanent (no end date):
    - Content permanently changes at start date
    - No automatic revert

  Temporary (with end date):
    - Content changes at start date
    - Content REVERTS at end date
    - Useful for: sales, seasonal promotions, holidays
```

### Campaign vs. Update

```
Terminology:
  Update   = A single scheduled change to one content item
             (e.g., change Homepage CMS page layout)

  Campaign = A collection of updates bundled together
             (e.g., "Black Friday Campaign" containing:
               - Homepage update
               - Banner update  
               - Catalog price rule activation
               - Product price changes)
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Multiple content changes** for one business event should be grouped into a **Campaign** for coordinated publishing.
- A Campaign has one **start/end date** that governs all its updates.
- You can view a **Preview** of a campaign to see all changes simultaneously before they go live.

---

### Staging + Products

Product staging is nuanced:

```
What CAN be staged for products:
  - Name, description, images
  - Price (including special prices)
  - Category assignments
  - Product status (enabled/disabled)
  - Tax class

What CANNOT be directly staged:
  - Inventory quantities (MSI qtys)
  - SKU changes
  - Product type changes
  - Tier prices (listed in unassignable attributes)
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Product price changes** CAN be staged — very common exam scenario ("client wants prices to automatically change during flash sale").
- Staging a product price change is more reliable than a Catalog Price Rule for precise timing.

---

## 12. Architect-Style Decision Framework

### The "What Would a Business Practitioner Recommend?" Matrix

Use this framework when reading any scenario question:

```
STEP 1: Identify the Business Need Category
  +---> Pricing differentiation?     -> Pricing tools
  +---> Content/visibility control?  -> Permission/Staging tools  
  +---> Inventory/fulfillment?        -> MSI tools
  +---> Order issues?                 -> Order management
  +---> B2B workflows?               -> B2B module features

STEP 2: Identify Edition
  +---> CE or EE? (look for clues: "enterprise", "B2B", "cloud")
  +---> If EE: more powerful options available
  +---> If CE: stick to CE-native solutions

STEP 3: Identify Scope
  +---> All customers or specific group?
  +---> All products or subset?
  +---> All stores or one website?

STEP 4: Match to Native Feature (prefer over custom dev)
  +---> Is there a native feature?  -> Recommend it
  +---> Is there no native feature? -> Flag as extension need
```

---

### Quick Scenario-to-Solution Reference Table

| Business Scenario | Correct Solution | Edition |
|---|---|---|
| Different prices for B2B vs. retail | Customer Group Tier Pricing | CE + EE |
| Different prices + hide products from retail | Shared Catalog | B2B EE |
| Per-customer negotiated prices | Negotiable Quotes | B2B EE |
| Category visible only to logged-in users | Catalog Permissions | EE |
| Personalized banner for high-spend customers | Customer Segments + Banners | EE |
| Ship from nearest of 3 warehouses | MSI Distance Priority SSA | CE + EE |
| All orders stuck in Processing | Invoice manually (Authorize Only mode) | CE + EE |
| Schedule homepage change for future date | Content Staging Update | EE |
| Preview site changes before publishing | Content Staging Preview | EE |
| B2B buyers reorder regular supplies | Requisition Lists | B2B EE |
| Corporate purchaser needs PO approval workflow | Purchase Orders + Approval Rules | B2B EE |
| Flash sale: auto-apply/remove discount | Catalog Price Rule with schedule OR Staged Product Price | CE (rule) / EE (staging) |
| EU merchant needs tax-exempt wholesale group | VAT Auto-Assignment to Customer Group | CE + EE |
| Single product, different price at qty 10+ | Tier Pricing | CE + EE |

---

### Common Exam Distractors

```
TRAP 1: "Customer wants products hidden from group"
  Wrong answer: Customer Groups (they control pricing, NOT visibility)
  Right answer: Catalog Permissions (EE) + Customer Groups

TRAP 2: "Dynamic content based on cart value"
  Wrong answer: Customer Groups (static, not real-time cart-aware)
  Right answer: Customer Segments (EE) — evaluates cart in real-time

TRAP 3: "Orders stuck in Processing = payment failed"
  Wrong answer: Refund and reorder
  Right answer: Check payment capture mode; create invoice to capture

TRAP 4: "Test new page = create a new page and swap"
  Wrong answer: Duplicate the CMS page, manually activate
  Right answer: Content Staging scheduled update with Preview (EE)

TRAP 5: "Multiple warehouses = just add multiple addresses"
  Wrong answer: Multiple shipping origins in config
  Right answer: MSI Sources + Stocks
```

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Pricing & Customer Groups
- [ ] Customer Groups exist in **CE and EE** — they are NOT EE-exclusive
- [ ] Tier Prices can be set per-group per-quantity on each product
- [ ] A customer belongs to **only one Customer Group** at a time
- [ ] **Shared Catalog = B2B EE only** — hides products AND sets custom prices per company
- [ ] Shared Catalog has two types: **Public** (replaces default) and **Custom** (per company)
- [ ] When Shared Catalog is enabled, it **replaces** the standard catalog as the default
- [ ] Catalog Price Rules run on **cron** — not real-time until reindex
- [ ] Negotiable Quotes allow **per-order price negotiation** — B2B EE only
- [ ] Negotiated quote prices are **locked** — immune to catalog price changes

### Content Visibility & Permissions
- [ ] **Catalog Permissions = EE only** — controls category browsing, price display, add-to-cart by group
- [ ] Must enable **Category Permissions** globally before applying per-category (config label is "Category Permissions")
- [ ] Catalog Permissions apply at **category level** and cascade to products
- [ ] "NOT LOGGED IN" Customer Group = guest customers
- [ ] **Customer Segments = EE only** — dynamic, real-time, behavior-based groupings
- [ ] Customer Segments power: banners, price rules, related products, private sales
- [ ] Customer Segments do NOT directly restrict catalog visibility — use Catalog Permissions for that
- [ ] Customer Segments cannot directly set prices — they condition Price Rules

### Multi-Source Inventory (MSI)
- [ ] MSI is available in **CE and EE** — not EE-exclusive
- [ ] **Source** = physical location; **Stock** = virtual pool assigned to a website
- [ ] **Salable Quantity** = aggregate across Sources minus reservations (what customer sees)
- [ ] Source Quantity is only **physically deducted** when a shipment is created
- [ ] **Source Priority SSA** — fulfills from Sources in admin-defined order (no external dependency)
- [ ] **Distance Priority SSA** — fulfills from nearest Source; **requires Google Maps API**
- [ ] A Stock is assigned to a **Sales Channel** (website)
- [ ] Default Source and Default Stock **cannot be deleted**
- [ ] Configurable product inventory managed at **child (simple) product** level
- [ ] MSI **reservations** are created at **order placement** (not cart add) — prevents overselling without changing source qty

### Order Processing & Payment Capture
- [ ] **Authorize Only mode** = #1 cause of orders stuck in Processing on exam
- [ ] Fix for Authorize Only = **create an invoice** to trigger payment capture
- [ ] `Payment Action = Authorize` → manual invoice required
- [ ] `Payment Action = Authorize and Capture` → auto-invoice created
- [ ] Order in Processing **with no invoice** = waiting for capture (Authorize Only)
- [ ] Order in Processing **with invoice** = waiting for shipment
- [ ] Order **States** are fixed/hardcoded; **Statuses** are configurable labels mapped to states
- [ ] You cannot create custom **States** — only custom **Statuses**
- [ ] One order can have **multiple invoices**, shipments, and credit memos (partial operations)
- [ ] Offline payment invoices do NOT move money — record-keeping only
- [ ] Online payment credit memos trigger a **refund API call** to gateway

### Content Staging & Preview
- [ ] **Content Staging = EE only** — CE has no native scheduling
- [ ] Staged content types: CMS pages, CMS blocks, categories, products, price rules, banners
- [ ] Permanent updates (no end date) persist indefinitely
- [ ] Temporary updates (with end date) **automatically revert** after end date
- [ ] **Preview** = shareable URL showing site at scheduled time — does NOT affect live site
- [ ] **Campaign** = multiple updates bundled together for one business event
- [ ] Product **prices can be staged** — useful for flash sales with precise timing
- [ ] Inventory quantities **cannot** be staged
- [ ] Staging Dashboard shows **timeline view** of all scheduled campaigns

### B2B Module Ecosystem
- [ ] All major B2B features require **Company Accounts** to be enabled first
- [ ] B2B module features: Company Accounts, Shared Catalog, Negotiable Quotes, Purchase Orders, Requisition Lists, Quick Order
- [ ] **Requisition Lists** = B2B equivalent of wish lists, for repurchase workflows
- [ ] **Quick Order** = order by SKU entry or CSV upload (defaults to disabled)
- [ ] **Purchase Orders** include approval rules — configurable workflow with dollar thresholds
- [ ] B2B configuration: `Admin > Stores > Configuration > General > B2B Features`

### Architect Decision Rules
- [ ] "Different prices for B2B" → Customer Group Tier Pricing (CE/EE) or Shared Catalog (B2B EE)
- [ ] "Hide products from non-members" → Shared Catalog (B2B EE) or Catalog Permissions (EE)
- [ ] "Content only for logged-in" → Catalog Permissions deny "NOT LOGGED IN" group
- [ ] "Personalized content based on behavior" → Customer Segments + Banners (EE)
- [ ] "Multiple warehouses, ship from nearest" → MSI Distance Priority SSA (+ Google Maps)
- [ ] "Multiple warehouses, control priority" → MSI Source Priority SSA
- [ ] "All orders stuck in Processing" → Authorize Only payment mode, create invoices
- [ ] "Test page before publishing" → Content Staging Update + Preview (EE)
- [ ] "Auto-publish on specific date" → Content Staging Scheduled Update (EE)
- [ ] "B2B buyer wants to save order templates" → Requisition Lists (B2B EE)
- [ ] "Corporate needs PO approval" → Purchase Orders with Approval Rules (B2B EE)
- [ ] CE + "need to hide categories" → No native solution; extension or EE upgrade required

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Shared Catalog product hiding and Catalog Permissions?
flashcards.answer: Shared Catalog (B2B EE) controls which products are visible AND sets custom pricing per company — unassigned products are completely hidden from search, categories, and direct URLs. Catalog Permissions (EE) controls category-level browsing, price display, and add-to-cart per customer group. Customer Groups alone cannot hide products.
flashcards.hint: One is B2B-focused and controls per-company visibility; the other restricts by category for any customer group.

flashcards.question: How do Customer Segments differ from Customer Groups, and which edition supports each?
flashcards.answer: Customer Groups (CE + EE) are static, manually assigned, and directly used for tier pricing. Customer Segments (EE only) are dynamic, real-time groupings based on behavior (cart contents, order history). Segments cannot directly set prices — they work through Price Rules that use the segment as a condition.
flashcards.hint: One is static and manual; the other is dynamic and behavior-based.

flashcards.question: What is the #1 exam cause of orders stuck in 'Processing' status, and what is the fix?
flashcards.answer: The #1 cause is Authorize Only payment mode. When Payment Action is set to 'Authorize' instead of 'Authorize and Capture', invoices are not auto-created. The fix is to create an invoice manually (Sales > Orders > [Order] > Invoice), which triggers the actual payment capture.
flashcards.hint: Look at whether an invoice exists — no invoice means the payment was never captured.

flashcards.question: What can and cannot be staged using Content Staging in Adobe Commerce EE?
flashcards.answer: Stageable content: CMS pages, CMS blocks, category attributes/images, product attributes/prices, catalog price rules, cart price rules, and banners. Cannot be staged: inventory quantities, SKU changes, product type changes, and tier prices. Content Staging is EE only — CE has no native scheduling.
flashcards.hint: Think about what defines a product vs what decorates it — the fundamental identity cannot be scheduled.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between a permanent and temporary Content Staging update?
flashcards.answer: A permanent update (no end date) persists indefinitely and becomes the new default. A temporary update (with end date) automatically reverts to the previous version after the end date. Multiple content changes for one business event should be grouped into a Campaign for coordinated publishing.
flashcards.hint: The presence or absence of an end date determines whether changes are automatically rolled back.

flashcards.question: What prerequisites does the Distance Priority Source Selection Algorithm require in MSI?
flashcards.answer: The Distance Priority SSA requires a Google Maps API key configured in the system, complete source addresses (latitude/longitude or full address), and a resolvable customer shipping address. Without these, you must use the Source Priority algorithm which requires no external dependencies.
flashcards.hint: Geographic calculation needs a mapping service and proper address data.

flashcards.question: What are the three condition types available for B2B Purchase Order approval rules?
flashcards.answer: Only three condition types exist: Order Total (grand_total), Shipping Cost (shipping_incl_tax), and Number of SKUs (number_of_skus). There is no category-based condition. PO approval rules are configured by the Company Admin, not the merchant admin. To always require approval, set Order Total > $0.
flashcards.hint: The conditions are about the order's size and cost, not what products are in it.

flashcards.question: When a merchant on EE wants to restrict a category to only logged-in Gold members, what two features are needed?
flashcards.answer: Two features working together: 1) Catalog Permissions (EE) to deny the 'NOT LOGGED IN' group and all non-Gold groups from browsing the category. 2) Customer Segments (EE) to dynamically identify Gold members based on lifetime spend criteria, which can feed into price rules for benefits.
flashcards.hint: One feature controls visibility; the other identifies qualifying customers dynamically.

flashcards.question: Why do Negotiable Quotes bypass catalog price rules, and what pricing applies instead?
flashcards.answer: Negotiable Quotes bypass catalog price rules because pricing is 100% manually negotiated between the buyer and sales rep. Tier prices and special prices are also not automatically applied. The sales rep has full manual control, and the negotiated price is locked when the buyer accepts and checks out.
flashcards.hint: The whole point of negotiation is that the agreed price overrides all automatic rules.

flashcards.question: What does an order in Processing state WITH an invoice mean versus WITHOUT an invoice?
flashcards.answer: Processing WITH no invoice means the order is waiting for payment capture (Authorize Only mode — the fix is to create an invoice). Processing WITH an invoice means payment was captured and the order is waiting for shipment to move to Complete state.
flashcards.hint: The presence of the invoice document tells you whether the payment step is done.

flashcards.question: What is the correct solution when a merchant needs products hidden from non-members — Customer Groups or Shared Catalog?
flashcards.answer: Customer Groups alone cannot hide products — they only control pricing, tax, and promotions. To hide products from non-members, use Shared Catalog (B2B EE) which controls product visibility per company, or Catalog Permissions (EE) which controls category browsing per customer group.
flashcards.hint: The trap is assuming that pricing groups also control visibility — they do not.

flashcards.question: Can one order have multiple invoices, shipments, and credit memos?
flashcards.answer: Yes, one order can have multiple invoices (partial invoicing), multiple shipments (partial shipping), and multiple credit memos (partial refunds). Partial invoicing captures payment for only some items. A partial credit memo keeps the order in 'processing' state; only a full credit memo moves it to 'closed'.
flashcards.hint: All three order documents support partial operations for flexible fulfillment.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between offline and online payment method behavior when creating invoices and credit memos?
flashcards.answer: For online payment methods (Braintree, PayPal), creating an invoice triggers an API capture call to the gateway, and credit memos trigger refund API calls. For offline methods (Check/MO, Bank Transfer), creating an invoice is purely record-keeping — no API call and no money movement. Funds must be managed manually.
flashcards.hint: One type communicates with external systems; the other is just bookkeeping.

flashcards.question: What does 'Discard subsequent rules' do in both Catalog and Cart Price Rules?
flashcards.answer: 'Discard subsequent rules' prevents lower-priority rules from applying once the current rule matches. In catalog rules, this means no further catalog price rules are applied. In cart rules, it prevents rule stacking. Lower priority number means higher priority (applied first).
flashcards.hint: It is a stop-processing flag that prevents further discounts from stacking.

## 3. Product Types Quick Reference

- **Exam focus:** Know which product types support which features (qty tracking, configurable options, weight/shipping, child products).

| Product Type | Child Products | Qty Tracked At | Configurable Options | Downloadable? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Simple** | No | Product level | No | No | Most basic unit; used as child in others |
| **Virtual** | No | Product level | No | No | No shipping required (services, memberships) |
| **Downloadable** | No | Product level | No | Yes | Has links/samples; delivery is digital file |
| **Grouped** | Yes (simple) | Each simple | No | No | Displayed together, bought separately |
| **Configurable** | Yes (simple) | Each simple child | Yes (attributes) | No | One SKU presented, child SKUs track stock |
| **Bundle** | Yes (simple/virtual) | Dynamic (each child) | Yes (options) | No | Fixed or Dynamic pricing; required or optional items |
| **Gift Card** | No | Product level | No | No | EE only; virtual, physical, or combined |

### Product Type Deep-Dive Notes

#### Configurable vs Bundle

```
Configurable:
  Parent SKU (e.g., T-Shirt)
     |--- Child SKU: T-Shirt-Red-S
     |--- Child SKU: T-Shirt-Red-M
     |--- Child SKU: T-Shirt-Blue-S
  Customer selects attribute value -> resolves to one child SKU
  Price: set on child, parent can show "as low as"

Bundle:
  Parent SKU (e.g., Camera Kit)
     |--- Option 1: Camera Body (required)
     |        |--- Simple A / Simple B
     |--- Option 2: Memory Card (optional)
     |        |--- 16GB / 32GB / 64GB
  Customer builds the bundle; price is sum or fixed
```

- **Exam focus:** Configurable products track stock at the **child (simple)** level. The parent has no physical stock.
- **Exam focus:** Bundle products can have **Fixed** or **Dynamic** price type. Dynamic price = sum of selected child prices.
- **Exam focus:** Grouped products do **not** have a combined cart line item — each simple is added separately.
- **Exam focus:** Gift Card is **EE only**.
- **Exam focus:** Virtual products do **not** trigger shipping calculation.
- **Exam focus:** Downloadable products have **links** (the file) and **samples** (previews); links can be purchased separately if configured.

#### Weight / Shipping

| Product Type | Has Weight | Triggers Shipping |
|---|---|---|
| Simple | Yes (configurable) | Yes |
| Virtual | No | No |
| Downloadable | No | No |
| Grouped | Per child simple | Per child simple |
| Configurable | Per child simple | Yes (child determines weight) |
| Bundle | Per components | Yes (if any physical child) |

## 4. Order States and Statuses Table

- **Exam focus:** **State** is system-level (code). **Status** is the human-readable label mapped to a state. Multiple statuses can map to one state.
- **Exam focus:** You can create **custom statuses** and assign them to states, but you cannot create new **states** — states are hardcoded.

### Core Order States

| State (Code) | Default Status | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `new` | Pending | Order placed, payment not yet captured/confirmed |
| `pending_payment` | Pending Payment | Awaiting payment gateway response |
| `processing` | Processing | Payment confirmed; order being fulfilled |
| `complete` | Complete | Fully invoiced, shipped, and no open returns |
| `closed` | Closed | Has a credit memo applied (refunded) |
| `canceled` | Canceled | Order was canceled |
| `holded` | On Hold | Manually placed on hold by admin |
| `payment_review` | Payment Review | Payment flagged for manual review (e.g., fraud check) |

### State / Status Flow Diagram

```
[Placed] --> new (Pending)
                |
                v
         pending_payment
         (awaiting gateway)
                |
                v
           processing  <--- Invoice created here
                |
          +-----+------+
          |            |
          v            v
       complete      closed
    (shipped +     (credit memo
     invoiced)      applied)

[Any state] --> canceled (if cancellable)
[Any state] --> holded   (manual hold)
```

### Key Facts About Statuses

```
State "new" can have statuses:
  - "Pending" (default)
  - Custom status you create (e.g., "Fraud Check Pending")

State "processing" can have statuses:
  - "Processing" (default)
  - Custom status (e.g., "Backordered", "Gift Wrapping")
```

- **Exam focus:** `closed` ≠ `canceled`. Closed = refunded. Canceled = never processed.
- **Exam focus:** An order cannot go back to `new` from `processing`.
- **Exam focus:** Credit memos set state to `closed`. Partial credit memos keep state as `processing`.
- **Exam focus:** `holded` state is the only state you can manually set AND manually release (`Unhold`).

## 6. Pricing Hierarchy

- **Exam focus:** Magento uses a **priority-based price waterfall**. The final price applied is the **lowest applicable price** after running through the hierarchy.

### Price Priority Waterfall (Highest to Lowest Priority)

```
Price Waterfall (lower number = higher priority)
+--------------------------------------------------+
| 1. Custom Price (admin order creation override)  |  <- Admin only
+--------------------------------------------------+
| 2. Special Price (date-limited)                  |
+--------------------------------------------------+
| 3. Tier Price (qty-based)                        |
+--------------------------------------------------+
| 4. Group Price (customer group)                  |  <- EE: also Shared Catalog price
+--------------------------------------------------+
| 5. Regular Price (base price)                    |
+--------------------------------------------------+
| After product price is determined:               |
+--------------------------------------------------+
| 6. Catalog Price Rules applied                   |
+--------------------------------------------------+
| 7. Cart Price Rules applied (at checkout)        |
+--------------------------------------------------+
```

> **Important:** Magento always picks the **lowest price** at each relevant level.

### Price Type Descriptions

| Price Type | Scope | Set Where | Beats |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Regular Price** | Website | Product edit page | Nothing (base) |
| **Special Price** | Website | Product edit, with dates | Regular price |
| **Tier Price** | Website | Product edit, qty breaks | Special + Regular |
| **Group Price** | Website | (Legacy — merged into tier) | Regular |
| **Custom Option Price** | N/A | Adds to base price | N/A (additive) |
| **Catalog Rule Price** | Website/Group | Catalog Price Rules | Computed price |
| **Cart Discount** | Quote | Cart Price Rules | Applied to cart total |
| **Shared Catalog Price** (EE) | Website/Company | Shared Catalog | Group price for B2B |

### Tier Price Example

```php
// Tier price structure:
// Qty >= 1:  $100.00 (regular)
// Qty >= 5:  $90.00  (tier)
// Qty >= 10: $80.00  (tier)
// Special:   $85.00 (date range active)

// Customer buys qty=1:  min($100, $85) = $85 (special wins)
// Customer buys qty=5:  min($90, $85)  = $85 (special wins vs tier)
// Customer buys qty=10: min($80, $85)  = $80 (tier wins vs special)
```

- **Exam focus:** If a **tier price** is lower than the **special price**, the tier price wins.
- **Exam focus:** Special price and tier price compete — the **lowest** is displayed.
- **Exam focus:** Catalog price rules run on the **product price** before the cart. Cart rules run **at checkout** on the cart total or items.
- **Exam focus:** `custom_price` set by admin in order creation overrides **everything**.

## 7. Cart Rule vs Catalog Rule

- **Exam focus:** This is a heavily tested distinction. Know all differences.

### Side-by-Side Comparison

| Attribute | Catalog Price Rule | Cart Price Rule |
|---|---|---|
| **When Applied** | Before cart (on product listing/detail) | At checkout / in cart |
| **Displayed As** | Strikethrough original price + new price | Discount line in cart totals |
| **Coupon Code** | No coupon codes | Optional coupon code |
| **Conditions** | Category, attribute, price | Cart total, qty, product attributes, customer segment |
| **Actions** | Apply % or fixed discount to price | Apply % or fixed to cart/item, free shipping, buy X get Y |
| **Customer Groups** | Yes | Yes |
| **Priority** | Lower number = higher priority | Lower number = higher priority |
| **Discard Subsequent Rules** | Yes (checkbox) | Yes (checkbox) |
| **Free Shipping** | No | Yes |
| **Buy X Get Y** | No | Yes |
| **Usage Limit** | No limit concept | Limit per coupon, per customer |
| **Auto-Apply** | Yes (always if conditions met) | Yes if no coupon; optional with coupon |
| **Staging (EE)** | Yes | Yes |
| **Scope** | Website | Website |
| **Affects** | Product price in catalog | Cart subtotal / line items |

### Visual Flow

```
Customer browses catalog:
  Product Price
      |
      v
  [Catalog Price Rule runs here]
      |
      v
  Displayed price on page (may show strikethrough)

Customer adds to cart and checks out:
  Cart Items (at catalog-rule-adjusted prices)
      |
      v
  [Cart Price Rules run here]
      |
      v
  Discounts/free shipping applied to cart total
```

### Catalog Price Rule Actions

```
1. Apply as percentage of original    -> reduces by X%
2. Apply as fixed amount              -> reduces by $X
3. Adjust final price to this %       -> sets to X% of original
4. Adjust final price to discount value -> sets to $X
```

### Cart Price Rule Actions

```
1. Percent of product price discount
2. Fixed amount discount
3. Fixed amount discount for whole cart
4. Buy X get Y free (discount)
5. Free shipping (standalone or combined)
```

- **Exam focus:** Only **cart price rules** support **coupon codes** and **free shipping**.
- **Exam focus:** Only **cart price rules** support **Buy X Get Y**.
- **Exam focus:** Catalog price rules show the discount **on the product page**; cart rules show in the **cart totals**.
- **Exam focus:** Both support "**Discard subsequent rules**" to prevent rule stacking. (The actual UI label is "Discard subsequent rules", not "Stop Further Rules Processing".)

### Negotiable Quote Flow

```
Step 1: Buyer adds products to cart
            |
            v
Step 2: Buyer requests a quote from cart
         (enters note, desired price/discount)
            |
            v
Step 3: Quote status = "Submitted"
            |
            v
Step 4: Admin (Sales Rep) reviews quote
         - Can change prices, add discounts, set expiry
         - Can add comments
            |
            v
Step 5: Admin sends quote back -> status = "Updated"
            |
            v
Step 6: Buyer reviews -> can accept, decline, or counter-offer

#### Negotiable Quote Statuses (Frontend)

| Status | Who Sets It | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Draft | Buyer | Saved but not yet submitted |
| Submitted | Buyer | Sent to admin for review |
| Open | Active | Active negotiation in progress |
| Pending | Admin reviewing | Admin has opened / is reviewing |
| Updated | Admin | Admin sent back to buyer |
| Ordered | System | Buyer converted quote to order |
| Closed | Admin/Buyer | Negotiation ended without order |
| Declined | Admin | Admin rejected the quote request |
| Expired | System | Quote passed expiry date |

Note: There are 9 frontend statuses. Backend statuses use different labels (e.g., STATUS_CREATED shows as "New" in backend, "Submitted" on frontend).

- **Exam focus:** A negotiable quote **locks prices** at the agreed amount when buyer checks out.
- **Exam focus:** Only users with `checkout` permission in their company role can convert a quote to an order.

### Purchase Orders (POs)

```
Buyer places order -> Creates Purchase Order (instead of immediate order)

      v
PO goes through Approval Rules (defined by Company Admin)

      |
      +-- If requires manual approval: notifies approvers

               v

               v

| Approval Rule Type | Example |
|---|---|

| Number of SKUs (number_of_skus) | Orders with > 10 unique SKUs need approval |
| Shipping cost (shipping_incl_tax) | If shipping > $50 needs approval |

## 9. MSI — Source, Stock, and Reservation

- **Exam focus:** MSI is available in **both CE and EE** (MSI modules have OSL-3.0 open-source license). Understand the three-layer model: Source → Stock → Sales Channel.

### MSI Conceptual Architecture

```
Physical Warehouses / Locations
+------------------+  +------------------+  +------------------+
|   SOURCE: WH-1   |  |   SOURCE: WH-2   |  |   SOURCE: WH-3   |
|  (New York)      |  |  (Los Angeles)   |  |  (London)        |
|  SKU-A: 100 qty  |  |  SKU-A: 50 qty   |  |  SKU-A: 200 qty  |
+------------------+  +------------------+  +------------------+
         |                    |                    |
         +--------+-----------+--------------------+
                  |
                  v
           +-------------+       +---------------+
           |  STOCK: US  |       |  STOCK: EU    |
           |  (WH-1,WH-2)|       |  (WH-3)       |
           +-------------+       +---------------+
                  |                    |
                  v                    v
         US Website (Main)         EU Website
         [Sales Channel]          [Sales Channel]
```

### Key Concepts

| Concept | Description |
|---|---|
| **Source** | Physical inventory location (warehouse, store, 3PL). Has address, contact, qty per SKU. |
| **Stock** | Logical aggregation of one or more Sources. Linked to a Sales Channel. |
| **Sales Channel** | A Website. Each stock is assigned to one or more websites. |
| **Source Item** | The qty of a specific SKU at a specific Source. |
| **Salable Quantity** | Calculated: Sum of source quantities minus reservations. Shown to customer. |
| **Reservation** | Temporary hold on quantity when order is placed (before shipment). |
| **Source Selection Algorithm (SSA)** | Algorithm that determines which source to ship from. |
| **Default Source** | The single source used for CE (single-source) setups. |
| **Default Stock** | The stock linked to the Default Source; always present. |

### Salable Quantity Formula

```
Salable Quantity = SUM(Source Quantities) - Reservations

Example:
  WH-1: 100 units of SKU-A
  WH-2: 50 units of SKU-A
  Open reservations (unshipped orders): 30 units

  Salable Qty = (100 + 50) - 30 = 120 units displayed to customer
```

### Reservation System

```
Order Placed:
  Reservation created: -X qty (negative, holds inventory)
    |
    v
  Salable qty decreases immediately

Order Shipped / Source Deducted:
  Source item qty decremented (actual warehouse qty reduced)
  Reservation "compensated" (positive reservation added to cancel out negative)
    |
    v
  Net reservation = 0 for that order
  Source qty is now the truth

Order Canceled:
  Compensation reservation (+X) added
    |
    v
  Salable qty restored
```

- **Exam focus:** Reservations are how MSI handles **concurrency** — prevents overselling while actual deduction happens asynchronously.
- **Exam focus:** The **Source** holds actual physical qty. The **Stock** holds salable qty for customers to see.

### Source Selection Algorithms (SSA)

| Algorithm | Description | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| **Priority-Based** | Ships from sources in priority order until qty filled | Default; simple priority list |
| **Distance-Based** | Ships from closest source to shipping address | Requires Google Maps API; minimizes shipping cost |
| **Custom** | Implement `SourceSelectionInterface` | Custom business logic |

- **Exam focus:** **Distance-Based SSA** requires Google Maps API configuration.
- **Exam focus:** You can set source **priority** per stock — lower number = higher priority.
- **Exam focus:** SSA is selected at **shipment creation time**, not configured per-stock in the admin. The default algorithm is Priority-Based.

### MSI Key Admin Actions

| Action | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Create Source | Stores > Inventory > Sources | Add warehouse/location |
| Create Stock | Stores > Inventory > Stocks | Aggregate sources; assign to website |
| Assign Source to Product | Product edit > Sources | Set qty per source |
| Transfer Inventory | Catalog > Products > Action | Bulk move qty between sources |
| Source Priority | Stock edit > Sources tab | Drag to reorder priority |

- **Exam focus:** In MSI, **each source is assigned to a product individually** with its own qty.
- **Exam focus:** The **Default Stock** cannot be deleted. The **Default Source** cannot be deleted or disabled.
